title: Aircraft Owned Through Trusts
idea: Rank registrant names and type_registrant codes to surface trust and LLC registrations, mapped by state. Viewer sees the states that function as aircraft ownership shells.
harm_angle: Anonymous aircraft ownership hides who is flying where, including in enforcement and trafficking cases.
caveat: county and country are cast to numbers which suggests those columns are codes or mis-typed; trust detection needs name-pattern matching.

title: Registration Address Clusters
idea: Map the street plus zip_code of registrants to find single addresses hosting dozens or hundreds of aircraft.
harm_angle: One mailbox holding hundreds of aircraft is the shape of a shell-ownership industry.
caveat: Address strings need normalization; some clusters are legitimate leasing companies.

title: Fleet Age by Owner Type
idea: Distribution of year_mfr by type_registrant and certification class. Viewer sees which owner categories fly the oldest airframes.
harm_angle: Old airframes in commercial-adjacent categories put passengers on aircraft older than the pilots.
caveat: year_mfr is an untyped passthrough; certification codes need decoding.

title: Expiring and Lapsed Registrations
idea: Timeline of expiration_date against last_action_date and status_code. Viewer sees aircraft flying on lapsed or about-to-lapse registrations.
harm_angle: A lapsed registration is a plane nobody is formally responsible for.
caveat: status_code semantics need the FAA codebook; date casts are try_to_date over text.

title: Hidden Co-Owner Chains
idea: Network linking n_number records that share other_names entries. Viewer sees ownership webs spanning many tail numbers.
harm_angle: Co-owner chains are how a single beneficial owner controls a fleet without appearing on any one registration.
caveat: other_names fields are frequently blank; name matching will produce false links.

title: FAA Dataset Inventory
idea: List FAA datasets by category, geographic scope and last updated date.
harm_angle: Shows which parts of aviation the FAA publishes on and which it does not.
caveat: Only 4 rows - genuinely too thin for more than an inventory listing; update_frequency is cast to a date which suggests a mis-typed column.

title: Catalog Fields That Do Not Fit
idea: Show the stray n_number, airport_id, lat and lon columns present on a 4-row catalog table as a data-quality exhibit.
harm_angle: A catalog table carrying aircraft-level columns is a sign the ingest merged two different things.
caveat: This is a data-quality artifact rather than a finding about the world.

title: Leveraged Money Versus Dealers
idea: Timeline of lev_money_positions_long_all against dealer_positions_short_all per market. Viewer sees speculative crowding building before market stress.
harm_angle: Speculative crowding in rate and index futures is what turns a market wobble into a pension loss.
caveat: 3,163 rows suggests a partial history; position columns are untyped passthroughs. The mart lives under the education schema, which looks like a mis-filed domain.

title: Weekly Position Swings
idea: Distribution of the change_in columns per trader class, to show which class moves fastest and largest.
harm_angle: Whoever moves first and largest sets prices everyone else pays.
caveat: Partial history; a market-by-market normalization is needed to compare.

title: Speculators in Food Commodities
idea: Timeline of noncommercial versus commercial long positions in agricultural contracts. Viewer sees speculative share of food markets rising ahead of price spikes.
harm_angle: Speculation in wheat and corn futures shows up as grocery prices in the poorest households.
caveat: 16,764 rows is likely a partial history; commodity grouping needs parsing out of the market name text.

title: Nonreportable Traders Squeezed Out
idea: Timeline of nonreportable_positions_long_all as a share of open interest per market. Viewer sees small traders shrinking out of markets over time.
harm_angle: Small traders vanishing means price formation is left entirely to institutions.
caveat: Partial history; nonreportable is a residual category not a real trader count.

title: Old Versus Other Crop Year Split
idea: Compare open_interest_old against open_interest_other per agricultural market to show positioning across harvest cycles.
harm_angle: Positioning across harvest years is where a bad harvest becomes a price shock for consumers.
caveat: Only meaningful for agricultural contracts; partial history.

title: Safety-Net Clinic Coverage Map
idea: Map FQHC enrollments by zip and state, showing counties with no federally qualified health center at all.
harm_angle: Counties with no FQHC are counties where uninsured people have no primary care option at all.
caveat: Snapshot with no time axis; incorporation_state is cast to a double which means that column is likely broken.

title: Nonprofit Versus For-Profit Safety Net
idea: Ranked bars of FQHC counts by proprietary_nonprofit and organization_type_structure per state. Viewer sees states where the safety net is run for profit.
harm_angle: A for-profit safety net answers to owners before it answers to uninsured patients.
caveat: Snapshot only; type-structure codes need decoding.

title: Clinic Chains Behind Local Names
idea: Group by associate_id and doing_business_as_name to find single owners operating many clinics under different local names.
harm_angle: Local-looking clinics owned by one distant operator means one business decision can close care in a dozen communities.
caveat: associate_id must be checked for population and distinctness before it is trusted as an owner key.

title: Age of the Safety Net
idea: Distribution of incorporation_date by state. Viewer sees where the safety net is old and established versus newly and thinly built.
harm_angle: Newly built safety nets in high-need states are thin and fragile exactly where they are needed most.
caveat: incorporation_date is a try_to_date cast over text and may be widely null.

title: Injury volume by product ranked
idea: Weighted national injury estimates by product code, ranked, naming the consumer products that put the most people in emergency rooms.
harm_angle: Every bar is thousands of real emergency room visits caused by something sold as safe.
caveat: Product codes need the NEISS code lookup to be readable; statistical_weight must be applied or counts are wrong.

title: Child injuries by product and age
idea: Heatmap of product against age band for patients under eighteen, weighted, showing which products hurt which ages.
harm_angle: Products concentrated on toddlers are design decisions with a body count.
caveat: NEISS encodes infant ages in a special numeric range meaning months and mis-parsing that inverts the chart.

title: Injury disparity by race and product
idea: Weighted injury rates by race code within product category, testing whether specific product harms fall unevenly.
harm_angle: If a product injures one group far more, that is a distribution and design failure, not bad luck.
caveat: Race coding changed over the survey's history and is often unknown; population denominators are not in this table.

title: Product harm early warning curves
idea: Small multiples of weighted injury counts by product over years, highlighting products whose curve bends sharply upward before any recall.
harm_angle: Catching a product's injury curve rising years before a recall is the difference between warning people and counting them.
caveat: Sampling noise at low volumes; a rising curve can reflect product popularity rather than risk without a sales denominator.

title: Severity mix by disposition
idea: Share of cases admitted or transferred versus treated and released, by product, separating the products that maim from those that scrape.
harm_angle: Admission rate is the honest measure of how badly a product hurts people.
caveat: Disposition codes need the lookup table; small-cell instability at product level.

title: Fire alcohol and drug involvement
idea: Timeline of cases flagged with fire, alcohol or drug involvement by product family, showing the contexts in which products turn dangerous.
harm_angle: Context flags separate a product defect from a use hazard nobody was warned about.
caveat: Involvement flags are often simply unrecorded rather than negative.

title: Revenue per employee across the top 100
idea: Plot each company as a dot with revenue on one axis and headcount on the other; distance from the diagonal shows how much revenue each worker generates. Outliers are the leanest-staffed giants.
harm_angle: Workers at the extreme revenue-per-head firms carry output that used to take many more people.
caveat: Snapshot only (100 rows, no year column) so no trend is possible; employees may be text.

title: Where the biggest employers actually sit
idea: Map each company to its headquarters city, sized by headcount and colored by industry. Shows how concentrated corporate command is in a handful of metros.
harm_angle: Regions with no headquarters have no local lever over the firms that employ them.
caveat: Headquarters is free text and needs geocoding; no lat/lon column exists.

title: Growth winners and shrinkers by industry
idea: Ranked bars of revenue growth grouped by industry, so whole sectors that are contracting stand apart from sectors that are booming.
harm_angle: Sector-wide contraction is the leading edge of mass layoffs.
caveat: Revenue growth is likely a percent string needing parsing.

title: The concentration curve of the top 100
idea: A cumulative curve showing what share of total top-100 revenue the first 5, 10 and 25 firms hold. Makes the steepness of corporate concentration visible in one line.
harm_angle: Concentrated revenue means concentrated pricing power over ordinary buyers.
caveat: Only covers the top 100 so it understates the true national tail.

title: Filings By Industry And Form
idea: Heatmap grid of SIC industry against form type, showing which sectors file what and how often.
harm_angle: Filing patterns show which industries face real disclosure and which slip through.
caveat: Only 200 rows landed -- a sample, not the corpus.

title: Incorporation Versus Operations
idea: Map of state of incorporation against entity location, showing the Delaware concentration.
harm_angle: Incorporating in one state to escape another state investor and worker protections.
caveat: 200-row sample and the business-location field is not in this select list.

title: Reporting Lag After Period End
idea: Distribution of days between report date and filing date, by form type.
harm_angle: Late filers keep investors and employees in the dark past the legal window.
caveat: Tiny sample and date types unverified.

title: Companies With Many Tickers
idea: Ranked bars of CIKs carrying multiple ticker symbols -- the multi-share-class structures.
harm_angle: Dual-class structures let founders keep control while outside shareholders carry the risk.
caveat: 10,414 rows; multi-class detection assumes one row per ticker.

title: Ticker Bridge Coverage Check
idea: Distribution of how many CIKs in the map carry a usable ticker, as a join-quality floor chart.
harm_angle: Weak on its own; it proves whether the CIK-to-ticker bridge is populated enough to trust joins on.
caveat: Descriptive only; value is as a data-quality check rather than a finding.

title: IPO And Prospectus Waves
idea: Timeline of registration and prospectus filings by month, showing the boom-bust rhythm of new offerings.
harm_angle: Offering waves mark when retail investors were pulled into the riskiest new issues.
caveat: 48,984 rows may be a partial crawl rather than full EDGAR.

title: Annual Report Gaps By Company
idea: Cohort grid of CIK by year showing which registrants skipped an annual report.
harm_angle: A registrant that stops filing annual reports leaves shareholders with no financial picture.
caveat: Partial crawl means missing rows may be collection gaps, not filing gaps.

title: Industry Filing Concentration
idea: Ranked bars of SIC codes by filing volume, shaded by state of incorporation.
harm_angle: Where filings concentrate is where regulatory attention already is, and where it is not.
caveat: sic_code fill rate unverified.

title: ISIN And EIN Coverage Audit
idea: Grid of filings by whether ISIN, EIN and ticker are populated, by year -- a bridge-quality map.
harm_angle: Broken identifiers are why corporate harm cannot be traced across datasets.
caveat: This is exactly the masked-id trap: columns may look full but hold blanks.

title: Lapsed Global Company IDs
idea: Ranked bars by country of the share of LEIs whose registration status is lapsed rather than issued.
harm_angle: Lapsed identifiers break the audit trail regulators rely on to follow money.
caveat: 3.4M rows and the status vocabulary is unverified.

title: Legal Address Versus Headquarters
idea: Flow diagram from legal-address country to headquarters country, exposing the letterbox-jurisdiction gap.
harm_angle: Companies legally domiciled where they have no operations are avoiding somebody tax or regulator.
caveat: Both country fields must be well populated and fill rate is unverified at this scale.

title: Entity Death And Succession
idea: Timeline of entity expiration dates by reason, with successor LEIs traced forward.
harm_angle: Following the successor chain is how liabilities get shed while the business continues.
caveat: Successor fields are sparse by design; only some dissolutions record them.

title: Who Validates The World Companies
idea: Ranked bars of managing local operating units by number of LEIs, showing concentration in the identity infrastructure.
harm_angle: A handful of private registrars gatekeep the global corporate identity record.
caveat: LOU identifiers are opaque codes needing a lookup.

title: Havens Punching Above Weight
idea: Map of LEI counts per country normalized by population, exposing micro-jurisdictions hosting outsized company counts.
harm_angle: Tiny jurisdictions hosting millions of companies is the visible signature of the offshore system.
caveat: Population is an external dataset that must be sourced elsewhere.

title: Addresses Shared by Many Entities
idea: Ranked bars of address nodes by how many offshore entities and officers cluster at them, naming the buildings that host thousands of vehicles.
harm_angle: One building holding five thousand companies is the physical address of hidden money.
caveat: This table is address nodes only; counting linked entities requires the relationship edges, which may not be in this slice.

title: Offshore Address Geography by Leak
idea: Map of address countries shaded by count, small-multipled by source leak, showing how the geography of secrecy shifted between the successive leaks.
harm_angle: Each leak captured a different era's preferred hiding place, and the shift shows where enforcement pushed the money next.
caveat: Leaks have different collection scopes, so differences may reflect what leaked rather than what exists.

title: Address Records That Expired
idea: Timeline of the validity cutoff per leak, showing when the snapshot of each address stopped being current.
harm_angle: Knowing the data's expiry date is how you avoid accusing someone based on a decade-old record.
caveat: valid_until is a provenance note string, likely not a clean date, and may be unparseable.

title: The Jurisdiction League Table
idea: Ranked bars of jurisdictions by count of offshore entities split by leak, naming the handful of places that host most of the world's shell companies.
harm_angle: A few tiny jurisdictions host the structures that let wealth escape the tax that funds schools and hospitals everywhere else.
caveat: Counts reflect what leaked from specific providers, not the true global population of offshore entities — that caveat must be on the chart.

title: Incorporation Waves Over a Century
idea: Timeline of incorporation dates by jurisdiction, showing the boom years for each secrecy haven and how they trade places over decades.
harm_angle: Each boom follows a law change somewhere else — the timeline maps how money outruns regulation.
caveat: Incorporation dates may be text in mixed formats; coverage is skewed by which providers happened to leak.

title: Service Providers Behind the Structures
idea: Ranked bars of service providers by entity count and jurisdiction spread, naming the firms that manufacture offshore vehicles at industrial scale.
harm_angle: A handful of firms built most of these structures, which makes them the accountable actors, not the anonymous owners.
caveat: Limited to the providers that were leaked; absence from this list is not innocence.

title: Struck Off Right After the Leak
idea: Distribution of struck-off and inactivation dates relative to each leak's publication, testing whether entities were dissolved en masse once exposed.
harm_angle: A dissolution spike right after exposure is evidence the structures were doing something their owners did not want seen.
caveat: Publication dates are not a column here and must be supplied by hand; struck-off dates may postdate the snapshot and be missing entirely.

title: Entities That Changed Their Name
idea: Ranked bars of entities whose original or former name differs from the current one, by jurisdiction, showing where renaming is routine practice.
harm_angle: Renaming an offshore vehicle breaks the paper trail linking it to whatever it did before.
caveat: former_name and original_name fill rates are unverified and may be near-empty.

title: Companies at the Same Address
idea: Ranked bars of registered addresses by number of companies registered there, surfacing the mailbox addresses hosting thousands of shells.
harm_angle: Mass-registration addresses are the plumbing of the fraud that empties real people's bank accounts.
caveat: Address strings need normalizing; the top of the list will include legitimate company-formation agents that must be labeled as such.

title: Serial Renaming Companies
idea: Ranked bars of companies by how many previous names they carry, plotted against incorporation date. Ten name changes is a pattern, not housekeeping.
harm_angle: Renaming is how a company sheds a bad reputation and keeps trading with the same victims.
caveat: Ten fixed name slots cap the count at ten, so a company with thirty renames looks identical to one with ten.

title: Overdue Accounts by Sector
idea: Heatmap grid of industry sector against how overdue the next accounts filing is, showing which industries systematically ignore filing deadlines.
harm_angle: Companies that never file accounts are invisible to anyone they owe money to.
caveat: SIC text is a combined code and description string; date fields may be text needing a parse.

title: Company Lifespan Distribution
idea: Distribution of days from incorporation to dissolution by company category, showing the sectors where companies are born and killed within a year.
harm_angle: Very short-lived companies in certain sectors are the signature of phoenix trading, where debts die and the same business restarts.
caveat: Dissolution date is null for live companies; survivorship must be handled explicitly or the distribution lies.

title: Mortgage Charges Never Satisfied
idea: Scatter of outstanding versus satisfied mortgage charges per company, with the far corner — many outstanding, none satisfied — as the flagged zone.
harm_angle: Unsatisfied charges pile up where creditors, often small suppliers, never got paid.
caveat: Charge counts are a snapshot of the register, not a payment history.

title: Spanish Corporate Acts By Type
idea: Ranked bars of act types (incorporation, dissolution, capital change, appointments) by province.
harm_angle: Corporate churn by region shows where Spanish businesses and their workers are collapsing.
caveat: Only 28 rows landed -- effectively a probe, not a dataset.

title: Gazette Coverage Check
idea: Timeline of issue dates present, purely to show how thin the current landing is.
harm_angle: Nothing yet; the value is knowing the source is unusable until re-landed.
caveat: 28 rows: this is a coverage audit, not a finding.

title: Irish Company Formation Waves
idea: Timeline of incorporations by year, with the Celtic Tiger and post-2008 collapse visible.
harm_angle: Formation and dissolution waves mark when Irish workers employers appeared and vanished.
caveat: 818,930 rows and status vocabulary is unverified.

title: Companies That Never Aged
idea: Distribution of company age at dissolution by company type, showing the short-lived shell population.
harm_angle: Companies dissolved within a year or two are often vehicles, not businesses.
caveat: Age is computed to the current date and dissolved companies may lack a dissolution date here.

title: Dublin Address Concentration
idea: Dot plot of registered addresses hosting hundreds of companies -- the Irish corporate service industry.
harm_angle: One Dublin address hosting thousands of companies is the visible face of profit shifting.
caveat: Address is a single free-text field needing normalization.

title: Status Mix By Company Type
idea: Heatmap grid of company type against status, showing which legal forms end in strike-off most often.
harm_angle: Legal forms with high strike-off rates are the ones creditors and workers should fear.
caveat: Status categories may include historical codes with unclear meaning.

title: UK Company Formation And Death
idea: Timeline of incorporations and dissolutions by month, showing net company creation across cycles.
harm_angle: Mass dissolutions mark where jobs and unpaid creditors were left behind.
caveat: 5.7M rows and the catalog shows no ingestion timestamp, so freshness is unknown.

title: Postcodes Hosting Thousands Of Firms
idea: Map of post codes by count of registered companies, exposing mail-forwarding addresses used at industrial scale.
harm_angle: Thousands of companies at one postbox is the standard setup for fraud and phoenix trading.
caveat: Address lines are unnormalized and a single address may split across variants.

title: Charges Against Small Companies
idea: Scatter of outstanding mortgage charges against company age, by category, showing who is loaded with secured debt.
harm_angle: Secured lenders get paid first when these firms fail; employees and suppliers do not.
caveat: Charge counts may be historical totals rather than current positions.

title: Dormant Accounts Share
idea: Ranked bars by company category of the share filing dormant or micro-entity accounts.
harm_angle: Dormant filings are how active trading is hidden from the public accounts.
caveat: account_category vocabulary unverified.

title: Foreign-Origin Companies Mapped
idea: Map of country of origin for UK-registered companies, showing which jurisdictions route through Britain.
harm_angle: Britain as a routing layer for foreign capital is how ownership gets one more step from scrutiny.
caveat: country_of_origin fill rate unverified and may be near-empty for domestic firms.

title: Who really controls UK companies
idea: Ranked bars of natures of control across all PSC records, showing how control is most commonly declared and how often it is the vaguest available category.
harm_angle: The stated nature of control is the only public answer to who can make a company act; vagueness there is by design.
caveat: SAMPLE ONLY: ~7.0M of ~10M records from a truncated load, so all totals are undercounts and the truncation is not random.

title: Controllers who live abroad
idea: Map of PSC country of residence, showing how much of UK corporate control is exercised from outside the UK.
harm_angle: Overseas controllers are the hardest for UK regulators and UK claimants to reach when a company causes harm.
caveat: Truncated 7M sample; country text is free-form with heavy variant spelling.

title: One person hundreds of companies
idea: Ranked bars of individuals matched on name plus birth month and year, by how many companies they control, surfacing the mass directors.
harm_angle: A single person nominally controlling hundreds of companies is the classic shell-factory signature behind fraud and wage theft.
caveat: Name plus partial DOB is the only available person key and will both merge and split real people; truncated sample undercounts.

title: Addresses hosting many controllers
idea: Map at postcode grain of addresses appearing as the registered address for large numbers of PSCs, isolating the formation-agent hubs.
harm_angle: A single office declared as home by thousands of company controllers is a shell address, and it is where enforcement letters go to die.
caveat: Truncated sample; address text needs normalisation before counting shared addresses.

title: Control declared then ceased
idea: Timeline of notified-on against ceased-on dates, showing how quickly control is transferred and which companies churn controllers fastest.
harm_angle: Rapid controller churn immediately before a company fails is how liability gets handed to someone with nothing to seize.
caveat: Dates parsed permissively from text; ceased_on is null for live entries by design; truncated sample.

title: Corporate Ownership Trees
idea: Network graph of parent-child ownership relationships, letting a viewer expand any company into its full tree and see how many layers sit between a brand and its ultimate owner.
harm_angle: Deep ownership layers are how a company puts distance between the harm it causes and the people who profit from it.
caveat: Column names are flattened JSON path strings; whether both node ids are actually populated identifiers is unverified.

title: Ownership Percentage Where Disclosed
idea: Distribution of ownership quantifier amounts by measurement method, showing how often a stake size is actually disclosed versus left as a bare relationship.
harm_angle: Undisclosed stake sizes mean nobody outside can tell who really controls a firm.
caveat: Five numbered quantifier slots suggest most are empty; slot 1 fill rate unverified.

title: Relationships That Lapsed
idea: Timeline of relationship period start and end dates, highlighting relationships whose registration went stale or whose renewal date has passed.
harm_angle: A lapsed ownership record is an ownership chain that quietly disappears from the public register.
caveat: Five period slots with different period_type meanings; picking slot 1 may be the wrong period.

title: Who Validates the Ownership Claims
idea: Ranked bars of the managing registrars by number of relationships and by validation evidence type, exposing which registrars accept the weakest documentation.
harm_angle: If a registrar rubber-stamps ownership claims, every downstream investigation inherits the lie.
caveat: Validation source vocabulary is a code list not shown in the model.

title: Who reports and who does not
idea: Heatmap grid of victim race and household income against whether the crime was reported to police. Shows which victims quietly absorb crime rather than calling.
harm_angle: Victims who never report get no investigation, no services, and no place in official crime counts.
caveat: Only 1,000 rows in the mart so cells will be thin; survey weights must be applied.

title: Injury without treatment
idea: Ranked bars of the share of injured victims who received no medical treatment, broken out by income band and age group.
harm_angle: Poor victims are hurt and then go untreated, compounding the harm.
caveat: Small sample; treatment coding may collapse several categories.

title: Weapon type and the victim it finds
idea: Dot plot of weapon category against victim demographics, sized by seriousness of the resulting injury.
harm_angle: Shows which people are on the receiving end of armed violence.
caveat: 1000-row extract may not be nationally representative without weights.

title: Victim services reached almost nobody
idea: Distribution of victim-service receipt across offense types and locality, exposing how rarely support services actually touch victims.
harm_angle: A victim-services system that reaches a tiny fraction of victims is a promise on paper only.
caveat: Extract size; unclear whether the field distinguishes offered from received.

source_names: FBI Crime Data Explorer State Crime Estimates
title: Clearance rate gap by offense and state
idea: Heatmap grid of state against offense with color as clearance rate. Dark rows are offenses that essentially never get solved anywhere.
harm_angle: Victims of never-cleared offenses get no resolution at all.
caveat: Monthly clearance divided by monthly offenses is approximate; clearances can belong to prior-month offenses.

source_names: FBI Crime Data Explorer State Crime Estimates
title: Forty years of offense rates by state
idea: Small multiples, one panel per state, of the offense rate per 100k over the full monthly series back to 1985. Divergent state trajectories jump out from the national story.
harm_angle: State-level divergence shows where policy choices actually changed who gets victimized.
caveat: Reporting-agency participation changed a lot over four decades; breaks may be artefacts.

source_names: FBI Crime Data Explorer State Crime Estimates
title: Seasonality of violence
idea: Cohort grid of month-of-year against year with color as offense rate, revealing the summer peak and whether it is intensifying.
harm_angle: Predictable seasonal peaks are a staffing and prevention question nobody funds for.
caveat: Mixing offense categories will wash out the pattern unless faceted.

source_names: FBI Crime Data Explorer State Crime Estimates
title: Where clearance collapsed fastest
idea: Slope chart of clearance rate at an early period versus the most recent period, one line per state, ordered by decline.
harm_angle: States where clearance collapsed have left a growing pool of victims with no case outcome.
caveat: Endpoint choice drives the story; reporting coverage differences distort the comparison.

title: Check volume by state and month
idea: Heatmap grid of state rows against monthly columns since 1998, color as total checks. Panic spikes after national events show up as vertical stripes.
harm_angle: Surge months are when guns enter homes fastest, ahead of any policy response.
caveat: Checks are not sales; no population column in this table for a true per-capita rate.

title: Permit rechecks are eating the totals
idea: Stacked timeline of check-type composition, showing how much of the headline total is permit and permit-recheck rather than an actual transfer.
harm_angle: Miscounting rechecks as sales distorts every public argument about gun availability.
caveat: Some states report permits in bulk which creates artificial cliffs.

title: Pawn redemptions as an economic stress signal
idea: Timeline of prepawn versus redemption checks, which track people pawning and reclaiming guns. Rising prepawn relative to redemption is a household-distress indicator.
harm_angle: Pawning a firearm is a marker of acute household financial distress.
caveat: Only some states report pawn categories; many zeros are non-reporting not zero activity.

title: Handgun versus long-gun mix shifting
idea: Slope chart per state from the earliest years to the most recent showing the share of checks that are handgun. A near-universal shift toward handguns would be the story.
harm_angle: Handgun-dominant markets are associated with different injury patterns than long-gun ones.
caveat: Multiple-gun checks are a separate column and muddy the mix.

title: Private-sale checks: the voluntary minority
idea: Ranked bars by state of private-sale checks as a share of all checks, exposing how few states channel private transfers through the system at all.
harm_angle: Untracked private transfers are the gap through which prohibited buyers get armed.
caveat: Column populated only where state law requires it; zeros mean no law rather than no sales.

title: Registry Non-Compliance By County
idea: Map of Missouri counties shaded by the share of registrants flagged non-compliant.
harm_angle: Counties where the registry has stopped tracking people offer the public a false sense of safety.
caveat: Compliance flag derived from a Y string; blanks may be misread as non-compliant.

title: Tier Versus Compliance
idea: Heatmap grid of registry tier against compliance status, testing whether the highest tiers are the least tracked.
harm_angle: If the highest-risk tier is also the least tracked, the tier system is theater.
caveat: Tier vocabulary unverified and may be blank for older registrations.

title: Registry Aging Curve
idea: Distribution of registrant age derived from date of birth, showing how much of the registry is elderly and lifetime-listed.
harm_angle: Lifetime registration of people now in their eighties raises whether the list still protects anyone.
caveat: Date of birth is an ISO timestamp string; parse failures and placeholder dates are likely.

title: Address Clusters Of Registrants
idea: Dot plot of addresses hosting many registrants -- the boarding houses and encampments the system pushes people into.
harm_angle: Housing bans concentrate people into a few addresses, which harms both them and the neighborhood.
caveat: Addresses include homeless and institutional placeholders that must be handled or the chart is nonsense.

title: Backsliding leaderboard
idea: Slope chart of total freedom score from earliest to latest edition per country, ranked by decline, the backsliding list.
harm_angle: Populations in fast-declining countries are losing rights in real time.
caveat: country_territory is number-cast over a name field so it will null -- the c_t or region column must carry identity instead.

title: Which freedom breaks first
idea: Small multiples of the A-G sub-indicator scores over time for backsliding countries, showing whether elections, media or courts go first.
harm_angle: Knowing which pillar falls first tells activists where to defend before the collapse.
caveat: Sub-indicator columns are single letters A..G with A1..G4 detail; mapping them to meaning requires the codebook.

title: Political rights versus civil liberties drift
idea: Scatter of PR rating against CL rating by edition, animated, showing countries that keep elections while gutting liberties.
harm_angle: Countries holding elections while crushing speech are the hardest for outsiders to see.
caveat: Ratings are ordinal 1-7 scales; treating them as continuous is a simplification.

title: Regional status flip grid
idea: Heatmap grid of country by edition shaded by free, partly-free or not-free status, faceted by region.
harm_angle: Shows whether backsliding is contagious within a region.
caveat: Status is only fully comparable back to 2013 in this file; earlier years are a separate workbook.

title: What Italy measures about itself
idea: Ranked bars of observation counts per dataflow, showing which statistical domains Italy instruments heavily and which are thin.
harm_angle: Under-instrumented domains are where policy failures go unmeasured.
caveat: Row counts reflect what was pulled from the API rather than what is published.

title: Missing and non-normal observations
idea: Heatmap grid of dataflow against year with color as the share of observations flagged non-normal or missing, exposing where the official series has holes.
harm_angle: Gaps in official statistics are gaps in the evidence citizens can hold government to.
caveat: Status codes need the SDMX legend; a pulled subset may not represent the full dataflow.

title: One dataflow followed through time
idea: Small multiples of absolute observation values by series key over time for a chosen dataflow, showing regional or cohort divergence within Italy.
harm_angle: Regional divergence inside a country is where unequal treatment lives.
caveat: Series keys are compound SDMX codes needing a codelist to become readable labels.

title: Mixed frequencies in one table
idea: Distribution of observation frequency codes per dataflow, a data-quality view showing where monthly and annual series are stacked together.
harm_angle: Mixing frequencies silently is how analysts produce wrong national conclusions.
caveat: Diagnostic rather than journalistic; useful mainly as a trust check.

title: Fertility collapse timelines
idea: Small multiples of fertility rate by country over the full record, ordered by speed of decline.
harm_angle: Rapid fertility collapse reshapes who will pay for the care of an aging population.
caveat: Entity mixes countries and aggregates; must filter on valid ISO code.

title: Below-replacement crossing map
idea: Ranked dot plot of the year each country first crossed below replacement fertility.
harm_angle: Countries crossing earliest face care-worker shortages first, and the shortfall lands on unpaid family carers.
caveat: Requires a fixed replacement threshold assumption; noisy series can cross and re-cross.

title: Convergence or divergence
idea: Distribution of country fertility rates by decade, showing whether the world's fertility spread is narrowing.
harm_angle: Narrowing spread means the demographic future is globally shared rather than regionally split.
caveat: Aggregate rows will distort the distribution if not filtered.

title: Induced Quakes Where None Belonged
idea: Map M2.5+ events by decade over regions with no historic seismicity - Oklahoma, west Texas, Ohio. Viewer watches a quiet map light up starting in the 2010s.
harm_angle: People in newly seismic regions live in houses never engineered for shaking and carry no earthquake insurance.
caveat: time is kept as a quoted raw column and may be text; needs parsing before any time slicing works.

title: Shallow and Small Still Hurts
idea: Scatter depth against magnitude, colored by region, to separate deep tectonic events from shallow ones that do damage at low magnitude.
harm_angle: Shallow low-magnitude quakes crack foundations in communities that get no hazard warning at all.
caveat: depth and mag are passed through untyped and may be strings requiring casts.

title: Detection Network Blind Spots
idea: Map the nst station count and gap azimuthal coverage per event. Viewer sees geographic regions where the monitoring network is thin and small events are likely missed entirely.
harm_angle: Under-monitored regions get undercounted hazard, which becomes under-regulated building and drilling.
caveat: nst and gap may be blank on older records; interpreting network quality needs domain care.

title: Quake Count Per Year Baseline
idea: Simple timeline of event counts by magnitude band per year across the full catalog.
harm_angle: Baseline for every induced-seismicity claim that follows.
caveat: Rising counts partly reflect better detection over time - not a pure hazard signal.

title: The Yield Curve Inverting
idea: Timeline of the spread between the ten-year and three-month constant maturity yields with inversions shaded.
harm_angle: Inversions precede recessions and recessions are where job and home loss show up.
caveat: No obvious date column in the model; the date appears to sit inside the series description field, unverified.

title: Full Yield Curve Over Time
idea: Small multiples or ridgeline of all maturities from one month to thirty years across the record showing the curve's shape shifting.
harm_angle: Context layer: the rate environment behind every mortgage, credit card and municipal budget on the platform.
caveat: Values are stored as text with placeholder codes in the raw format so casting may fail.

title: Rate Shock Backdrop Layer
idea: A thin reference strip designed to sit under other charts showing the short rate over time so any spending or lending series can be read against it.
harm_angle: Rate spikes are the mechanism that turns affordable debt into foreclosure and bankruptcy.
caveat: Utility depends entirely on the date column being recoverable.

title: Household Versus Corporate Net Worth
idea: Timeline of selected flow-of-funds series comparing the household sector against the nonfinancial corporate sector across quarters.
harm_angle: The widening gap between household and corporate balance sheets is the macro backdrop for every harm on this platform.
caveat: Columns are raw Fed series codes with no human labels; a series dictionary is required before any of this is readable.

title: Sector Flow Of Funds Grid
idea: Small multiples of the sector aggregate series by quarter with one panel per sector using a series-code dictionary to label them.
harm_angle: Shows which sector is absorbing debt and which is shedding it over each cycle.
caveat: Only 304 rows (quarters) but hundreds of unlabeled columns; unusable without a code dictionary.

title: Nonprofits Stripped Of Status
idea: Timeline of automatic revocations by revocation date split by exemption type showing waves of enforcement.
harm_angle: A revoked nonprofit that keeps soliciting is taking donations that are no longer deductible.
caveat: Table sits at exactly 500,000 rows suggesting a load cap; revocation dates may be text.

title: Revoked And Never Reinstated
idea: Distribution of time from revocation to reinstatement with the never-reinstated group shown as an open-ended bar.
harm_angle: Organizations that never come back were often the small community groups that could not afford the paperwork.
caveat: Reinstatement date is likely null for most rows; probable 500k row cap.

title: Revocations By State And ZIP
idea: Choropleth of revocations per capita by state drilling to zip-level clusters.
harm_angle: Clusters of revocations mark neighborhoods where the civic infrastructure quietly collapsed.
caveat: Requires external population data; probable row cap may bias geography.

title: Same Address Many Revocations
idea: Ranked bars of addresses with the highest count of distinct revoked organizations exposing shell-nonprofit clusters.
harm_angle: A single mailbox hosting dozens of revoked charities is a fundraising operation, not a charity.
caveat: Address is free text needing normalization; registered-agent offices will produce false positives.

title: Deductibility Status Breakdown
idea: Ranked bars of eligible donees by deductibility status code and state.
harm_angle: Donors relying on a status code they do not understand may lose the deduction they were promised.
caveat: Table sits at exactly 500,000 rows and is likely truncated well below the real universe.

title: Charity Density By State
idea: Choropleth of eligible donees per capita by state showing where the charitable sector is thick and where it is absent.
harm_angle: Charity deserts mean no local organization stands between a family and a crisis.
caveat: Probable 500k row cap; needs external population data.

title: Foreign Registered Eligible Donees
idea: Ranked bars of eligible donees registered outside the United States by country.
harm_angle: Deductible giving flowing to foreign entities deserves the same scrutiny as domestic charity.
caveat: Country field may be blank for the overwhelming majority of rows.

title: Charity Assets Against Revenue
idea: Scatter of asset amount against revenue amount by mission category showing endowment-heavy organizations that spend little.
harm_angle: Foundations sitting on assets while spending little are hoarding money meant to reach people in need.
caveat: Only 2,450 rows, so this is a sample-of-interest file, not the full charity universe.

title: Charity Types By Mission Category
idea: Ranked bars of organizations and total assets by mission code group showing which causes hold the money.
harm_angle: Where charitable dollars pool tells you which harms get addressed and which are ignored.
caveat: 2,450 rows; mission codes need grouping into readable families.

title: Filing Requirement Versus Size
idea: Heatmap grid of filing requirement code against asset and income code bands showing large organizations with light filing obligations.
harm_angle: Large organizations with minimal filing duties are the ones the public can least audit.
caveat: Small table; code meanings need the IRS business master file codebook.

title: Charity Geography And Wealth
idea: Choropleth of total charity assets by state and zip showing where nonprofit wealth is physically headquartered.
harm_angle: Nonprofit wealth headquartered far from the communities it claims to serve is a distribution question.
caveat: 2,450 rows will make most states thin.

title: National debt the long line
idea: Timeline of total debt outstanding across the full record. The plain floor chart everything else gets compared against.
harm_angle: Reference baseline; the denominator behind every fiscal argument aimed at cutting programmes people depend on.
caveat: Only 237 rows so likely annual or quarterly grain; coverage window unstated in metadata.

title: Debt growth rate by fiscal year
idea: Bars of year-over-year change in debt outstanding by fiscal year, so acceleration and pauses read directly rather than as slope on a curve.
harm_angle: Shows which years actually moved the number, against the political story told about them.
caveat: Fiscal year fields are untyped; mixing fiscal and calendar framing would break the chart.

title: Quarterly debt seasonality
idea: Small multiples of debt level by fiscal quarter across years, testing whether the debt climbs on a predictable within-year rhythm.
harm_angle: Predictable seasonal borrowing is the backdrop to every debt-ceiling standoff that puts benefit payments at risk.
caveat: With 237 rows the per-quarter cells may be very thin or the grain may be annual only.

title: Daily money into the Treasury
idea: Timeline of daily deposit amounts by transaction category, showing the real-time pulse of federal cash coming in.
harm_angle: The daily cash position is what determines whether benefit payments go out on time in a shutdown.
caveat: Row count is exactly 10,000, the signature of a loader page cap; the series may be truncated rather than complete.

title: Which categories dominate the till
idea: Ranked bars of fiscal-year-to-date deposit totals by transaction category, showing the handful of streams that carry federal cash flow.
harm_angle: Reveals how much of federal revenue rests on a few sources that a single policy change could move.
caveat: FYTD amounts are cumulative; naive summing across rows will double count badly.

title: Deposit spikes against the calendar
idea: Heatmap grid of day-of-month by month, shaded by deposit volume, to expose the tax-deadline spikes and the quiet stretches between.
harm_angle: Cash-flow troughs are exactly when the government stalls payments to the people least able to wait.
caveat: Truncated 10,000-row window may not cover full months evenly.

title: Categories that appear and vanish
idea: Cohort grid of transaction categories by the months they appear in, so discontinued and newly created accounting lines stand out as gaps.
harm_angle: Accounting lines that quietly disappear are how spending changes escape the public summary.
caveat: Category renames will look like disappearances; the 10,000-row cap will manufacture false gaps at the edges.

title: Where federal revenue comes from
idea: Ranked bars of net monthly receipts by classification, showing how heavily the government leans on individual income and payroll taxes versus corporate.
harm_angle: The split between what workers pay and what corporations pay is the clearest picture of who funds the state.
caveat: Rows include parent and child classification levels; summing without respecting sequence_level_nbr will double count.

title: Refunds against gross receipts
idea: Timeline of gross receipts and refunds side by side by classification, so the categories where large refunds claw back most of the gross become visible.
harm_angle: Large refund flows in one category next to none in another shows who the tax code hands money back to.
caveat: Refund amounts may be sign-flipped or zero-filled for most classifications.

title: This year against last year
idea: Slope chart of fiscal-year-to-date net receipts by classification, current year versus prior year, so shifts in the revenue mix read in one glance.
harm_angle: A quiet shift of the tax burden between categories moves real money out of specific households' pockets.
caveat: FYTD comparisons are only valid at matched month positions; needs record_date filtering.

title: The receipts hierarchy tree
idea: Network built from parent_id to classification_id, exposing how the published revenue categories roll up and where detail stops.
harm_angle: Where the official hierarchy stops splitting is where the public loses the ability to ask who paid.
caveat: PARENT_ID population and self-consistency unverified from metadata.

title: Corporate ownership web
idea: Network of parent-to-subsidiary links across the global LEI system, drawn as a graph so the sprawling multinational structures become visible as shapes.
harm_angle: Ownership chains are how a company that harms people in one country keeps its assets somewhere the victims cannot reach.
caveat: Node ids are typed by nodeidtype and may not all be LEIs; 481k edges need heavy filtering to be drawable.

title: How deep does ownership go
idea: Distribution of chain depth from ultimate parent down to the leaf entity, showing how many layers sit between a household name and its operating subsidiaries.
harm_angle: Every extra layer is another step a regulator or a claimant has to climb before reaching whoever actually decides.
caveat: Requires recursive traversal; cycles and incomplete chains in the LEI data are common and would distort depth.

title: Lapsed ownership declarations
idea: Ranked bars of relationships by status, isolating lapsed and inactive declarations that were never updated, grouped by managing registrar.
harm_angle: Stale ownership records mean the official answer to who owns this company is simply wrong.
caveat: Several registration fields were cast with try_to_double which suggests they are codes or dates that will not parse as intended.

title: Ownership percentage cliffs
idea: Distribution of declared ownership percentages, looking for pile-ups just under disclosure thresholds like the 25 and 50 percent lines.
harm_angle: Stakes engineered to sit just below a reporting threshold are control without the accountability that control is supposed to carry.
caveat: Quantifier amount population is unknown and units may mix percentages with absolute values.

title: Excuses for not naming a parent
idea: Ranked bars of the reasons entities give for reporting no parent, across 6.3M exception records. The most common excuse is the most common way ownership stays hidden.
harm_angle: Every accepted exception is a company that legally does not have to say who owns it.
caveat: Reason fields are enumerated codes whose plain meanings are not in the model; needs a code lookup.

title: Direct versus ultimate parent gaps
idea: Heatmap grid of exception category against reason, separating entities hiding their immediate owner from those hiding the top of the chain.
harm_angle: Hiding the ultimate parent is the move that puts the real decision-maker beyond reach.
caveat: Multi-reason rows mean a single LEI may appear several times; counting rows as entities would overstate.

title: Entities with stacked exceptions
idea: Ranked bars of LEIs claiming multiple exception reasons at once, the entities working hardest to avoid declaring an owner.
harm_angle: An entity with five stacked excuses for not naming its owner is a deliberate opacity structure, not an accident.
caveat: Trailing reason columns may be almost entirely null, leaving too few multi-reason cases to rank.

title: Exception references as breadcrumbs
idea: Exploratory view of what the exception reference fields actually contain, since a reference to a legal provision or another entity is a lead in itself.
harm_angle: The provision a company cites to stay anonymous names the loophole that needs closing.
caveat: Reference fields may be null or contain uninterpretable registry codes; contents unverified.

title: Inequality trajectories by country
idea: Small multiples of the Gini coefficient over time, one panel per world region with country lines, so regional inequality stories separate from the global average.
harm_angle: Rising inequality shows up as worse health and shorter lives at the bottom.
caveat: Gini is not numeric-cast in the model so it may be text; survey methods differ across countries and years.

title: Countries that got measurably more unequal
idea: Slope chart from earliest to latest available Gini per country, sorted by increase, with the biggest risers named.
harm_angle: Sharp Gini increases mark populations whose share of national income was taken away.
caveat: Uneven start and end years per country make slopes non-comparable without care.

title: Inequality coverage blind spots
idea: Heatmap grid of country against year showing where an inequality measure exists at all. The blank regions are countries that do not measure their own inequality.
harm_angle: Unmeasured inequality cannot be argued about, let alone fixed.
caveat: Blank cells may be extract gaps rather than genuine non-measurement.

title: Debt without earnings scatter
idea: Scatter of median student debt against median earnings ten years out colored by control type, with the high-debt low-pay quadrant flagged.
harm_angle: Students in that quadrant are paying for a credential that never pays them back.
caveat: Earnings and debt fields cover federally aided students only; suppression at small schools.

title: Default concentration by sector
idea: Distribution of two- and three-year default rates by control type and Pell share, showing where borrowers default most.
harm_angle: Default follows a borrower for life through wage garnishment and credit destruction.
caveat: Default rate definitions changed over time and the file's vintage is unverified.

title: Money in versus money to teaching
idea: Scatter of instructional spend per student against tuition revenue per student, showing schools that collect far more than they spend on teaching.
harm_angle: When tuition dollars do not reach the classroom, students borrowed for overhead.
caveat: Per-student accounting varies by sector; both fields cast unverified.

title: Minority-serving institution funding gap
idea: Dot plot comparing instructional spend, completion and earnings at historically Black, tribal and Hispanic-serving institutions against peer schools of similar size.
harm_angle: Underfunded minority-serving schools produce worse outcomes for students the country underinvested in twice.
caveat: Peer matching needs care; small-institution suppression removes many tribal colleges.

title: Closed campuses map
idea: Map of institutions no longer operating, plotted by coordinates and colored by control type, showing the geography of college closures.
harm_angle: A closure strands enrolled students with debt and credits nobody will accept.
caveat: currently_operating is a snapshot flag with no closure date; coordinate population unverified.

title: Net price versus Pell share
idea: Scatter of net price against the share of students on Pell grants by locale, showing schools charging the poorest students the most.
harm_angle: A high net price on a Pell-heavy campus is a bill the students cannot actually carry.
caveat: Two separate net-price columns must be combined correctly by control type.

title: Chronic absence against graduation rate
idea: Scatter of chronic absenteeism rate against graduation rate, one dot per reporting unit, colored by subgroup. The lower-right cluster is where kids stop showing up and stop graduating.
harm_angle: Chronically absent students are the ones the system is losing.
caveat: Only 33 rows landed, so this is a shape test not an analysis; grain unclear (state, district or school).

title: Subgroup gaps in proficiency
idea: Dot plot per subgroup of proficiency level for a given subject, showing how far apart student groups sit within the same system.
harm_angle: Persistent subgroup gaps are children being educated to different standards in the same building.
caveat: 33 rows is far too thin to be representative; this source needs a re-ingest before use. Two ideas is the honest ceiling.

title: Program taxonomy growth
idea: Count of program codes by family and by action taken in the 2020 revision, showing which fields of study the taxonomy expanded or deleted.
harm_angle: Deleted program codes make whole fields of study statistically invisible in later data.
caveat: Pure reference table of 2318 rows with no real time axis; only two ideas because it is genuinely thin.

title: Fields that vanished from the list
idea: The specific program codes marked deleted or moved, listed with their old titles, showing exactly what got reclassified.
harm_angle: Reclassification breaks the time series any student-outcome study depends on.
caveat: action coding unverified; single-revision snapshot.

title: Provisional ballot rejection by jurisdiction
idea: County-level map of provisional ballots cast versus rejected, so the jurisdictions that throw out the most provisional votes stand out.
harm_angle: A rejected provisional ballot is a citizen who showed up and was not counted.
caveat: Survey columns are opaque question codes needing the codebook to map to meaning; many jurisdictions leave items blank.

title: Voters per polling place
idea: Ranked bars of registered voters per polling place by jurisdiction, showing where people wait longest to vote.
harm_angle: Fewer polling places per voter means hours-long lines that push working people out of voting.
caveat: Requires the codebook to confirm which coded columns hold registration and polling-place counts.

title: Mail ballots sent versus returned versus counted
idea: Flow diagram from mail ballots transmitted to returned to counted to rejected, per state, making the attrition at each stage visible.
harm_angle: Every step of the funnel is a place a mail voter's ballot silently dies.
caveat: Column-to-question mapping must come from the codebook; states define stages differently.

title: Jurisdictions that answer nothing
idea: Heatmap grid of jurisdiction against survey section with color as the share of items left blank, exposing which election offices simply do not report.
harm_angle: An election office that reports nothing cannot be audited by the public it serves.
caveat: Blank versus not-applicable is not distinguished without the codebook.

title: Poll worker recruitment difficulty
idea: State map colored by reported difficulty recruiting poll workers, paired with jurisdiction size, showing where election administration is thinnest.
harm_angle: Understaffed polling places mean longer lines and more errors for the voters served.
caveat: The difficulty items are categorical survey responses needing codebook decoding.

title: Uncontested House seats over time
idea: Timeline of the number of districts with only one major-party candidate, showing how many Americans have no real choice on the ballot.
harm_angle: Voters in uncontested districts have their representative chosen for them.
caveat: Definition of uncontested depends on how minor parties and write-ins are treated.

title: Vote share versus turnout by district
idea: Scatter of winning vote share against total votes cast per district-year, where safe seats cluster with low turnout - the disengagement spiral.
harm_angle: Safe seats depress turnout, which further insulates the incumbent from the people.
caveat: Total votes is not a turnout rate without a registered-voter denominator this table lacks.

title: Write-in and minor-party pressure
idea: Small multiples by state of the combined minor-party and write-in vote share over time, showing where third-party pressure is real.
harm_angle: Sustained third-party share signals voters who feel unrepresented by both majors.
caveat: Party labels vary by state and year and need normalising.

title: Vote mode shift by state
idea: Stacked timeline of vote share by mode (in person, mail, early) per state, showing which states moved their electorate to mail and when.
harm_angle: How a state lets people vote determines who can actually vote.
caveat: Mode is only reported by some states and years; blanks are unreported not zero.

title: Fifty years of state margins
idea: Heatmap grid of state rows against election years with color as the two-party margin, so realignments read as color sweeping across the grid.
harm_angle: Realignment determines whose policy priorities get served for a generation.
caveat: Two-party margin must be computed from candidate rows; strong third-party years complicate it.

title: Third-party spoilers by state
idea: Dot plot per state-year of third-party vote share against the winning margin, isolating races where the third party exceeded the margin.
harm_angle: Races decided by less than the third-party vote are where the electoral system misrepresented voter intent.
caveat: Party classification into major and minor needs a hand-built list.

title: Turnout growth versus flat participation
idea: Timeline of total votes cast per state across elections, indexed to a baseline year, showing which states expanded participation and which flatlined.
harm_angle: Flat participation over decades of population growth means fewer people getting a say.
caveat: No population denominator in this table so indexed growth confounds population with turnout.

title: Special elections and their turnout penalty
idea: Dot plot of total votes in special versus regular Senate elections in the same state, showing how much participation collapses in specials.
harm_angle: Specials decide six-year terms with a fraction of the electorate present.
caveat: Special elections are rare so per-state comparisons will be thin.

title: Senate margin compression by state
idea: Small multiples per state of winning vote share across five decades, showing states that went from competitive to locked.
harm_angle: Locked states mean two senators chosen without a real contest.
caveat: Staggered six-year classes make each state's series irregular.

title: Party label drift
idea: Flow diagram of detailed party labels collapsing into simplified categories over time, exposing how much party naming has churned in state records.
harm_angle: Inconsistent party labelling is how election analysis quietly goes wrong.
caveat: Diagnostic rather than a public story; depends on the publisher's own simplification choices.

title: Utility roles by entity type
idea: Heatmap of entity type against the owner, operator and asset-manager role flags, showing who actually controls generation versus who just owns it.
harm_angle: When the operator and the owner are different companies, ratepayers cannot tell who to hold responsible for an outage or a leak.
caveat: Single 2024 snapshot of 6643 rows; role flag coding unverified.

title: Utility headquarters concentration
idea: Map of utility headquarters by state sized by count, showing states hosting many out-of-state owners.
harm_angle: Distant owners make the decisions about local rates and local pollution.
caveat: Headquarters address is not where the plants are; that needs the plant table.

title: Municipal versus investor-owned mix
idea: Distribution of utilities by entity type per state, showing where public power survives and where investors run everything.
harm_angle: Investor-owned utilities answer to shareholders on rate decisions that hit household bills.
caveat: Entity type categories unverified; single-year snapshot.

title: Coal ash ponds mapped
idea: Map of plants with ash impoundments colored by whether the impoundment is lined and by status, showing unlined coal ash sitting next to communities.
harm_angle: Unlined coal ash ponds leach arsenic and heavy metals into the groundwater of nearby, usually poor, communities.
caveat: Impoundment fields may be sparse or oddly coded; single 2024 snapshot.

title: Water source stress map
idea: Plants mapped by their named water source, showing how many plants draw from the same stressed river.
harm_angle: Multiple plants drawing and heating one river hits the fisheries and drinking water of everyone downstream.
caveat: Water source is free text with heavy variation; no withdrawal volume in this table.

title: Regulatory status by sector
idea: Cross-tab of regulatory status against sector, showing how much generation sits outside traditional rate regulation.
harm_angle: Unregulated generation means no rate case where a household can contest what it is charged.
caveat: Status coding unverified; capacity lives in the generator table, not here.

title: Gas pipeline dependency network
idea: Network of plants to their named natural gas pipelines, showing pipelines that single-handedly supply many plants.
harm_angle: One pipeline failure freezing a whole state's generation is exactly how people die in a cold snap.
caveat: Pipeline names are free text; only three slots per plant, truncating multi-pipeline plants.

title: Balancing authority footprint map
idea: Plants mapped and colored by balancing authority, showing the grid islands and who controls each.
harm_angle: Grid islands with no interconnection are why one region's failure cannot be rescued by its neighbors.
caveat: Snapshot only; interconnection capacity is not in this table.

title: Retirement cliff by fuel
idea: Timeline of nameplate capacity by planned retirement year and energy source, showing how much capacity is scheduled to disappear and when.
harm_angle: Retirement without replacement is the setup for the blackouts that kill people in heat waves.
caveat: Planned dates are utility intentions, not commitments; 2024 snapshot only.

title: Aging fleet by state
idea: Distribution of generator operating year weighted by capacity, by state, showing states running on machines built in the 1960s.
harm_angle: Old, brittle generation fails first in extreme weather, and the people who lose power are the ones who cannot leave.
caveat: Repowered units may still carry their original operating year.

title: Winter versus summer capacity gap
idea: Scatter of summer against winter capacity per generator colored by technology, exposing units that lose most of their output in the season they are needed.
harm_angle: Capacity that vanishes in a cold snap is how a grid promises power it cannot deliver when people freeze.
caveat: Derates are reported, not measured, and some technologies legitimately differ by season.

title: Carbon capture claims versus reality
idea: Count and capacity of generators reporting carbon capture technology by state and fuel, showing how vanishingly small the deployed fleet actually is.
harm_angle: Carbon capture is used to justify keeping a plant open next to a neighborhood, so its near-absence is a broken promise to the people breathing the exhaust.
caveat: Flag semantics unverified and may include planned rather than operating capture.

title: Fuel switching optionality
idea: Share of capacity able to switch between oil and gas or cofire fuels by state, showing where the grid has a fallback and where it does not.
harm_angle: No fuel flexibility means a supply disruption becomes an outage in someone's home.
caveat: Flags unverified; balancing region would require joining the plant table.

title: Turbine vendor market share
idea: Ranked bars of predominant turbine manufacturers by installed capacity and generator count, showing the handful of vendors behind the fleet.
harm_angle: Vendor concentration means one manufacturer's defect grounds a large share of the country's clean capacity.
caveat: Manufacturer names are free text; 1563 rows and a 2024 snapshot.

title: Wind buildout by county
idea: Map of wind generators by county sized by capacity and colored by operating year, showing where the buildout landed.
harm_angle: Host counties absorb the noise and land use while the power and profit leave.
caveat: No coordinates in this table so county mapping only; single-year snapshot.

title: Turbine height and wind quality
idea: Scatter of hub height against design wind speed and capacity colored by wind quality class, showing how the machines got taller as the good sites ran out.
harm_angle: Taller turbines in marginal wind areas mean more visual and noise burden per unit of power for host communities.
caveat: Height and speed fields cast unverified; wind class coding unverified.

title: Aging wind fleet end of life
idea: Distribution of wind capacity by operating year and status, showing the first generation of turbines reaching end of life.
harm_angle: Decommissioning costs land on host landowners when the developer is long gone.
caveat: Status coding unverified; no retirement fields in this schedule.

title: Where Solar Actually Got Built
idea: Map every solar generator as a point sized by nameplate capacity and colored by sector, so the viewer sees which states and counties got utility-scale build-out and which got nothing.
harm_angle: Counties with no build-out get none of the local tax base or cheap generation while still hosting the older dirty plants.
caveat: No lat/lon in this schedule -- geography is state/county text only, so mapping needs a county crosswalk.

title: Net Metering Is Not For You
idea: Ranked bars by state of the share of solar capacity that carries a net-metering or virtual-net-metering agreement, splitting utility-scale from small distributed sectors.
harm_angle: Households in states where net metering is rare pay full retail and get nothing back for the power they push to the grid.
caveat: Net-metering flags may be Y/N text with blanks; unknown how many rows are populated.

title: Cheap Fixed Tilt vs Tracking
idea: Small multiples by state showing the mix of fixed-tilt, single-axis and dual-axis tracking solar, revealing which regions get the cheaper lower-yield hardware.
harm_angle: Cheaper fixed hardware means less generation per acre of land taken from a community.
caveat: Tracking columns are likely mutually exclusive flags; overlap unverified.

title: DC Overbuild Ratio By Owner
idea: Scatter of DC net capacity against AC nameplate capacity per generator, colored by utility, exposing which operators systematically overbuild panels relative to what they can deliver.
harm_angle: Overbuilt DC that gets clipped is land and money burned that ratepayers ultimately fund.
caveat: DC capacity column may be sparsely reported.

title: The Solar Build Wave
idea: Timeline of solar capacity brought online by operating year and month, split by sector, showing the shape of the boom and any policy-driven cliffs.
time_axis: yes (operating year back-history in a 2024 snapshot)
harm_angle: Cliffs in the build curve mark moments a policy change stalled cheap power for whole regions.
caveat: Snapshot only contains generators still listed in 2024 -- retired projects are invisible, so early years undercount.

title: Who Gets Battery Backup
idea: Map of battery storage points sized by nameplate energy capacity in MWh and colored by whether the backup-power use case is flagged, showing which regions have grid resilience and which do not.
harm_angle: Regions without storage take the blackouts when the grid is stressed.
caveat: Use-case flags may be multi-select Y/N with heavy blanks; no lat/lon in this schedule.

title: Batteries For Trading Not Reliability
idea: Ranked bars of storage capacity by declared use case -- arbitrage and frequency regulation versus backup power and peak shaving -- split by sector, revealing whether storage serves markets or people.
harm_angle: If storage is built to trade rather than to keep lights on, ratepayers fund an asset that never protects them.
caveat: A single unit can flag many use cases, so shares will overlap and must be read as non-exclusive.

title: Storage Duration Distribution
idea: Distribution of hours of storage (energy capacity divided by max discharge rate) across all units, split by storage technology, showing how much is truly multi-hour versus minutes of grid smoothing.
harm_angle: Short-duration batteries sold to the public as blackout insurance cannot actually carry a household through an outage.
caveat: Discharge rate may be null on older units, which would drop them silently from the distribution.

title: Storage Tethered To Fossil Units
idea: Network graph linking storage units to the generators they directly support, colored by the supported unit type, revealing where batteries prop up existing fossil plants rather than renewables.
harm_angle: Storage marketed as a clean-energy asset may be extending the life of the plant polluting the neighborhood.
caveat: Direct-support id columns are likely sparsely populated; only three support slots exist.

title: Plants That Can Switch To Oil
idea: Map of multi-fuel generators able to switch between gas and oil, sized by capacity and colored by how fast they can switch, showing which communities can be dosed with oil burning on short notice.
harm_angle: Neighbors of a switchable plant breathe oil-burn emissions during gas price spikes with no notice or say.
caveat: Switch-time fields may be free text categories rather than numbers.

title: Air Permits As The Only Brake
idea: Ranked bars by state counting generators whose fuel switching is limited by air permit limits versus storage limits versus nothing at all, showing where regulation is the only thing stopping a dirtier burn.
harm_angle: Where no permit limit is recorded, nothing legally stops an operator from burning the dirtier fuel next to a community.
caveat: Limit fields are likely Y/N flags; a blank may mean 'not reported' rather than 'no limit', which would invert the read.

title: Capacity Lost On The Backup Fuel
idea: Slope chart per generator from net summer capacity on gas to net summer capacity on oil, showing how much firm capacity quietly evaporates when the switch happens.
harm_angle: Capacity counted as reliable in planning may not exist in the cold snap when the switch is thrown, and customers lose power.
caveat: Both capacity columns may be null for units that do not switch, leaving a small usable sample.

title: The Cofire Fuel Menu
idea: Heatmap grid of cofire energy sources against prime mover types, showing what unusual fuels get burned in what equipment across the fleet.
harm_angle: Waste-derived cofire fuels concentrate exotic emissions in whichever host community drew the plant.
caveat: Six cofire slots must be unpivoted; codes are unlabeled and need an EIA fuel-code lookup.

title: Who Really Owns The Grid
idea: Network graph of owners to jointly-owned generators weighted by percent owned, revealing the small set of firms that hold slices of a huge share of national generating capacity.
harm_angle: Concentrated hidden ownership means the same handful of firms set the terms in markets that look competitive.
caveat: Owner names are free text with no id, so the same firm will appear under many spellings unless normalized.

title: Out Of State Absentee Owners
idea: Map flow lines from owner state to plant state weighted by owned capacity share, showing where the profits from a local plant leave the state that breathes its emissions.
harm_angle: Communities host the pollution while the ownership income and tax base sit in another state.
caveat: Owner state is a mailing address, which can be a registered-agent state rather than the true home of the owner.

title: Ownership Fragmentation By Plant
idea: Distribution of how many distinct owners each jointly-owned generator has, with the most-split units called out, showing where accountability for a plant is diffused across many hands.
harm_angle: When a plant has a dozen part-owners, nobody is the responsible party a harmed neighbor can name.
caveat: Grain assumed one row per plant-generator-owner per the model docs; unverified whether ownership shares sum to 100.

title: Owners Hiding At One Address
idea: Ranked bars of owner mailing addresses that host many distinct owner names, exposing shell-style clustering behind generation assets.
harm_angle: Shell layers between the public and a plant owner make it impossible to hold anyone to account for local harm.
caveat: Address strings are unnormalized free text; law-firm and corporate-services addresses will produce benign false positives.

title: Boiler To Generator Web
idea: Network graph of boilers linked to the generators they serve within each plant, showing which units share a smokestack and therefore share a pollution footprint.
harm_angle: Shared boilers mean one control failure hits the emissions of several generators at once, all onto the same neighborhood.
caveat: This is a pure bridge table with no measures -- it needs the boiler and generator tables to say anything about harm.

title: Most Tangled Plants
idea: Ranked bars of plants by how many boiler-to-generator links they carry, surfacing the most complex sites where emissions attribution is hardest.
harm_angle: Complex plants are where regulators lose the thread on which unit caused which exceedance.
caveat: Complexity is a proxy, not a harm measure; thin table with only seven columns.

title: Steam Plant Type Mix
idea: Distribution of boiler-generator links by steam plant type across utilities, a plain descriptive read of what kind of thermal fleet each operator runs.
harm_angle: Fleet type sets who lives with continuous versus peaking emissions.
caveat: Genuinely thin source -- it is a bridge, so only a few honest single-source charts exist.

title: Boilers With No Mercury Control
idea: Map by state of boilers reporting no existing mercury control strategy, sized by count, showing where the toughest pollutant goes uncontrolled.
harm_angle: Mercury from uncontrolled boilers lands in local water and food and hits children hardest.
caveat: Blank control strategy may mean 'not applicable' rather than 'none installed'; needs the regulation flag to disambiguate.

title: Promised Controls That Never Came
idea: Dot plot per boiler comparing existing control strategies against proposed ones for sulfur and nitrogen, with the compliance year on the axis, showing controls perpetually promised for a future date.
harm_angle: Neighbors breathe the same air for another decade while a control that exists only on paper keeps sliding.
caveat: Single-year snapshot means we cannot see a proposal that was made and then dropped -- only what was still proposed in 2024.

title: Compliance Deadlines Stacked Ahead
idea: Timeline histogram of compliance years for sulfur, nitrogen, particulate and mercury, showing how far into the future the fleet has pushed its obligations.
harm_angle: Every year of deferred compliance is another year of measured pollution on a real population.
caveat: Compliance year columns may hold text or sentinel values like 9999; cast behavior unverified.

title: New Source Review Dodgers
idea: Ranked bars of utilities by share of boilers with no New Source Review permit recorded despite an active boiler status, flagging where the major permitting gate was never triggered.
harm_angle: NSR is the rule that forces modern controls when a plant is rebuilt -- skipping it locks a community into 1970s emissions.
caveat: Absence of an NSR record is not proof of avoidance; many boilers legitimately never triggered review.

title: Standard Strictness By Region
idea: Heatmap grid of states against pollutant, colored by median permitted emission rate standard, exposing where a plant is allowed to emit several times what the same plant type may emit elsewhere.
harm_angle: Two identical boilers, two different legal pollution ceilings -- one community is simply worth less.
caveat: Rates come with separate unit and averaging-period columns, so cross-state comparison is invalid unless units are normalized first.

title: Smart Meter Haves And Have Nots
