idea: Heatmap grid of statute code against compliance-monitoring agency type, showing which laws are federally enforced versus delegated.
harm_angle: Delegation patterns predict where a resident's complaint reaches nobody with power.
caveat: COMP_MONITOR_AGENCY_TYPES appears to be a packed multi-value field.

title: Facilities never inspected twice
idea: Ranked bars of facilities by years since their most recent inspection, worst first, the cold-case inspection list.
harm_angle: A plant last checked fifteen years ago is unmonitored in every practical sense.
caveat: Cannot distinguish a closed facility from a neglected one without a facility status source.

title: Inspection surge and collapse cycle
idea: Slope chart of inspections per region between two eras, showing which regions collapsed hardest.
harm_angle: Regions that fell off a cliff left specific communities unwatched.
caveat: Era boundaries are arbitrary and could be cherry-picked; needs date coverage confirmed first.

title: Water dischargers on impaired waters
idea: Point map of permitted discharge facilities colored by whether they sit on an impaired waterway, showing pollution stacked on already-sick rivers.
harm_angle: Communities drawing from an impaired river get more discharge, not less.
caveat: IMPAIRED_WATERS population and encoding unverified; lat/lon are try_to_double and may be widely null.

title: Discharge facility density by county
idea: Choropleth of permitted water-discharge facilities per county, revealing counties that host a disproportionate share.
harm_angle: A handful of counties absorb the nation's wastewater discharge burden.
caveat: COUNTY_CODE is a try_to_number and may not be a FIPS code joinable to county geometry.

title: Facility type mix by state
idea: Small multiples per state of the mix of facility type codes, showing where industrial versus municipal dischargers dominate.
harm_angle: Industrial-heavy states shift the pollution burden onto private actors with weaker public accountability.
caveat: Facility type codes are uncoded and need a lookup.

title: Geocode quality blind spots
idea: Map of the share of discharge facilities missing usable coordinates by state, showing where the public literally cannot find the polluter.
harm_angle: You cannot organize against a plant whose location the government never recorded.
caveat: Missing coordinates may reflect a data-vintage issue rather than a real records gap.

title: Missed compliance-schedule deadlines
idea: Distribution of days between the scheduled date and the actual date for compliance-schedule events, showing how far behind cleanups run.
harm_angle: Every month a cleanup slips is a month of continued discharge into someone's water.
caveat: Rows with a null actual date are the worst cases and would drop out of a simple difference.

title: Time from detection to resolution
idea: Distribution of days from noncompliance detection to resolution, split by resolution code, showing which exits are fast and which are real.
harm_angle: Fast resolutions may mean the violation was written off rather than fixed.
caveat: Resolution codes are uncoded; distinguishing fixed from forgiven needs a code lookup.

title: Most common schedule violations
idea: Ranked bars of violation descriptions among compliance-schedule violations, the plain list of what permittees fail at.
harm_angle: Names the specific promises polluters routinely break.

title: Federal versus state penalty split
idea: Timeline of total federal penalty dollars versus state and local penalty dollars per settlement year, showing who actually collects.
harm_angle: If penalties shrink while discharge continues, the cost of polluting falls on residents instead.
caveat: Penalty amounts are try_to_double over text and zeros may mean no-penalty or unrecorded.

title: Penalty size distribution
idea: Distribution of assessed federal penalty amounts on a log scale, showing the enormous mass of tiny fines and the rare big one.
harm_angle: A thousand-dollar fine for poisoning a river is cheaper than fixing the pipe.
caveat: Zero and null penalties must be handled explicitly or the shape lies.

title: Permittees with the biggest cumulative fines
idea: Ranked bars of NPDES permit ids by total penalty dollars across all settlements, the water-pollution hall of fame.
harm_angle: Puts a dollar figure on who has hurt watersheds most and still holds a permit.
caveat: NPDES_ID identifies a permit, not a company; one firm can hide behind many permits.

title: Zero-dollar formal actions
idea: Timeline of the share of formal enforcement actions carrying no penalty at all, by agency, showing enforcement theater.
harm_angle: A formal action with a zero fine looks tough in a press release and costs the polluter nothing.
caveat: Zero versus null penalty may be indistinguishable after the text-to-double cast.

title: Warning volume versus official flag
idea: Timeline of informal water enforcement actions split by the official flag, showing how much activity is unofficial nudging.
harm_angle: Unofficial nudges leave no legal record for a community to point to later.
caveat: OFFICIAL_FLG semantics unverified from metadata.

title: Warning-heavy permits
idea: Ranked bars of NPDES permits by lifetime count of informal actions, surfacing permits drowning in letters.
harm_angle: Permits with dozens of warnings and no penalty show a regulator that will not escalate.
caveat: About 827k rows; counts are dominated by permit age, so a rate would be fairer.

title: Agency behavior fingerprints
idea: Heatmap grid of agency against informal action type share, showing each regulator's signature enforcement style.
harm_angle: Some regulators literally never use their stronger tools, and their residents pay.
caveat: AGENCY values may be free text with variants.

title: Water inspections per year nationally
idea: Timeline of NPDES inspections per year split by state-versus-EPA flag, the baseline picture of who watches the water.
harm_angle: Falling inspections mean discharge violations go undiscovered.
caveat: 1.9M rows across an unknown date span; early years may be sparse.

title: Inspections that find nothing
idea: Timeline of the share of inspections with a benign activity outcome, by inspection type, showing whether checks are getting softer.
harm_angle: Inspections that never find anything are ritual, not protection.
caveat: Outcome codes are uncoded; benign versus adverse needs a lookup that may not exist.

title: Inspection type mix drift
idea: Small multiples over time of the inspection type mix, showing a shift from on-site visits to desk reviews.
harm_angle: Swapping site visits for paperwork review is a quiet deregulation nobody voted on.
caveat: Type descriptions may have been recoded mid-history, faking a trend.

title: Permits with zero recent inspections
idea: Dot plot of permits by years since last inspection, the long-neglected water permit list.
harm_angle: Unwatched permits discharge into rivers that people fish and drink from.
caveat: Inactive permits will dominate the tail unless permit status is available.

title: Industry profile of water permits
idea: Ranked bars of NAICS descriptions among water-discharge permits, showing which industries hold the most discharge rights.
harm_angle: Shows which sectors are legally allowed to put things in the water.
caveat: A lookup-style table with no dates; thin on its own and mostly useful as a joiner.

title: Permits with many industry codes
idea: Distribution of how many NAICS codes each permit carries, flagging sprawling multi-activity sites.
harm_angle: Complex multi-activity sites are the hardest for a regulator or a neighbor to understand.
caveat: This is a thin crosswalk table with only four columns; interpretation is limited without joining the permit tables.

title: Permit-schedule slippage over time
idea: Timeline of permit-schedule violations per year by violation type, showing whether permittees are missing more deadlines.
harm_angle: Missed permit milestones mean promised pollution controls never got built.
caveat: Date parsing risk and unknown coverage window.

title: Detection-to-resolution lag by type
idea: Distribution of days from noncompliance detection to resolution split by violation description, showing which failures linger.
harm_angle: Long-lingering violations mean months of untreated discharge.
caveat: Unresolved cases drop out; the visible distribution is the optimistic half.

title: Late reporting as a warning sign
idea: Scatter of report-received date against schedule date per permit, where points far off the diagonal are chronic late reporters.
harm_angle: Chronically late reporters are the permits regulators lose track of first.
caveat: Both dates are text-cast; a systematic format problem would fake the pattern.

title: Quarterly noncompliance rate nationally
idea: Timeline by year-quarter of the share of reporting permits in significant noncompliance, the single best pulse of water compliance.
harm_angle: A rising share means more communities getting illegal discharge quarter after quarter.
caveat: YEARQTR is kept as text; ordering requires parsing and the 7.9M-row grain is assumed permit-quarter.

title: Permits permanently in noncompliance
idea: Cohort grid of permits by first noncompliant quarter, tracking how many are still noncompliant every quarter after.
harm_angle: Permits that never leave noncompliance are ongoing, tolerated harm.
caveat: HLRNC code values are uncoded; which values mean significant noncompliance must be confirmed.

title: Effluent exceedance counts over time
idea: Timeline of total effluent exceedance counts summed across permits per quarter, the raw volume of limits broken.
harm_angle: Each exceedance is a measured amount of pollutant above the legal limit entering water.
caveat: Count columns are kept as-is and may be text; their exact definitions are guessed from the column names.

title: Noncompliance seasonality heatmap
idea: Heatmap grid of quarter against year for the noncompliance rate, testing whether violations cluster in particular seasons.
harm_angle: Seasonal spikes point to plants that dump when they think nobody is measuring.
caveat: Seasonality could be a reporting artifact rather than real discharge behavior.

title: Single-event spills over time
idea: Timeline of single-event water violations per year by violation description, capturing discrete spills and upsets.
harm_angle: Each single event is a discrete moment a waterway got hit.
caveat: Coverage window unknown; date is a text cast.

title: How long a spill lasts
idea: Distribution of days from single-event start to end date, showing which kinds of events run for weeks.
harm_angle: A spill that runs for a month is a month of exposure for anyone downstream.
caveat: End date may be null for ongoing or poorly recorded events.

title: State versus federal spill detection
idea: Ranked bars of single-event agency type share, showing who actually catches spills.
harm_angle: If only the polluter self-reports spills, unreported spills are invisible by design.
caveat: Agency type codes uncoded; self-report versus agency-found may not be distinguishable.

title: Comment-text spill taxonomy
idea: Ranked bars of recurring phrases in the free-text spill comments, letting the operators' own words classify the failures.
harm_angle: The raw language of spill reports often admits causes the codes hide.
caveat: Free-text field may be mostly empty or boilerplate.

title: Legacy industry codes on water permits
idea: Ranked bars of SIC descriptions attached to water permits, showing the old-economy industries still holding discharge rights.
harm_angle: Old industrial classifications often flag aging plants with aging pollution controls.
caveat: Thin four-column crosswalk with no dates or geography; limited standalone value.

title: SIC versus NAICS coverage gap
idea: Ranked bars of permits carrying only an old SIC code and no modern NAICS code, showing records frozen in the last century.
harm_angle: Permits never re-coded are permits never re-examined.
caveat: Requires the NAICS crosswalk table to complete; alone it only shows one side.

title: Hazardous-waste penalties over time
idea: Timeline of total proposed, final, and supplemental penalty dollars per year, showing whether hazardous-waste fines are shrinking.
harm_angle: Falling fines mean cheaper illegal dumping near the people who live beside it.
caveat: Amounts are try_to_number over text; blanks versus zeros are indistinguishable.

title: Proposed versus final penalty haircut
idea: Scatter of proposed penalty against final penalty per action, where points far below the diagonal are the discounts.
harm_angle: The gap between the announced fine and the collected fine is the discount polluters actually get.
caveat: Some actions legitimately settle low; without case context the discount can be misread.

title: Which agency discounts hardest
idea: Ranked bars of median final-to-proposed penalty ratio by enforcement agency, naming the softest touch.
harm_angle: Residents in soft-touch states get less protection for the same violation.
caveat: Agency values may mix state and federal labels inconsistently.

title: Repeat hazardous-waste defendants
idea: Dot plot of handler ids by count of enforcement actions and cumulative penalty, isolating the frequent-flyer dumpers.
harm_angle: Names the companies that keep getting caught and keep operating.
caveat: ID_NUMBER is the RCRA handler id and may be reused across sites; state suffix handling matters.

title: Supplemental projects instead of fines
idea: Timeline of the share of actions where a supplemental environmental project amount replaces a cash penalty.
harm_angle: Swapping fines for voluntary projects can leave the harmed community with neither money nor cleanup.
caveat: Column meanings of the four amount fields are inferred from abbreviations and could be wrong.

title: Evaluations that find violations
idea: Timeline of the share of RCRA evaluations flagged as finding a violation, by evaluating agency.
harm_angle: A regulator whose inspections never find anything is not looking.
caveat: FOUND_VIOLATION is trimmed text; the yes/no encoding is unverified.

title: Hit rate by evaluation type
idea: Ranked bars of violation-finding rate per evaluation type, showing which inspection methods actually catch things.
harm_angle: If cheap desk reviews replace real inspections, violations stop being found.
caveat: Type mix may have shifted over time, confounding the rate comparison.

title: State inspection intensity map
idea: Map of evaluations per year per state derived from the activity-location code, showing enforcement deserts.
harm_angle: States that barely inspect leave hazardous waste unchecked next to homes.
caveat: ACTIVITY_LOCATION is assumed to be a state code; that assumption is unverified.

title: Evaluation cadence collapse
idea: Small multiples per state of evaluations per year, showing which states quietly stopped inspecting.
harm_angle: A state that stops inspecting has effectively repealed the law for its residents.
caveat: Date parsing risk on a text field; a bad cast would fake a collapse.

title: Hazardous-waste handler map
idea: Point map of RCRA handlers colored by federal waste generator category, showing where the biggest generators cluster.
harm_angle: Large-quantity generators concentrated in one area concentrate risk on those residents.
caveat: Coordinates are try_to_number over text and may be widely null or zero-filled.

title: Generator size mix by state
idea: Small multiples per state of the federal waste generator category mix, showing states that host the heavy end.
harm_angle: States loaded with large generators carry more exposure risk per resident.
caveat: Generator category codes are uncoded and need a lookup.

title: Full-enforcement universe coverage
idea: Ranked bars by state of the share of handlers in the full enforcement universe, showing where the strict rules apply.
harm_angle: Facilities outside the enforcement universe face almost no scrutiny.
caveat: Flag semantics inferred from column names only.

title: Handler clusters by zip
idea: Heatmap grid of zip codes by handler count, isolating the postcodes carrying dozens of hazardous-waste sites.
harm_angle: A zip with thirty handlers is a neighborhood absorbing a whole industry's waste.
caveat: Zip formats may be five or nine digit and need normalization; 1.6M rows include many inactive handlers.

title: Industries generating hazardous waste
idea: Ranked bars of NAICS codes among RCRA handlers, showing which sectors dominate the hazardous-waste universe.
harm_angle: Names the industries whose ordinary operations produce the waste communities live beside.
caveat: NAICS code is raw text with no description column, so the chart needs an external code label.

title: State industrial waste fingerprints
idea: Heatmap grid of state against NAICS-sector share of handlers, giving each state a hazardous-waste industry signature.
harm_angle: Shows which residents live in a chemicals state versus a metals state.
caveat: Only two substantive columns; this is a thin crosswalk table and most value comes from joining it.

title: Time to return to compliance
idea: Distribution of days from violation determination to actual return-to-compliance date, by violation type.
harm_angle: Long return-to-compliance times mean hazardous waste mishandled for months.
caveat: Never-resolved violations have a null return date and would vanish from the distribution.

title: Violations that never returned to compliance
idea: Timeline of the count of determined violations still lacking a return-to-compliance date, by year determined.
harm_angle: These are open, admitted hazardous-waste violations nobody closed out.
caveat: A null return date may mean unreported rather than open; needs a data-quality read first.

title: Missed compliance deadlines
idea: Scatter of scheduled compliance date against actual return-to-compliance date, where the spread above the diagonal is lateness.
harm_angle: Deadlines that slip by years show a schedule nobody enforces.
caveat: Both dates are text casts; a formatting problem would scatter points meaninglessly.

title: Which agency determines violations
idea: Ranked bars of violations by determining agency and violation type, showing state versus federal detection patterns.
harm_angle: Violation types only ever found by federal inspectors go unfound wherever the feds are absent.
caveat: Agency labels may be inconsistent free text.

title: Monthly significant noncompliance trend
idea: Timeline by month of the count of handlers flagged as significant noncompliers, the hazardous-waste compliance pulse.
harm_angle: Rising significant noncompliance means more sites mishandling hazardous waste right now.
caveat: YRMONTH is trimmed text and must be parsed; flag encoding is unverified.

title: Handlers stuck in noncompliance for years
idea: Cohort grid of handlers by their first significant-noncompliance month, tracking how long they stay flagged.
harm_angle: Sites flagged for years running are tolerated, ongoing hazards.
caveat: Requires a continuous monthly panel; gaps in reporting would break the streak logic.

title: State noncompliance heat over time
idea: Heatmap grid of state against month shaded by the share of handlers in violation, making state-level collapses visible.
harm_angle: A state whose row goes hot and stays hot is failing its residents systematically.
caveat: ACTIVITY_LOCATION assumed to be a state code; 2.7M rows means the panel is long but coverage per state is unknown.

title: Violation flag versus escalation rate
idea: Slope chart of the share of violating handlers escalated to significant noncompliance, comparing early and late eras.
harm_angle: If escalation rates fall while violations hold steady, the regulator is downgrading, not improving.
caveat: Era boundaries arbitrary; the significant-noncompliance criteria may have changed definition mid-history.

title: Water system milestones missed
idea: Distribution of days between the scheduled event end date and the actual event date, showing how far behind water-system fixes run.
harm_angle: Every slipped milestone is more months of the same drinking water.
caveat: Milestone codes are uncoded; null actual dates mean never done and would drop out.

title: Milestone type mix over time
idea: Timeline of milestone events by milestone code per quarter, showing which corrective steps are common and which vanished.
harm_angle: Corrective steps that stopped being used are protections quietly retired.
caveat: SUBMISSIONYEARQUARTER is text and needs parsing to order correctly.

title: Systems with the most overdue milestones
idea: Ranked bars of water system ids by count of milestones past their end date with no actual date recorded.
harm_angle: Names the water systems whose promised fixes never happened.
caveat: A missing actual date might be a reporting lag rather than a real failure.

title: Water source type mix nationally
idea: Ranked bars of water source and facility type codes across drinking-water facilities, the basic map of where tap water comes from.
harm_angle: Source type drives which contaminants a community is exposed to.
caveat: Codes are uncoded and need a lookup; 1.5M rows are quarterly snapshots, so deduplication is required.

title: Unfiltered surface water systems
idea: Ranked bars of systems whose facilities show surface water with no treatment indicator, the highest-risk configurations.
harm_angle: Untreated surface water is the classic setup for an outbreak.
caveat: FILTRATION_STATUS_CODE is cast to a double, which suggests the codes may be being mangled.

title: Water resale chains
idea: Network of systems linked by seller relationships, showing chains where one wholesaler's water reaches many small systems.
harm_angle: One contaminated wholesaler can poison dozens of downstream communities at once.
caveat: SELLER_PWSID population is unverified and may be blank on most rows.

title: Deactivated facilities over time
idea: Timeline of facility deactivation dates, showing waves of drinking-water infrastructure going offline.
harm_angle: Systems losing facilities may be losing redundancy that keeps water safe.
caveat: Deactivation date is a text cast and may be sparsely populated.

title: Tribal water system coverage
idea: Map of water systems serving tribal areas by state, showing where tribal drinking water is administered.
harm_angle: Tribal water systems are historically the most underfunded and least inspected.
caveat: TRIBAL_CODE population is unverified; it may be blank on the overwhelming majority of rows.

title: Systems serving many zip codes
idea: Distribution of the number of zip codes served per water system, showing the sprawling systems and the tiny ones.
harm_angle: Very small systems serving a few zips are the ones with no engineer and no budget.
caveat: Quarterly snapshot rows will duplicate zip pairs unless deduplicated.

title: Zip codes served by multiple systems
idea: Heatmap grid of zips by count of distinct serving systems, exposing fragmented patchwork water service.
harm_angle: Fragmented service means residents on one street can be on wildly different water quality.
caveat: Zip-to-system overlap may be an artifact of imprecise geographic coding.

title: Lead sample results distribution
idea: Distribution of lead and copper rule sample measures by contaminant, with the action level marked, showing the tail above the line.
harm_angle: Every sample above the action level is a household drinking leaded water.
caveat: SAMPLE_MEASURE is left uncast in the model and may be text; units vary by row and must be normalized.

title: Systems with the worst lead samples
idea: Ranked bars of water systems by their highest recorded lead sample, the worst-tap list.
harm_angle: Names the specific systems where somebody's tap tested worst.
caveat: Unit normalization is essential or the ranking is nonsense; result sign codes mark non-detects.

title: Lead sampling frequency gaps
idea: Dot plot of systems by years since their most recent lead sample, showing where nobody has tested in a long time.
harm_angle: A system untested for years has no idea whether its pipes are leaching lead.
caveat: Sampling requirements vary by system size, so a long gap can be legal rather than negligent.

title: Lead levels trend over decades
idea: Timeline of the ninetieth-percentile lead result per year across all systems, showing whether tap water is actually getting cleaner.
harm_angle: A flat line despite decades of rules means the fix never reached households.
caveat: Sampling protocols changed over the record; a trend may reflect method change, not exposure change.

title: Non-detect reporting suspicion
idea: Timeline of the share of samples flagged with a less-than result sign, testing whether systems report suspiciously many non-detects.
harm_angle: Gaming sample selection to produce non-detects hides real lead exposure from residents.
caveat: Result sign code encoding is unverified and non-detects can be entirely legitimate.

title: Public notification failures over time
idea: Timeline of public-notification violations per year, showing how often systems failed to tell residents their water was unsafe.
harm_angle: A failure to notify means people kept drinking water they would have avoided.
caveat: Date parsing risk; the linkage semantics between notification violation and related violation are inferred.

title: Silence duration after a violation
idea: Distribution of days in the non-compliance period for notification violations, showing how long communities were kept in the dark.
harm_angle: The length of the silence is the length of the unwitting exposure.
caveat: Open periods with null end dates would drop out.

title: Contaminants people were not told about
idea: Ranked bars of contaminant codes attached to notification failures, showing which hazards go unannounced most often.
harm_angle: Systems staying quiet about the scariest contaminants is the worst version of this failure.
caveat: Contaminant codes need a lookup table to be readable.

title: Population served by system size
idea: Distribution of population served across water systems, showing the enormous tail of tiny systems serving a few hundred people.
harm_angle: Tiny systems have no budget, no staff, and the worst compliance records.
caveat: POPULATION_SERVED_COUNT is a try_to_number and may be stale or zero on inactive systems.

title: Schools and daycares on their own water
idea: Map of systems flagged as serving a school or daycare, by state, showing where children drink from the smallest systems.
harm_angle: Children are the most vulnerable to lead and pathogens and often drink from the smallest systems.
caveat: The school/daycare flag population is unverified and may be sparsely used.

title: Who owns the water
idea: Ranked bars of owner type by total population served, showing how many Americans drink from privately owned systems.
harm_angle: Private ownership changes who answers when the water goes bad.
caveat: Owner type codes are uncoded; quarterly snapshots must be deduplicated to one row per system.

title: Reduced monitoring privileges map
idea: Map of the share of systems granted reduced monitoring or outstanding-performer status by state, showing where testing was relaxed.
harm_angle: Relaxed monitoring means fewer chances to catch contamination before people drink it.
caveat: Flag encodings unverified; reduced monitoring is a legitimate reward and needs careful framing.

title: Deactivated systems and who they served
idea: Timeline of system deactivations weighted by population previously served, showing communities that lost their water utility.
harm_angle: When a small system dies, its residents may end up on untested private wells.
caveat: Deactivation may mean a merger rather than a loss of service.

title: What kind of places get served
idea: Ranked bars of service area type codes, showing whether systems serve residential, institutional, or transient populations.
harm_angle: Transient-population systems serve people who never learn the water was bad.
caveat: Only six columns and no geography; this table is thin on its own and mostly a joiner.

title: Service area reporting drift
idea: Timeline by submission quarter of the count of systems reporting each service area type, exposing reporting gaps.
harm_angle: Systems that stop reporting their service area become invisible to oversight.
caveat: Thin table with only two substantive dimensions; a quarter-over-quarter change may be pure reporting noise.

title: Water sanitary survey cadence
idea: Timeline of drinking-water site visits per year by agency type, showing whether required sanitary surveys are happening.
harm_angle: Skipped sanitary surveys mean structural problems in the water plant go unseen.
caveat: Visit date is a text cast; 2.5M rows are quarterly snapshots that may repeat visits.

title: What inspectors actually check
idea: Heatmap grid of the dozen evaluation area codes by their finding distribution, showing which parts of a plant fail most.
harm_angle: The failing area codes point at the exact mechanism by which bad water reaches taps.
caveat: Each evaluation code has its own uncoded value set; a shared lookup may not exist.

title: Financially failing water systems
idea: Ranked bars of systems whose financial evaluation code shows deficiency across repeated visits, the about-to-fail utility list.
harm_angle: A broke utility cannot fix its pipes, and its customers drink the consequence.
caveat: Financial evaluation code meaning is inferred from the column name.

title: Systems never visited
idea: Dot plot of water systems by years since their last recorded site visit, ranked worst first.
harm_angle: A plant nobody has walked through in a decade is a blind spot serving real households.
caveat: Absence of a visit record is not proof no visit happened; state reporting varies.

title: Health-based drinking water violations
idea: Timeline of health-based drinking water violations per year, split by rule family, the core safe-water accountability chart.
harm_angle: Health-based violations mean measurable contaminants above the legal limit in people's taps.
caveat: 15.4M rows are quarterly snapshots; deduplication by violation id is essential or counts inflate wildly.

title: Violations that never get enforced
idea: Ranked bars by state of the share of health-based violations with no enforcement record attached.
harm_angle: Unenforced health violations are the government watching contamination and doing nothing.
caveat: A null enforcement id may reflect a joining artifact of the flattened violation-enforcement grain.

title: Days from violation to enforcement
idea: Distribution of days between the non-compliance start and the enforcement date, by enforcement category, showing the lag.
harm_angle: A two-year lag is two years of drinking the contaminated water.
caveat: Both dates are text casts; enforcement rows may be many-to-one against violations.

title: Repeat offender water systems
idea: Cohort grid of water systems by first health-based violation year, tracking how many violate again every subsequent year.
harm_angle: Systems that violate every single year for a decade are chronic, tolerated harm.
caveat: Requires clean deduplication of the quarterly snapshot grain first.

title: Exceedance size versus the legal limit
idea: Scatter of the measured violation value against the federal maximum contaminant level, showing how far over the line systems run.
harm_angle: Being ten times over the limit is a different harm from being barely over, and the data can say which.
caveat: VIOL_MEASURE, FEDERAL_MCL and STATE_MCL are all left uncast and may be text with mixed units.

title: State limits weaker than federal
idea: Dot plot comparing state maximum contaminant levels against the federal limit per contaminant, flagging states that set looser rules.
harm_angle: A weaker state limit legalizes exposure that would be a violation one state over.
caveat: The state limit field may be blank on most rows or simply mirror the federal value; units may differ.

title: Superfund Sites and Their Acreage
idea: Map of Superfund sites by city and state, sized by area, showing the physical footprint of contamination across the country.
harm_angle: People live, go to school, and drink water next to these footprints.
caveat: Polygon geometry was not landed — attributes only — so this is a centroid map, not a true boundary map. gis_area_units may vary by row.

title: NPL Status by Region
idea: Heatmap grid of EPA region against national priorities list status, showing where sites sit proposed, listed, deleted, or in limbo.
harm_angle: A site stuck in proposed status for decades is a community waiting on a cleanup that never starts.
caveat: Status codes need a lookup not present in the model; 2114 features across 1908 sites means dedupe on epa_id first.

title: How Long Since Anyone Touched the Record
idea: Distribution of time between the record's original creation and its last change per site, showing sites whose records have gone untouched for many years.
harm_angle: A record nobody updates is often a cleanup nobody is working on.
caveat: Update dates reflect GIS data maintenance, not cleanup progress — a real risk of over-reading.

title: Federal Facility Superfund Sites
idea: Ranked bars of states by count of Superfund sites carrying the federal-facility flag, separating government-caused contamination from private.
harm_angle: When the polluter is the government, the community's route to redress is much narrower.
caveat: federal_facility_code fill rate and code meanings are unverified.

title: Toxic releases mapped nationally
idea: Point map of 2023 reporting facilities sized by total releases and colored by whether the chemical is a carcinogen.
harm_angle: Every dot is a place where a known carcinogen was legally released into a neighborhood.
caveat: Release-quantity columns are left uncast in the model and may be text; single-year 2023 snapshot only.

title: PFAS releases by facility
idea: Ranked bars of facilities by total releases of chemicals flagged as PFAS, the forever-chemicals leaderboard.
harm_angle: PFAS never breaks down, so today's release is a permanent addition to somebody's water.
caveat: PFAS flag encoding unverified; totals need numeric casting and unit normalization across pounds and grams.

title: Parent companies behind the releases
idea: Ranked bars of standardized parent company by total on-site releases, rolling many facilities up to the corporation responsible.
harm_angle: Names the actual corporate decision-makers rather than the anonymous plant.
caveat: Standardized parent name population is unverified; foreign parents sit in a separate column.

title: Releases on tribal land
idea: Map of facilities carrying a tribe or tribal-area code sized by total releases, showing the toxic burden on tribal land.
harm_angle: Tribal communities carry pollution with the least regulatory recourse.
caveat: The tribal fields may be blank on nearly all rows, leaving too few points to map.

title: Release pathway sankey
idea: Flow diagram from industry sector through release pathway (fugitive air, stack air, water, underground, landfill) to total, showing how each industry disposes.
harm_angle: Pathway determines exposure route: air hits lungs, water hits taps, landfill hits groundwater later.
caveat: All pathway columns are uncast text in the model; sums require casting and unit handling.

title: Carcinogen burden by zip
idea: Heatmap grid of zip codes by total carcinogen releases, isolating the postcodes carrying the heaviest cancer-linked load.
harm_angle: Concentrated carcinogen release in one zip is a measurable harm to identifiable households.
caveat: Release totals need casting; zip formats vary; the single-year snapshot limits trend claims.

title: Toxic facility registry map
idea: Point map of all toxic-release reporting facilities colored by open versus closed status, showing the full reporting universe.
harm_angle: The registry itself shows which communities host reporting facilities and which host none.
caveat: Coordinates are try_to_number over text; preferred versus facility coordinates may disagree.

title: Corporate concentration of toxic sites
idea: Ranked bars of standardized parent company by number of reporting facilities, showing which corporations own the most sites.
harm_angle: A handful of parent companies own a large share of the nation's toxic-release footprint.
caveat: Standardized parent field population unverified; company name variants may fragment counts.

title: Foreign-owned toxic facilities
idea: Map of facilities with a foreign parent company by state, showing where the responsible owner sits outside US jurisdiction.
harm_angle: When the owner is offshore, the community's leverage over the polluter is thinner.
caveat: Foreign parent fields may be blank on the vast majority of rows.

title: Federal facilities in the toxic registry
idea: Ranked bars of federal agencies by count of assigned reporting facilities, showing the government's own toxic footprint.
harm_angle: The government polluting its own neighbors is the least-covered version of this story.
caveat: Federal indicator and agency fields may be sparsely populated.

title: Mailing address versus plant location
idea: Flow diagram from facility state to corporate mailing state, showing how far the decision-makers sit from the smokestack.
harm_angle: Absentee ownership means nobody deciding about the plant breathes its air.
caveat: Mailing address may be a law firm or registered agent rather than a real headquarters.

title: Deaths per event by hazard type
idea: Ranked bars of direct plus indirect deaths per thousand events by hazard type, showing that the deadliest hazards per occurrence are not the most frequent ones.
harm_angle: Heat and flood kill quietly and frequently while tornadoes get the coverage.
caveat: The mart comment says 69,801 rows while the catalog claims 1.78M - the landed slice may be one year only; check coverage before claiming a national picture.

title: County map of storm fatalities
idea: County choropleth of cumulative direct deaths, forecast-zone rows excluded, showing where extreme weather actually kills people.
harm_angle: Repeated fatal-weather counties are places where warning and shelter systems keep failing.
caveat: Rows where the zone type is Z are forecast zones not counties and must be dropped before any FIPS join.

title: Damage dollars versus lives lost
idea: Scatter of parsed property damage against deaths per event type, showing which hazards destroy property versus which destroy people.
harm_angle: Hazards that kill without destroying much property attract the least recovery money.
caveat: Damage fields are text with K/M/B suffixes and must be parsed; no inflation adjustment.

title: Time-of-day danger by hazard
idea: Cohort grid of hour-of-day against hazard type with color as fatality rate, exposing the overnight tornado and flash-flood problem.
harm_angle: Overnight events kill more because people are asleep and warnings do not reach them.
caveat: Times are in local zone per the timezone column and need normalising before comparison.

title: Tornado tracks drawn begin to end
idea: Map drawing a line from begin lat/lon to end lat/lon for each tornado, colored by F-scale, giving the actual swath rather than a point.
harm_angle: Track corridors show which specific communities keep sitting in the path.
caveat: End coordinates are often missing for weaker events; only tornado rows carry this data.

title: Alert severity mix by forecast office
idea: Heatmap grid of forecast office against alert event type with color as count, showing how differently offices use severe categories.
harm_angle: Inconsistent severity language across offices means the same danger reads differently depending on where you live.
caveat: Only 287 rows - a live-API snapshot, not a history, so any pattern is a moment in time.

title: Alert lifetime from onset to expiry
idea: Distribution of hours between onset and expiry by event type, showing which hazards get long standing warnings and which get minutes.
harm_angle: Short-fuse warnings leave no time for people without a car or a shelter to act.
caveat: Snapshot of active alerts only; several timestamp fields are not date-cast in the model.

title: Where the alerts were live
idea: Map of alert points and zones at snapshot time colored by severity, a picture of the country's simultaneous hazard load.
harm_angle: Simultaneous multi-hazard load is when emergency systems get overwhelmed and people fall through.
caveat: 287 rows from a single pull; the geometry column may be a text blob.

title: The secondary extract's coverage gap
idea: Timeline of this 116k extract's records by date, purely to show which years the smaller feed actually covers.
harm_angle: Documents where the public record is partial, which matters before anyone counts anything from it.
caveat: This is an overlapping extract of the same NRC feed; treating it as independent would double count incidents.

title: Responsible org types ranked
idea: Ranked bars of responsible organisation type, separating private companies from government bodies and private citizens as sources of release calls.
harm_angle: Shows how much of the release burden is corporate versus public-sector, against the usual public assumption.
caveat: ORG_TYPE coding scheme unverified and may be sparsely filled.

title: What the unlabeled columns hide
idea: Exploratory small multiples of the five unnamed publisher columns' value distributions, to work out what the publisher stopped labelling.
harm_angle: Unlabeled fields in a public safety feed are public information the publisher effectively withheld.
caveat: Contents genuinely unknown; may be all null or pure noise, in which case there is no chart.

title: Companies that keep spilling
idea: Ranked bars of responsible companies by number of pollution and release calls over the full record, with the repeat names at the top named outright.
harm_angle: The same firms generate release after release while the communities downwind absorb every one of them.
caveat: Company names are free text with heavy spelling variation; needs normalisation or the leaderboard fragments.

title: Spill call map by state
idea: Map shaded by incident count per responsible-party state, layered against call type, to show where releases concentrate.
harm_angle: Marks the states carrying the physical burden of the country's chemical and fuel handling.
caveat: Responsible-party state is the company's address, not necessarily where the spill happened; that distinction could invert the story.

title: Decades of release calls
idea: Timeline of incident counts by call type across the whole record, testing whether reported releases are actually falling or just being categorised differently.
harm_angle: If releases are flat while regulation tightened, the enforcement story being told publicly is wrong.
caveat: Two date fields plus a src_year text field may disagree; try_to_timestamp over trimmed text may drop rows silently.

title: How long incidents stay open
idea: Distribution of the gap between when a call was received and when it was marked complete, split by call type and by responsible org type.
harm_angle: Incidents that sit open for months are incidents nobody is cleaning up while people live next to them.
caveat: DATE_TIME_COMPLETE may be null for open or abandoned records, biasing the distribution toward fast closures.

title: Zip codes that never stop calling
idea: Map at zip-code grain of repeat release locations, sized by incident count and coloured by how many distinct companies are responsible there.
harm_angle: A zip code with hundreds of releases from a rotating cast of companies is a sacrifice zone with no single villain to sue.
caveat: Zip is the responsible party's zip, not the incident location; the whole reading depends on which one it actually is.

title: Critical minerals import reliance
idea: Ranked bars of import reliance percentage by commodity, sorted, showing which materials the country cannot supply for itself.
harm_angle: Supply shocks in high-reliance minerals hit manufacturing jobs and consumer prices.
caveat: Import reliance is populated only for the commodity-summary rows, not the site-level records mixed into this table.

title: Every mine site mapped by development status
idea: Point map of mineral sites colored by development status (producer, past producer, prospect) and sized by production size class, showing the abandoned-site landscape.
harm_angle: Abandoned and past-producer sites leave contamination that residents inherit.
caveat: This table mixes national commodity statistics with site-level records; the grain must be split before mapping.

title: Production span and the towns left behind
idea: Timeline bars from first to last production year per site, grouped by state, showing regions where extraction ended decades ago.
harm_angle: Communities built around a mine that closed forty years ago carry the cleanup and the unemployment.
caveat: Production year fields are sparsely populated across the site records.

title: Commodity co-occurrence network
idea: Network of commodities that appear together at the same sites, revealing which contaminants travel with which valuable metals.
harm_angle: Knowing which toxic byproducts accompany a target metal tells communities what to test their water for.
caveat: Commodity fields are free text with inconsistent naming and abbreviations.

title: Monitoring station coverage map
idea: Point map of all monitoring sites colored by the parameter measured, exposing the watersheds nobody is measuring.
harm_angle: Unmonitored watersheds are where contamination goes undetected until people are sick.
caveat: 6.7M observation rows means the site list must be de-duplicated first; sites may be temporary.

title: Streamflow drought signature by basin
idea: Small multiples of streamflow over time by hydrologic unit, indexed to the historical median, showing basins in sustained decline.
harm_angle: Basins in sustained decline are communities heading toward water restrictions and dry wells.
caveat: Parameter codes must be filtered to discharge only; datetime is not timestamp-cast in the model.

title: Qualified and provisional readings
idea: Heatmap grid of state against year with color as the share of readings carrying a qualifier flag, a map of where the water record is least trustworthy.
harm_angle: Unreliable water data means regulators cannot prove a violation even when one happened.
caveat: Qualifier coding needs the agency legend; provisional data is normal for recent dates.

title: Gauges that went dark
idea: Map of sites colored by last-observation date, showing where monitoring stopped and never resumed.
harm_angle: A discontinued gauge is a community that lost its early warning for floods and contamination.
caveat: The landed extract may simply not include recent data for some sites; apparent silence could be an ingest artefact.

title: Water-quality parameter distribution by basin
idea: Distribution of measured values for a chosen contamination parameter by hydrologic unit, with any regulatory threshold drawn as a line.
harm_angle: Basins whose distribution sits above the threshold are people drinking or swimming in it.
caveat: Units differ by parameter and site; thresholds are not in this table and must be supplied externally.

title: Watershed atlas base map
idea: Map of all 2,456 HUC-8 subbasins labelled by name and area, the reference layer everything water-related gets placed onto.
harm_angle: Reference base; without it no water-harm story can be aggregated to the unit that actually shares the water.
caveat: Model holds attributes and area but no geometry column; drawing real boundaries needs a shapefile that may not be on the platform.

title: Watersheds that cross state lines
idea: Ranked bars of subbasins by how many states they touch, isolating the water bodies where no single state regulator is in charge.
harm_angle: Multi-state watersheds are where pollution flows across a jurisdiction line and enforcement stops at the border.
caveat: STATES is a delimited string needing splitting; format consistency unverified.

title: Watershed size distribution
idea: Distribution of subbasin area, showing how uneven the hydrologic units are and why per-watershed counts are not comparable without normalising.
harm_angle: Methodological floor chart that stops later water analyses from comparing a tiny basin to a giant one.
caveat: Purely descriptive; no direct human harm angle on its own.

title: Where nobody is watching the water
idea: Map of monitoring stations by watershed, with the subbasins that hold zero or one station highlighted rather than the well-covered ones.
harm_angle: Communities in unmonitored watersheds cannot prove their water is contaminated because nobody is measuring it.
caveat: Only 5,818 stations in this extract which may itself be a partial pull; absence here may not mean absence in reality.

title: Who runs the monitoring network
idea: Ranked bars of organisations by number of stations, showing how much of water monitoring is federal versus state versus volunteer groups.
harm_angle: When monitoring depends on volunteers and thin state budgets, coverage vanishes exactly where budgets are tightest.
caveat: Organisation coverage in this extract may not represent the full national portal.

title: Groundwater wells versus surface sites
idea: Ranked bars of station type by state, separating groundwater wells from streams and lakes, to show which states monitor the water people actually drink.
harm_angle: Where drinking-water aquifers go unmonitored, contamination is discovered by illness rather than by measurement.
caveat: Type vocabulary is long-tailed and needs grouping; well depth is likely null for surface sites.

title: Aquifers named in the record
idea: Ranked bars of named aquifers by station count, showing which underground water supplies have eyes on them and which are named but barely watched.
harm_angle: Aquifers with almost no monitoring stations serve real households whose only warning would come too late.
caveat: AQUIFERNAME likely null for most non-well stations; small extract limits the ranking's reliability.

title: Where the ground shakes hardest
idea: Point map of modeled peak ground acceleration with site-soil stiffness, sized by hazard level, over the mosaic's coverage.
harm_angle: Populations sitting on soft soil in high-hazard zones face the deadliest building collapses.
caveat: Only 12 rows in the mart -- this is almost certainly a model-registry sample, not the hazard grid itself.

title: Soft soil multiplies the shaking
idea: Scatter of site stiffness against modeled shaking, showing that the same quake hurts far more where the ground is soft.
harm_angle: Soft-soil neighborhoods -- often the cheapest land -- absorb disproportionate quake damage.
caveat: 12 rows; vs30 may be a text descriptor rather than a numeric value.

title: Model coverage gaps worldwide
idea: Map of which national and regional hazard models exist versus which geographies have none, treating the absence of a model as the finding.
harm_angle: Countries with no published hazard model cannot write protective building codes, so residents build blind.
caveat: country is wrapped in try_to_number over a name field, which will null it out -- fips or hazard_model_id must carry geography instead.

source_names: Global Witness Land and Environmental Defenders
title: Killings of defenders by year
idea: Timeline of recorded killings and attacks per year since 2012, split by incident type, the baseline count of the body toll.
harm_angle: Land defenders murdered for opposing extraction; the count is the direct human cost.
caveat: 232 rows is far below Global Witness published totals -- likely a partial extract, so trend shape may be distorted.

source_names: Global Witness Land and Environmental Defenders
title: Which industry kills defenders
idea: Ranked bars of incidents by the industry sector tied to the conflict (mining, logging, agribusiness, dams), with perpetrator type stacked inside each bar.
harm_angle: Names the industries whose projects correlate with dead defenders, and who pulls the trigger.
caveat: Sector and perpetrator are free text; will need grouping. Small n per sector.

source_names: Global Witness Land and Environmental Defenders
title: Indigenous defenders overrepresented
idea: Dot plot comparing the indigenous share of recorded victims against the indigenous share of population by region, showing systematic overexposure.
harm_angle: Indigenous communities absorb a share of lethal violence far above their population share.
caveat: Requires an external population denominator; indigenous_status may be sparsely coded.

source_names: Global Witness Land and Environmental Defenders
title: Impunity over time
idea: Cohort grid of incidents by year and region, shaded by whether the source report notes any prosecution or accountability, to show how rarely anyone answers.
harm_angle: Killings that produce no prosecution teach the next community that opposing a mine is free to punish.
caveat: Accountability is only in free-text notes_context -- would require text classification, which is not a stored field.

source_names: Global Witness Land and Environmental Defenders
title: Gendered pattern of attacks
idea: Small multiples by region of incident counts split by victim gender and incident type, surfacing whether women defenders face different attack forms.
harm_angle: Women defenders may face threat and disappearance patterns invisible in headline killing counts.
caveat: Tiny n once split three ways; gender may be largely blank.

title: Facilities traced to a parent company
idea: Ranked bars of ultimate parent companies by how many EPA-regulated facilities they own, the leaderboard of who actually runs America's polluting infrastructure.
harm_angle: Facility-level enforcement lets a parent absorb dozens of small fines; rolling facilities up to the parent shows the real scale of the harm.
caveat: This is a match table, so parent attribution is only as good as match_confidence; low-confidence rows must be excluded and shown.

title: How confident is the match
idea: Distribution of match confidence by match method, the methodological chart that has to run before anyone trusts the parent leaderboard.
harm_angle: Overclaiming a corporate parent link would smear the wrong company; showing the confidence spread is the honesty check.
caveat: MATCH_CONFIDENCE scale and MATCH_METHOD vocabulary are undocumented in the model.

title: Facilities with no parent found
idea: Ranked bars of facility counts for records where no parent LEI or CIK could be matched, mapping the ownership blind spot.
harm_angle: Facilities whose owner cannot be identified are facilities where nobody can be held responsible at the corporate level.
caveat: Unmatched may reflect crosswalk gaps rather than genuinely orphan facilities; state is not a column here so geography needs a join.

title: Records flagged for human review
idea: Ranked bars of review-flagged matches grouped by parent name, showing where the automated crosswalk itself is unsure who owns what.
harm_angle: The flagged pile is a to-do list of ownership questions nobody has answered.
caveat: REVIEW_FLAG semantics unverified; may be a boolean or a free-text reason.

title: Same parent three identifiers
idea: Overlap view of how often a parent carries an LEI, a CIK and a UEI together versus only one, mapping where the identity system breaks.
harm_angle: A company existing under three unlinked identifier systems can be a polluter, a contractor and a public filer without anyone connecting the three.
caveat: Identifier columns may be sentinel-masked or blank-string filled; distinct-count and value sampling are mandatory before trusting fill rates.

source_names: OWID Annual CO2 emissions by country
title: Who filled the atmosphere
idea: Stacked area of cumulative emissions by country over the full record, showing the historical responsibility split rather than the annual snapshot.
harm_angle: Countries suffering worst climate damage contributed almost nothing to the stock of emissions.
caveat: Entity column mixes countries with regional and income aggregates; must filter on a valid ISO code.

source_names: OWID Annual CO2 emissions by country
title: Emissions per country ranked now
idea: Ranked bars of latest-year emissions by country, the plain descriptive floor chart.
harm_angle: Establishes who currently emits most, the denominator for every accountability claim.
caveat: Aggregate rows inflate the top of the ranking if not filtered.

source_names: OWID Annual CO2 emissions by country
title: The pledge-versus-path gap
idea: Slope chart per country from a chosen baseline year to latest, showing which countries actually bent their emissions curve down and which only talked.
harm_angle: Populations in countries that pledged and never cut are exposed to the warming their governments promised to prevent.
caveat: No pledge or target field exists in this table -- the pledge side is external context, not data here.

source_names: OWID Annual CO2 emissions by country
title: Small emitters, big exposure
idea: Scatter of a country's total emissions against a climate-vulnerability measure, expected to show a near-inverse relationship.
harm_angle: The least responsible countries sit in the most exposed positions -- the core climate-injustice shape.
caveat: Vulnerability is not in this table; needs an external or sibling source, so treat as a two-source idea.

title: The warming stripes
idea: Timeline of global temperature anomaly with the uncertainty band, the canonical baseline chart.
harm_angle: The single line every local harm story is measured against.
caveat: 531 rows suggests multiple entities or a long series; entity mix unverified.

title: Certainty grew as warming grew
idea: Timeline plotting the width of the uncertainty band alongside the anomaly itself, showing the science got more certain exactly as the signal got larger.
harm_angle: Undercuts the delay argument that the science was too uncertain to act on.
caveat: Band width must be derived; bounds may be null in early years.

title: Hemispheric split
idea: Small multiples of anomaly by entity if the table holds hemisphere or regional series, showing uneven warming.
harm_angle: Warming is not evenly distributed, so neither is the harm.
caveat: Entity may only contain a single global series, in which case this idea dies.

title: Agency Budget Share Ranking
idea: Rank agencies by budget_authority_amount and percentage_of_total_budget_authority for the current fiscal year.
harm_angle: The reference frame every other spending chart in the platform needs.
caveat: 111 rows and a single-year snapshot - it is a dimension table more than a story.

title: Who Spends What They Are Given
idea: Scatter obligated_amount against current_total_budget_authority_amount per agency, with outlay overlaid. Viewer sees agencies sitting on unobligated authority.
harm_angle: Unobligated authority is appropriated help that never reaches anyone.
caveat: Single-snapshot fiscal quarter; mid-year figures naturally look under-obligated.

title: Application Windows Too Short to Use
idea: Distribution of days between posted_date and close_date by agency and eligible applicant type. Viewer sees agencies posting grants with windows so short only incumbents can respond.
harm_angle: Short windows lock out small community organizations that have no grant-writing staff.
caveat: Only 100 rows in the mart - a live-search snapshot, not a historical corpus.

title: Ceiling Versus Expected Awards
idea: Scatter award_ceiling against expected_number_of_awards, sized by estimated_total_program_funding. Viewer sees programs advertising big ceilings while planning very few awards.
harm_angle: Programs that look generous but award almost nobody waste applicant time and hope.
caveat: 100-row snapshot; ceiling and floor are untyped text passthroughs.

title: Who Is Allowed to Apply
idea: Ranked bars of dollars by eligible_applicants category. Viewer sees how much federal grant money is structurally closed to community nonprofits and tribes.
harm_angle: Eligibility rules are the quietest way to exclude the communities a program claims to serve.
caveat: Eligibility is a multi-value text field; 100 rows only.

title: Business-Type Flag Wall
idea: Grid of every socioeconomic flag column - veteran-owned, women-owned, HUBZone, tribal, minority-owned - showing dollars flowing to each. Viewer sees which designations actually carry money and which are decorative.
chart_shape: heatmap grid of flags against dollars
harm_angle: Designations that carry no dollars are a promise of inclusion the government never kept.
caveat: Explicitly a 50,000-row capped sample per the model header - shape only, never totals.

title: Place of Performance Versus Recipient Home
idea: Flow from recipient state to place-of-performance state, weighted by dollars. Viewer sees money nominally spent in poor states actually banked in a few rich ones.
harm_angle: A community hosting the work but not the payroll gets the disruption without the income.
caveat: 50k-row sample; state codes need normalization for territories.

title: Undefinitized Actions
idea: Timeline of contracts flagged undefinitized_action - work started before terms were agreed - by agency.
harm_angle: Starting work before agreeing a price is how cost overruns get locked in on the public tab.
caveat: Sample only; the flag is code-based and may need decoding.

title: Foreign-Owned Federal Vendors
idea: Map and rank contractors flagged foreign_owned by dollars and by agency, including defense. Viewer sees how much sensitive federal work sits with foreign-owned entities.
harm_angle: Accountability gets harder to enforce the further the owner sits from US courts.
caveat: Model covers a single year window (2024-10 to 2025-09); foreign_owned is a self-reported flag.

title: Parent Company Rollup
idea: Collapse recipient_uei into recipient_parent_uei and rank parents by total obligations. Viewer sees the true concentration hidden behind hundreds of subsidiary names.
chart_shape: ranked bars before and after rollup
harm_angle: Subsidiary sprawl is how a handful of conglomerates look like a competitive market.
caveat: Parent UEI completeness is unverified; a blank parent silently understates concentration.

title: Where the Work Actually Happens
idea: Compare recipient_state_code against primary_place_of_performance_state_code per contract, mapped as a mismatch rate.
harm_angle: Local hiring claims fall apart when the contractor and the work live in different states.
caveat: One-year window; place of performance is coarse for services contracts.

title: Executive Pay Against Contract Size
idea: Scatter highly_compensated_officer_1_amount against current_total_value_of_award per vendor.
harm_angle: Public contracts funding outsized private pay is a distribution question with real losers.
caveat: Exec comp is only reported above thresholds and is heavily incomplete.

title: Competition Is Disappearing
idea: Timeline of the share of contract dollars awarded with other_than_full_and_open_competition, by agency, FY2007 onward. Viewer sees agencies quietly abandoning competition.
harm_angle: Noncompetitive contracting means the public overpays and no one can point to a cheaper bid that lost.
caveat: Model is a view over a 20M-row landing table so any scan is expensive; competition fields may be code-only.

title: One Offer Received
idea: Distribution of number_of_offers_received by contract value band and agency. Viewer sees the pile of large contracts where exactly one company bid.
harm_angle: Single-bid contracts at scale are how a small set of firms captures public budgets.
caveat: number_of_offers_received is often 1 by reporting convention rather than reality - verify before claiming capture.

title: Set-Aside Programs That Feed Giants
idea: For contracts flagged with a small-business or disadvantaged set-aside, plot the recipient parent company total federal revenue. Viewer sees set-aside dollars flowing to subsidiaries of very large parents.
chart_shape: scatter of set-aside dollars against parent size
harm_angle: Set-asides exist to help genuinely small firms; capture by giants takes that ladder away.
caveat: Parent UEI may be blank on many rows; parent-size rollup is an in-source aggregation not a verified fact.

title: Contract Value Creep
idea: Slope chart from base_and_exercised_options_value to potential_total_value_of_award per award, ranked by growth. Viewer sees contracts that ballooned far past what was originally bought.
harm_angle: Ballooning contracts absorb budget that was appropriated for something else people needed.
caveat: Transaction grain means values repeat - must take the latest modification per award key.

title: Executive Pay Inside Federal Vendors
idea: Ranked dot plot of highly_compensated_officer_1_amount across vendors, against each vendor total federal obligations. Viewer sees named executives paid heavily out of near-entirely-federal revenue.
harm_angle: Public money paying private executive salaries while the delivered service is thin.
caveat: Exec comp reporting is only required above thresholds - coverage is partial and self-reported.

title: Subaward Skim Distribution
idea: Distribution of subaward amount by prime recipient, showing how much of a prime award is passed down versus retained.
harm_angle: The gap between the prime award and the subaward is the middleman cut of public money.
caveat: Explicitly a 5,000-row API slice - shape only; the prime award amount is not in this mart so the retained share cannot be computed here.

title: Repeat Subcontractor Ring
idea: Network of prime recipient to subaward recipient_name. Viewer sees closed loops where the same firms subcontract to each other across awards.
harm_angle: Closed contracting rings keep new and local firms permanently outside.
caveat: 5,000-row slice; the prime recipient may only exist inside the raw record_json blob.

title: Obligation Versus Outlay Gap by Agency
idea: Ranked dot plot of total_obligation against total_outlay per awarding agency. Viewer sees agencies that announce far more than they spend.
harm_angle: Unspent obligations are services the intended population never received.
caveat: Only 300 rows - an API sample, not the full corpus; totals are not authoritative.

title: Subaward Pass-Through Rate
idea: Scatter subaward_count against award_amount by award_type. Viewer sees big awards that immediately fan out to subcontractors - a pass-through layer taking a cut.
harm_angle: Every pass-through layer skims money before it reaches the work.
caveat: 300-row sample; subaward_count is a reported roll-up that is frequently understated.

title: Long Awards Short Money
idea: Distribution of award_duration_days against award_amount, faceted by cfda_title.
harm_angle: Multi-year commitments funded at a trickle strand the programs people depend on.
caveat: Tiny sample; derived duration relies on both dates being clean.

title: Assistance Dollars Per County
idea: Map federal assistance obligations per county of performance across FY2007-FY2026. Viewer sees the counties that receive almost nothing decade after decade.
harm_angle: Counties that never appear on the assistance map are also the ones with the worst health and housing outcomes.
caveat: 20M-row transaction grain needs aggregation care so modifications are not double counted; FIPS may be text with lost leading zeros.

title: Loans Versus Grants by Place
idea: Split assistance by assistance_type_description into grants versus loans and map the ratio by state. Viewer sees which places get money they must repay and which get money they keep.
harm_angle: Communities handed debt instead of grants carry the repayment burden the richer places never take on.
caveat: Loan face value and obligation are on different scales - the ratio needs an explicit definition.

title: Disaster Money That Arrives Late
idea: For awards carrying disaster_emergency_fund_codes, plot the gap between action_date and period_of_performance_start_date by fund code. Viewer sees how long emergency money takes to actually start working.
harm_angle: Every month of delay in disaster money is a month of people living in damaged housing.
caveat: DEF codes are a concatenated multi-value text field; dates are untyped passthroughs.

title: Obligated But Never Outlaid
idea: Scatter total_obligated_amount against total_outlayed_amount_for_overall_award per award, colored by agency. Viewer sees announced money that never actually moved.
harm_angle: Announced-but-unspent money is a press release the intended recipients never see.
caveat: Outlay fields are award-level repeated on every transaction row - must dedupe by award key first.

title: COVID and IIJA Money Trails
idea: Sankey from supplemental funding source through agency to CFDA program to place of performance, using the COVID and IIJA supplemental columns.
harm_angle: Shows whether once-in-a-generation infrastructure and pandemic money reached the places that needed it most.
caveat: Supplemental columns are award-level and may be mostly null; sankey needs aggressive aggregation at 20M rows.

title: Audit Firms That Never Find Problems
idea: For each auditor_firm_name, plot the share of its audits disclosing a material weakness or noncompliance against its audit volume. Viewer sees high-volume firms with implausibly clean records.
chart_shape: scatter with volume on x and finding rate on y
harm_angle: Rubber-stamp audits let grant money serving poor communities go unaccounted for.
caveat: Boolean-looking columns are passed through untyped and may be Y/N text; low finding rates can be genuine for small-client portfolios.

title: Going Concern Cluster Map
idea: Map auditees flagged is_going_concern_included by state and entity_type, sized by total_amount_expended. Viewer sees where federally-funded organizations are financially failing.
harm_angle: A going-concern flag on a clinic or housing nonprofit means services are about to stop for the people who use them.
caveat: Going concern flag may be sparse; auditee_zip is text and may include ZIP+4 variants.

title: Repeat Offenders Never Downgraded
idea: Cohort grid of auditees by year showing material weakness disclosed alongside is_low_risk_auditee. Viewer sees organizations that keep getting findings yet keep the low-risk label.
harm_angle: Low-risk status means lighter future scrutiny for the exact organizations that already failed.
caveat: Requires auditee_ein to be stable across years; EIN columns are a known masking trap on this platform.

title: Oversight Agency Workload
idea: Ranked bars of audits per oversight_agency and cognizant_agency against total dollars expended under each. Viewer sees which agency is nominally watching the most money with the least attention.
harm_angle: Overloaded oversight agencies are why bad grantees keep drawing money.
caveat: Agency codes may need a lookup to be readable; dollars column is untyped in the model.

title: Late Audit Filers
idea: Distribution of the gap between fy_end_date and fac_accepted_date, by entity_type and state. Viewer sees which classes of grantee chronically file years late.
harm_angle: Years-late audits mean misuse is discovered long after the money and the harm are gone.
caveat: Date casts are try_to_date over text and may drop rows silently.

title: Offshore Banking Capacity by Country
idea: Map countries shaded by number of registered foreign financial institutions, showing where the world's capacity to hold US-person money actually sits.
harm_angle: Jurisdictions with vastly more registered institutions than population are structurally built to hold other people's hidden money.
caveat: Only three real columns — this source is genuinely thin, so ideas must lean on name and country patterns alone.

title: Institution Name Families
idea: Group registered institutions by shared name stem and plot the biggest families as ranked bars, exposing single brands operating hundreds of registered vehicles.
harm_angle: One brand with three hundred registered entities across forty jurisdictions is a purpose-built structure, not organic growth.
caveat: Name-stem grouping is fuzzy and will produce false families; no parent identifier exists in this table.

title: Identifier Country Mismatch
idea: Cross-tab of the jurisdiction encoded inside each institution's global identifier against its reported country name, flagging institutions where the two disagree.
harm_angle: A mismatch between where an institution says it is and where its identifier says it is is worth explaining.
caveat: Depends on the identifier's internal structure being parseable and consistent, which the model does not show; may be a dead end.

title: Ninety years of bank failures
idea: Timeline of failures per year with total estimated loss as a second series, so the 1980s thrift wave and 2008-2010 stand as distinct mountains.
harm_angle: Each failure spike is a wave of depositors, borrowers and local employers cut adrift.
caveat: Estimated loss is not inflation-adjusted and is null for older records.

title: Loss-to-assets ratio by resolution type
idea: Distribution of the loss-to-assets ratio split by resolution type, showing which resolution strategies cost the insurance fund most per dollar of bank.
harm_angle: A costlier resolution path is money that ultimately comes out of the banking public.
caveat: Ratio is null where assets are missing; resolution categories changed definition over decades.

title: Who bought the failed banks
idea: Network linking failed banks to acquiring institutions, revealing serial acquirers who consolidated a region through other banks' failures.
harm_angle: Serial acquirers turn local failures into regional banking concentration and fewer local lending options.
caveat: Acquirer names are unstandardized text and acquirers themselves later failed or merged.

title: Young banks fail fastest
idea: Distribution of years insured before failure, split by era, testing whether the newest charters are the most fragile.
harm_angle: Fragile new charters take community deposits into a short life.
caveat: Insured date may be missing for older institutions; survivorship excluded by construction.

title: Supervisor scoreboard
idea: Ranked bars of failures and total loss grouped by supervisory agency and era, asking whether some regulators presided over costlier failures.
harm_angle: Weak supervision converts into public losses and shuttered local banks.
caveat: No denominator of supervised institutions in this table so raw counts mislead.

title: Thirty Years Of Branch Closures
idea: County-level map small-multipled across survey year showing net branch count change 1994-2025 and exposing banking deserts.
harm_angle: Communities losing every branch lose access to cash, credit and small-business lending.
caveat: Branch counts include non-retail service types; branch service type should be filtered.

title: Banking Deserts Ranked By County
idea: Ranked bars of counties with the largest percentage drop in branch count since their peak year with current branch count annotated.
harm_angle: Names the specific counties where people now have no local bank.
caveat: Small rural counties will dominate percentage rankings unless a floor is set.

title: Deposit Concentration Into Fewer Hands
idea: Timeline of the share of total branch deposits held by the top ten holding companies per survey year showing consolidation of the deposit base.
harm_angle: Concentrated deposits mean fewer local lenders deciding who gets a mortgage or a business loan.
caveat: Holding-company RSSD may be blank for independents, inflating the unaffiliated bucket.

title: Where The Branches Actually Are
idea: Point map of every branch by SIMS latitude and longitude for the latest survey year colored by branch service type.
harm_angle: Baseline geography of who can physically reach a bank.
caveat: SIMS coordinates may be missing or default-centroid for some branches.

title: Community Banks Versus The Giants
idea: Slope chart of deposit share by bank class and community bank flag between an early and a recent survey year with a metro versus non-metro split.
harm_angle: If community banks vanish fastest outside metros, rural borrowers lose the lender most likely to say yes.
caveat: Community bank flag definition changed over the survey history.

title: Deposits Booked Far From Home
idea: Scatter of branch deposits against branch count per institution flagging branches whose reported deposits are implausibly large for their location.
harm_angle: Deposit-booking distortions make state-level lending obligations look met when local money never arrives.
caveat: Requires understanding the deposit reporting-method code; not verified.

title: Who Gets Federal Home Loan Bank Money
idea: Ranked bars of member counts by member type and charter type per district, showing whether the housing-bank system serves banks, credit unions or insurers.
harm_angle: A housing liquidity system dominated by insurers rather than local lenders is not funding homes.
caveat: Member type codes are unexplained in the model and may need a lookup.

title: Membership Growth Timeline
idea: Timeline of member approval dates versus membership dates by district showing waves of entry into the system.
harm_angle: Shifts in who joins the housing bank system foreshadow who controls mortgage liquidity.
caveat: Only approval and membership dates present; no exit date, so churn is invisible.

title: Members On The Map
idea: Point or state map of members by district showing whether district boundaries leave any region thinly served.
harm_angle: Regions with few member lenders have less access to subsidized housing liquidity.
caveat: No coordinates in the model; geocoding by city state and zip required.

title: Insurers Inside The Housing Bank
idea: Small multiples per district of the share of members carrying an insurance-regulator id versus a bank cert or credit-union id over membership year.
harm_angle: Insurance companies borrowing cheap federal housing money without making home loans is a quiet subsidy leak.
caveat: Id columns may be blank rather than null; needs a distinct-value check before trusting.

title: Venue Membership Overlap
idea: Grid of market-participant ids by which trading venues they belong to showing how many firms touch every venue versus only one.
harm_angle: Firms wired into every venue see order flow nobody else sees and the concentration is the story.
caveat: Flags may be text Y/N rather than boolean; no time axis in the table.

title: Market Participants By Type
idea: Ranked bars of participant-id counts by participant type with the firms holding the most ids called out.
harm_angle: One firm operating many market identities is harder for regulators and the public to follow.
caveat: Snapshot only; no history of when ids were registered or retired.

title: Where Wall Street Sits
idea: Map of market participants by reported location showing the geographic concentration of the trading industry.
harm_angle: Baseline geography of who runs the market machinery.
caveat: Location is free text of unknown granularity; may be city or full address.

title: Municipal Bond Gatekeepers By State
idea: Map of registered municipal securities firms by state, sized by count, showing which states are served by many firms and which by almost none.
