harm_angle: Towns in states with only one or two municipal bond dealers pay whatever those dealers charge, and residents pay it back through taxes and utility bills.
caveat: Only 925 rows and state is the firm's registered state, likely headquarters, not where it does business.

title: Dealer Versus Advisor Split
idea: Ranked bars of registrant types, showing how many firms are dealers, municipal advisors, or both, and how many wear two hats.
harm_angle: Firms registered as both advisor and dealer can advise a town to buy what they themselves sell.
caveat: Dual registration must be inferred by finding the same msrb_id under two registrant types; whether that pattern exists is unverified.

title: Municipal Advice Deserts
idea: Dot plot of states ranked by municipal advisors per state, calling out states in single digits.
harm_angle: Small municipalities with no local independent advisor get their financing advice from the people selling them the debt.
caveat: Tiny table; no population or municipality-count denominator inside this source.

title: Why Credit Unions Disappear
idea: Ranked bars of the stated reason each merging credit union gave up its charter, showing whether failure, expansion, or lost sponsorship drives consolidation.
harm_angle: Every merged-away credit union is a community that lost its own lender and got absorbed into a bigger one's rulebook.
caveat: Only 27 rows in this mart, which is far too few to be a full merger history; likely a single snapshot period.

title: Size Mismatch In Mergers
idea: Scatter of merging credit union assets against continuing credit union assets, showing how often a tiny community lender is swallowed by a giant.
harm_angle: A 5-million-dollar community lender absorbed into a 5-billion-dollar institution means local underwriting judgment disappears.
caveat: 27 rows; assets are text-cast to numbers and may be null for many rows.

title: Field Of Membership Drift
idea: Flow diagram from each merging credit union's field of membership to the continuing one's, showing whose eligibility rules replace whose.
harm_angle: When a workplace-based credit union folds into a community charter, the original members' preferential terms can quietly end.
caveat: Field of membership strings are long free text; a flow chart needs categorization first. Only 27 rows.

title: Low Income Designated Credit Unions Map
idea: Map of federally insured credit unions by state, shaded by the share carrying a low-income designation, showing where the poverty-serving lenders actually are.
harm_angle: States with almost no low-income-designated credit unions leave poor households to payday lenders instead.
caveat: State is the mailing address state, which may differ from branch footprint; single-quarter snapshot.

title: Loan To Share Ratio Distribution
idea: Distribution of loan-to-share ratios split by low-income designation, showing whether poverty-serving credit unions lend out more or less of what they hold.
harm_angle: A low-income credit union sitting on deposits it will not lend is a community whose own savings are not coming back to it.
caveat: Ratio scale (percent versus fraction) is unverified; outliers may be data errors.

title: Small Credit Unions Under Pressure
idea: Scatter of total assets against four-quarter member growth, colored by return on average assets, showing the small shrinking institutions heading for merger.
harm_angle: The bottom-left cluster is a shortlist of communities about to lose their local financial institution.
caveat: Growth fields are text-cast; single snapshot means the trend is only the source's own four-quarter field, not a real time series.

title: Net Worth Cushion By Region
idea: Small multiples by NCUA region of the net worth ratio distribution, showing which regions hold the thinnest-capitalized institutions.
harm_angle: Thin capital means a regional shock takes out the lenders that low-income members have no substitute for.
caveat: Ratio is text-cast; regulatory thresholds are not in the data and would have to be added as reference lines.

title: Deposits Growing Loans Not
idea: Slope chart of four-quarter deposit growth versus four-quarter loan growth per credit union, highlighting institutions taking in money without lending it back.
harm_angle: Deposits flowing in while loans stall means a community's savings are being parked elsewhere instead of financing local homes and cars.
caveat: Both growth fields are text-cast percentages of unverified scale; extreme values from small bases will dominate.

title: National Bank Charter Map
idea: Map of national bank charters by state and city, showing where federally chartered banks are headquartered.
harm_angle: States with almost no chartered banks headquartered in them export their deposits and import their credit decisions.
caveat: Only 724 rows and headquarters city is not branch footprint; snapshot with no date column at all.

title: Charter Number Vintage
idea: Distribution of banks by charter number, which runs roughly chronologically, showing how many surviving national banks date to the 1800s.
harm_angle: Old charters signal entrenchment; the incumbents that survived every consolidation wave set terms in their markets.
caveat: Charter number as a proxy for age is an assumption not stated in the data; reissued numbers would break it.

title: Identifier Crosswalk Completeness
idea: Ranked bars of how many national banks carry a usable deposit-insurance certificate and Federal Reserve id, measuring how joinable this list actually is.
harm_angle: Missing crosswalk ids mean bank misconduct in one federal database cannot be matched to the bank in another.
caveat: cert and rssd are text-cast to numbers and may be blank or sentinel-filled; must check distinct counts not just non-null.

title: Where Thrifts Survive
idea: Map of the remaining federally chartered thrifts by state and city, showing the shrunken geography of the savings-and-loan sector.
harm_angle: Thrifts were the mortgage lender of last resort for working families, and their disappearance from a state is a mortgage access story.
caveat: Only 218 rows and no date column, so this is one undated snapshot with no way to show the decline itself.

title: Thrift Crosswalk Gaps
idea: Ranked bars of thrifts with and without a deposit-insurance certificate or Federal Reserve id, showing how many are unlinkable to financial performance data.
harm_angle: Unlinkable institutions are ones whose lending record cannot be audited against their community.
caveat: 218 rows; genuinely thin source with only seven real columns and no time axis, hence only two ideas.

title: Audit Partner Workload
idea: Ranked bars of individual engagement partners by number of public-company audits signed in a year, exposing partners signing far more than a person can supervise.
harm_angle: An overloaded audit partner is how a company's books go unchecked, and the pensioners and employees holding the stock pay for the miss.
caveat: Partner id stability across firms is unverified; multiple audits per issuer per year would inflate counts.

title: The Audit Market Concentration
idea: Ranked bars of audit firms by number of issuers audited, showing how few firms check the books of nearly every public company.
harm_angle: When four firms audit almost everything, there is nowhere for a company to go for a genuinely independent second opinion.
caveat: firm_id versus firm_name mismatches from member-firm structures could split or merge networks incorrectly.

title: Audit Report Timing Crunch
idea: Distribution of the gap between fiscal period end and audit report date, faceted by firm, showing which auditors sign off fastest.
harm_angle: An audit signed off in record time on a complex company is a red flag that investors and employees never see.
caveat: Both dates are text-cast and may fail on some rows; industry complexity is not in this table so fast is not automatically bad.

title: Partner Rotation Compliance
idea: Cohort grid of issuer against year colored by which partner signed, making visible any issuer whose partner never rotates despite the five-year rule.
harm_angle: A partner who never rotates off a client is the exact relationship the rotation rule was written to prevent after Enron.
caveat: Requires accurate partner ids across years; name-based fallback would be unreliable. Rule details are not in the data.

title: Offshore Audit Participation
idea: Flow diagram from issuer country to audit firm issuing country, showing how much of a US company's audit work is performed by firms in other jurisdictions.
harm_angle: Audit work done in a jurisdiction the US regulator cannot inspect means nobody is truly checking the numbers behind American retirement accounts.
caveat: Participation percentages are stored as text and may be ranges rather than numbers; issuer country is not directly in this table.

title: Amendment Churn By Firm
idea: Heatmap grid of audit firm against amendment reason flags, showing which firms most often go back and correct their filings.
harm_angle: Frequent corrections to who signed an audit suggest a firm that does not know its own engagement records.
caveat: Amendment flags are text indicators with an undocumented vocabulary; fill rates unknown.

title: Who Manages Institutional Money
idea: Ranked bars of filing managers by number of quarterly filings, giving the roster of the institutions that hold America's invested savings.
harm_angle: These are the entities voting the shares in companies that employ and house people, and most of the public has never heard their names.
caveat: Manager name is free text and the same firm appears under many spellings; 344k rows are filings not firms.

title: The Confidential Treatment Trail
idea: Timeline of filings claiming confidential treatment and of confidentiality denials or expirations, showing who tries to hide positions and whether the regulator says no.
harm_angle: Confidential holdings mean the public cannot see who is quietly building a stake in the company they work for.
caveat: Both confidentiality date fields are text-cast and may be null for the overwhelming majority of rows.

title: Amendment Behavior By Manager
idea: Heatmap grid of filing manager against amendment type and count, showing who routinely restates what they said they held.
harm_angle: Routine restatement of holdings makes the public disclosure regime effectively unreadable in real time.
caveat: Amendment fields are uncast text; manager name normalization needed.

title: Money Management Geography
idea: Map of filing managers by city and state, showing the extreme concentration of institutional asset management in a few zip codes.
harm_angle: Decisions affecting jobs and housing nationwide are made from a handful of neighborhoods.
caveat: The state-or-country field is wrongly cast to a number in this model, which will null out most values; city and zip are the usable fields.

title: Most Widely Held Securities
idea: Ranked bars of securities by how many distinct institutional managers hold them, showing the handful of companies that nearly every institution owns.
harm_angle: Universal ownership means the same investors sit on both sides of a labor dispute, a merger, or a price increase.
caveat: 101 million rows in a view, so this is expensive to compute; issuer name is free text and CUSIP is the reliable key.

title: Common Ownership Network
idea: Network view of the biggest managers and the issuers they jointly hold, drawing the web of overlapping ownership across competing companies.
harm_angle: When the same funds own every competitor in an industry, competition on price and wages is nobody's interest.
caveat: Requires joining holdings to the submissions table for manager identity; very large table so sampling by quarter is essential.

title: Voting Power Without Ownership
idea: Scatter of position value against sole voting authority, isolating positions where a manager holds shares but disclaims the vote.
harm_angle: Separating money from votes is how influence over a company gets hidden from the people the company employs.
caveat: Voting authority fields are left uncast as text in this model and may need heavy cleaning; value_col scale (dollars versus thousands) changed historically.

title: Put And Call Overlay
idea: Ranked bars of issuers by the volume of put positions disclosed against them, showing which companies institutions are betting against.
harm_angle: Heavy short interest in hospital, housing, or utility operators is a signal about companies whose customers cannot leave.
caveat: The putcall field is sparsely used by design; only some managers report derivative positions.

title: Delegated Management Chains
idea: Flow diagram from filing manager to the other manager credited on each position, exposing who actually controls the shares behind the named filer.
harm_angle: Layered discretion arrangements make it impossible for a worker or pensioner to know who really controls their employer's shares.
caveat: othermanager is a positional reference code, not a name, and needs the cover-page table to resolve; time_axis value here should be read as no.

title: Who Owns a Given Company
idea: For a chosen security, ranked bars of institutional holders by reported value, showing how few managers hold most of it.
harm_angle: Concentrated institutional ownership means a few managers decide the fate of companies whose workers and customers get no vote.
caveat: 202M rows; must be filtered to one issuer to render at all. 13F value units changed historically between dollars and thousands.

title: Put and Call Overlay on Holdings
idea: Small multiples per issuer showing long positions against reported put and call positions, revealing where institutions bet against what they hold.
harm_angle: Betting against a company while holding it shapes decisions that hit that company's workforce.
caveat: putcall is sparsely used in 13F filings; the interesting cells may be near-empty.

title: Voting Power Versus Economic Stake
idea: Scatter of reported value against sole voting authority per position, so positions with big money and zero votes stand out as a distinct class.
harm_angle: Money without votes and votes without money both distort who actually controls a company.
caveat: Voting authority fields may be inconsistently reported across filers.

title: Positions Delegated to Other Managers
idea: Network graph of filers to the other-manager values they cite, exposing sub-advisory chains where the named filer is not the real decision-maker.
harm_angle: If the filer is not the decider, disclosure names the wrong party and accountability evaporates.
caveat: othermanager is often a positional index into a separate table rather than a name; may be unusable without that table.

title: Filing Timeliness by Institution
idea: Distribution of days from period of report to filing date per filer, revealing chronic late filers among institutional managers.
harm_angle: Late disclosure means the public sees ownership only after it stops mattering.
caveat: The singular submission mart appears to duplicate the positions column list; the plural submissions model holds the filer identity fields — confirm which table is live before building.

title: Amended Filings as a Signal
idea: Timeline of submission type mix over quarters, tracking the share of amendments and restatements as an indicator of sloppy or strategic disclosure.
harm_angle: A manager who routinely amends can time what the public learns and when.
caveat: Same singular/plural model confusion as above; submission type codes need a lookup.

title: The Filer Population Over Decades
idea: Timeline of distinct filers each quarter, showing the growth of the institutional manager population that crossed the reporting threshold.
harm_angle: More of the economy owned by disclosed institutions, with a disclosure regime that has not scaled to match.
caveat: Reporting threshold changes over time confound the trend.

title: Institutional Filing Volume Over Time
idea: Timeline of 13F submissions per quarter, showing the growth in the number of institutions large enough to be required to report.
harm_angle: Growth in the reporting population tracks the concentration of household savings into a few hundred institutions.
caveat: Date fields are passed through uncast in this model and may be text; the reporting threshold has not been updated for decades, which confounds the trend.

title: Late Filers
idea: Distribution of the gap between period of report and filing date by institution, showing who consistently reports at the last legal moment or later.
harm_angle: Late disclosure means the public learns who owns what only after the trades that mattered are long done.
caveat: Both dates are uncast text in this model; deadline rules are not in the data and would have to be applied externally.

title: Submission Type Mix
idea: Ranked bars of submission types over time, showing the balance of original reports, notices, and amendments.
harm_angle: A rising share of notice-only filings means more holdings reported by someone else and harder for the public to trace.
caveat: Submission type vocabulary is undocumented in the model; dates uncast.

title: Business Development Company Roster
idea: Ranked bars and a map of the registered business development companies by state, showing the small club of vehicles lending to mid-sized private firms.
harm_angle: These vehicles are a major source of high-cost debt for mid-sized employers, and their terms flow through to those workers.
caveat: Only 212 rows and it is a registration roster, not financials.

title: Registration Wave Timeline
idea: Timeline of filing dates for business development company registrations, showing the boom periods when the sector expanded.
harm_angle: Registration booms precede the credit cycles that later leave mid-sized employers over-leveraged.
caveat: 212 rows; filing_date is text-cast and may cover only recent filings.

title: Shared Addresses Among Managers
idea: Ranked bars of street addresses hosting multiple registered vehicles, exposing manager families running many entities from one office.
harm_angle: One office running a dozen lending vehicles means concentration that the entity-by-entity view completely hides.
caveat: Address strings need normalization; with only 212 rows the finding may be small even if real.

title: Closed End Fund Sponsor Clusters
idea: Ranked bars of shared addresses and city clusters among registered closed-end funds, showing which sponsors run whole families of funds.
harm_angle: Retail investors buying what look like independent funds are often buying many products from one sponsor with one set of incentives.
caveat: 973 rows; address normalization required and sponsor identity must be inferred rather than read directly.

title: Closed End Fund Registration Timeline
idea: Timeline of closed-end fund registrations by filing type, showing launch waves and which market conditions produced them.
harm_angle: Fund launch waves at market peaks are the products retail savers buy right before they lose money.
caveat: 973 rows; filing_date is text-cast and coverage window is unstated.

title: Fund Geography Versus Investor Geography
idea: Map of registered closed-end funds by state, an intentionally lopsided map showing the sector lives in three states.
harm_angle: Products sold to savers nationwide are designed and governed in a handful of places with no local accountability.
caveat: Address is the registrant's, not the investor base's; the contrast is implied rather than shown by this source alone.

title: Filer Industry Mix Q1 2024
idea: Ranked bars of quarterly financial-statement filers by industry code, showing which sectors dominate the public markets that quarter.
harm_angle: Which industries are publicly traded determines which industries face any public disclosure at all.
caveat: 6,028 rows for one quarter; SIC codes are self-selected and often stale.

title: Incorporated Elsewhere Operated Here
idea: Flow diagram from state of incorporation to state of business address, showing how many companies operating in one state are chartered in Delaware or offshore.
harm_angle: Chartering elsewhere lets a company operating in your town answer to another state's corporate law and courts.
caveat: The country fields are wrongly cast to numbers in this model and will null out; the state fields remain usable.

title: Filing Lateness Distribution
idea: Distribution of the gap between period end and filing date by filer size category, showing which filers habitually file at the wire.
harm_angle: Late financial disclosure is a warning sign that employees and pensioners typically learn about only after the fact.
caveat: period and filed are passed through uncast and may be text; filer-size codes are undocumented in the model.

title: Former Names Trail Q2 2024
idea: Ranked bars of filers that reported a former name and the date it changed, surfacing companies that recently rebranded.
harm_angle: A company that changes its name after a scandal makes itself unsearchable to the people it harmed.
caveat: The former-name and changed fields may be blank for most rows; changed is uncast text.

title: Well Known Seasoned Issuer Split
idea: Ranked bars by industry of the share of filers flagged as well-known seasoned issuers, the class that gets the fastest-track registration.
harm_angle: Fast-track issuers face the least pre-review, so their disclosures get the least scrutiny before the public buys.
caveat: Flag vocabulary undocumented; one-quarter snapshot only.

title: Business Versus Mailing Address Divergence
idea: Ranked bars of filers whose business and mailing addresses are in different states or countries, mapping the paper-headquarters pattern.
harm_angle: A registered agent's mailbox standing in for a headquarters is how service of process and accountability get slowed down.
caveat: Country fields are wrongly numeric-cast in this model; the address fields themselves are free text needing normalization.

title: Multi Registrant Filings Q3 2024
idea: Distribution of filings by the number of co-registrant companies on them, exposing single filings that cover dozens of legal entities at once.
harm_angle: A single filing covering forty subsidiaries is forty entities whose individual conduct nobody can isolate.
caveat: nciks and aciks are passed through uncast; the co-registrant list is a packed string needing parsing.

title: Detail Level Of Disclosure
idea: Ranked bars by industry and filer size of whether filings carry detailed tagged data or only summary level, showing who discloses the least.
harm_angle: Companies filing only summary-level data are companies whose numbers cannot be automatically compared to their peers.
caveat: detail flag vocabulary is undocumented in the model; single-quarter snapshot.

title: Fiscal Year End Clustering
idea: Distribution of fiscal year end dates across filers by industry, showing the industries that deliberately avoid the December reporting crowd.
harm_angle: Off-cycle year ends bury results in quiet news weeks, which is a small but real way to reduce scrutiny.
caveat: fye is a four-character code passed through uncast; one quarter of filers only.

title: Filing-deadline crush calendar
idea: Plot every filing by the day it was filed against its period-end date. Viewers see the wall of filings landing in the last 48 hours before each deadline, and the stragglers filing weeks late.
harm_angle: Late and bunched filings are the window where investors and workers are flying blind about a company's real condition.
caveat: FILED and PERIOD may be text in YYYYMMDD form; the epoch trap applies if cast naively.

title: Incorporated there operating here
idea: Sankey from state of incorporation to state of the business address. The Delaware ribbon should swamp everything, showing how many companies answer to a legal home they do not physically occupy.
harm_angle: Communities host the payroll and the pollution while legal accountability sits in a state they have no vote in.
caveat: STPRINC may be blank for foreign filers; COUNTRYINC was cast to a number which suggests it holds a code not a name.

title: Who is allowed to say less
idea: Ranked bars of filer-status class against how many filings are detail-tagged versus summary only. Shows which size class of company routinely discloses the least machine-readable detail.
harm_angle: Filers with the thinnest disclosure are the hardest for the public to scrutinise, which is where problems hide longest.
caveat: AFS coding scheme unknown from metadata; DETAIL may be a 0/1 flag or text.

title: Industry mix of the filing quarter
idea: Ranked bars of filer counts by SIC industry code for the quarter, with the tail of one-off industries left visible rather than lumped into other.
harm_angle: Shows which industries the public record actually covers and which barely appear at all.
caveat: SIC may be blank for many filers; needs an SIC-to-plain-English lookup that may not exist on the platform.

title: The amended-filing repeat offenders
idea: Scatter of companies by how many of their filings are flagged as previously reported versus their total filings, with names on the outliers.
harm_angle: Companies that keep restating what they already told the public are the ones whose numbers should never be taken at face value.
caveat: PREVRPT semantics unverified; within a single quarter per-company counts may be too small to mean anything.

title: Corporate headquarters density map
idea: Point map of every filer's business city, sized by how many filings the city produced. Shows the handful of metros that host almost all US public companies.
harm_angle: Capital concentrates in a few zip codes while the harm from those companies is spread everywhere else.
caveat: City/state text needs geocoding; no lat/long in the model.

title: Mailing address versus street address
idea: Dot plot of filers whose mailing state differs from their business state, grouped by industry. Flags the registered-agent and mail-drop pattern.
harm_angle: A company reachable only through a mail drop is a company that is hard for a harmed person to serve papers on.
caveat: Mailing address is often just a corporate secretary and may be innocuous; needs a plausibility filter.

title: Fiscal year ends off the calendar
idea: Distribution of fiscal-year-end month across filers, industry by industry. Reveals which sectors deliberately close their books away from December.
harm_angle: Off-cycle books make cross-company comparison harder for anyone watching from outside.
caveat: FYE is likely an MMDD text code; industries with few filers will be noisy.

title: Filings with multiple registrants
idea: Ranked bars of filings listing more than one CIK, showing the corporate groups that file as a bundle rather than as separate companies.
harm_angle: Bundled filers make it hard to see which specific legal entity is responsible for a given harm.
caveat: ACIKS is likely a delimited list needing parsing; NCIKS may be almost always 1.

title: Form-type mix over the quarter
idea: Timeline of filings by form type across the quarter, stacked, so the annual-report wave and the event-driven filings separate visually.
harm_angle: Establishes the baseline rhythm of disclosure so gaps and silences become visible.
caveat: FILED date parsing unverified.

title: Companies that changed their name
idea: Dot plot of filers with a former-name entry and the date it changed, ordered by recency. Name changes often follow scandals or restructurings.
harm_angle: A renamed company is harder for the public to connect to its own past record.
caveat: FORMER may be sparsely populated; CHANGED date format unverified.

title: Foreign-incorporated US filers
idea: Ranked bars of country of incorporation for filers whose business address is in the US, isolating the offshore-domiciled slice.
harm_angle: Offshore incorporation is the standard route for putting assets beyond the reach of US claimants.
caveat: COUNTRYINC was cast with try_to_number which strongly suggests a code, and it may be mostly null for domestic filers.

title: Well-known seasoned issuer club
idea: Distribution of the well-known-seasoned-issuer flag by industry, showing which sectors get the lightest-touch registration path.
harm_angle: The lightest disclosure burden goes to the biggest players, the ones whose failures hurt the most people.
caveat: WKSI may be Y/N text or 0/1; SIC blanks will distort industry shares.

title: Acceptance lag after the deadline bell
idea: Distribution of the gap between when a filing was accepted and when it was filed, split by form type. The long tail is where processing friction lives.
harm_angle: Filings stuck in processing are filings the public cannot read yet.
caveat: ACCEPTED and FILED are both untyped text here and may need timestamp parsing that fails.

title: EIN reuse across registrants
idea: Network of employer-ID numbers shared by more than one CIK, exposing sibling entities filing under a common tax identity.
harm_angle: Shared tax identities let a corporate family present itself as unrelated separate companies.
caveat: EIN is a documented masking trap on this platform; confirm distinct-count and value shape before trusting it.

title: Newest quarter filer roll call
idea: Ranked bars of filers by industry for the most recent quarter, as the current-state snapshot of who is in the public-company universe.
harm_angle: Baseline of who is currently accountable to public disclosure at all.
caveat: Partial quarter coverage likely; the lower row count may be recency rather than decline.

title: Zip-code clustering of registrants
idea: Map of filer business zip codes shaded by count, to expose the specific office towers and registered-agent addresses hosting dozens of filers.
harm_angle: A single address hosting dozens of companies is a shell-structure signature worth a reporter's time.
caveat: ZIPBA formatting inconsistent (5 vs 9 digit); BAS1 street text needs normalising to find shared addresses.

title: Filer size class against industry
idea: Heatmap grid of filer-status class by industry, showing which sectors are dominated by large accelerated filers and which by the smallest reporting companies.
harm_angle: Shows where the public record is thinnest by design.
caveat: AFS code meanings unknown from metadata alone.

title: Companies with many tickers
idea: Ranked bars of CIKs carrying more than one ticker, revealing dual-class share structures and multi-listed entities behind a single legal company.
harm_angle: Dual-class structures are how founders keep control while outside shareholders carry the risk.
caveat: Grain is (CIK, ticker) so multiplicity is expected; care needed not to read routine share classes as anomalies.

title: Exchange market-share snapshot
idea: Ranked bars of listing counts by exchange, showing how concentrated US listings are on two venues.
harm_angle: Venue concentration means a few private gatekeepers decide who gets access to public capital.
caveat: EXCHANGE may be blank for some rows; snapshot only, no history.

title: Same name different companies
idea: Cluster view of near-identical company names attached to different CIKs, exposing lookalike naming across the registry.
harm_angle: Lookalike corporate names confuse investors and complicate holding the right entity responsible.
caveat: Needs fuzzy name matching; false positives from common words like Capital and Holdings are certain.

title: The ticker alphabet
idea: Distribution of ticker length and first letter by exchange, a light reference chart establishing what a normal listing symbol looks like.
harm_angle: Reference-only floor chart; establishes the shape of the listing universe.
caveat: Genuinely descriptive with no direct harm angle.

title: Fund families ranked by share classes
idea: Ranked bars of registrants by how many share classes they operate. The top of this chart is the handful of firms holding most Americans' retirement money.
harm_angle: A few fund complexes sit between ordinary savers and the entire market; concentration there is systemic risk.
caveat: cik_number is text-trimmed not cast to number; needs normalising before joining to other SEC data.

title: Classes per fund distribution
idea: Distribution of how many share classes each series carries. The long right tail is funds sliced into a dozen fee tiers for different buyer types.
harm_angle: More share classes usually means the same portfolio sold at very different fee levels, and small savers land in the expensive tiers.
caveat: Fee levels are not in this table; the chart implies but cannot prove the fee spread.

title: Where the fund industry sits
idea: Map of registrant addresses by state and city, sized by classes managed. Concentration in a few metros should be stark.
harm_angle: Shows how few places control the savings infrastructure most households depend on.
caveat: Address is the registrant's filing address, which may be a service agent rather than a real office.

title: Unticketed share classes
idea: Ranked bars of fund families by the share of their classes carrying no public ticker, isolating the classes ordinary buyers cannot see quoted.
harm_angle: Classes with no public quote are typically sold through intermediaries, where the buyer never comparison-shops.
caveat: class_ticker blank may simply mean not-yet-issued; blank-vs-null semantics unverified.

title: Who advises the cash funds
idea: Ranked bars of investment advisors by number of money-market share classes, exposing how few firms manage the nation's parked cash.
harm_angle: Money-market funds are where households and small businesses park emergency cash; one advisor stumbling hits everyone at once.
caveat: Advisor names are free text needing deduplication across spelling variants.

title: Sub-advisor hidden layer
idea: Network linking registrant to advisor to sub-advisor, showing the second layer of managers most fund buyers never learn about.
harm_angle: The firm actually picking the assets is often not the firm whose name is on the fund.
caveat: SUB_ADVISOR likely blank for most rows; small table (1,206 rows) so the graph may be sparse.

title: Fund category mix by month
idea: Timeline of share-class counts by fund category across report months, showing shifts between government, prime and tax-exempt cash funds.
harm_angle: Migration between categories is the early tell of short-term funding stress that ordinary depositors never see coming.
caveat: REPORTMONTH is untyped text; coverage window unknown and may be a single month.

title: One advisor many registrants
idea: Dot plot of advisors against the number of distinct registrant CIKs they serve, flagging advisors spread across many legal fund shells.
harm_angle: One manager behind many nominally separate funds concentrates risk that looks diversified on paper.
caveat: Small table; advisor name variants may split or merge counts incorrectly.

title: Cost of borrowing by security type
idea: Small multiples of average interest rate over time, one panel per security type, so the divergence between bills, notes and savings bonds is visible.
harm_angle: Rising debt service crowds out the budget lines that fund public services.
caveat: Pure macro series - no direct human subject without pairing to spending data.

title: The small saver's return versus the market's
idea: Timeline of the average rate on savings-bond style securities against marketable debt, showing the gap between what small savers and institutions earn.
harm_angle: Ordinary savers holding government paper may be systematically earning less than institutions.
caveat: Security descriptions need careful grouping; no inflation series here to compute real returns.

title: Rate regimes as a heat strip
idea: Heatmap grid of security type rows against month columns with color as rate, giving one image of every rate regime since the series began.
harm_angle: Regime shifts precede the mortgage and credit costs households actually feel.
caveat: Series start dates differ by security type leaving ragged edges.

title: Public versus intragovernmental debt split
idea: Stacked timeline of debt held by the public against intragovernmental holdings with the percentage lines, showing the changing composition rather than just the scary total.
harm_angle: Intragovernmental holdings are largely the trust funds people's benefits depend on.
caveat: Daily series with no per-capita or GDP denominator in this table.

title: Debt-ceiling flatlines
idea: Timeline zoomed to show the flat plateaus where total debt sits pinned at a ceiling before jumping. The plateaus are the standoffs.
harm_angle: Debt-ceiling standoffs delay payments people are counting on.
caveat: Identifying a plateau as a ceiling standoff requires external context not in the table.

title: Fiscal year-end borrowing spikes
idea: Cohort grid of day-of-fiscal-year against fiscal year with color as daily change in total debt, exposing the recurring end-of-year pattern.
harm_angle: Predictable borrowing spikes are a budgeting artefact, not a crisis, and framing matters for public policy.
caveat: Daily deltas are noisy around holidays and settlement days.

title: Illicit flows in and out by country
idea: Diverging ranked bars of inflow versus outflow value per country, showing which economies are drained and which absorb.
harm_angle: Money leaving a poor country through misinvoicing is public revenue that never funds its hospitals.
caveat: Only 25 rows and the country column is cast to a number in the model, so country labels may be unusable.

title: Illicit flow trend where series exist
idea: Timeline of estimated illicit flow value by direction for whichever countries have multiple years.
harm_angle: Growing outflows mean widening gaps in the budgets that pay for schools and clinics.
caveat: 25 rows total - almost certainly too thin for a trend. Genuinely thin source; two ideas is the ceiling.

title: Trading venues by country
idea: Map of market identifier codes by country, sized by venue count, showing where the world's trading infrastructure is registered.
harm_angle: Where venues register determines whose regulator, if anyone, watches the trades that move prices people's pensions depend on.
caveat: Small registry (2,864 rows) and country is the registration country, not necessarily where the matching engine runs.

title: Venues that quietly expired
idea: Timeline of venue creation against expiry dates, showing the churn of trading venues that opened and shut within a few years.
harm_angle: Short-lived venues are where thinly regulated trading happens and then disappears before anyone reviews it.
caveat: Dates parsed with a fixed YYYYMMDD format; expiry is null for live venues by design.

title: Operators running many segments
idea: Ranked bars of operating MICs by how many segment MICs sit under them, showing the groups that run whole families of venues under one roof.
harm_angle: A single operator running dozens of venue segments concentrates market power behind what looks like competition.
caveat: LEI population in this registry is unverified and may be sparse.

title: Canada's regulated institution register
idea: Ranked bars of institutions by type and industry, the plain roll call of who OSFI actually supervises.
harm_angle: Reference floor: anyone not on this list is a financial firm nobody federally supervises.
caveat: Only 343 rows; a snapshot with no dates, so no trend is possible.

title: Foreign banks operating in Canada
idea: Dot plot separating institutions whose Canadian trade name differs from their legal company name, isolating the foreign-parented operations.
harm_angle: Customers deal with a friendly local trade name while the balance sheet and the decisions sit in another country.
caveat: Trade-name field may be null for domestic institutions, and the count of true foreign parents is unverified.

title: Insurance classes authorised
idea: Heatmap grid of insurer against authorised insurance classes, showing which risks each licensed insurer is actually allowed to write.
harm_angle: Gaps in who is licensed to write a class of risk are gaps in who can get covered at all.
caveat: Insurance classes is a delimited free-text list needing splitting; likely null for banks.

idea: Map all 77,514 licensees by their premise coordinates, colored by lic_type. Viewer sees dealer concentration relative to population.
harm_angle: Dealer density is one of the strongest correlates of local gun-trace volume - it maps onto who gets shot.

chart_shape: map plus ranked bars by state
harm_angle: Residential dealers are the hardest for ATF to inspect and a known diversion channel.

title: License Type Mix by State
idea: Heatmap of lic_type against state. Viewer sees which states host manufacturers and importers versus retail dealers.
harm_angle: Where guns are made and imported determines where they enter the illegal market.
caveat: lic_type codes need the ATF codebook to be readable.

title: Same Person Many Licenses
idea: Group by license_name and business_name to find operators holding multiple FFLs across districts.
harm_angle: Multi-license operators can move inventory between entities in ways a single-license inspection never sees.
caveat: Name matching across a snapshot will merge distinct people with common names.

title: What the world's food statistics actually cover
idea: Ranked bars of datasets by row count grouped by topic, showing which parts of the food system are richly measured and which are thin.
harm_angle: Under-measured parts of the food system are where hunger goes unnoticed.

harm_angle: A stale hunger statistic means decision-makers are steering with old numbers.

source_names: FAOSTAT Suite of Food Security Indicators
title: Countries going backwards on hunger
idea: Slope chart of undernourishment prevalence from a decade ago to the latest year, showing only the countries that got worse.
harm_angle: Reversal means more people are hungry now than were a decade ago.
caveat: Data flags mark estimated versus reported values and should be shown; year coverage varies by country.

source_names: FAOSTAT Suite of Food Security Indicators
title: Severe versus moderate food insecurity gap
idea: Scatter of severe food-insecurity prevalence against moderate-or-severe, one dot per country-year, where distance from the diagonal shows how deep the insecurity runs.
harm_angle: Countries deep in severe insecurity have households skipping whole days of food.
caveat: The two indicators are separate item rows and must be pivoted; some countries report only one.

source_names: FAOSTAT Suite of Food Security Indicators
title: Estimated versus measured hunger numbers
idea: Distribution of the data-flag values across countries and years, showing how much of the world's hunger statistic is modelled rather than surveyed.
harm_angle: Modelled hunger figures can hide fast-moving crises in the countries least able to survey.
caveat: Flag coding needs the publisher's legend to interpret correctly.

title: Famine phase populations by country
idea: Stacked ranked bars of population in each phase per country, with the famine phase broken out on top so the catastrophic slice is unmissable.
harm_angle: Phase 5 is people actually starving to death right now.
caveat: Country column is cast to a number in the model so labels may be broken; the 735-row landing looks national-level only, not admin1 or area.

title: Current versus projected deterioration
idea: Slope chart per country from the current-period population in crisis phases to the projected-period figure, showing where things are officially expected to get worse.
harm_angle: An official projection of deterioration is a warning that goes unheeded until people die.
caveat: Current versus projection is encoded in validity_period text and must be parsed reliably.

title: Share of a nation in crisis
idea: Dot plot of the percentage of population in phase 3 or worse, sorted, so countries with a majority of citizens in crisis sit at the top.
harm_angle: When most of a country is in food crisis, the state has stopped being able to feed its people.
caveat: Percentages are of the analysed population which may not equal the whole country.

title: How stale the famine assessments are
idea: Timeline dot plot of date of analysis per country, showing which crises have not been assessed for a long time.
harm_angle: An unassessed crisis gets no aid appeal and no attention.
caveat: Absence of a recent analysis may mean access denial rather than improvement.

title: Promised Versus Delivered Aid
idea: Per country and fiscal year, plot obligation_amount against disbursement_amount. Viewer sees countries where aid is announced repeatedly but never lands.
chart_shape: scatter with reference line plus country ranking
harm_angle: Announced aid that never disburses leaves people relying on services that were never funded.
caveat: Amount fields are untyped passthroughs; obligations and disbursements can legitimately lag across fiscal years.

title: Aid Sector Mix by Country
idea: Stacked shares of usg_sector and dac_category per country over time. Viewer sees which countries get health and food aid and which get mostly security assistance.
harm_angle: Security-heavy aid mixes often mean the population sees weapons before it sees clinics.
caveat: Sector taxonomies changed over the years; categories may not be comparable across the full span.

title: Which Agency Runs Which Country
idea: Heatmap of managing_agency against country, colored by dollars. Viewer sees countries where the aid relationship is run by defense rather than development agencies.
harm_angle: Who administers the aid determines whose interests it serves on the ground.
caveat: Agency naming may vary across years and needs normalization.

title: Aid Whiplash Timeline
idea: Timeline of each country total obligations with year-over-year swings highlighted. Viewer sees countries whose aid gets cut off abruptly for political reasons.
harm_angle: Abrupt aid cutoffs shutter clinics and schools mid-year with no wind-down.
caveat: Fiscal-year text field may need casting; mixing transaction_type values could double-count.

title: Who votes with whom
idea: Network of country pairs weighted by voting agreement, per decade, showing bloc formation and collapse.
harm_angle: Voting blocs decide which populations get UN protection and which get ignored.
caveat: 1.8M dyad-year rows; must be aggregated before any layout is possible.

title: Ideal-point drift over 70 years
idea: Timeline of country ideal points, small multiples, showing which states drifted away from the Western bloc and when.
harm_angle: Realignment predicts which countries stop being shielded by great-power sponsors.
caveat: Dyadic grain means ideal points repeat across rows; must be deduplicated per country-year.

title: The isolation index
idea: Ranked bars of countries by average distance from the global median ideal point per decade, naming the most isolated states.
harm_angle: Isolated states face sanctions whose cost lands on their civilians, not their leaders.
caveat: Country codes are Correlates-of-War codes and need a crosswalk to be readable.

title: Agreement collapse heatmap
idea: Heatmap grid of major-power pairs by year shaded by agreement rate, showing the exact years cooperation broke.
harm_angle: When great powers stop agreeing, humanitarian resolutions stall and civilians pay.
caveat: col_0 is an unnamed index column; row grain should be confirmed as one row per dyad-year.

title: Species Coverage Imbalance
idea: Ranked bars of annotated feature counts per species and assembly. Viewer sees how lopsided genomic reference coverage is across the tree of life.
harm_angle: Species and populations with thin reference data get worse diagnostics and worse conservation decisions.
caveat: Only 643 rows - an API probe sample, not the Ensembl corpus; cannot support coverage claims.

title: Variant Consequence Mix
idea: Distribution of consequence_type across biotypes, to show what fraction of catalogued variants are predicted damaging versus silent.
harm_angle: Variant interpretation gaps are the reason genetic tests come back inconclusive more often for under-studied ancestries.
caveat: 643-row sample; population_name is cast to a double which strongly suggests the column is mis-typed or empty.

title: A century of mapping coverage
idea: Timeline of map publication dates by state, showing when each part of the country was last surveyed at scale.
harm_angle: Places last mapped decades ago are the places federal attention left.
caveat: publicationdate is left as raw text (not date-cast) in the model; 250 rows is a sample.

title: Map scale by place
idea: Heatmap grid of state by map scale, revealing which regions only ever got coarse coverage.
harm_angle: Coarse-only mapping means worse flood, hazard and land-rights records for those residents.
caveat: 250-row sample; counties is number-cast over what may be a name list, likely nulling.

title: The vanishing place names
idea: Dot plot of historical map titles whose place names no longer appear in modern records, an archaeology of erased towns.
harm_angle: Erased towns are often Black, Indigenous or company towns that were displaced and unrecorded.
caveat: Requires a modern gazetteer to compare against; not present in this table.

title: Conflict versus cooperation map
idea: Point map of events by action location colored by quad class (verbal or material, cooperation or conflict), sized by article count.
harm_angle: Locates where in the world coercion is happening and how much attention it gets.
caveat: 1015 rows is a tiny slice of one 15-minute file, not the real GDELT corpus.

title: Attention gap: severity vs coverage
idea: Scatter of event severity score against number of articles, with the far-severe low-coverage quadrant labeled as the underreported events.
harm_angle: Severe events with near-zero coverage are the harms nobody will ever be held to account for.
caveat: Sample slice; goldsteinscale is a coded scale, not a harm measure, so severity is a proxy at best.

title: Who acts on whom
idea: Network of actor1 to actor2 by country code, edge width by event count, colored by conflict tone.
harm_angle: Maps which states and organizations repeatedly act against which populations.
caveat: Country code columns are number-cast over alpha codes, which will null them out entirely.

title: Tone of coverage by region
idea: Heatmap grid of region by event root code shaded by average media tone, exposing where reporting is systematically harsher.
harm_angle: Systematically negative framing of one region shapes the policy that region's people live under.
caveat: Tone is a media artifact, not ground truth; sample slice cannot support a global claim.

title: Source concentration per event
idea: Distribution of distinct sources per event, showing how many world events are known only through a single outlet.
harm_angle: Single-source events are the ones most easily denied or disappeared.
caveat: Tiny sample; numsources semantics are GDELT-specific.

title: Corruption score trajectories
idea: Small multiples of CPI by country over time, grouped by region, showing which states cleaned up and which rotted.
harm_angle: Corruption is a tax paid disproportionately by people who cannot afford to bribe.
caveat: CPI methodology changed over time; long-run comparisons across the break are questionable.

title: Biggest movers both ways
idea: Slope chart of CPI from earliest to latest year, ranked, naming the sharpest improvements and collapses.
harm_angle: Sharp corruption collapses usually track a specific political event with immediate cost to residents.
caveat: Requires both endpoint years present; aggregates must be filtered.

title: Regional convergence grid
idea: Heatmap grid of country by year shaded by CPI, faceted by region, revealing whether corruption is regionally contagious.
harm_angle: Regional corruption clusters mean cross-border harms with no clean jurisdiction to appeal to.
caveat: CPI is a perceptions index, not a measure of actual corruption -- always caveat.

title: Who chairs what
idea: Network of members to committees, with chairs highlighted, showing the concentration of gavels in a few hands.
harm_angle: Committee chairs decide which harms get a hearing and which never reach the floor.
caveat: Snapshot only -- no date column, so this is a current-Congress still frame with no history.

title: Seat load per member
idea: Ranked bars of committee and subcommittee assignments per member, showing who is stretched across everything and who has one quiet seat.
harm_angle: Members overloaded across many panels cannot scrutinize any of them properly.
caveat: No date column; is_subcommittee flag semantics unverified.

title: Party control of the gavels
idea: Heatmap grid of committee by party share of seats, with chair party marked, showing where the majority's grip is tightest.
harm_angle: The panels with the most lopsided control are where oversight quietly dies.
caveat: Snapshot grain; party may be blank for independents.

title: The overlap web
idea: Network of committees linked by shared members, revealing which panels are effectively the same room of people.
harm_angle: Overlapping membership means a single bloc can shape several policy areas at once.
caveat: Snapshot only; 3879 rows may include stale or duplicated assignments.

title: Two centuries of who serves
idea: Timeline of Congress composition by gender and party across all terms, the demographic history of the institution.
harm_angle: Shows how long the people making the laws looked nothing like the people living under them.
caveat: term_start and term_end are not date-cast in the model, so they may be text and need parsing.

title: Tenure distribution by chamber
idea: Distribution of number of terms served, split House versus Senate, showing how entrenched incumbency actually is.
harm_angle: Long incumbency without turnover means constituents cannot dislodge a member who stops representing them.
caveat: n_terms derivation unknown; historical members may inflate the tail.

title: The ID crosswalk completeness map
idea: Heatmap grid of member by identifier system shaded by whether that ID exists, exposing which members are invisible to which accountability datasets.
harm_angle: Members missing from money or vote datasets are members who cannot be tracked by watchdogs.
caveat: IDs may be sentinel-blank strings rather than nulls -- must check distinct values before trusting fill rates.

title: Age of Congress over time
idea: Timeline of median member age at term start by chamber, computed from birthday, showing the institution aging away from its electorate.
harm_angle: An aging legislature legislates on housing, debt and climate it will not live to experience.
caveat: birthday is not date-cast; historical birthdays may be partial or missing.

title: State delegation churn
idea: Small multiples by state of member turnover per decade, showing which states recycle the same families and which churn.
harm_angle: Low-churn states concentrate power in a handful of political families for generations.
caveat: Requires clean term dates; district is text and may include at-large codes.

title: Industry to agency flow
idea: Flow diagram from industry sector to federal agency, width by number of appointees, showing which industries staff which regulators.
harm_angle: Regulators staffed by the industry they police do not protect the people that industry harms.
caveat: 406 rows and a snapshot grain -- no time axis, so this is one administration's still frame.

title: Multi-sector appointees
idea: Ranked bars of appointees by count of distinct industry ties, surfacing the people with the widest web of corporate connections.
harm_angle: Appointees with many industry ties have many conflicts across the areas they oversee.
caveat: sector_count is derived; the wide sector1..16 layout suggests messy source data underneath.

title: Which agencies are most captured
idea: Ranked bars of agencies by share of positions flagged revolving-door or political-appointee, a capture index by agency.
harm_angle: The most-captured agencies are where enforcement quietly stops for the people it should protect.
caveat: Flags are derived from free-text position_type matching; misclassification is likely.

title: Sector-agency network
idea: Network of sectors and agencies linked through shared individuals, showing clusters where a whole policy area is one industry's staffing pipeline.
harm_angle: Clustered capture means an entire policy domain has no independent voice inside it.
caveat: 406 rows; person_name is the only identifier, so the same person under name variants may split.

title: The polarization fan
idea: Timeline of party ideology medians by congress and chamber, the canonical widening-gap chart back to 1789.
harm_angle: A polarized Congress cannot pass the bills that address slow-moving harms.
caveat: 51k member-congress rows; party_code needs a lookup to be readable.

title: The vanishing moderates
idea: Distribution of member ideology per congress as a ridgeline of small multiples, showing the middle emptying out decade by decade.
harm_angle: With no moderates, cross-party deals on health, housing and wages stop happening.
caveat: nominate_dim1 is text-typed in the model (no numeric cast) -- may need casting before plotting.

title: The second dimension's return
idea: Scatter of dim1 against dim2 by congress, animated, showing when race and region formed a second axis of division and when it collapsed.
harm_angle: The second dimension historically tracked civil-rights splits -- the axis on which people's rights were traded.
caveat: dim2 is noisy in modern congresses; interpretation is contested.

title: Members who drift
idea: Slope chart of individual members' ideology from first to last congress served, showing who moved and in which direction.
harm_angle: Members who drift away from their district's position after election are the ones constituents cannot hold to their pitch.
caveat: Requires at least two congresses per member; DW-NOMINATE constrains drift by construction, so movement may be understated.

title: Error rate versus extremity
idea: Scatter of the model's vote-prediction error count against member extremity, flagging members whose votes are least predictable.
harm_angle: Unpredictable members are the last remaining swing votes for anything that helps people.
caveat: Error counts are a model artifact, not a behavioral measure.

title: How close were the votes
idea: Distribution of yea-minus-nay margins per congress, showing whether Congress decides by landslide or by one vote.
harm_angle: One-vote margins mean a single member's choice decided a policy affecting millions.
caveat: date is untyped in the model; congress and chamber ordering should be used instead if parsing fails.

title: Procedural votes crowding out substance
idea: Timeline of the share of roll calls that are procedural versus substantive by congress, based on vote question text.
harm_angle: A chamber voting mostly on procedure is a chamber not voting on people's problems.
caveat: Requires classifying free-text vote_question; no stored procedural flag.

title: Voting volume collapse
idea: Timeline of roll-call counts per session by chamber, showing the long-run decline in how often Congress actually votes.
harm_angle: Fewer recorded votes means fewer moments a constituent can hold a member accountable.
caveat: 3364 rows suggests a subset of congresses, not the full 1789-present roll-call set.

title: Contested votes cluster on which bills
idea: Ranked bars of bills by number of near-tied roll calls, showing which measures were fought hardest.
harm_angle: The most-contested bills are usually the ones redistributing something real.
caveat: bill_number formatting may not join cleanly to the billstatus table.

title: Who skips the votes
idea: Ranked bars of missed-vote rate per member per congress, with the worst absentees named.
harm_angle: A member who does not show up leaves their district unrepresented on every one of those votes.
caveat: Missed votes depend on cast_code semantics (absent vs not-in-office); misreading the codes inverts the whole chart.

title: Vote-similarity clustering
idea: Network of members linked by how often they vote identically, laid out per congress, showing factions the party labels hide.
harm_angle: Hidden voting blocs are the real units deciding which harms get addressed.
caveat: 945k rows means the pairwise similarity matrix is expensive; must be pre-aggregated.

title: Party unity by member
idea: Distribution of party-unity scores by congress, showing which members defect and how often.
harm_angle: Defectors are the members whose constituents actually pull them off the party line.
caveat: Requires joining to roll-call metadata for the party majority position; not derivable from this table alone.

title: Prediction failures as conscience votes
idea: Scatter of the model's vote probability against actual cast, isolating the votes members cast against their own ideology.
harm_angle: Low-probability votes are the moments a member broke pattern -- often under pressure or on principle.
caveat: prob is a scaling artifact; treating it as conscience is interpretive.

title: Arms race trajectories
idea: Timeline of military expenditure by country, small multiples grouped by region, showing which rivalries are accelerating.
harm_angle: Money spent on arms is money not spent on the health and housing of the same population.
caveat: Regional aggregate rows tagged SIPRI must be filtered out or they dominate every chart.

title: Guns versus everything else
idea: Slope chart per country of military spending change against a social-spending or health measure change over the same window.
harm_angle: When defense budgets rise and clinics close, the tradeoff has a body count.
caveat: The social-spending side is not in this table; strictly this needs a second source.

title: Regional spending concentration
idea: Ranked bars of latest-year spending by country within each region, showing how one state dominates each neighborhood.
harm_angle: Smaller neighbors respond to a dominant spender by cutting domestic budgets to keep up.
caveat: Taiwan (TWN) presence is flagged as uncertain in the source notes -- verify before any China or Taiwan framing.

title: What appeared and what vanished
idea: Timeline of file links present at each snapshot, with disappearing links highlighted, showing what DOJ quietly pulled.
harm_angle: Documents that vanish from a public library are documents the public was meant to see and now cannot.
caveat: Needs multiple monthly snapshots in the table; if only one fetch exists, there is nothing to diff.

title: Publication burst pattern
idea: Timeline of link counts by page of origin over fetch dates, showing whether releases come in bursts around news events.
harm_angle: Release timing reveals whether disclosure is driven by law or by news cycle management.
caveat: 777 links across 12 dataset pages; snapshot cadence unverified.

title: Link text versus file reality
idea: Ranked bars of link-text patterns per page, exposing inconsistent or uninformative labeling that makes the library hard to search.
harm_angle: An unsearchable public archive is functionally a closed one for survivors and reporters.
caveat: Link text is free-form; grouping is judgment-heavy.

source_names: Wayback replay of DOJ deep pages
title: Deep Page Link Graph
idea: Network of page_url to resolved_url across all captures. Viewer sees the shape of the document set and which nodes were removed.
harm_angle: Mapping what was published is the only way to prove what was withdrawn.
caveat: 2,542 links only and a partial replay, so absence proves nothing on its own.

source_names: Wayback replay of DOJ deep pages
title: Capture Coverage Gaps
idea: Timeline of captures per page showing the intervals with no archive coverage at all.
harm_angle: Gaps in the archive are exactly where a change can be made unobserved.
caveat: Gaps reflect Wayback crawl behavior, not necessarily anything about DOJ.

source_names: Wayback replay of DOJ listing pages
title: Files That Vanished From DOJ
idea: Cohort grid of resolved_url against capture date. Viewer sees documents that were linked on a DOJ listing page at one capture and gone at the next.
chart_shape: cohort grid of URL against capture
harm_angle: Documents that quietly disappear from a public page are records the public was supposed to keep.
caveat: Absence from a later capture may mean pagination or a crawl gap rather than removal - needs care.

source_names: Wayback replay of DOJ listing pages
title: Page Churn Timeline
idea: Timeline of distinct page_digest values per page_url. Viewer sees the exact moments a public page content changed.
harm_angle: Silent edits to public records pages are undocumented changes to the public record.
caveat: Digest changes can be triggered by boilerplate, not substance.

source_names: Wayback replay of DOJ listing pages
title: Link Text Rewrites
idea: Track cases where the same resolved_url carries different link_text across captures. Viewer sees documents relabeled over time.
chart_shape: dot plot of URL against label variants
harm_angle: Relabeling a document changes what a reader thinks it contains without changing the file.
caveat: Whitespace and case noise will generate false variants unless normalized.

source_names: CDC Indicators of Anxiety or Depression
title: Which groups broke hardest
idea: Small multiples of the anxiety and depression indicator by subgroup over time periods, showing which demographic never recovered.
harm_angle: The subgroups that never returned to baseline are the ones the mental-health system failed.
caveat: Household Pulse survey grain; wide confidence intervals on small subgroups can make differences meaningless.

source_names: CDC Indicators of Anxiety or Depression
title: State mental-health map over time
idea: Animated state map shaded by the indicator value per time period, showing the geography of distress.
harm_angle: Locates where people are in distress and whether services followed.
caveat: State rows may be a separate c_group from the demographic breakdowns; mixing them double counts.

source_names: CDC Indicators of Anxiety or Depression
title: Confidence interval width as data quality
idea: Dot plot of each subgroup by CI width, showing which populations the survey measures worst.
harm_angle: Populations measured with huge error bars are populations policymakers can safely ignore.
caveat: CI columns may be text; width must be derived.

source_names: CDC Indicators of Anxiety or Depression
title: Survey phase breaks
idea: Timeline of the indicator with phase boundaries marked, exposing where methodology changes create false trend breaks.
harm_angle: A methodology break misread as a real improvement lets an agency claim progress that did not happen.
caveat: Phase change dates and their methodological meaning are not documented in the table.

title: What CDC measures and where
idea: Heatmap grid of topic by state shaded by how many indicators exist, exposing the states and topics with almost no public health data.
harm_angle: States with thin data cannot be held to account for outcomes nobody measures.
caveat: 15000 rows is a portal sample; gaps may reflect the crawl rather than real coverage.

title: Stale datasets
idea: Dot plot of dataset by last-updated date, ranked, showing which public health series CDC quietly stopped updating.
harm_angle: An abandoned surveillance series means an ongoing harm stops being counted.
caveat: updated_at may be a crawl timestamp rather than a true dataset refresh date.

title: Indicator coverage by year
idea: Timeline of distinct indicators reported per year, showing whether public health measurement expanded or contracted.
harm_angle: Contraction in what gets measured is contraction in what gets funded.
caveat: Sample of the portal; year fill rate unverified.

title: Zip-level coverage rarity
idea: Map of which geographies have any zip-level indicator at all, showing that almost all public health data stops at the state line.
harm_angle: State-level-only data hides the neighborhood where the harm actually concentrates.
caveat: zip_code fill rate is very likely near zero; this may end up a coverage-gap finding rather than a map.

source_names: NCHS Drug Poisoning Mortality by County
title: The overdose map by county
idea: County choropleth of age-adjusted drug poisoning death rate for the latest year, the base geography of the overdose crisis.
harm_angle: Counties in the top rate band are where families are burying people fastest.
caveat: The rate column is banded into 11 categories as ranges, not a continuous number -- it must be treated as ordinal.

source_names: NCHS Drug Poisoning Mortality by County
title: Counties that never came down
idea: Small multiples by state of county rate bands over time, highlighting counties stuck in the worst band every single year.
harm_angle: Counties permanently in the top band are places where a decade of federal response changed nothing.
caveat: Banded rates mean small real changes are invisible; band boundaries may shift across editions.

source_names: NCHS Drug Poisoning Mortality by County
title: Rural versus metro divergence
idea: Dot plot of county rate bands split by county population size, testing whether small counties are worse off.
harm_angle: Rural counties with no treatment capacity carry the highest death rates and the least help.
caveat: Population is a county total, not a rurality classification; rurality must be approximated.

source_names: NCHS Drug Poisoning Mortality by County
title: The band-shift cohort grid
idea: Cohort grid of counties by their starting band and their ending band, showing how many counties improved, held, or fell.
harm_angle: Counting counties that got worse over a decade is the plainest measure of national failure.
caveat: Requires consistent band definitions across years -- if the bands were redefined, the grid is meaningless.

source_names: CDC Indicators of Health Insurance Coverage
title: Uninsured by subgroup
idea: Small multiples of the uninsured indicator by demographic subgroup over time periods, showing who loses coverage first.
harm_angle: The subgroups losing coverage fastest are the ones who will skip care and show up in an ER later.
caveat: Household Pulse survey; suppression_flag and wide CIs limit small-subgroup claims.

source_names: CDC Indicators of Health Insurance Coverage
title: Coverage map over time
idea: Animated state map shaded by uninsured rate per time period, revealing the expansion versus non-expansion split.
harm_angle: Non-expansion states leave a permanent uninsured population with no route to care.
caveat: Medicaid expansion status is not in this table; the split must be labeled from outside knowledge.

source_names: CDC Indicators of Health Insurance Coverage
title: Where the data is suppressed
idea: Heatmap grid of subgroup by time period shaded by suppression, showing which populations are chronically too small to count.
harm_angle: Chronically suppressed groups are invisible in every coverage debate about them.
caveat: suppression_flag values and meaning unverified.

source_names: CDC Indicators of Health Insurance Coverage
title: Quartile churn
idea: Slope chart of states moving between coverage quartiles from first to last period, ranking the biggest movers.
harm_angle: States dropping quartiles are states where people actively lost coverage during the window.
caveat: quartile_number derivation is CDC-internal; comparability across periods unverified.

source_names: CDC Injury, Overdose and Violence — County
title: County injury death rate map
idea: Choropleth of county-level rate by intent for the latest period showing which counties carry the heaviest injury and violence death burden.
harm_angle: Residents of counties with the highest violent and overdose death rates are invisible in state-level reporting.
caveat: Period field may be a text label rather than a parseable date; rate may be suppressed in small counties.

source_names: CDC Injury, Overdose and Violence — County
title: Suppression is its own map
idea: Map counties where the count is suppressed rather than reported and show that the data blackout clusters in small rural and tribal-adjacent counties.
harm_angle: Rural residents get no published injury statistics at all so their harm never enters the national conversation.
caveat: Depends on count_sup actually encoding suppression rather than a plain count; unverified.

source_names: CDC Injury, Overdose and Violence — County
title: Intent mix by state
idea: Small multiples of the share of injury deaths by intent (homicide vs suicide vs unintentional) for each state's counties to show states with radically different violence profiles.
harm_angle: Shows which states' residents die by other people's hands versus their own — different policy failures entirely.
caveat: Intent categories unknown until inspected; may be only two or three values.

source_names: CDC Injury, Overdose and Violence — County
title: Widest confidence intervals ranked
idea: Dot plot of counties ranked by the width of the rate confidence interval to expose where the official numbers are statistically almost meaningless.
harm_angle: Counties with unusable estimates get excluded from funding formulas that rely on measured need.
caveat: rate_m_ci may be a half-width or a bound; interpretation unverified.

source_names: CDC Injury, Overdose and Violence — County
title: Rate drift across periods
idea: Slope chart of county rates between the earliest and latest period highlighting counties that got sharply worse while the national trend improved.
harm_angle: Counties quietly deteriorating against a improving national average are the ones nobody is watching.
caveat: Requires multiple comparable periods; period may be a rolling twelve-month window that overlaps.

source_names: NCHS Leading Causes of Death by State
title: Death Rate Gap Between States
idea: Slope chart from 1999 to 2017 of the age-adjusted death rate per state for a chosen cause, showing states that improved against states that got worse.
harm_angle: Two people with the same disease die at different rates depending on which state line they live behind.
caveat: The table includes a United States rollup row per year and cause that must be excluded from state rankings or it distorts everything.

source_names: NCHS Leading Causes of Death by State
title: Cause Mix Shift Over Two Decades
idea: Small multiples per state of cause share over 1999 to 2017, showing where drug and suicide deaths displaced heart disease in the ranking.
harm_angle: The changing cause mix names which crisis a state failed to head off.
caveat: The leading-causes list is a fixed short list, so share is share of listed causes only, not of all deaths.

source_names: NCHS Leading Causes of Death by State
title: The Worst State for Each Cause
idea: Ranked dot plot per cause of the highest and lowest state rates in the final year with the national line marked. Makes the spread undeniable.
harm_angle: A three-fold gap between the best and worst state for the same cause is policy, not biology.
caveat: Rates may be text needing a numeric cast; suppressed small-count cells may be blank.

source_names: NCHS Leading Causes of Death by State
title: Choropleth of Excess Death Burden
idea: Map states shaded by how far their age-adjusted rate sits above the national rate for a chosen cause, steppable across 1999 to 2017.
harm_angle: Persistent excess in the same states year after year is a durable failure with a body count.
caveat: Coverage ends in 2017 per the source name; presenting it as current would be wrong.

source_names: CDC VSRR Provisional Drug Overdose Death Counts
title: State overdose death timeline
idea: Monthly provisional overdose death counts by state over the full series with the national trend overlaid to show which states never came down.
harm_angle: Overdose deaths are still rising in states that fell off the national narrative once the aggregate curve flattened.
caveat: Indicator column mixes many measures; must filter to a single indicator or the chart mixes units.

source_names: CDC VSRR Provisional Drug Overdose Death Counts
title: Reported versus predicted gap
idea: Scatter of the raw reported count against the CDC predicted value per state-month to expose states whose reporting lag forces the biggest statistical guesswork.
harm_angle: Where the count is guessed rather than counted the public and responders are flying blind during a live crisis.
caveat: predicted_value may be sparsely populated; unverified.

source_names: CDC VSRR Provisional Drug Overdose Death Counts
title: Death investigation backlog heatmap
idea: Heatmap grid of state by month coloured by the percent of deaths still pending investigation showing chronic medical-examiner backlogs.
harm_angle: Families in backlogged states wait months for a cause of death and the state undercounts its own epidemic.
caveat: percent_pending_investigation may be null for many state-months.

source_names: CDC VSRR Provisional Drug Overdose Death Counts
title: Which drug drove which state
idea: Small multiples per state of the indicator-specific series (synthetic opioids vs psychostimulants vs cocaine) to show the drug mix diverging regionally.
harm_angle: Treatment and naloxone funding aimed at the wrong substance leaves whole regions unserved.
caveat: Indicator label text values unknown from metadata.

source_names: CDC VSRR Provisional Drug Overdose Death Counts
title: Footnote as a warning layer
idea: Timeline of each state's series shaded wherever a footnote is attached to reveal how much of the official record carries a data-quality caveat nobody reads.
harm_angle: Numbers used in policy debates carry hidden caveats that would change their meaning.
caveat: Footnote may be nearly always populated making the chart uniform and useless.

source_names: CDC NCHS Death Rates for Suicide by Demographics
title: Suicide rate by demographic slice
idea: Small multiples of the suicide estimate over years for each demographic stub (sex age race) so divergent trajectories are visible side by side.
harm_angle: Some demographic groups' suicide rates rose steadily while the headline national rate looked stable.
caveat: Stub structure is a nested NCHS layout; mixing stub levels will double-count.

source_names: CDC NCHS Death Rates for Suicide by Demographics
title: Age gradient over decades
idea: Heatmap grid of age band by year coloured by suicide rate showing whether the burden shifted from older men to younger people.
harm_angle: A generational shift in who dies by suicide changes who prevention money should reach.
caveat: Age bands may change definition across the series.

source_names: CDC NCHS Death Rates for Suicide by Demographics
title: Flagged and missing estimates
idea: Grid of demographic slice by year marking cells where the estimate is flagged or absent to show which small populations are never measured.
harm_angle: Small racial and age groups are statistically erased so their crises never register.
caveat: Flag semantics unknown; may simply mark rounding.

source_names: CDC NCHS Death Rates for Suicide by Demographics
title: Widest and narrowest gaps
idea: Slope chart of the highest versus lowest demographic group in the first and last year to show whether the inequality gap widened.
harm_angle: If the gap widened despite national prevention spending the programs missed the people most at risk.
caveat: Comparability across stub levels unverified.
