source_names: CDC WONDER Underlying Cause of Death
title: Cause of death mix over two decades
idea: Stacked timeline of national deaths by ICD chapter from the earliest to latest year showing which causes displaced which.
harm_angle: Shifts in what kills Americans reveal which public health systems stopped working.
caveat: National-only by CDC API policy so no geographic story here; deaths null means CDC suppressed under ten.

source_names: CDC WONDER Underlying Cause of Death
title: Male versus female cause divergence
idea: Slope chart per ICD chapter of the male and female crude rate showing causes where one sex carries a far heavier and growing burden.
harm_angle: Sex-skewed causes of death signal screening and care systems that only serve one half of the population.
caveat: Crude rate not age-adjusted so an ageing population confounds the trend.

source_names: CDC WONDER Underlying Cause of Death
title: Where the record goes dark
idea: Grid of year by ICD chapter marking suppressed (null deaths) cells to show which causes are systematically too rare to be published.
harm_angle: Rare causes of death stay invisible so nobody funds research into them.
caveat: Only 880 rows; suppression may be very sparse at national grain.

title: Trials that never report results
idea: Ranked bars of lead sponsors by the share of completed trials with no results posted exposing who runs studies on people and buries the outcome.
harm_angle: Patients volunteered for studies whose findings were never published so the risk they took bought nothing.
caveat: Only 500 rows in the mart which may be a sample rather than the full registry.

title: Days to results posting distribution
idea: Distribution of the days between first posting and results posting split by sponsor class (industry vs academic vs government) to show who reports fast and who stalls.
harm_angle: Delayed results keep unsafe or ineffective treatments in use longer than they should be.
caveat: Derived field is null whenever results were never posted which biases the visible distribution.

title: Why trials stop
idea: Ranked bars of the stated reason a trial was terminated or withdrawn grouped into themes and split by sponsor class.
harm_angle: Trials stopped for business reasons rather than safety leave participants exposed for nothing.
caveat: why_stopped is free text and needs grouping; small row count.

title: Who is allowed in the trial
idea: Scatter of minimum age against enrollment by phase showing how many drugs are tested on populations that exclude the elderly who will actually take them.
harm_angle: Drugs approved on trials that excluded older and female patients are then prescribed to exactly those people.
caveat: Age fields are text with units so parsing is needed; gender field may be mostly 'All'.

title: Oversight committee presence by phase
idea: Grid of phase by FDA-regulated flag coloured by the share of trials with a data monitoring committee to show where safety oversight is thinnest.
harm_angle: Early-phase trials without independent safety monitoring put the first humans dosed at greatest risk.
caveat: Flag columns may be sparsely populated in older records.

title: Chain-owned dialysis mortality gap
idea: Distribution of facility mortality rate split by chain organization to show whether patients at the big dialysis chains die at higher rates than at independents.
harm_angle: Kidney patients have almost no choice of clinic so a chain's worse outcomes are inescapable.
caveat: Mortality rate is risk-standardised by CMS but case mix differences may still confound.

title: Transplant waitlisting by ownership
idea: Ranked bars of chains by the percentage of prevalent patients waitlisted for a kidney transplant exposing clinics that keep patients on dialysis instead of moving them toward a transplant.
harm_angle: A patient not referred for transplant stays a recurring revenue stream and dies sooner.
caveat: Waitlisting depends on medical eligibility which this table does not capture.

title: Dialysis deserts and station capacity
idea: Map of facilities sized by number of dialysis stations with counties having no facility shaded to show where patients must travel three times a week.
harm_angle: Patients in dialysis deserts drive hours three times a week or skip sessions and die.
caveat: No latitude or longitude column so mapping relies on zip or county geocoding.

title: Stars versus actual outcomes
idea: Scatter of the five-star rating against the facility mortality rate to test whether the public-facing star a patient sees actually predicts survival.
harm_angle: If the star rating does not track survival then the only tool patients have to choose a clinic is decorative.
caveat: Five star is a text or number field of unknown type; rating incorporates mortality so partial circularity.

title: Infection and catheter burden grid
idea: Heatmap of chains by infection ratio and long-term catheter use percentage to expose operators whose practice patterns drive preventable sepsis.
harm_angle: Long-term catheters cause bloodstream infections and chains that leave them in are choosing convenience over lives.
caveat: Data availability codes mark many facilities as unreportable; must exclude them.

title: Providers stretched across many facilities
idea: Distribution of how many distinct facilities each provider is affiliated with with the long tail of clinicians listed at dozens of sites called out.
harm_angle: A clinician on paper at forty nursing homes cannot actually be supervising care at any of them.
caveat: Affiliation is self-reported and may be stale so a high count can be bookkeeping rather than reality.

title: Facility staffing network
idea: Network graph of facilities linked when they share affiliated providers revealing tightly interlocked clusters that behave as one system without common ownership.
harm_angle: Informal facility networks move patients and money among themselves with no regulator watching the whole.
caveat: 2.26M rows makes a full network unrenderable; needs aggregation to a region or facility type first.

title: Facility type mix per provider
idea: Ranked bars of facility types by how many distinct providers claim affiliation showing which parts of the care system are thinly covered.
harm_angle: Facility types with almost no affiliated clinicians are where patients get the least physician attention.
caveat: Facility type vocabulary unknown from metadata.

title: Facilities with a single named clinician
idea: Map or ranked list of facilities where only one provider is affiliated to find sites operating with effectively no medical staff on the record.
harm_angle: A facility with one affiliated clinician gives residents nobody to see when that person is away.
caveat: Missing affiliations may be a reporting gap rather than a real staffing gap.

title: Charity care versus profit
idea: Scatter of net margin against cost of charity care as a share of total costs per hospital coloured by type of control to expose profitable nonprofits giving almost nothing back.
harm_angle: Nonprofit hospitals get tax exemptions in exchange for charity care and some deliver almost none while patients get sued for bills.
caveat: Charity care reporting is inconsistent across filers; cost report fields are notoriously dirty.

title: Bad debt versus uncompensated care
idea: Slope chart per hospital of bad debt expense and charity care over years to show hospitals shifting patients from charity write-off into aggressive collections.
harm_angle: Reclassifying a poor patient from charity to bad debt is the paperwork step before a lawsuit and a wage garnishment.
caveat: Only 6103 rows so this may be a single year rather than a panel; year coverage unverified.

title: Cost-to-charge markup ranked
idea: Ranked bars of hospitals by cost-to-charge ratio showing which hospitals bill uninsured patients many multiples of what care actually costs.
harm_angle: Uninsured and out-of-network patients are billed the sticker charge which at the worst hospitals is ten times cost.
caveat: Cost to charge ratio derivation in the mart is unverified and outliers are common.

title: Rural hospital balance-sheet distress
idea: Scatter of current ratio against occupancy rate split by rural versus urban to map which rural hospitals are financially closest to closing.
harm_angle: When a rural hospital closes the nearest emergency room moves an hour away and people die in transit.
caveat: Balance sheet fields are frequently blank in filed cost reports.

title: Contract labor dependence
idea: Distribution of contract labor for direct patient care as a share of total salaries by hospital control type to show which hospitals run on travellers rather than staff.
harm_angle: Heavy agency staffing means constant turnover at the bedside and worse outcomes for patients.
caveat: Contract labor field is optional on the worksheet and often zero.

title: Medicaid share versus margin
idea: Scatter of net revenue from Medicaid as a share of total patient revenue against net margin to show that serving poor patients tracks with financial fragility.
harm_angle: Hospitals that serve the most Medicaid patients are the least financially able to survive which concentrates closures in poor areas.
caveat: Medicaid revenue capture in HCRIS varies by state supplemental payment programs.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Home Health Agencies
title: Home health quality by ownership
idea: Distribution of the quality of patient care star rating split by type of ownership to test whether for-profit home health agencies deliver worse care.
harm_angle: Home health patients are homebound and least able to switch or complain about a bad agency.
caveat: Star rating field may be text with footnote placeholders.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Home Health Agencies
title: Preventable hospitalization outliers
idea: Ranked bars of agencies by potentially preventable hospitalization risk-standardised rate with performance categorisation coloured to expose the worst repeat offenders.
harm_angle: Patients sent to hospital from home health for problems the agency should have caught are the visible harm.
caveat: Risk standardisation and small denominators make agency-level ranking fragile.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Home Health Agencies
title: Spending versus outcome quadrant
idea: Scatter of Medicare spending per episode against the quality star rating to find agencies that cost the most and deliver the least.
harm_angle: High-cost low-quality agencies drain the program while leaving patients worse off.
caveat: The spending column is a ratio to national average and may be blank for small agencies.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Home Health Agencies
title: Service menu gaps by state
idea: Heatmap grid of state by service offered (nursing therapy social work aide) showing states where whole service lines are effectively unavailable.
harm_angle: In states where no agency offers social work or aide services the frailest patients get only a nurse visit and no help living.
caveat: Offered-service flags are self-reported and may be near-universally yes.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Home Health Agencies
title: Suppressed by footnote
idea: Grid of measures by state coloured by how often a footnote replaces the actual score to show where the public quality record is mostly blanks.
harm_angle: Patients choosing an agency in these states see footnotes instead of numbers and pick blind.
caveat: Many footnote columns; needs consistent handling of which footnote codes mean suppression.

title: Home health deserts by state
idea: Rate of enrolled home-health agencies per state, ranked, so states with almost no in-home care capacity stand out against dense ones.
harm_angle: Elderly and disabled people in thin-supply states have to leave home for care.
caveat: No population denominator in this table; per-capita needs an external population source.

title: For-profit vs nonprofit home health
idea: Share of home-health agencies flagged proprietary versus nonprofit, mapped by state, revealing where in-home elder care is almost entirely investor-owned.
harm_angle: Where care is entirely for-profit, cost-cutting pressure lands on homebound patients.
caveat: proprietary_nonprofit coding scheme unverified; may be sparse or free text.

title: Address clusters hiding many agencies
idea: Count of distinct agencies sharing one street address, ranked, exposing shell-like clusters of agencies operating from a single suite.
harm_angle: Paper agencies at one address are a classic Medicare fraud pattern that drains care dollars.
caveat: Address strings not normalized; suite-level differences may split real clusters.

title: Agency incorporation wave timeline
idea: Home-health agencies by incorporation year, showing bursts of new company formation that often follow reimbursement rule changes.
harm_angle: Formation booms preceding fraud waves show who rushes in when the money gets easy.
caveat: incorporation_date is a try_to_date cast; nulls and bad parses likely.

title: Agencies wearing many NPIs
idea: Share of agencies carrying the multiple-NPI flag by state, dot plot, showing where one operator wears many identities.
harm_angle: Multiple identities per operator make it harder for patients and regulators to track a bad actor.
caveat: Flag semantics unverified; may be near-uniformly one value.

title: Hospice ownership shift map
idea: Map of hospices coloured by ownership type showing the geographic concentration of for-profit hospice growth.
harm_angle: For-profit hospices have been repeatedly found enrolling patients who are not dying and abandoning those who are.
caveat: Thin table (12 columns) with no quality measures so ownership is the only lever.

title: New hospice entry wave
idea: Timeline of hospice certification dates by state to show the explosion of newly certified hospices in a handful of states.
harm_angle: Sudden clusters of new hospices in one county is the known signature of Medicare hospice fraud.
caveat: Certification date may be a text field; a date-cast failure would silently drop rows.

title: Same-address hospice clusters
idea: Ranked bars of street addresses hosting multiple distinct hospice CCNs to expose paper hospices sharing one storefront.
harm_angle: Shell hospices billing Medicare from a shared mailbox take money meant for dying patients' care.
caveat: Address strings need normalising before grouping; suite numbers may hide legitimate co-tenancy.

title: Hospice access per capita by region
idea: Dot plot of CMS region by hospice count per elderly resident to show regions where dying at home with support is simply unavailable.
harm_angle: In hospice deserts terminal patients die in hospitals or alone instead of with palliative support.
caveat: Requires an external population denominator not present in this source.

title: Hospice ownership mix by state
idea: Proprietary versus nonprofit hospice share by state, mapped, showing states where end-of-life care is nearly all investor-owned.
harm_angle: For-profit hospice concentration is linked to shorter and thinner care for dying patients.
caveat: proprietary_nonprofit value coding unverified.

title: Hospice chains behind many brands
idea: Organizations whose legal name covers many doing-business-as names, ranked, revealing the branding layer between chains and families.
harm_angle: Families choosing a local-sounding hospice may be buying from a national chain with a record.
caveat: Name matching is fuzzy; no owner id column here.

title: Hospice formation surge by year
idea: New hospices by incorporation year and state, small multiples, spotlighting the recent explosion of new hospices in a handful of places.
harm_angle: Sudden hospice booms have preceded documented enrollment fraud against dying patients.
caveat: incorporation_date parse quality unknown; no enrollment date present.

title: One address many hospices
idea: Hospices sharing a single street address, ranked, exposing suite-farm clusters.
harm_angle: Address farms suggest paper hospices billing for patients no one visits.
caveat: Address normalization not guaranteed.

source_names: CMS Hospital Compare / Provider Data Catalog
title: Hospitals worse on every measure group
idea: Heatmap grid of hospitals by measure group (mortality safety readmission patient experience) coloured by count of worse-than-average measures to find the consistently bad.
harm_angle: Hospitals worse than average on mortality safety and readmissions at once are killing people and staying open.
caveat: Measure counts depend on how many measures a hospital reports at all so low reporters look clean.

source_names: CMS Hospital Compare / Provider Data Catalog
title: Ownership and the star rating
idea: Distribution of hospital overall rating by hospital ownership category to show whether government for-profit or nonprofit hospitals rate worst.
harm_angle: Patients in areas served only by one ownership type inherit that type's average quality with no alternative.
caveat: Overall rating is a text field with 'Not Available' values that must be excluded not treated as zero.

source_names: CMS Hospital Compare / Provider Data Catalog
title: Emergency services absent
idea: Map of hospitals without emergency services to show communities whose nearest 'hospital' cannot take an ambulance.
harm_angle: A town whose only hospital has no emergency department has no emergency care at all.
caveat: Specialty and psychiatric hospitals legitimately lack EDs so the map needs hospital_type filtering.

source_names: CMS Hospital Compare / Provider Data Catalog
title: Measures not reported at all
idea: Ranked bars of hospitals by how many measure groups are entirely footnoted out to identify hospitals whose public quality record is essentially empty.
harm_angle: A hospital that reports nothing cannot be compared and effectively opts out of accountability.
caveat: Footnote codes have distinct meanings; some indicate too-few-cases rather than non-reporting.

source_names: CMS Hospital Compare / Provider Data Catalog
title: Birthing friendly designation map
idea: Map of hospitals meeting the birthing-friendly criteria against those that do not to show maternity care deserts and low-standard obstetric regions.
harm_angle: Mothers giving birth at non-designated hospitals in maternity deserts face the worst US maternal mortality in the rich world.
caveat: Designation is recent so many hospitals may be blank rather than failing.

title: Psychiatric bed coverage map
idea: Hospitals flagged as psychiatric or carrying a psychiatric unit, mapped by state, showing where mental-health inpatient capacity simply is not.
harm_angle: People in crisis in bare states get jail or an ER hallway instead of a bed.
caveat: Subgroup flags may be sparse or inconsistently populated.

title: Rural hospitals converting away
idea: Hospitals with a rural-emergency-hospital conversion flag plotted over conversion date, tracking the quiet loss of inpatient beds in rural towns.
harm_angle: Conversion means the nearest maternity or inpatient bed just moved an hour away.
caveat: Conversion program is recent; row counts may be small.

title: Hospital service-type profile grid
idea: Heatmap of states by the mix of hospital subgroups such as acute, children's, long-term, rehab and specialty, showing which states are missing whole categories of care.
harm_angle: Whole categories of care absent from a state means patients travel or go without.
caveat: Flag population and encoding unverified.

title: Specialty hospitals versus ownership
idea: Cross-tab of proprietary and nonprofit status against specialty and acute-care flags, revealing who owns the profitable niches versus the safety net.
harm_angle: Investor ownership concentrating in lucrative specialties leaves general care to strained nonprofits.
caveat: Coding of the ownership field unverified.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Hospital General Information
title: Rating versus emergency access
idea: Grid of state by hospital rating band showing states where the low-rated hospitals are also the only ones with emergency services.
harm_angle: In some states an ambulance can only go to a one-star hospital.
caveat: Near-duplicate of hospital_compare with a CCN key instead of facility_id; overlap unverified.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Hospital General Information
title: Critical access hospital quality
idea: Distribution of overall rating by hospital type isolating critical access hospitals to show whether the rural safety net rates systematically lower.
harm_angle: Rural patients get the lowest-rated care because the alternative is no care.
caveat: Critical access hospitals are exempt from many measures so their ratings may be missing rather than low.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Hospital General Information
title: County hospital ownership monoculture
idea: Map of counties coloured by whether every hospital in them shares one ownership type revealing single-operator counties.
harm_angle: In a single-operator county a patient with a grievance has nowhere else to go.
caveat: County_parish text needs normalising to FIPS; no FIPS column present.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Inpatient Rehab Facilities
title: Rehab facility ownership and access
idea: Map of the 1222 inpatient rehab facilities coloured by ownership type with state counts to show states with almost no rehab capacity.
harm_angle: Stroke and trauma patients without a rehab bed nearby never regain function they could have.
caveat: Thin table with no quality or bed-count fields so this is access-only.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Inpatient Rehab Facilities
title: Rehab certification wave
idea: Timeline of certification dates by ownership type to show whether for-profit chains drove recent rehab expansion.
harm_angle: Rapid for-profit rehab expansion has historically preceded admissions of patients who did not need inpatient rehab.
caveat: Certification date may be text; only 1222 rows so trends are coarse.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Inpatient Rehab Facilities
title: Rehab beds per state population
idea: Dot plot of states ranked by rehab facilities per capita exposing the widest access gaps.
harm_angle: States at the bottom leave recovering patients to go straight home with no rehabilitation.
caveat: Needs an outside population denominator; no bed counts in this table.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Long-Term Care Hospitals
title: Where the 311 LTCHs are
idea: Map of long-term care hospitals sized by total beds showing that most states have none and a handful of metros have clusters.
harm_angle: Ventilator-dependent patients in states with no LTCH are transferred hundreds of miles from family.
caveat: Only 311 rows; bed count field may be text or blank.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Long-Term Care Hospitals
title: LTCH ownership concentration
idea: Ranked bars of ownership type by total beds to show what share of the nation's long-term acute capacity sits with for-profit operators.
harm_angle: A single for-profit operator controlling long-term acute beds sets the standard of care for the sickest patients with no competitor.
caveat: Ownership type is a coarse category not a corporate parent name.

source_names: CMS Care Compare — Long-Term Care Hospitals
title: LTCH certification timeline
idea: Timeline of certification dates showing the mid-2000s boom and the post-payment-reform freeze in new long-term care hospitals.
harm_angle: Payment rule changes froze capacity in place leaving the geography of access permanently unequal.
caveat: Small n and possible text date field.

title: What CMS publishes and how often
idea: Ranked bars of CMS datasets by update frequency and format to show how much of the Medicare record is refreshed annually versus never.
harm_angle: Datasets that are never refreshed let outdated provider and spending information drive real decisions.
caveat: Catalog table of only 158 rows; it describes datasets not people.

title: Publisher fragmentation
idea: Network or ranked bars of publishers within CMS by dataset count showing how many separate offices publish the same subject matter differently.
harm_angle: Fragmented publishing means a citizen tracking one issue must find and reconcile a dozen incompatible files.
caveat: Tiny table; publisher values may all be 'CMS'.

title: Diabetes prevention blank spots
idea: Map of the roughly one thousand diabetes prevention sites by ZIP, showing enormous swaths of the country with no supplier at all.
harm_angle: A prevention benefit with no nearby provider is a benefit that does not exist for those patients.
caveat: Only 1037 rows; no date column, so a snapshot with no trend.

title: Who dominates prevention delivery
idea: Ranked bars of organizations by number of program locations, showing whether the benefit is delivered by many local groups or a few national ones.
harm_angle: A benefit run by two national vendors is fragile for the patients depending on it.
caveat: Small table; organization names may be inconsistent.

title: Supplier category mix
idea: Distribution of sites by category, showing what kinds of entities actually deliver the program.
harm_angle: Understanding who delivers prevention shows who to hold to account when it fails.
caveat: category values unknown; may be near-single-valued.

title: Dialysis chain quality slope
idea: Average measure scores by chain over years, showing whether the two giant dialysis chains score better or worse than independents.
harm_angle: Kidney patients are captive to whichever chain owns the nearest clinic and score gaps are their outcomes.
caveat: Tall measure-per-row format; measure_score may be text or suppressed. Catalog row count (12.4M) conflicts with the model comment (500k) so grain is unverified.

title: ESRD network score heatmap
idea: Heatmap of ESRD networks by measure, colored by average score, revealing which regional networks systematically underperform.
harm_angle: Whole regions of dialysis patients getting worse care than others is a policy failure with names attached.
caveat: Measure comparability across measure ids is not guaranteed; scores may need per-measure normalizing.

title: Bad clinics that never close
idea: Facilities in the worst score decile for three or more consecutive years, mapped as points, showing bad clinics that persist.
harm_angle: Patients on a fixed three-day-a-week schedule cannot leave a clinic that stays bad for years.
caveat: Requires stable measure definitions across years; suppression may break the streak logic.

title: Ownership type versus modality
idea: Distribution of treatment modalities offered by ownership type, showing whether for-profit chains skew away from home dialysis.
harm_angle: Home dialysis is better for many patients but less profitable; the mix shows whose interest wins.
caveat: modality field format unknown; may be multi-valued text.

title: Referrers feeding hundreds of suppliers
idea: Scatter of referring providers by number of distinct suppliers against Medicare paid amount, with the far corner flagged as extreme referral fan-out.
harm_angle: Doctors whose signature powers hundreds of equipment suppliers are the hinge of the equipment fraud that drains patients' benefits.
caveat: Single-year snapshot with no date column visible; outliers may be legitimate large practices.

title: Equipment spend versus patient mix
idea: Scatter of equipment payment per beneficiary against the share of beneficiaries who are Black or dual-eligible, testing whether the highest-spend referrers concentrate on the most vulnerable patients.
harm_angle: Predatory equipment schemes historically target poor and dual-eligible seniors; this shows whether the pattern holds.
caveat: Beneficiary demographic counts are suppressed below thresholds, biasing small providers out.

title: Rural versus urban equipment access
idea: Equipment payment per beneficiary by rural-urban commuting area category, showing whether rural patients get less equipment or just more expensive access.
harm_angle: Rural seniors without a supply chain wait longer for wheelchairs and oxygen.
caveat: RUCA reflects the referrer's location, not the patient's.

title: Drug versus device referral split
idea: Small multiples by specialty of the drug, device and prosthetic payment split, showing which specialties are unexpectedly heavy on one bucket.
harm_angle: Specialties billing far outside their normal mix are where the money is being steered.
caveat: Suppression indicators mean bucket totals do not always sum to the overall total.

title: Markup on the same wheelchair code
idea: For one common equipment code, the spread of average submitted charge against Medicare allowed amount across suppliers, showing who charges ten times the allowed rate.
harm_angle: Patients on the hook for coinsurance and the uninsured pay off the inflated sticker price.
caveat: Charge fields may be text; extreme ratios may be data artifacts rather than real pricing.

title: Rental versus purchase steering
idea: Share of services billed as rental by supplier and equipment category, ranked, exposing suppliers who rent everything indefinitely instead of selling.
harm_angle: Perpetual rental quietly multiplies what a patient and Medicare pay for one device.
caveat: Rental indicator semantics unverified; category mapping via rbcs may be coarse.

title: Services per beneficiary outliers
idea: Scatter of services per beneficiary against beneficiary count per supplier and code, isolating suppliers billing implausible volumes per patient.
harm_angle: Impossible per-patient volumes mean either phantom patients or patients buried in equipment they never asked for.
caveat: Some codes legitimately bill many units per patient; needs per-code normalization.

title: Supplier concentration by state
idea: Share of a state's equipment payments captured by its top ten suppliers, ranked by state, showing where a handful of firms own the market.
harm_angle: Concentrated supply means patients have no alternative when one firm delivers badly.
caveat: Only averages, not totals, are present; totals must be reconstructed from services times average.

title: Provider type mix by state
idea: Heatmap of states against provider type, share-normalized, showing which states are structurally short of primary care or specific specialties.
harm_angle: Patients in provider-type deserts wait months or travel for basic care.
caveat: Enrollment counts are not the same as active practice; no dates in this table.

title: One operator many enrollments
idea: Distribution of enrollment records per PECOS control id, showing individuals or entities holding dozens of separate Medicare enrollments.
harm_angle: Sprawling enrollment footprints let one operator keep billing after one identity is sanctioned.
caveat: pecos_asct_cntl_id is cast with try_to_number, which may null out non-numeric ids.

title: Multi-NPI flag by provider type
idea: Share of enrollments flagged as multiple-NPI, ranked by provider type, showing which corners of Medicare run on tangled identities.
harm_angle: Identity tangle is what makes it hard to tell a patient who is actually treating them.
caveat: Flag may be overwhelmingly one value.

title: Same name enrolled in many states
idea: Providers whose identical name appears enrolled in many states, ranked, as a rough map of multi-state operators.
harm_angle: Multi-state operators are hard for any single state board to discipline.
caveat: Name collisions are common; without a verified person key this is suggestive only.

title: Charge-to-payment ratio ranked
idea: Hospitals ranked by total submitted charges divided by total payments, showing which list ten or twenty times what they actually receive.
harm_angle: That inflated list price is the number uninsured and out-of-network patients get billed.
caveat: tot_submtd_cvrd_chrg is not explicitly cast to a number in the model and may be text.

title: Who serves the dual-eligible poor
idea: Scatter of hospitals by share of dual-eligible beneficiaries against payment per discharge, showing whether the hospitals carrying the poorest patients are paid least per case.
harm_angle: Safety-net hospitals paid least for the sickest poor patients is the structural squeeze that closes them.
caveat: Dual counts may be suppressed at small hospitals, dropping exactly the ones of interest.

title: Segregation inside the hospital map
idea: Map of hospitals sized by discharges and colored by how far their Black beneficiary share sits from their metro's, revealing de facto sorting of patients between hospitals in one city.
harm_angle: Two hospitals a mile apart serving racially separate patient bodies is measurable and persistent medical segregation.
caveat: Requires a metro benchmark this table does not carry; race counts are suppressed at low volumes.

title: Rural hospital length of stay
idea: Covered days per discharge by rural-urban category, showing whether rural hospitals hold patients longer or transfer them out fast.
harm_angle: Fast transfers out of rural hospitals mean families driving hours to visit a sick relative.
caveat: Days fields may be text; transfers are not directly observable here.

title: Sickest patients least paid
idea: Scatter of average beneficiary risk score against Medicare payment per discharge, with hospitals far below the trend flagged as underfunded for their case mix.
harm_angle: Hospitals treating the sickest for the least money end up rationing care to the people who need it most.
caveat: bene_avg_risk_scre is not explicitly numeric-cast in the model.

title: Same procedure wildly different price
idea: For one common diagnosis-related group, the spread of average submitted charge across every hospital, showing a twenty-fold price range for identical care.
harm_angle: The same hip replacement priced twenty times higher across town is what bankrupts uninsured patients.
caveat: Charge field may be text; single-year snapshot with no year column visible.

title: Hospital markup fingerprint grid
idea: Heatmap of top hospitals against top diagnosis groups, colored by charge-to-payment ratio, showing whether hospitals mark up everything or target specific procedures.
harm_angle: Targeted markup on procedures the uninsured need most is a deliberate choice, visible here.
caveat: Charge and payment casts differ; the ratio may be noisy for low-volume groups.

title: Which services rural hospitals lost
idea: Discharge share by diagnosis group split by rural-urban category, small multiples, showing which services have quietly vanished from rural hospitals.
harm_angle: When a rural hospital stops doing births or cardiac care, the nearest option is an ambulance ride.
caveat: Absence of a code in the file could be suppression rather than genuine absence.

title: Upcoding signature by severity pairs
idea: For diagnosis-group families that split into with-complication and without-complication versions, each hospital's share of the higher-paying variant, ranked.
harm_angle: Systematic coding to the sicker variant inflates the bill on every patient who walks in.
caveat: Pairing complication variants requires parsing drg_desc text; genuine case-mix differences confound it.

title: Outpatient price spread by service
idea: For each common outpatient service class, the distribution of average submitted charges across hospitals, showing where the price range is widest.
harm_angle: Outpatient is where most people meet a hospital bill and wide spread means luck of address decides the debt.
caveat: Charge field cast unverified; single snapshot year.

title: Outlier payment leaders
idea: Hospitals plotted by outlier services as a share of total services against average outlier amount, exposing sites where unusually costly cases are routine.
harm_angle: Routine outliers mean patients are being run through the most expensive path by default.
caveat: Outlier fields may be sparse; denominator semantics of capc_srvcs unverified.

title: Rural outpatient service menus
idea: Count of distinct outpatient service classes offered per hospital plotted against rural-urban category, showing how thin the menu gets outside metros.
harm_angle: A short service menu means every extra procedure is a day off work and a long drive.
caveat: Low-volume services are suppressed, which shortens rural menus artificially.

title: Allowed versus charged gap map
idea: State map colored by the median ratio of submitted charge to allowed amount for outpatient care, showing which states' hospitals inflate hardest.
harm_angle: State-level inflation patterns point at which regulators are asleep.
caveat: Case mix differs by state; the ratio needs service-level standardization.

title: Drug billing share by specialty
idea: Scatter of each provider's drug payment share against total payments, faceted by specialty, isolating practices that are effectively drug dispensaries.
harm_angle: Practices whose revenue is mostly infused drugs have an incentive pointing away from the patient's best treatment.
caveat: Suppression indicators blank the drug bucket for small providers.

title: Patients per provider extremes
idea: Distribution of beneficiaries and services per provider within specialty, with the top tail flagged as implausible caseloads.
harm_angle: A provider billing more patient encounters than hours exist is either fraud or care no one really got.
caveat: Group practices billing under one NPI can produce legitimate extremes.

title: Who takes the dual-eligible patients
idea: Map of providers by share of dual-eligible beneficiaries, showing neighborhoods where almost no provider serves the poorest seniors.
harm_angle: Poor seniors with no local provider willing to see them simply stop getting care.
caveat: Dual counts suppressed below thresholds; ZIP is the provider's, not the patient's.

title: Non-participating provider clusters
idea: Map of the share of providers not flagged as Medicare-participating, by ZIP, showing where seniors face balance billing.
harm_angle: Non-participating providers can bill seniors above the Medicare rate and concentration means no escape.
caveat: Participation flag coding unverified and may be near-universally yes.

title: Mental illness burden versus supply
idea: Scatter of providers' average share of patients with serious mental illness against the count of behavioral-health providers in their state, showing where the sickest populations have the fewest specialists.
harm_angle: High mental-illness burden with no specialists means those patients are managed by whoever is left.
caveat: Condition percentages are provider-panel averages, not population prevalence.

title: Same code same city price gap
idea: For one high-volume procedure code, the spread of average submitted charge across providers within a single metro, showing neighbors charging triple.
harm_angle: Price for the exact same fifteen-minute service varying threefold across one city is a bill patients cannot shop for.
caveat: Charge fields may be text; place-of-service differences confound comparison.

title: Highest complexity visit bias
idea: Share of a provider's office-visit services billed at the highest complexity level, ranked within specialty, a classic upcoding signature.
harm_angle: Every patient billed as a complex visit pays a higher coinsurance for the same fifteen minutes.
caveat: Requires knowing which HCPCS codes are the visit-level family; genuinely sicker panels confound it.

title: Facility versus office site shift
idea: Share of services billed at facility versus office place-of-service by specialty, showing the migration to the higher-paying facility setting.
harm_angle: The same care rebilled as hospital outpatient costs the patient more in coinsurance for nothing extra.
caveat: Single snapshot; a shift narrative needs multiple years this table may not carry.

title: Rare procedure single-provider hubs
idea: Procedures where one provider accounts for most of the national volume, ranked, surfacing single-operator concentrations of unusual procedures.
harm_angle: A single doctor doing most of the country's volume of an odd procedure is either a rare specialist or a scheme.
caveat: Legitimate ultra-specialists produce the same signature.

source_names: Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider
title: Billing outliers by specialty
idea: Distribution of total Medicare payment per beneficiary within each provider type with the extreme upper tail flagged to find specialty-adjusted billing outliers.
harm_angle: Providers billing many multiples of their peers per patient are either over-treating patients or over-billing taxpayers.
caveat: Single program year in the mart so year-over-year confirmation is not possible here.

source_names: Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider
title: Charge markup versus allowed amount
idea: Scatter of total submitted charges against total Medicare allowed amount per provider to show how far above the allowed rate providers bill.
harm_angle: The submitted charge is what an uninsured or balance-billed patient is asked to pay and it bears no relation to the allowed rate.
caveat: Allowed and submitted amounts are annual totals so per-service markup is only an average.

source_names: Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider
title: Dual-eligible patient panel geography
idea: Map of providers' state by the share of their beneficiaries who are dual-eligible to show which regions' clinicians carry the poorest patients.
harm_angle: Clinicians serving mostly dual-eligible patients are paid least and burn out fastest which shrinks access for the poor.
caveat: Beneficiary demographic counts are suppressed for small panels.

source_names: Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider
title: Race mix of patient panels
idea: Scatter of the Black beneficiary share of a provider's panel against average risk score and payment per beneficiary to test whether providers serving Black patients are paid less for sicker panels.
harm_angle: If providers with Black patient panels get less payment for higher-risk patients that is a funding mechanism for unequal care.
caveat: Race counts are suppressed below eleven beneficiaries which biases toward large practices.

source_names: Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider
title: Rural versus urban service intensity
idea: Distribution of services per beneficiary by RUCA rurality band and specialty to show whether rural patients get fewer visits for the same conditions.
harm_angle: Rural patients getting fewer services for the same illness burden is undertreatment dressed up as efficiency.
caveat: RUCA is the provider's location not the patient's.

source_names: Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider
title: Behavioral health burden of panels
idea: Heatmap grid of specialty by the average share of beneficiaries with depression anxiety or substance use to show which non-psychiatric clinicians are absorbing the mental health load.
harm_angle: Primary care doctors carrying the mental health caseload without training means patients get pills instead of treatment.
caveat: Chronic condition percentages are CMS-derived flags with their own definitional caveats.

source_names: NADAC National Average Drug Acquisition Cost
title: Generic price spikes
idea: Timeline of per-unit acquisition cost for generics with the steepest increases highlighted to expose sudden unexplained price jumps on old drugs.
harm_angle: A generic drug that quintuples in price puts a routine medication out of reach for people paying cash.
caveat: Effective date coverage and whether all years are loaded is unverified.

source_names: NADAC National Average Drug Acquisition Cost
title: Brand to generic gap distribution
idea: Distribution of the brand-to-generic price ratio across drugs to show how many brands cost fifty or a hundred times their identical generic.
harm_angle: Patients kept on the brand by a prescriber or a formulary quirk pay a multiple for the same molecule.
caveat: brand_to_generic_ratio is a derived field whose formula is not visible in metadata.

source_names: NADAC National Average Drug Acquisition Cost
title: Drugs whose generic never arrived
idea: Ranked bars of high-cost drugs with no corresponding generic price over the whole series showing where competition never appeared.
harm_angle: No generic means no price ceiling and patients ration doses of a drug that is cheap to make.
caveat: Null generic price may mean 'not applicable' rather than 'no generic exists'.

source_names: NADAC National Average Drug Acquisition Cost
title: Over-the-counter versus prescription cost path
idea: Slope chart of acquisition cost from earliest to latest date split by OTC flag and pharmacy type to see who absorbed the price increases.
harm_angle: OTC price rises hit cash-paying uninsured patients hardest because no insurer negotiates for them.
caveat: Pharmacy type indicator may be single-valued in this extract.

source_names: NADAC National Average Drug Acquisition Cost
title: Price churn as a fingerprint
idea: Heatmap of drugs by month coloured by whether the price changed at all revealing drugs repriced weekly versus frozen for years.
harm_angle: Constant repricing makes it impossible for a patient or pharmacy to plan and hides increases in the noise.
caveat: 359k rows in the mart versus a 1.5M row comment in the model suggests a partial load.

title: Provider density map
idea: Map of providers per capita by state or ZIP using the practice location address to show the national geography of who has a clinician nearby.
harm_angle: Provider deserts mean sick people wait months or drive hours for basic care.
caveat: Exact NPPES column names not visible in the model (select star from staging); mailing versus practice address confusion is a known trap.

title: Deactivation churn timeline
idea: Timeline of NPI deactivations and reactivations by month to show waves of providers leaving the system and where.
harm_angle: Mass provider exits in a region are an early warning of a coming access collapse for its patients.
caveat: Deactivation dates are cast in staging but may be sparsely populated.

title: Specialty supply versus need
idea: Ranked bars of provider taxonomy (specialty) counts by state normalised per capita highlighting the specialties nearly absent outside metros.
harm_angle: A state with three paediatric psychiatrists has effectively no paediatric mental health care.
caveat: Taxonomy code needs an external crosswalk to a readable specialty name.

title: Addresses shared by many NPIs
idea: Ranked bars of practice addresses hosting hundreds of distinct NPIs to find billing mills and virtual-office clusters.
harm_angle: Hundreds of providers at one mailbox is the classic signature of Medicare billing fraud that drains care money.
caveat: Large legitimate hospitals also share one address so the tail needs hand triage.

title: The EIN that is not there
idea: Grid showing NPPES columns by their real populated rate to make visible that fields like EIN read as full but are entirely sentinel-masked.
harm_angle: A registry whose employer field is masked makes it impossible to trace which corporation employs which clinician.
caveat: Would need column-level profiling not a plain query; the staging model already documents the masking.

title: Staffing hours versus star rating
idea: Scatter of reported total nurse staffing hours per resident day against overall rating coloured by ownership type to show how much of the star is staffing.
harm_angle: Residents in understaffed homes go unturned unfed and unwashed and the star rating may not warn their families.
caveat: Staffing is payroll-based and case-mix adjusted separately; using the reported rather than adjusted column understates differences.

title: Weekend staffing collapse
idea: Distribution of the gap between weekday and weekend nurse hours per resident day by chain to show which operators empty the building on Saturdays.
harm_angle: Residents who fall or aspirate on a weekend in a skeleton-staffed home die of a preventable event.
caveat: Weekend hours may be null for a large share of facilities.

title: Chains ranked by abuse icon rate
idea: Ranked bars of chains by the share of their facilities carrying the CMS abuse icon or special focus status exposing the worst corporate operators.
harm_angle: Chains that repeatedly earn abuse citations across many buildings are a corporate pattern not a bad-apple facility.
caveat: Chain name is free text and needs normalising; chain_id population unverified.

title: Fines that do not change behaviour
idea: Scatter of total fines in dollars against health deficiency score with repeat cycles overlaid to show homes fined repeatedly with no improvement.
harm_angle: If fines never change the deficiency score then the penalty is a cost of doing business paid out of residents' care.
caveat: Fines are cumulative to date while cycles are point-in-time so the comparison is directional only.

title: Turnover map of the frailest care
idea: Map of facilities coloured by total nursing staff turnover with administrator departures sized to show the geography of institutional chaos.
harm_angle: Constant turnover means nobody knows a resident's baseline so decline goes unnoticed until it is fatal.
caveat: Latitude and longitude come with a geocoding footnote column meaning some points are approximate.

title: Ownership change then decline
idea: Slope chart of health inspection rating across rating cycles for facilities flagged as having changed ownership in the last twelve months versus those that did not.
harm_angle: Private equity acquisitions of nursing homes have been linked to falling staffing and rising resident deaths.
caveat: The ownership-change flag is a snapshot so it cannot align to the cycle dates precisely.

title: Harm-level citations by state
idea: Rate of citations at the harm or immediate-jeopardy severity levels per facility by state, mapped, showing which states' inspectors find and record real harm.
harm_angle: States that never cite harm are not safer, they are unwatched, and residents pay for it.
caveat: Scope-severity letter grades must be ordered correctly; state inspection intensity varies.

title: Repeat offenders that never stop
idea: Facilities cited on the same deficiency tag across three or more inspection cycles, ranked, showing homes that repeat the same failure indefinitely.
harm_angle: A home cited for the same neglect year after year is a place families keep being sent to anyway.
caveat: inspection_cycle semantics unverified; correction dates may reset the pattern.

title: Complaint versus routine finding gap
idea: Share of citations arising from complaint inspections versus standard surveys, by state, showing where problems only surface when a family complains.
harm_angle: If only complaints find harm, residents with no family to complain are invisible.
caveat: Flag population unverified; a citation can be both.

title: Infection control after the pandemic
idea: Timeline of infection-control citations by month, showing whether the pandemic-era surge in scrutiny held or collapsed back.
harm_angle: If infection scrutiny evaporated, the next outbreak lands on the same residents.
caveat: survey_date parse quality unknown; reporting lags distort recent months.

title: Which citations get disputed
idea: Deficiency tags ranked by the share appealed through informal dispute resolution, showing which findings operators fight hardest to erase.
harm_angle: The citations operators fight to delete are the ones that would have warned families.
caveat: Dispute flags may be sparsely populated.

title: Time to correct by severity
idea: Distribution of days between survey date and correction date split by severity level, showing whether the worst findings get fixed fastest.
harm_angle: Slow correction of a harm-level finding is weeks of a resident living inside the harm.
caveat: Both date fields may be text; uncorrected rows have null correction dates and must not be silently dropped.

title: Fire safety failures mapped
idea: Map of nursing homes by count of life-safety-code citations, sized by severity, showing clusters of firetraps housing immobile residents.
harm_angle: Residents who cannot walk are the ones who die when a fire code failure is never fixed.
caveat: ZIP-level mapping only; no coordinates in the model.

title: Uncorrected fire citation backlog
idea: Count of fire-safety citations with no correction date, aged by months open, showing the standing backlog of unfixed hazards.
harm_angle: Every open month is a month residents sleep behind a door that will not hold.
caveat: A missing correction date may mean not-yet-reported rather than not-fixed.

title: Most common fire failures
idea: Ranked bars of fire-safety tags by frequency and by average severity, naming the specific failures that repeat nationwide.
harm_angle: Naming the exact repeated failure is what makes a fix demandable.
caveat: Tag versioning may split the same failure across codes.

title: Fire citations versus care citations
idea: Scatter of facilities by fire-safety citation count against care-deficiency count, testing whether the same homes fail both ways.
harm_angle: Homes failing on every axis at once are the ones no family is warned about.
caveat: Uses the sibling deficiency table for one axis so strictly this is a two-table view.

title: Fine size versus harm found
idea: Scatter of facility fine totals against their count of harm-level citations, naming the homes that harm most and pay least.
harm_angle: When the fine is smaller than a week of profit, a resident's harm is priced as a cost of business.
caveat: Harm counts come from the deficiencies table; fine_amount cast unverified.

title: Payment denial length distribution
idea: Distribution of denial-of-payment durations in days by state, showing which states use the real enforcement lever and which never do.
harm_angle: Denial of payment is the penalty operators actually feel, so where it is unused nothing changes.
caveat: Denial fields may be sparse; length may be text.

title: Enforcement intensity timeline
idea: Total fine dollars and penalty counts by quarter, showing enforcement rising and falling with administrations.
harm_angle: Enforcement that swings with politics leaves residents protected only in some years.
caveat: penalty_date parse quality unknown; recent quarters may be incomplete.

title: Chains absorbing many fines
idea: Facilities grouped by provider-name family and ranked by total fines, revealing chains that carry penalties across dozens of homes.
harm_angle: A chain that treats fines as overhead spreads the same neglect across every home it owns.
caveat: No owner id column here, so chain grouping must be inferred from names, which is fuzzy.

title: Who pays the most doctors
idea: Ranked bars of manufacturers by total payment dollars and by count of distinct physicians paid to show breadth versus depth of industry influence.
harm_angle: Payments shape prescribing and the patient never sees the invoice that changed their treatment.
caveat: Manufacturer names are not normalised so one company appears under several strings.

title: Payment nature by specialty
idea: Heatmap grid of physician specialty by nature of payment (food travel consulting speaking royalty) to show which specialties get bought with meals and which with royalties.
harm_angle: A twenty-dollar lunch measurably shifts prescribing so the cheapest influence is the most widespread harm.
caveat: Specialty text is free-form and long; needs grouping.

title: Payment concentration curve
idea: Distribution showing what share of all industry dollars goes to the top one percent of paid physicians to reveal extreme concentration.
harm_angle: A small circle of highly paid key opinion leaders sets treatment norms for everyone else's patients.
caveat: 15M rows; aggregation cost is real though the shape is simple.

title: Payments by state per physician
idea: Map of states by average industry payment per physician to show geographic hot spots of marketing intensity.
harm_angle: Patients in heavily marketed states get the newest and most expensive drug for conditions with cheap alternatives.
caveat: Needs a physician-count denominator which this table can only approximate from distinct NPI.

title: Teaching hospital money flow
idea: Flow diagram from manufacturers to teaching hospitals showing which academic centres take the most industry money.
harm_angle: Academic centres train the next generation of doctors so industry money there compounds across careers.
caveat: Teaching hospital name is only populated for the teaching-hospital recipient type.

title: Physician ownership stakes
idea: Ranked bars of manufacturers by the number of paid physicians who also hold an ownership indicator to expose doctors with equity in what they prescribe.
harm_angle: A doctor who owns stock in a device profits directly from implanting it in you.
caveat: Ownership indicator on general payments may be nearly always 'No'; ownership detail lives in a separate CMS file.

title: Pandemic-year payment pattern
idea: Timeline of monthly payment totals across the 2022 program year by nature of payment to show which categories rebounded after the pandemic collapse in in-person marketing.
harm_angle: The return of in-person industry marketing to clinics is a return of its documented effect on prescribing.
caveat: Date of payment may be text; single program year limits the trend.

title: Payments to non-physician recipients
idea: Ranked bars of covered recipient primary type showing how much money flows to nurse practitioners and physician assistants now that they can prescribe.
harm_angle: Industry moved its marketing to the fastest-growing and least-scrutinised prescriber groups.
caveat: PY2022 was the first full year covering these recipient types so comparisons to earlier years are invalid.

title: Manufacturer home state versus recipient state
idea: Flow diagram of payments from manufacturer state to recipient state to show the geography of who funds whose doctors.
harm_angle: Concentrated manufacturer money into a handful of states shapes regional standards of care.
caveat: Manufacturer state is the submitting entity address not necessarily where decisions are made.

title: Small payments many times
idea: Distribution of payment amounts on a log scale by nature of payment to show that the bulk of industry contact is thousands of tiny meals not big cheques.
harm_angle: Regulation focused on large payments misses the millions of small ones that actually move prescribing.
caveat: 14.7M rows; log binning needed or the chart is one spike.

title: Specialty concentration ranked
idea: Ranked bars of specialties by total dollars received divided by the number of physicians in that specialty to normalise for how many doctors exist.
harm_angle: The most heavily paid specialties per head are where a patient should ask hardest why this drug.
caveat: Denominator of practising physicians per specialty is not in this table.

title: Form of payment mix
idea: Heatmap of manufacturer by form of payment (cash in-kind stock) to identify companies paying doctors in equity rather than fees.
harm_angle: Paying a doctor in stock ties their personal wealth to how many patients get the product.
caveat: Form of payment vocabulary unknown; stock may be rare in general payments.

title: Specialty makeup of paid recipients
idea: Ranked bars of primary specialty among covered recipients on industry payment rosters, showing which specialties industry courts most.
harm_angle: Specialties heaviest on industry money are where prescribing pressure lands on patients.
caveat: This is the roster, not the payments; dollar volume needs the payment tables.

title: Multi-state license holders
idea: Distribution of recipients by number of state licenses held, showing the multi-state prescriber population.
harm_angle: Multi-state licensure lets a disciplined prescriber keep working across the state line.
caveat: Later license slots may be almost entirely blank.

title: Alias and shadow profile network
idea: Recipients whose alternate name fields differ from their primary name, plus profiles linked by associated-profile ids, drawn as identity clusters.
harm_angle: Duplicate identities let a payment history be split so no single record looks alarming.
caveat: Associated-profile fields may be mostly null; alternate names may be routine variants.

title: NPI coverage of the roster
idea: Share of covered-recipient profiles with a usable NPI, by profile type and state, showing where the industry-payment record cannot be tied to a real provider.
harm_angle: Payments that cannot be linked to a licensed provider are payments no patient can look up.
caveat: npi is kept as text and may be blank or sentinel-masked; count distinct before trusting.

title: Opioid treatment deserts
idea: Map of the roughly fifteen hundred opioid treatment programs by ZIP, showing wide areas with no methadone access at all.
harm_angle: No nearby treatment program means a daily-dosing patient cannot get treatment at all.
caveat: Only 1558 rows and no coordinates so ZIP centroid mapping only; no overdose denominator in this table.

title: When programs came online
idea: Timeline of Medicare effective dates for opioid treatment programs, showing the rollout wave and where it stalled.
harm_angle: Late-arriving states left patients years without covered treatment.
caveat: Effective date field may be text or sparsely populated.

title: Programs per state ranked
idea: Programs per state, ranked, the plain floor chart of who has capacity.
harm_angle: Thin state capacity is the first thing a person seeking treatment runs into.
caveat: No capacity or slot count in the table, only site counts.

title: Doctors opting out of Medicare
idea: Timeline of opt-out effective dates by specialty, showing which specialties are walking away from Medicare and when the exodus accelerated.
harm_angle: Every opt-out is a door closing on seniors who cannot pay cash.
caveat: Date fields cast unverified; opt-outs auto-renew, so end dates may mislead.

title: Opt-out concentration map
idea: Opt-out providers per ZIP mapped, showing wealthy areas where a large share of a specialty has left the program.
harm_angle: Concentrated opt-out creates cash-only medical neighborhoods that seniors are priced out of.
caveat: Provider ZIP is the practice address; no denominator of total providers per ZIP in this table.

title: Which specialties leave
idea: Ranked bars of specialties by opt-out count, exposing psychiatry and other concierge-heavy fields.
harm_angle: Psychiatry opting out at scale is why insured patients cannot find a covered psychiatrist.
caveat: Share of specialty requires a denominator from a provider registry not in this table.

title: Opted out but still referring
idea: Cross-tab of opted-out providers by whether they remain eligible to order and refer, showing providers outside the program who still steer its spending.
harm_angle: Providers outside the program still directing its money is accountability with a hole in it.
caveat: Eligibility flag coding unverified.

title: Referral privilege coverage grid
idea: Heatmap of the five ordering privileges covering part B, equipment, home health, power mobility and hospice, showing how many providers hold each combination.
harm_angle: The privilege combinations map exactly onto the service lines with the worst fraud histories.
caveat: Flags are likely Y/N text; no dates, so a snapshot only.

title: Power mobility gatekeepers
idea: Count of providers eligible to order power mobility devices, showing how narrow that gate is.
harm_angle: Power wheelchair schemes run through a small set of signing providers and counting them sizes the choke point.
caveat: This table has no state column, so geography needs a join to a provider registry.

title: Name collisions in the referral list
idea: Distribution of how many NPIs share the exact same first and last name in the referral roster, showing the identity ambiguity investigators face.
harm_angle: Ambiguous identities let a sanctioned provider hide behind a common name.
caveat: Mostly a data-quality view; thin on human harm without a sanctions list to compare against.

source_names: Medicare Part D Prescribers by Provider
title: Opioid prescribing rate outliers
idea: Map or ranked bars of prescribers by opioid prescribing rate within specialty to find the extreme tail after controlling for what they do.
harm_angle: Communities with a handful of extreme opioid prescribers carry the addiction and overdose burden for decades after.
caveat: Specialty adjustment is essential — pain and oncology prescribers legitimately top the raw list.

source_names: Medicare Part D Prescribers by Provider
title: Antipsychotics in the elderly
idea: Distribution of antipsychotic claims for beneficiaries over sixty-five by prescriber type to show off-label chemical restraint of older patients.
harm_angle: Antipsychotics given to dementia patients to keep them quiet raise their death rate and are widely used anyway.
caveat: Suppression flags blank out small counts which hides small facilities.

source_names: Medicare Part D Prescribers by Provider
title: Low-income subsidy patient burden
idea: Scatter of the low-income-subsidy share of a prescriber's drug cost against their total cost per beneficiary to show who serves the poorest and at what cost.
harm_angle: Prescribers serving mostly subsidy patients are the thin layer keeping poor seniors medicated.
caveat: LIS cost fields carry their own suppression flags.

source_names: Medicare Part D Prescribers by Provider
title: Brand loyalty by rurality
idea: Heatmap of RUCA rurality band by specialty coloured by brand share of claims to see whether rural prescribers use more or fewer generics.
harm_angle: Higher brand use anywhere means patients paying more out of pocket for the same effect.
caveat: Brand and generic claim counts have separate suppression flags.

source_names: Medicare Part D Prescribers by Provider
title: Antibiotic prescribing intensity map
idea: Map of states by antibiotic claims per thousand beneficiaries to show the geography of overprescribing that drives resistance.
harm_angle: Antibiotic resistance created by overprescribing kills patients who never took the unnecessary prescription.
caveat: Denominator choice (beneficiaries vs claims) changes the map substantially.

source_names: CMS Medicare Part D Prescribers by Provider and Drug
title: Opioid prescribing outliers
idea: Scatter of total day supply against beneficiary count per prescriber for opioid drugs, with the far-outlier prescribers named.
harm_angle: Extreme prescribers supply the pills that kill people in their own county.
caveat: DY2022 single-year snapshot; suppression flags mean small-count prescribers are hidden, biasing the tails.

source_names: CMS Medicare Part D Prescribers by Provider and Drug
title: Brand versus generic by geography
idea: State map of the brand share of total drug cost, showing where beneficiaries pay for brand when a generic exists.
harm_angle: Brand-heavy prescribing drains the same beneficiaries' out-of-pocket money for no clinical gain.
caveat: Brand and generic distinction must be derived by comparing brnd_name to gnrc_name; 25.9M rows makes this heavy.

source_names: CMS Medicare Part D Prescribers by Provider and Drug
title: Cost per claim by specialty
idea: Distribution of cost per claim by prescriber specialty, showing which specialties drive the most expensive prescribing.
harm_angle: Beneficiaries in high-cost specialties hit the coverage gap sooner and skip doses.
caveat: prscrbr_type and prscrbr_type_src may disagree; specialty text needs normalization.

source_names: CMS Medicare Part D Prescribers by Provider and Drug
title: The 65-plus suppression map
idea: Heatmap grid of state by drug shaded by how often the over-65 counts are suppressed, showing where the data goes dark on the oldest patients.
harm_angle: Suppression protects privacy but also hides small-town prescribing patterns from scrutiny.
caveat: Suppression flag values and meanings unverified from metadata alone.

source_names: CMS Medicare Part D Prescribers by Provider and Drug
title: Single-drug prescribers
idea: Ranked bars of prescribers whose claims concentrate almost entirely in one drug, the pill-mill signature.
harm_angle: Concentration in one high-risk drug is the clearest data signature of a mill harming patients.
caveat: Legitimate specialists (oncology, HIV) will look identical; needs specialty controls.

title: Pending non-physician enrollment queue
idea: Count of non-physician applications sitting in the initial enrollment queue, shown beside the physician queue for scale.
harm_angle: Every pending application is a clinician not yet able to see Medicare patients.
caveat: Only three columns, no dates and no geography; genuinely thin and snapshot-only, which is why there are just two ideas.

title: Pending applicants already enrolled
idea: Overlap between the pending queue and the active enrollment roster by NPI, testing whether pending applicants are new or re-applying.
harm_angle: Re-applicants may be providers previously removed quietly coming back in.
caveat: Requires the enrollment table as a second source; NPI population in this thin table unverified.

title: Physician enrollment backlog size
idea: Count of physicians pending initial enrollment shown against the non-physician queue, as the plain size of the onboarding bottleneck.
harm_angle: A long queue means doctors ready to work cannot bill for seniors yet.
caveat: Three columns and no dates; the trend that would matter is not available from a snapshot, so only two ideas here.

title: Pending versus opted-out overlap
idea: NPIs appearing both in the pending queue and the opt-out affidavit list, surfacing providers re-entering after opting out.
harm_angle: Providers cycling in and out of Medicare create coverage gaps their patients absorb.
caveat: Cross-table by construction; the overlap may be near zero.

title: Terminated facilities timeline
idea: Timeline of facility program terminations by category and state to map where Medicare participation is collapsing.
harm_angle: When facilities terminate in clusters the patients they served lose their only nearby option.
caveat: Termination code semantics unknown; voluntary and involuntary terminations mean very different things.

title: Ownership change churn
idea: Ranked bars of facilities by change-of-ownership count with the most-flipped facilities named to show assets traded repeatedly between operators.
harm_angle: Every ownership flip resets staffing and management and residents absorb the disruption.
caveat: chow_cnt may be a cumulative counter of unknown reset behaviour.

title: Specialty bed capacity by state
idea: Heatmap of state by specialty bed type (AIDS Alzheimer's ventilator paediatric head trauma) to show which states have literally zero beds for a condition.
harm_angle: A family whose state has no ventilator or head-trauma beds must move across the country or give up.
caveat: Specialty bed counts are self-reported and often zero-filled rather than null.

title: Compliance status by control type
idea: Distribution of compliance status codes by general control type (for-profit nonprofit government) to test whether ownership predicts staying compliant.
harm_angle: Facility types that chronically fall out of compliance keep operating and residents keep living there.
caveat: Compliance code values unknown from metadata.

title: Multi-facility organizations mapped
idea: Network or ranked bars of multi-facility organization names by how many CCNs and beds they control to reveal the real operators behind facility names.
harm_angle: The corporate parent making staffing decisions is invisible to families choosing a facility by its local name.
caveat: Organization name is free text so entity resolution is required before counting.

title: Regulatory waivers granted
idea: Heatmap of state by which waivers facilities hold (24-hour RN room size sprinkler) to show where safety rules are routinely waived.
harm_angle: A waived 24-hour nurse requirement means a resident's night-time crisis is met by nobody licensed.
caveat: Waiver switches may be very sparsely used making the heatmap mostly blank.

title: Small practices punished by scoring
idea: Distribution of final score and payment adjustment split by practice size and rural status, showing small rural practices clustered at the penalty end.
harm_angle: Penalizing the small rural practice pushes it to close and its patients lose the only clinic in town.
caveat: Score fields cast unverified; year coverage not visible in the model.

title: Safety net penalty gradient
idea: Scatter of final score against dual-eligibility ratio with safety-net status colored, testing whether serving poorer patients mechanically lowers your score.
harm_angle: A scoring system that penalizes serving the poor defunds exactly the clinics the poor rely on.
caveat: complex_patient_bonus is meant to offset this and whether it does is the real question; needs careful reading.

title: Who invokes hardship exemptions
idea: Share of clinicians with extreme-circumstance or hardship reweighting by state and practice size, showing who can work the exemption machinery.
harm_angle: Exemptions available only to those who know to ask are a hidden subsidy to the well-resourced.
caveat: Exemption flags may encode multiple meanings; the reweighting fields are numerous and overlapping.

title: Non-reporting clinician map
idea: Share of clinicians flagged non-reporting by state and shortage-area status, showing where the quality program simply is not being played.
harm_angle: Non-reporting concentrated in shortage areas means the patients with least care are also unmeasured.
caveat: non_reporting semantics unverified and may include exempt clinicians.

title: Score versus billing scale
idea: Scatter of final score against allowed charges and Medicare patient count, showing whether high scores simply track size and back-office sophistication.
harm_angle: If the score measures paperwork capacity rather than care, patients at small clinics are punished for nothing.
caveat: Charge and patient count fields cast unverified.

title: Rural health clinic coverage map
idea: Rural health clinics mapped by ZIP with state fill, showing the rural areas the program never reached.
harm_angle: A rural county with no clinic means the nearest primary care is an hour away.
caveat: No dates so snapshot only; ZIP centroid mapping only.

title: Rural clinic ownership shift
idea: Proprietary versus nonprofit share of rural health clinics by state, showing where rural primary care went investor-owned.
harm_angle: Investor-owned rural clinics close faster when margins thin, and the town has no fallback.
caveat: Ownership coding unverified.

title: Rural clinic formation timeline
idea: Rural health clinics by incorporation year, showing whether new rural primary care is still being built.
harm_angle: A flat formation line means no replacement for the rural clinics that close.
caveat: incorporation_date is a cast and may be widely null.

title: Rural clinic chain clusters
idea: Organizations operating rural clinics across many states, ranked, revealing national operators behind local-looking clinics.
harm_angle: When a distant operator owns the only rural clinic, closure decisions are made far from the patients.
caveat: associate_id grouping semantics unverified; name matching is fuzzy.

title: Nursing facility affiliation network
idea: Network of skilled nursing facilities linked by affiliation entity id, showing the ownership webs behind homes that appear independent.
harm_angle: Families cannot see that a dozen homes answer to one owner with one record.
caveat: affiliation_entity_id population unverified and may be largely blank; count distinct before trusting.

title: Chain footprint by state
idea: Ranked bars of affiliation entities by number of facilities and states covered, sizing the biggest nursing chains.
harm_angle: Chain scale determines how many residents a single management decision affects.
caveat: Affiliation fields may be sparse.

title: Ownership structure mix
idea: Distribution of facilities by organization type structure and proprietary status, showing the dominance of limited-liability structures in elder care.
harm_angle: Layered corporate structures are how liability is kept away from the residents harmed.
caveat: Type coding unverified.

title: Facilities that changed names
idea: Facilities where the nursing home provider name differs from the enrolled organization name or trade name, mapped, surfacing rebrands that reset a home's public reputation.
harm_angle: A rebranded home with the same owner sheds its citation history in the eyes of families searching online.
caveat: Name differences are often benign legal-versus-trade-name variation.

title: Opioid pills per person by county
idea: Map of buyer county coloured by total morphine milligram equivalents per resident over the period showing the counties flooded with pills.
harm_angle: The counties that received the most pills per person are the counties burying the most people.
caveat: Needs an external population denominator; 178M rows makes any full scan expensive.

title: Distributor to pharmacy flow
idea: Flow diagram from reporter (distributor) to buyer business activity showing which distributors supplied the pharmacies in the hardest-hit regions.
harm_angle: Distributors shipped volumes no pharmacy could dispense legitimately and the towns absorbed the difference.
caveat: Huge row count; needs pre-aggregation. reporter_family grouping quality unverified.

title: Pharmacies that took impossible volumes
idea: Ranked bars of individual buyer DEA numbers by MME received per year with the top outliers named to find the pill-mill pharmacies.
harm_angle: A single pharmacy taking millions of pills a year is the physical distribution point of a community's addiction.
caveat: A pharmacy inside a hospital or long-term care legitimately takes high volume; needs business-activity filtering.

title: When the shipments stopped
idea: Timeline of national MME shipped by drug showing the peak and the abrupt supply cutoff that pushed dependent patients toward street supply.
harm_angle: When legal supply was cut without treatment capacity dependent patients moved to fentanyl and death rates rose.
caveat: Date coverage of the loaded extract is unverified; ARCOS public data historically ends around 2019.

title: Manufacturer to labeler chain
idea: Network of company name to labeler name to reporter showing the corporate chain of custody from maker to the counties hit hardest.
harm_angle: Mapping the whole chain shows the harm was manufactured upstream not created by a few crooked pharmacists.
caveat: Name fields are free text at massive scale; entity resolution is the whole problem.

title: Drug mix shift over time
idea: Stacked timeline of shipments by ingredient showing oxycodone giving way to hydrocodone and then to buprenorphine.
harm_angle: The substitution pattern shows whether the system moved patients to treatment or just moved the problem.
caveat: Buprenorphine may not be in the retail summary scope.

title: Opioid pills per person by county
idea: Map of morphine-equivalent volume shipped per resident by buyer county and year, the county-level flood map of the opioid supply.
harm_angle: The counties buried in pills are the counties that buried people; this is the mechanism made visible.
