idea: Heatmap grid of gross income band against inspection outcome and eligibility testing whether poorer applicants are more often ruled insufficiently damaged.
harm_angle: If low-income applicants are disproportionately ruled out at inspection, the process itself is the harm.
caveat: Income may be self-reported and heavily missing; truncated load.

title: Households With Elderly Or Access Needs
idea: Cohort grid of registrations by presence of occupants 65 and over and the access and functional needs flag against award outcome and shelter need.
harm_angle: The households least able to self-recover are the ones whose outcomes matter most.
caveat: Access-needs flag may be sparsely recorded; truncated load.

title: Applied Date To Aid Clock
idea: Distribution of days between applied date and rental assistance end date by disaster showing how long help actually lasts.
harm_angle: Short assistance windows push displaced families back into unstable housing before repairs finish.
caveat: Date columns are cast from text and may fail to parse; truncated load.

title: Communities Outside The Flood Program
idea: Map of communities by flood-program participation flag highlighting non-participating communities where residents cannot buy federal flood insurance.
harm_angle: Residents of non-participating communities are uninsurable against the flood that is coming.
caveat: Community-to-geography mapping is by name only; no coordinates in the model.

title: Flood Maps Decades Out Of Date
idea: Distribution and map of years since the currently effective flood map date exposing communities being priced and permitted off ancient maps.
harm_angle: Homes built to a 1980s flood map flood in a 2020s storm and the owners had no warning.
caveat: Effective map date is parsed from a messy text field with a two-digit year; parse failures likely.

title: Who Gets The Flood Discount
idea: Ranked bars of states by average community rating discount alongside the share of communities with no rating at all.
harm_angle: Discounts reward communities with staff and money to do paperwork while poorer places pay full premiums.
caveat: Most communities likely have no rating, so averages must exclude them explicitly.

title: Tribal Communities In The Flood Program
idea: Dot plot comparing tribal and non-tribal communities on participation rate, map age and rating class.
harm_angle: If tribal communities have older maps and no discounts, flood risk falls hardest where it is least funded.
caveat: Tribal flag population unverified; tribal community count may be small.

title: Half A Century Of Program Entry
idea: Timeline of community entry into the flood program by original entry date colored by whether they are still participating.
harm_angle: Baseline of when the flood safety net was built and where it has since been abandoned.

source_names: FHFA House Price Index Master File
title: Two Decades of Divergence
idea: Slope chart of house price index change from 2000 to the latest year for every county series, sorted so the fastest-appreciating and flat-lining counties sit at opposite ends.
harm_angle: People in flat-index counties build no housing wealth while owners elsewhere gain hundreds of thousands for free.
caveat: Index bases differ by series (1980/1991/1995) so cross-series comparison needs rebasing; county series are annual only.

source_names: FHFA House Price Index Master File
title: The Volatility Belt
idea: Map of counties shaded by the size of their largest peak-to-trough index drop, exposing where homeowners are most exposed to a crash.
harm_angle: Households in high-volatility counties lose their equity in downturns and are the first to fall underwater.
caveat: place_id is FHFA's own code and is not raw FIPS at every level, so mapping requires deriving FIPS; early periods have nulls or HPI=100 base.

source_names: FHFA House Price Index Master File
title: Seasonal Adjustment Gap
idea: Small multiples comparing the seasonally adjusted and unadjusted index for the same geographies, showing where the published headline number diverges most from raw prices.
harm_angle: Buyers and policymakers reading only the adjusted series can be misled about what a house actually costs this month.
caveat: index_sa exists only for national and division monthly series; nulls elsewhere.

source_names: FHFA House Price Index Master File
title: Where the Data Thins Out
idea: Heatmap grid of geography level against year showing coverage counts and standard-error size, exposing which places the federal price index barely measures.
harm_angle: Communities with no reliable price index are invisible to the mortgage and appraisal system that uses it.
caveat: rstderr may be blank for most series; coverage is a metadata chart, harm link is indirect.

source_names: FHFA House Price Index Master File
title: Tract-Level Price Cliffs
idea: Map neighboring census tracts by index level and highlight adjacent tract pairs with the widest gap -- the invisible lines where property value falls off a cliff.
harm_angle: A hard price line between adjacent blocks is usually a boundary someone drew, and the people on the wrong side inherit it.
caveat: Tract series are annual and sparse; adjacency requires external geometry; place_id-to-tract-FIPS derivation is unverified.

source_names: FHFA National Mortgage Database Public Use File
title: Mortgage Distress by Metro
idea: Timeline of the delinquency and performance statistics for each metro, small-multipled, showing which housing markets carry chronic distress rather than a one-off shock.
harm_angle: Persistently high delinquency metros are places where families are one paycheck from losing the house.
caveat: statistic_name is a long free-text catalog; picking the right statistic requires a value inventory this pass cannot run.

source_names: FHFA National Mortgage Database Public Use File
title: What the Sample Can and Cannot See
idea: Heatmap grid of dataset family against geography type, counting available statistics, exposing which mortgage questions simply cannot be asked at local level.
harm_angle: Local harms invisible in a national 5% sample never make it into federal housing policy.
caveat: 19M rows means a heavy aggregate; geo_type value set unverified.

source_names: FHFA National Mortgage Database Public Use File
title: New Loans vs Outstanding Stress
idea: Dual timeline per state of new-origination volume against outstanding-loan performance, revealing markets where lenders keep writing new loans into a distressed book.
harm_angle: Fresh lending into an already-distressed market sets up the next wave of foreclosures on the same families.
caveat: Requires matching two statistic_name families that may not share geography or period grain.

source_names: FHFA National Mortgage Database Public Use File
title: Release Lag Audit
idea: Scatter of release date against the period the statistic covers, showing how stale the mortgage picture is when the public finally sees it.
harm_angle: Housing distress that takes a year to publish is a year of families the system did not warn.
caveat: release_date parsed with try_to_date so may be widely null; period_value is a double, not a date.

title: Subsidized Housing and Neighborhood Poverty
idea: Scatter of tract poverty rate against tract minority share for every HUD project, sized by units. Shows whether assisted housing is systematically sited in the poorest, most segregated tracts.
harm_angle: Siting subsidized housing only in high-poverty tracts locks families into the conditions the subsidy was meant to escape.
caveat: Tract-level fields are contextual attachments; grain is project-level so tract stats repeat across projects in the same tract.

title: Who Lives in HUD Housing
idea: Small multiples per program of the demographic percentage columns — female-headed, disabled, elderly, minority — showing how tenant profile differs by program type.
harm_angle: Different HUD programs serve very different people, and the least-funded programs often serve the most vulnerable.
caveat: Percent columns are suppressed for small projects and may be blank rather than zero.

title: The Waiting Time Map
idea: Map of projects colored by months waiting, showing where families queue years for a unit and where they walk in.
harm_angle: Years on a waitlist is years in unsafe or unaffordable housing for a real family.
caveat: months_waiting is an average of current tenants' prior wait, not current queue length — very easy to misread.

title: Projects That Stopped Reporting
idea: Distribution of months since last report and percent reported per project and program, exposing the projects HUD has no current data on at all.
harm_angle: Unreported projects are tenants whose conditions nobody at HUD is watching.
caveat: Reporting gaps may reflect program rules rather than neglect; program context is essential to avoid a false accusation.

title: Rent Burden Versus Tenant Income
idea: Scatter of household income against rent per month and subsidy spending per month, colored by program. Shows where the subsidy covers the gap and where it does not.
harm_angle: When the subsidy does not close the gap, the household eats the difference out of food and medicine.
caveat: Project-level averages hide the worst-off households inside each project.

title: Overcrowding and Bedroom Mix
idea: Heatmap grid of bedroom-size mix against people per unit and percent overhoused, by program, revealing where unit stock does not match family size.
harm_angle: A family of six in a two-bedroom is a housing authority's inventory problem lived out by children.
caveat: The overhoused measure covers too-large units; the crowded direction must be inferred from people per unit against bedroom mix.

title: What HUD Actually Publishes
idea: Ranked bars of HUD datasets by how many geographies and years each one covers, exposing which housing programs are documented and which are effectively dark.
harm_angle: Programs with no published data cannot be audited, so their failures land on tenants unseen.
caveat: Only 77 rows -- this is a dataset index or a thin extract, not program-level data.

title: HUD Coverage Holes by State
idea: Map shading states by how many HUD datasets carry any value for them, showing which states the federal housing record barely covers.
harm_angle: States absent from HUD's own data get no federal scrutiny of their housing conditions.
caveat: 77 rows makes state coverage nearly meaningless; fips and zip population unverified.

title: The EIN Column Nobody Uses
idea: Dot plot of HUD records that carry an organization EIN against those that do not, by dataset, flagging the bridge that would connect housing programs to corporate filings.
harm_angle: Without a usable organization id, the landlords and developers taking HUD money cannot be traced to their other conduct.
caveat: EIN may be entirely blank or sentinel-masked -- a bare null check has produced false full-population readings on this platform before.

title: Who Originates FHA Loans
idea: Ranked bars of originating mortgagees by loan count and average interest rate exposing lenders charging more for the same government-backed product.
harm_angle: Borrowers steered to a high-rate lender pay tens of thousands more for an identical federal guarantee.
caveat: Snapshot only; rate differences may reflect time period rather than lender behavior.

title: Rate Spread By County
idea: County map of average insured interest rate for the same endorsement period showing geographic pricing differences.
harm_angle: Same federal guarantee, different price depending on your zip code, is textbook modern redlining.
caveat: County names without FIPS may be ambiguous; the snapshot may cover a single vintage only.

title: Down Payment Source Patterns
idea: Heatmap grid of down payment source against loan purpose and property type showing reliance on gifts and seller-funded assistance.
harm_angle: Buyers who need gifted down payments are the thinnest-margin borrowers most likely to default.
caveat: Source categories may be sparse or lumped into an other bucket.

title: Sponsors Behind The Originators
idea: Network of sponsor to originating mortgagee showing how a few sponsors sit behind many originator brands.
harm_angle: Consumers think they chose a lender when often they chose one storefront of the same sponsor.
caveat: Sponsor number may be blank for retail originations.

title: Endorsement Volume Seasonality
idea: Timeline of endorsement counts by year and month showing insured lending volume through rate cycles.
harm_angle: Volume collapses show when first-time buyers were priced out of the market entirely.
caveat: Snapshot coverage window unknown from metadata.

title: Federally Backed Apartments By State
idea: State map of firm commitment mortgage amounts and total units showing where federal multifamily money actually goes.
harm_angle: States getting little federal multifamily money build fewer affordable apartments.
caveat: Fiscal year coverage window unverified.

title: Refinance Versus New Construction
idea: Timeline of mortgage amount split between new construction, substantial rehab and refinancing activity by fiscal year.
harm_angle: If most federal money refinances existing buildings, no new affordable units are being created.
caveat: Activity grouping needs interpretation of program codes.

title: Lenders Capturing The Insurance
idea: Ranked bars of lenders by total insured mortgage amount and unit count showing concentration in the multifamily program.
harm_angle: A handful of lenders steering federal housing insurance decide which projects get built.
caveat: Lender names are free text with spelling variants.

title: Subsidy Stacking Patterns
idea: Heatmap grid of projects by which subsidy flags they carry (tax credits, tax-exempt bonds, HOME, block grants, HOPE VI) showing how deals are assembled.
harm_angle: Deals needing five stacked subsidies reveal how broken the economics of affordable housing are.
caveat: Flag columns may be Y/N text or blank rather than boolean.

title: Cost Per Unit Rising
idea: Scatter of mortgage amount against total units by fiscal year with the implied cost-per-unit trend line.
harm_angle: Rising cost per unit means each federal dollar houses fewer families than it did.
caveat: Unit counts of zero would break the ratio and must be filtered.

title: The Rent Subsidy Expiration Cliff
idea: Timeline of assisted units by contract expiration date showing the wave of affordability protections about to lapse.
harm_angle: Every expiring contract is a set of households who may lose their rent protection.
caveat: Contracts are routinely renewed, so expiration is a risk signal not a guaranteed loss.

title: Rents Above Fair Market
idea: Distribution of the rent-to-fair-market-rent ratio across contracts split by program type showing where subsidized rents exceed the local benchmark.
harm_angle: Above-market subsidized rents mean fewer families housed for the same federal dollar.
caveat: Ratio definition and vintage unverified.

title: Family Sized Units Are Scarce
idea: Ranked bars of total assisted units by bedroom count showing how few three-plus bedroom subsidized units exist.
harm_angle: Large families cannot use a stock of studios and one-bedrooms, so they stay on waitlists forever.
caveat: Bedroom counts may be zero-filled where unreported.

title: Short Contract Terms Cluster
idea: Distribution of contract term months by program type and administering party showing which properties get one-year renewals instead of long commitments.
harm_angle: Short-term renewals keep tenants and owners in permanent uncertainty about the building's future.
caveat: Term quantity may include renewal stubs that distort the distribution.

title: Contract Status Over Time
idea: Timeline of contracts by status name and effective date showing terminations versus active contracts.
harm_angle: Terminated contracts are units that left the affordable stock permanently.
caveat: Status vocabulary unverified.

title: Vacant Public Housing Amid Waitlists
idea: Map of housing authorities by vacancy percentage and unit count highlighting large authorities sitting on empty units.
harm_angle: Empty public housing units while families sleep in cars is the sharpest form of this harm.
caveat: Vacancy may reflect units offline for renovation rather than mismanagement.

title: Capital Funding Versus Portfolio Size
idea: Scatter of capital fund amount per unit against total units colored by performance designation showing which authorities are starved of repair money.
harm_angle: Underfunded capital budgets are why public housing tenants live with mold, leaks and broken elevators.
caveat: Performance designation vocabulary unverified; funding may be reported inconsistently.

title: Troubled Authorities And Their Tenants
idea: Ranked bars of authorities designated troubled weighted by occupied units and share of elderly and disabled residents.
harm_angle: A troubled designation means the people most dependent on housing are being failed by their landlord of last resort.
caveat: Designation may be stale relative to the snapshot date.

title: Spending Per Unit Year Over Year
idea: Slope chart of monthly spending against the prior year figure per authority revealing sudden funding cuts.
harm_angle: A sharp cut in operating spend shows up as unrepaired heating and unanswered maintenance calls.
caveat: Only two periods available, so this is a change snapshot not a trend.

title: Who Lives In Public Housing
idea: Heatmap grid of authorities by resident composition (elderly share, disabled share, children count) against median income and urban versus rural status.
harm_angle: Names the actual population depending on each authority so funding decisions have faces attached.
caveat: Composition percentages may be self-reported and stale.

title: Reporting Compliance Gaps
idea: Distribution of percent reported by authority size exposing large authorities submitting incomplete data.
harm_angle: Authorities that do not report cannot be held to account for the conditions their tenants live in.
caveat: Reporting fields may relate to a specific form not identified in the model.

source_names: Mapping Inequality: Redlining in New Deal America
title: The 1930s Grades Redrawn
idea: Map every HOLC neighborhood polygon colored by its A-through-D grade across all roughly 200 cities, so the national scale of the grading system is visible in one frame.
harm_angle: Every D-graded neighborhood is a place where federal policy told lenders not to invest, and residents paid for generations.
caveat: geometry may be stored as text needing parsing; 1155 rows suggests city-level or partial coverage rather than all polygons.

source_names: Mapping Inequality: Redlining in New Deal America
title: Which Cities Got Graded Hardest
idea: Ranked bars of cities by the share of their mapped area given a C or D grade, showing where the federal graders were most punitive.
harm_angle: Cities graded almost entirely hazardous were written out of the mortgage market wholesale.
caveat: Share-of-area needs polygon area; row counts per city are an imperfect proxy.

source_names: Mapping Inequality: Redlining in New Deal America
title: The Language of the Downgrade
idea: Text-frequency comparison of the area descriptions for A-graded versus D-graded neighborhoods, surfacing the explicit racial and ethnic terms that justified each grade.
harm_angle: The written justifications name the residents whose presence was itself treated as a reason to deny credit.
caveat: area_description_data is likely nested or semi-structured; text mining quality is unverified.

source_names: Mapping Inequality: Redlining in New Deal America
title: Grades Stacked by State
idea: Distribution of HOLC grades within each state as stacked bars, ordered by the D-grade share, giving a state ranking of federal downgrading.
harm_angle: States with the heaviest D-grade share carry the deepest inherited wealth gap.
caveat: Only cities HOLC surveyed are present, so state totals are not population-representative.

source_names: Mapping Inequality: Redlining in New Deal America
title: Grade Boundaries as Fault Lines
idea: Zoomed map of adjacent A-and-D polygon pairs across all cities, isolating the exact street lines where the federal grade flipped from best to hazardous.
harm_angle: A single street separating 'best' from 'hazardous' shows the grade was about who lived there, not about the housing.
caveat: Adjacency detection needs real geometry parsing; geometry field format unverified.

title: Rural affordable housing cliff
idea: Timeline of units whose restrictive clause or tax credit expires each year ahead, showing the wave of rural apartments about to lose affordability protection.
harm_angle: Every expiring clause is a specific number of rural households who can be priced out of their home on a known date.
caveat: Date parsing uses a fixed MM/DD/YYYY format; rows in another format become null and would understate the cliff.

title: Map of rural subsidised housing
idea: Point map of every active project using its own latitude and longitude, sized by unit count and coloured by share of units on rental assistance.
harm_angle: Shows exactly where the rural safety-net housing stock physically is, and where whole regions have none.
caveat: Lat/long parsed from text; zeros or nulls would pile projects in the ocean and need filtering.

title: Landlords behind the portfolio
idea: Ranked bars of management companies by total units and by total rental-assistance units, naming the firms that run most of rural subsidised housing.
harm_angle: A handful of management companies control the housing of tens of thousands of low-income rural tenants who have nowhere else to go.
caveat: MANAGEMENT_NAME is free text needing deduplication; borrower_id may be the more reliable operator key.

title: Vacancy against accessibility
idea: Scatter of vacant units against accessible units per project, coloured by state, to find whether accessible stock sits empty or is chronically full.
harm_angle: Disabled rural tenants have the thinnest housing options of anyone; the accessible unit count is the whole supply.
caveat: Vacancy is a snapshot with no date; a point-in-time vacancy figure may be stale.

title: Bedroom mix versus county
idea: Heatmap grid of county against bedroom-size mix, showing where the rural stock is all studios and one-beds and families simply cannot be housed.
harm_angle: Families with children get squeezed out of the rural subsidised stock wherever the mix skews small.
caveat: FIPS code is text-trimmed and may include or omit the leading zero, breaking county joins.

title: Denial Rate by Race Holding Income
idea: Grid of denial rate by applicant_race_name_1 within income bands, per metro area. Viewer sees Black and Latino applicants denied at higher rates than white applicants with the same reported income.
chart_shape: heatmap grid of race against income band
harm_angle: This is the numeric shape of modern redlining - families denied a mortgage their income supported.
caveat: Income is the only control available here; without credit score and DTI the gap is suggestive not causal.

title: Denial Reasons by Neighborhood
idea: Map denial_reason_name_1 shares against tract minority_population percentage. Viewer sees which reasons cluster in majority-minority tracts.
chart_shape: scatter of tract minority share against reason share
harm_angle: Credit-history and collateral denials concentrated in minority tracts are the mechanism, not the excuse.
caveat: Denial reason reporting was optional for some agencies - coverage varies by regulator.

title: High-Cost Loans by Tract
idea: Map rate_spread and hoepa_status concentrations against tract_to_msamd_income. Viewer sees expensive credit funneled into poorer tracts.
harm_angle: High-cost lending strips wealth from the exact neighborhoods with the least of it.
caveat: rate_spread is only reported above a threshold, so most loans are blank by design.

title: Lenders Who Only Lend Where It Is White
idea: For each respondent_id, plot the minority-population profile of the tracts it lent in against its total volume. Viewer sees lenders whose entire book avoids minority tracts.
chart_shape: scatter of volume against tract minority share
harm_angle: A lender that never lends in a neighborhood is redlining whether or not it ever denies anyone.
caveat: respondent_id is only unique within agency_code - must pair the two; 2015-2017 only.

title: Who Buys the Loan After
idea: Sankey from originating lender through purchaser_type_name. Viewer sees which lenders originate to immediately sell and to whom.
harm_angle: Originate-to-sell removes any incentive for the lender to care whether the borrower can pay.
caveat: Purchaser is only recorded for loans sold within the same calendar year.

title: Denial Gap With Real Controls
idea: The denial-rate-by-race grid controlling for debt_to_income_ratio, loan_to_value_ratio and credit score type. Viewer sees whether the racial gap survives the controls lenders always cite.
harm_angle: If the gap survives the lender own stated risk controls, the excuse collapses.
caveat: Explicitly a 17,474-row sample of a multi-million-row corpus per the model header - shape only, never a lending-pattern claim.

title: Closing Costs by Borrower Group
idea: Distribution of total_loan_costs, origination_charges and discount_points by derived_race and derived_sex.
harm_angle: Identical loans priced differently at the closing table is wealth extraction that never shows up in the interest rate.
caveat: 17k-row sample; cost fields are exempt from reporting for some institution classes.

title: Automated Underwriting Outcomes
idea: Cross the aus_1 through aus_5 system used against action_taken and derived_race. Viewer sees whether particular automated underwriting systems produce more denials for particular groups.
chart_shape: heatmap grid of system against outcome
harm_angle: An algorithm that denies one group more often is discrimination nobody has to sign their name to.
caveat: 17k-row sample is far too small for subgroup claims; AUS fields are frequently blank.

title: Manufactured Home Loan Terms
idea: Compare interest_rate, loan_term_months and prepayment_penalty_term for manufactured-home loans against site-built, by borrower group.
harm_angle: Manufactured-home buyers are the poorest homebuyers and are routinely sold the worst terms in the market.
caveat: Small sample; manufactured-home rows may be a handful of records.

title: Lenders That Never Bridged
idea: Show the 2017 respondent IDs that have no LEI match. Viewer sees the lenders whose pre-2018 and post-2018 records can never be linked.
chart_shape: ranked bars plus a coverage bar
harm_angle: Broken lender identity across the 2018 rule change makes long-run redlining patterns unprovable.
caveat: 5,399 rows and it is a crosswalk, not a story - value is as a bridge. Column names are inferred from the staging model name, not read from a select list.

title: One Lender Many Identities
idea: Find LEIs mapping to multiple 2017 respondent IDs, indicating consolidation across the identifier change.
harm_angle: Consolidation hidden behind an ID change lets a merged lender shed its old record.
caveat: Crosswalk completeness is unverified; a many-to-one may be a data artifact.

harm_angle: When the only public encounter table is nine rows, no one outside the agency can audit how people at the border are treated.
caveat: This is a metadata-about-the-gap chart, not a data finding; needs the upstream release for comparison.

idea: Stacked timeline of monthly encounters split by the per-country columns, showing how the nationality composition of enforcement shifts with policy changes.
harm_angle: Sharp shifts in which nationalities get enforced against reveal policy targeting rather than changing migration.

title: Border vs Interior Enforcement Split

harm_angle: Interior enforcement means arrests at homes, workplaces and courthouses, hitting settled families rather than new arrivals.
caveat: border and interior columns may be populated on only a subset of sheets; encounter_type taxonomy unverified.

title: Families in the Enforcement Machine
idea: Heatmap grid of family status against encounter type and month, showing which enforcement actions fall most on family units versus single adults.
harm_angle: Family-unit enforcement means children are inside the detention and removal process.

title: Criminality Label Under the Numbers

title: Sheet-Level Data Integrity Grid
idea: Heatmap of source file and sheet against which columns are populated, exposing that this single table is really a dozen incompatible published tables stacked.
harm_angle: Analysts who treat this as one table will publish wrong enforcement numbers about real people.
caveat: Purely diagnostic; no direct human harm shown, though it protects downstream claims.

title: Green Cards vs Removals Over Time
idea: Dual timeline of lawful permanent resident admissions against enforcement actions by fiscal year, showing when the country's front door narrows as the back door widens.
harm_angle: Every year removals outpace admissions is a year more families are split than joined.
caveat: Only 27 rows in the mart -- almost certainly a table index, not the full yearbook series.

idea: Ranked bars of visa classes by admission count with year-over-year change, showing which immigration pathways are quietly being throttled.

title: Country of Birth Field Is Suspect
idea: Dot plot of distinct values in country_of_birth and country_of_last_residence against row count, to show whether these join keys are real or empty.
harm_angle: A broken country field means nationality-based disparities in immigration outcomes cannot be checked at all.

source_names: OFLC Foreign Labor Certification Disclosure Data

source_names: OFLC Foreign Labor Certification Disclosure Data

harm_angle: Filing a senior job at Level 1 legally underpays the visa worker by tens of thousands a year.
caveat: pw_wage_level_1 value set unverified; employer_name needs normalizing since one company files under many spellings.

source_names: OFLC Foreign Labor Certification Disclosure Data
title: Denial Rates by Law Firm

harm_angle: Workers who paid a high-volume firm and got denied lose their status and their money at once.

source_names: OFLC Foreign Labor Certification Disclosure Data

harm_angle: Dense H-2A clusters are the places where housing, heat and wage abuses concentrate on workers with no ability to quit.

source_names: OFLC Foreign Labor Certification Disclosure Data
title: Willful Violators Still Certified
idea: Timeline of certifications granted to employers flagged as willful violators or H-1B dependent, showing whether the flag actually changes the outcome.
harm_angle: An employer already found to have willfully violated wage law keeps being handed more workers to violate against.

title: Only One Column Survived
idea: Ranked bars of the case_type values that are all this 12.6-million-row mart currently exposes, making the collapse of a rich FOIA dataset into one column the finding.
harm_angle: The richest record of how immigration courts treat people is landed but unusable, so nobody can audit those decisions.
caveat: The mart genuinely selects only case_type -- every other EOIR field is stranded in raw; this is a build gap, not a data story yet.

title: Case Type Mix Over Time
idea: Stacked timeline of immigration court case types once the date and court columns are exposed, showing how the docket composition shifts with each administration.
harm_angle: A docket flooded with one case type means judges spend minutes per person on life-or-death claims.

title: Judge-Level Grant Rate Grid
idea: Heatmap of immigration judges against asylum grant rate, ordered within each court, exposing the lottery of which judge a person draws.
harm_angle: Two people with identical claims get opposite outcomes based purely on the judge assigned.
caveat: Requires judge, decision and court columns that the current mart does not expose; classic finding but blocked on the model.

title: Detainers by Facility and Region

harm_angle: A county jail issuing thousands of detainers is a local government choosing to act as an immigration arm.
caveat: Facility geography is city and state text only; a real map needs geocoding. 609k person-level rows.

title: Detainers Where the Charge Is Nothing

harm_angle: Detainers issued against people with no criminal conviction are the sharpest test of the worst-first claim.

title: Threat Level Versus Actual Sentence

harm_angle: If the threat label does not track the sentence, the label is a discretionary judgment dressed as a fact.

title: Who Gets Detained by Country and Age

title: Detainers Lifted and Why

title: Apprehension Method Shift Over Time

title: Detention Far From Legal Help

title: Who Runs The Facilities
idea: Ranked bars of facility counts by detailed type separating contracted county jails, private operators and service processing centers.
harm_angle: Detention in a county jail contract means immigration detainees held under criminal jail conditions.

title: Detention By Area Of Responsibility
idea: Heatmap grid of area of responsibility against facility type and state showing the regional enforcement architecture.
harm_angle: Regional differences in facility mix mean detainees face different conditions purely by where they were arrested.

title: The Detention Map
idea: Map every active ICE detention facility as a point colored by detailed facility type, showing how much of the network is contracted local jails rather than federal sites.
harm_angle: People held in contracted county jails fall outside federal detention standards and oversight.

title: Who Runs Detention
idea: Ranked bars of facility type counts within each ICE area of responsibility, showing which regions lean hardest on private and county-run beds.
harm_angle: Regions dominated by private beds have a financial incentive to keep people detained longer.
caveat: No capacity or population column, so this counts facilities, not people; operator identity is only implied by type code.

title: Detention Deserts and Clusters
idea: Map showing distance from each facility to the nearest immigration court and to major cities, highlighting facilities placed far from lawyers.
harm_angle: Remote detention placement is how people lose access to counsel and lose their cases.
caveat: Requires external court locations; this list has no coordinates, only city and state.

title: How Long People Are Held
idea: Distribution of days between book-in and book-out, small-multipled by facility, exposing facilities where stays run months longer than average.
harm_angle: Months of extra detention at one facility is months of a person's life taken by an operational choice.

title: Bond Set Versus Bond Posted
idea: Scatter of initial bond set against bond actually posted, with never-posted cases shown as a separate band. The gap is who could not pay.
harm_angle: Bond set above what a person can pay converts a release decision into indefinite detention by wealth.
caveat: Multiple bond columns including lowest-seen variants plus a duplicate-likely-bond flag signal known data quality problems in exactly this field.

title: Detention Length by Race and Nationality
idea: Cohort grid of race and ethnicity against citizenship country shaded by median detention length, testing whether identical case categories produce different stay lengths.
harm_angle: Same case category, longer detention for one group, is discrimination measurable in days of a person's life.
caveat: Race and ethnicity are agency-assigned rather than self-reported and their reliability is unknown; the chart must say so.

title: Release Reasons by Facility
idea: Heatmap grid of facility against release reason, showing facilities that release almost entirely by removal versus those that release on bond or supervision.
harm_angle: Where you are detained determines whether you go home or get deported, which should not be true.
caveat: Two release reason columns may disagree; facility populations differ by case mix and that must be controlled for.

title: The Detention Transfer Network
idea: Network graph of people moving between facilities across consecutive stints, showing the transfer routes that move detainees far from their lawyers and families.
harm_angle: Transferring someone across the country severs them from counsel and family right when they need both.

title: Dams Overdue For Inspection
idea: Distribution of years since last inspection, split by hazard class, isolating the longest-unlooked-at high hazard dams.
harm_angle: Where inspections stopped is where a preventable failure is most likely.
caveat: last_inspection_date null share unknown; inspection_frequency is free text.

title: Who Owns The Riskiest Dams
idea: Ranked bars of high hazard dams by primary owner type (private, local, state, federal, utility).
harm_angle: Private and local owners often lack money to fix what federal owners can, and residents carry the risk.
caveat: owner_types is multi-value; primary_owner_type coding unverified.

title: No Emergency Plan, High Hazard
idea: Heatmap grid of states by share of high hazard dams lacking an emergency action plan.
harm_angle: No plan means no warning for the towns downstream when it goes.
caveat: EAP flag derived from a YES string; blanks may be misread as no.

title: Aging Concrete Curve
idea: Scatter of year completed against condition rating for high hazard dams, testing whether the 1950s-60s build boom is the failing cohort.
harm_angle: An entire generation of infrastructure hitting end-of-life above populated valleys.
caveat: Condition is categorical text; ordering it is a judgment call.

title: Single-Supplier Buyers in Ecuador
idea: For each buyer_name, plot supplier concentration - the share of contract value going to its top supplier. Viewer sees public buyers with one favored vendor.
chart_shape: scatter of buyer volume against top-supplier share
harm_angle: Captured procurement in health and school-feeding means children and patients get whatever the favored vendor delivers.
caveat: OCDS records may be partial per contracting process; currency mixing needs handling.

title: Tender to Contract Value Drift
idea: Slope chart from tender_value_amount to award_value_amount to contract_value_amount per process. Viewer sees where the final price diverges from what was tendered.
harm_angle: Price drift after award is how public budgets get quietly drained.
caveat: Values may be in different currencies per row; some blocks are null for incomplete processes.

title: Direct Award Share by Method
idea: Timeline of contract value by tender_procurement_method, highlighting direct and emergency awards.
harm_angle: Emergency procurement rules used routinely turn oversight off permanently.
caveat: Method taxonomies may change across the 2015-present span.

title: Speed From Publication to Signature
idea: Distribution of days from tender_date_published to contract_date_signed, by method and buyer. Viewer sees contracts signed impossibly fast.
harm_angle: Contracts signed days after publication were decided before the public ever saw them.
caveat: Date completeness varies by OCDS publisher stage.

title: What Egypt publishes and stops publishing
idea: Heatmap grid of indicator by year shaded by whether a value exists, exposing the years a statistic quietly disappears.
harm_angle: Statistics that vanish in politically inconvenient years hide who is getting worse off.

title: Indicator coverage by category
idea: Ranked bars of how many indicators and years exist per category, showing which subjects the state measures and which it ignores.
harm_angle: Unmeasured domains are unaccountable domains.
caveat: 150-row sample cannot support a claim about the full portal.

title: Time series spot-check
idea: Small multiples of the longest available indicator series, the plain descriptive read of the portal.
harm_angle: Baseline national trends for a population rarely covered in Western data work.
caveat: country is number-cast over a name field so it will null; units are inconsistent across indicators.

title: Which members report late
idea: Heatmap grid of country by time period shaded by observation status flags, revealing which member states chronically miss or flag their data.
harm_angle: Late or flagged reporting delays the EU-level policy that residents depend on.

title: Provisional data that never firms up
idea: Timeline of observations by status code, showing how long provisional numbers stay provisional.
harm_angle: Decisions get made on provisional numbers that are later quietly revised.
caveat: Requires multiple vintages of the same observation; the mart likely holds only the latest.

title: Cross-country spread on one indicator
idea: Dot plot of the latest value per country for a chosen dataflow, ranked, with the EU median marked.
harm_angle: Shows which member state's residents sit worst on a given social or health measure.

title: Two centuries of who judges
idea: Timeline of the federal bench composition by race and gender from 1789 to today, the demographic history of the judiciary.
harm_angle: Litigants have faced a bench that looked nothing like them for almost the entire history of the country.
caveat: Demographics sit alongside appointment 1..6 wide columns; multi-appointment judges need unpivoting first.

title: The ABA rating and who gets confirmed
idea: Ranked bars of confirmation outcomes by ABA rating and appointing-president party, showing whether the rating actually gates the bench.
harm_angle: Poorly rated judges seated anyway decide cases affecting people for life.
caveat: ayes_nays is a combined text field, not two numbers; requires parsing.

title: Nomination to confirmation, getting slower
idea: Timeline of days from nomination to confirmation by year and appointing party, showing the collapse of the confirmation pipeline.
harm_angle: Vacant benches mean litigants -- including people in jail awaiting trial -- wait years for a hearing.
caveat: Wide 1..6 layout means only the first appointment is captured unless unpivoted.

title: The law school pipeline
idea: Ranked bars of judges by law school, showing how few institutions supply the entire federal bench.
harm_angle: A bench drawn from a handful of schools brings a narrow set of life experiences to every ruling.

title: Seats that stay empty
idea: Dot plot of seat ids against gap length between one judge's termination and the next commission, ranking the longest-vacant seats.
harm_angle: Long vacancies concentrate caseloads and push defendants into longer pretrial detention.
caveat: Requires the unpivoted service table to be accurate; seat_id continuity across eras unverified.

title: Confirmation vote margins over time
idea: Timeline of yea and nay margins per confirmation, showing the collapse from near-unanimous to party-line.
harm_angle: Party-line judges decide rights cases with no cross-party legitimacy behind them.
caveat: ayes_nays is one text field combining both counts and must be split.

title: Presidents' bench footprints
idea: Ranked bars of judgeships filled per president, normalized by term length, showing who reshaped the courts most.
harm_angle: One president's appointment run can set the legal environment for a generation.
caveat: Recess appointments and reappointments may double count without care.

title: The hearing bottleneck
idea: Scatter of nomination-to-hearing days against hearing-to-confirmation days, with stalled nominations sitting far out on one axis.
harm_angle: Nominations stalled in committee leave courts short-staffed and cases unheard.
caveat: Older records have sparse hearing dates; nulls concentrate in the early period.

title: Senior status as a strategic exit
idea: Timeline of senior-status dates relative to presidential party turnover, testing whether judges time their retirements politically.
harm_angle: Strategically timed retirements let a judge choose the politics of their own replacement.
caveat: Requires an external president-party-by-date series to align against.

source_names: Judicial Common Space -- Courts of Appeals
title: Circuit ideology spread
idea: Distribution of judge ideology within each circuit, showing which appellate courts are uniform and which are genuinely split.
harm_angle: Which circuit hears your case decides your rights -- a lottery by geography.
caveat: Only 705 rows and no time column, so this is a lifetime-score snapshot with no history.

source_names: Judicial Common Space -- Courts of Appeals
title: The circuit lottery
idea: Ranked bars of circuits by median judge ideology, with the spread shown, illustrating how much outcome depends on where you filed.
harm_angle: Identical claims get opposite results depending on the circuit -- a systemic inequity in access to justice.
caveat: No time axis and no case outcomes here; the inequity claim needs an outcomes source to prove.

source_names: Judicial Common Space -- Courts of Appeals
title: Outliers on the bench
idea: Dot plot of every appellate judge on the ideology scale, circuit-faceted, with the extreme tails named.
harm_angle: Outlier judges writing binding precedent set the law for millions in their circuit.
caveat: name is the only key; joining to the FJC directory requires fuzzy name matching.

title: Four institutions, one scale
idea: Timeline of the median ideology of SCOTUS, House, Senate and president on one common scale, showing when the branches diverge.
harm_angle: When the court sits far from the elected branches, rights get decided against the electorate's position.
caveat: Only 102 rows -- one per year; median columns are untyped text in the model and may need casting.

title: Circuit drift versus Congress
idea: Small multiples of each circuit's median over time against the congressional median, showing which circuits drifted furthest from the country.
harm_angle: Circuits far from the elected median produce rulings the public has no way to reverse.
caveat: Circuit medians are 13 wide columns and need unpivoting; standard deviations are separate columns.

title: Widest gap years
idea: Ranked bars of years by the gap between the Supreme Court median and the congressional median, naming the most counter-majoritarian moments.
harm_angle: Counter-majoritarian years are when the court overrode what the public voted for.
caveat: 102 rows; scale comparability across institutions is the whole premise of JCS but still an assumption.

title: Every justice on one line, 1937-2022
idea: Timeline of each justice's ideology by term as overlapping lines, the shape of the court's whole modern history.
harm_angle: The court's composition decides which rights survive; this is the record of that composition.
caveat: 782 rows, one per justice-term; jcs is untyped text in the model and may need casting.

title: The median justice's journey
idea: Timeline of the court's median justice score by term, with the name of the median justice annotated, showing who actually held the balance.
harm_angle: The median justice is one person deciding national rights for hundreds of millions.
caveat: Requires deriving the per-term median from the justice rows; term coverage gaps unverified.

title: Replacement shocks
idea: Slope chart of the court median before and after each seat change, ranking the confirmations that moved the court most.
harm_angle: A single replacement can flip settled rights; this ranks the ones that did.
caveat: Seat changes must be inferred from justices appearing and disappearing between terms.

title: Federal Prison Population Composition
idea: Ranked bars of BOP metrics by category for the latest report date, laying out the population, staffing and facility picture in one frame.
harm_angle: Population-to-staff ratios are the mechanism behind lockdowns, missed medical care and violence inside.
caveat: Only 50 rows -- a published summary snapshot, not facility-level detail.

title: Snapshot Drift Over Reports
idea: Timeline of each metric across report dates, showing which BOP numbers move and which have been frozen for years.
harm_angle: Frozen published metrics mean conditions inside are not actually being measured.
caveat: 50 rows may represent one snapshot only, leaving no time axis at all.

title: Facility Type Where Available
idea: Dot plot of metrics by facility type and state fips, showing how little geographic detail the federal prison system publishes.
harm_angle: Without facility-level data, deaths and abuse in a specific prison never surface in the national numbers.
caveat: facility_type and state_fips may be null on most of the 50 rows.

title: Case filings by nature of suit
idea: Timeline of federal case filings by nature-of-suit category, showing which kinds of harm people bring to court and when those waves crested.
harm_angle: The mix of suits is a running record of what is being done to people and who bothers to sue.
caveat: The catalog gives no mart row count while the model comment says 71.7M rows so grain and completeness are unverified; nature_of_suit is inconsistently populated across courts.

title: Time from filing to termination
idea: Distribution of days between filing and termination by court, showing where a plaintiff waits years for a decision.
harm_angle: Justice delayed by four years is justice a wage-theft or eviction plaintiff cannot afford to wait for.
caveat: Date fields may be text; open cases have null termination dates and must not be silently dropped.

title: Blocked and hidden dockets
idea: Count of dockets flagged blocked over the date they were blocked, by court, surfacing where the public record goes dark.
harm_angle: A sealed or blocked docket is a harm the public is not allowed to see.
caveat: Blocked in this dataset may mean search-engine blocking rather than sealing; semantics must be checked.

title: Judge caseload imbalance
idea: Heatmap of assigned judges against nature-of-suit sized by docket count, revealing judges who draw a striking share of one case type.
harm_angle: Single-judge divisions let filers pick their outcome, and the losing side is usually the individual.
caveat: assigned_to_str is free text with heavy variation; assigned_to_id population unverified.

title: Multidistrict litigation growth
idea: Timeline of dockets carrying multidistrict-litigation status by cause, tracking mass-harm consolidations.
harm_angle: Mass-tort consolidations are where thousands of injured people are processed at once.
caveat: mdl_status may be sparse.

title: Judges filing amended disclosures
idea: Share of disclosure filings marked amended by year, showing how often judges have to go back and correct what they reported.
harm_angle: Amendments often follow journalism finding an omission so the pattern shows the honor system failing.
caveat: is_amended coding unverified; year_col is a cast.

title: Redacted addendum prevalence
idea: Count of disclosures with redacted addendum content by year and report type, showing the growing share of the judicial financial record kept private.
harm_angle: Redacted disclosures mean litigants cannot check whether their judge has a stake in the case.
caveat: Redaction flag semantics unverified.

title: Unreadable disclosure coverage
idea: Share of filings never machine-extracted, by year, showing where the public record exists only as an unreadable scan.
harm_angle: A disclosure nobody can read is a disclosure that does not hold anyone to account.
caveat: Extraction status reflects the archive's pipeline, not the judiciary's.

title: Disclosure length over time
idea: Distribution of page counts per filing by year, showing whether judges' financial lives have grown more complex.
harm_angle: Longer disclosures signal more entanglements a litigant would want to know about.
caveat: Page count reflects form changes as much as substance.

title: Judges' most-held assets
idea: Ranked bars of the most frequently listed investment descriptions across judicial disclosures, naming the companies judges most commonly own.
harm_angle: Widely held stocks are the recusal conflicts most likely to go unnoticed in litigation.
caveat: description is free text needing heavy normalization; the round 500000 row count looks like a load cap.

title: Judicial trading activity timeline
idea: Timeline of disclosed transactions by month, showing whether judicial trading clusters around market or docket events.
harm_angle: A judge trading a company's stock while its case is on the docket is the conflict litigants fear.
caveat: transaction_date is derived from a raw text field; population and precision unverified.

title: How much of it is guesswork
idea: Share of investment rows with inferred rather than reported values, by disclosure year, showing how much of the judicial wealth record is estimated.
harm_angle: If the numbers are inferred, no one can actually verify a judge's holdings.
caveat: Year requires joining to the disclosures table.

title: Redacted holdings by value band
idea: Cross-tab of redaction flag against gross value code, testing whether the largest holdings are the ones most often hidden.
harm_angle: If the biggest holdings are the ones redacted, the disclosure regime protects exactly what matters.
caveat: Value codes are bands, not amounts; redaction flag semantics unverified.

source_names: CourtListener Judge and Financial Disclosure Database

harm_angle: A bench that does not resemble the people it judges produces predictable blind spots in sentencing.

source_names: CourtListener Judge and Financial Disclosure Database
title: Judicial Financial Disclosure Size

harm_angle: Judges with large outside income have financial relationships that can quietly shape rulings affecting ordinary litigants.

source_names: CourtListener Judge and Financial Disclosure Database
title: Bench Longevity and Turnover

harm_angle: Decades-long tenure means a single person's views govern a whole region's litigants for a generation.

source_names: CourtListener Judge and Financial Disclosure Database
title: Alias Records and Record Quality
idea: Dot plot of judges with an alias-of pointer, an FJC id, and a completed date, exposing how much of the reference database is duplicate or unfinished.

source_names: CourtListener Judge and Financial Disclosure Database

title: Confirmation wait timeline
idea: Distribution of days from nomination to confirmation by decade, showing the judicial confirmation process grinding slower.
harm_angle: Long vacancies mean overloaded courts and litigants waiting years for a hearing.

title: Revolving door before the bench
idea: Ranked bars of the organizations judges held positions at before appointment, showing which firms and agencies feed the federal bench.
harm_angle: A bench drawn from corporate defense firms decides the cases of the people those firms fight.

title: Why judges leave
idea: Distribution of termination reasons over time, showing retirements, elevations and resignations including the rare disciplinary exits.
harm_angle: How judges exit is the only visible accountability the judiciary has.

title: Appointer lineage network
idea: Network of appointers to appointees, showing the chains of patronage that populate the courts.

title: Close confirmation votes
idea: Scatter of yes-vote percentage against confirmation date, showing the collapse of consensus confirmations.

title: Who Defrauds Which Agency
idea: Flow diagram from fraud type to defrauded agency sized by settlement amount, showing where federal money leaks and who takes it.

title: The Whistleblower's Cut
idea: Scatter of relator share against total settlement amount, showing what portion of recovered fraud goes to the person who risked their job to report it.
harm_angle: Whistleblowers who lose careers over reporting fraud recover a fraction of what they saved taxpayers.

title: Settlement Size by District
idea: Ranked dot plot of settlement amounts by federal district, revealing whether some districts systematically settle cheap.
harm_angle: A district that settles cheap is a district where defrauding the government is a good bet.

title: Fifteen Rows of Bank Enforcement

title: Order Text Mining for Penalty Type
idea: Ranked bars of enforcement order types extracted from the raw order text -- cease-and-desist, civil money penalty, removal -- showing the mix of what regulators actually do.
harm_angle: Removal orders mean an individual banker was barred; penalties without removal mean the person keeps working.

title: Suspensions By State
idea: State map or ranked bars of suspended counterparties by state with individuals separated from companies.

idea: Network of individuals and companies appearing on more than one suspension order showing clusters of related actors.

title: Unpublished Opinions by Circuit
idea: Heatmap of circuit against year shaded by the share of decisions issued unpublished, showing which appeals courts decide most cases invisibly.

idea: Distribution of days from docket date to judgment date by circuit and appeal type, exposing circuits where an appeal takes years.

title: How Long An Appeal Takes
idea: Distribution of days from docket date to judgment date by circuit small-multipled by nature of suit.

title: Pro Se Bankruptcy Discharge Gap

title: Chapter 13 Conversion Traps
idea: Flow diagram from original filing chapter to closing chapter, showing how many Chapter 13 filers end up converted or dismissed with nothing discharged.

title: Debt Discharged vs Debt Kept
idea: Scatter of debt discharged against debt not discharged per case, colored by chapter, showing how much relief bankruptcy actually delivers.
harm_angle: Non-dischargeable debt -- student loans, taxes, support -- is what people still owe after losing everything.

title: Bankruptcy Geography by ZIP
idea: Map of debtor ZIP codes shaded by filings per capita, revealing the neighborhoods where household finance collapses most often.

title: Income vs Expenses at Filing
idea: Distribution of average monthly income minus expenses at filing, by chapter and district, showing how deep in the hole people are when they finally file.

title: Chapter 7 Versus 13 By Place
idea: County or district map of the ratio of chapter 13 to chapter 7 filings exposing districts where debtors are steered into the longer harder chapter.

idea: Cohort grid of self-represented filers versus represented filers against final disposition and whether debt was discharged.

idea: Distribution of average monthly income minus expenses at filing split by chapter and by whether the case ended in discharge.
harm_angle: The gap between what people earn and what they owe each month is the mechanism that produces bankruptcy.

title: Repeat Filers And The Debt Treadmill
idea: Cohort grid of the prior-filing flag against outcome and time to close showing how often bankruptcy fails to end the cycle.
harm_angle: A second or third filing means the first one did not fix anything for that household.

title: Time to Termination by District
idea: Distribution of days from file date to termination date per district, small-multipled, exposing courts where civil justice takes years longer.

idea: Scatter of amount demanded against amount received for cases ending in judgment by nature of suit.
harm_angle: Shows how much of a claimed injury the system actually compensates.
caveat: Amount fields are often coded in thousands and unpopulated for most cases.

title: Trials Have Nearly Vanished
idea: Timeline of the share of civil cases that ever reach trial by decade and district showing the disappearing jury.
harm_angle: A system where nothing goes to trial resolves harm in private settlements nobody can audit.
caveat: Trial date fields may be sparsely populated.

title: Class Actions Filed Versus Surviving
idea: Slope chart of cases filed as class actions against those still class actions at termination by nature of suit.
harm_angle: Decertification strips the only mechanism that lets many small victims sue at all.
caveat: The class action flags may not mean formal certification.

title: Judge-Level Dismissal Rates
idea: Dot plot of filing judges by case volume and share of cases dismissed before merits within a single district to hold case mix roughly constant.
harm_angle: Which judge you draw should not decide whether your claim is heard.
caveat: Judge identifiers are codes; case mix varies even within a district.

title: Sentence Length by Offense and District
idea: Distribution of prison months for the same offense code across districts, showing how much your sentence depends on where you were charged.
harm_angle: Two people with the same offense serve years more or less based purely on geography.
caveat: prison_total uses coded sentinel values for life and probation-only; offense codes need the FJC codebook.

title: Trial Penalty Made Visible
idea: Slope chart of average sentence for defendants who pleaded versus those who went to trial, for the same offense, quantifying the price of exercising a jury right.
harm_angle: Defendants who insist on a trial serve dramatically longer, which is how the system buys guilty pleas.
caveat: Requires correctly mapping disposition codes to plea vs trial; count columns ct_pn/ct_tr semantics need the codebook.

title: Fines That Nobody Can Pay
idea: Distribution of total fine amount against offense severity, showing financial penalties imposed on defendants who are also serving prison time.
harm_angle: A large fine on top of prison follows a person for life and blocks reentry, housing and employment.
caveat: fine_total may be coded in buckets; severity codes need mapping.

title: Fugitive Status Duration
idea: Timeline of fugitive start-to-end spans as horizontal bars grouped by district, showing how long warrants stay open and for which offenses.
harm_angle: Long-open warrants for minor offenses trap people out of jobs and housing for years without any trial.
caveat: Fugitive dates may be sparsely populated; date fields may be text.

title: Charge Stacking as Leverage
idea: Distribution of the number of populated filing-offense slots per defendant against final sentence, testing whether stacking five charges produces a longer plea.
harm_angle: Stacked charges are the lever prosecutors use to make a plea the only rational choice.
caveat: The five repeated offense blocks may be sparsely used; correlation here is suggestive, not causal.

title: Sentence Length By District
idea: Distribution of total prison months for the same lead offense code across districts exposing geographic sentencing disparity.
harm_angle: Two people convicted of the same crime serving very different terms depending on where they were charged.
caveat: Prison time fields use special codes for life or indeterminate sentences that must be handled separately.

title: Charged Versus Convicted Offense Drift
idea: Flow diagram from filing offense code to terminating offense code showing how charges are bargained down or up.
harm_angle: Charge stacking at filing is the leverage that produces guilty pleas and this makes the leverage visible.
caveat: Offense codes need the court codebook; multi-count cases complicate the flow.

title: Almost Nobody Goes To Trial
idea: Timeline of the share of defendants disposed by plea versus trial by offense category and decade.
harm_angle: A plea rate near total means guilt is negotiated, not proven, and innocent defendants take deals.
caveat: Count fields need interpretation; disposition codes require the codebook.

title: Counsel Type And Sentence
idea: Cohort grid of filing counsel type against sentence length and disposition for matched offense codes.
harm_angle: If appointed counsel correlates with longer sentences for the same offense, poverty adds years.
caveat: Counsel codes unverified; offense-severity matching is imperfect.

title: Fines Versus Prison By Offense Class
idea: Scatter of total fine amount against total prison months by offense code showing which offenses buy their way out.
harm_angle: White-collar offenses paying fines while drug offenses serve years is the two-tier system in one chart.
caveat: Fine amounts are likely zero for most defendants; log scaling needed.

title: Time From Charge To Sentence
idea: Distribution of days from file date to sentence date by district and fugitive status.
harm_angle: Long pretrial periods mean detention without conviction for defendants who cannot make bail.
caveat: Pretrial detention status is not in the model; fugitive status is only a weak proxy.

title: Supervised Release Piles On
idea: Ranked bars of offense codes by average supervised release and probation months added on top of prison time.
harm_angle: Years of supervision after release is a second sentence that quietly returns people to prison on technicalities.
caveat: Units for supervised release may be months or a coded value.

title: Repeat Respondents
idea: Ranked bars of companies by number of separate FTC actions filed against them, exposing firms that treat enforcement as a cost of doing business.
harm_angle: A company sued repeatedly for the same consumer harm keeps harming consumers between cases.
caveat: respondent is free text with name variation; ein column population unverified and likely mostly blank.

title: Enforcement Topics Over Time
idea: Stacked timeline of FTC actions by topic, showing which consumer harms the agency chased in each era and which it dropped.
harm_angle: Topics the FTC stops enforcing are harms consumers absorb with no recourse.
caveat: topic taxonomy may be inconsistent; 1200 rows may be a partial scrape of the FTC case index.

title: How Long Cases Stay Open
idea: Distribution of case status by filing year, showing the share of FTC actions still pending years after filing.
harm_angle: An action pending for years means the conduct continues while the case sits.
caveat: No resolution-date column, so duration is inferred from filing date and current status only.

title: Consumer Protection vs Antitrust Balance
idea: Slope chart of the annual split between consumer-protection and antitrust case types, showing where the agency's attention shifted.
harm_angle: When antitrust attention drops, consolidation raises prices on everyone with no case ever filed.
caveat: case_type value set unverified; partial scrape may bias the mix.

title: Where Mass Harm Concentrates
idea: Ranked bars of pending MDLs by number of pending actions, labeled by litigation name, showing which mass injuries currently hold the most plaintiffs.
harm_angle: Each pending action is a person injured by the same product waiting on one consolidated ruling.
caveat: Snapshot only -- no time axis, so trends need repeated pulls.

title: The MDL Judge Concentration
idea: Dot plot of individual judges against total actions they oversee across MDLs, showing how a handful of judges control mass-tort outcomes for millions.
harm_angle: One judge's rulings on evidence or settlement decide compensation for hundreds of thousands of injured people.
caveat: Judge names are free text; only pending MDLs are in scope, so closed mega-MDLs are missing.

title: Districts as Mass-Tort Magnets
idea: Map of federal districts sized by total MDL actions hosted, revealing the small set of courthouses where national product litigation lands.
harm_angle: Concentrating national injury litigation in a few districts means local procedural norms govern nationwide compensation.
caveat: 162 rows; district-to-geography mapping needed; no product or defendant column beyond the litigation title.

title: Pending vs Total Case Attrition
idea: Scatter of pending against total actions per MDL, with the diagonal marking no attrition, showing which mass torts have resolved most of their claims and which are stuck.
harm_angle: An MDL with high total and low resolution is thousands of injured people still waiting.
caveat: Total vs pending definitions may differ across MDL types; single snapshot.

title: Forty Years of Multistate Money
idea: Timeline of total settlement amount by year, split into state share and federal share, showing how the size and structure of AG settlements changed since 1980.
harm_angle: Large settlements that route little to consumer restitution mean harmed people never see the money.
caveat: Amount fields are likely text with currency formatting; DATERESOLVED format unverified.

title: Who Actually Gets Restitution
idea: Scatter of consumer restitution against total settlement amount, with the diagonal marking full pass-through, exposing settlements where consumers got almost nothing.
harm_angle: When restitution is a sliver of the settlement, the injured consumers subsidized a state budget line.
caveat: CONSUMER_RESTITUTION likely null for many rows and text-formatted; definitions vary across decades.

title: Partisan Participation Grid
idea: Heatmap of settlements over time against the Democratic and Republican participating-state counts, showing which industries draw bipartisan action and which split on party lines.
harm_angle: Consumers in states whose AG sat out an industry-wide settlement got no relief at all.
caveat: Party count fields may be text lists rather than counts; industry taxonomy inconsistent over 40 years.

title: Repeat Defendants Across Campaigns
idea: Network of defendants to enforcement campaigns, showing corporations that appear in multiple multistate actions across different issue areas.
harm_angle: A company settling repeatedly across industries and decades has priced the penalty into the business model.
caveat: DEFENDANTS is a free-text list needing splitting and name normalization.

title: Corporate Monitors: Teeth or Theater
idea: Slope chart comparing settlement amounts with and without a corporate monitor provision, by industry, testing whether monitored companies settle for more or less.
harm_angle: Settlements without ongoing monitoring let the same conduct resume the day the check clears.
caveat: CORPORATE_MONITOR_PROVISION population unverified; provision types are free text.

title: Settlements by Presidential Era
idea: Small multiples of settlement volume and value by presidential administration, showing how federal posture shapes state enforcement appetite.
harm_angle: Enforcement droughts are years consumers were harmed with no one bringing a case.
caveat: Administration field may be inconsistently labeled; correlation with policy is inferential.

title: Argument to Decision Lag
idea: Distribution of days from argument date to decision date by term, showing which cases the Court sat on longest.
harm_angle: Cases held longest are usually the ones where rights hang unresolved for the people who brought them.

title: Who Gets Heard at the Court
idea: Ranked bars of advocates by number of oral arguments, exposing the small elite Supreme Court bar that argues most cases.
harm_angle: An elite repeat-player bar means well-resourced parties get better representation before the highest court.
caveat: advocate_names is likely a nested list needing unpacking; 25-row mart is far too thin today.

title: Audio Coverage Gaps by Era
idea: Timeline of the share of cases with audio and transcript available by term, exposing the decades where the public cannot hear its own Supreme Court.
harm_angle: Missing audio means the public can never check what was actually argued in cases that reshaped their rights.
caveat: 25-row mart; has_audio is derived from URL presence, not verified playability.

title: Justice Ideology Drift
idea: Slope chart per justice of their liberal-direction vote share early versus late in their tenure, showing who moved and who never did.
harm_angle: A justice's drift changes the outcome of rights cases for millions without any election.
caveat: direction_code semantics need the SCDB codebook; unclear-vote rows must be excluded.

title: When the Court Strikes Down Laws
idea: Timeline of cases declaring a law unconstitutional, split by whether federal or state law, showing the eras of maximum judicial override.
harm_angle: Every struck-down statute is a protection legislators built for people that the Court removed.
caveat: declaration_unconstitutional codes distinguish types that must not be collapsed.

title: Who Wins Before the Court
idea: Heatmap of petitioner type against respondent type shaded by petitioner win rate, showing whether businesses beat individuals and governments beat everyone.
harm_angle: If individuals lose systematically against government and business, the Court is not a neutral forum for ordinary people.
caveat: Party codes are a large SCDB taxonomy needing collapsing; case-level rows are duplicated per justice vote and must be deduped.

title: Issue Areas That Vanished
idea: Stacked timeline of decisions by issue area, showing which categories of grievance the Court stopped agreeing to hear entirely.
harm_angle: An issue area the Court abandons is a class of harm with no national remedy left.
caveat: Vote-grain rows require dedup to case grain first; issue codes need the codebook.

title: Precedent Alteration Clusters
idea: Timeline of precedent-altering decisions marked as events, colored by issue area, showing the bursts where the Court rewrote settled law.
harm_angle: Clustered precedent reversals mean people planned their lives around rules that were then removed.
caveat: precedent_alteration is self-declared by the SCDB coders and undercounts silent overrulings.

title: The 5-4 Coalition Network
idea: Network of justices linked by how often they voted together in split decisions, per natural court, revealing the real blocs behind the numbers.
harm_angle: Stable blocs mean outcomes on rights cases are determined by composition, not argument.
caveat: Requires pairwise agreement computation across 83k vote rows; natural_court boundaries must be respected.

title: Filings vs Terminations Backlog
idea: Scatter of filings against terminations per district with the parity diagonal, exposing courts falling further behind every year.
harm_angle: A district that terminates fewer cases than it takes in is a place where justice is simply delayed indefinitely.
caveat: Only 50 rows -- a table index rather than the caseload series; filings/terminations left untyped.

title: What the Courts Publish About Themselves
idea: Ranked bars of published tables by topic and subtopic, showing which parts of the federal judiciary are measured and which are not.
harm_angle: Unmeasured court functions -- pretrial detention, probation revocation -- affect people invisibly.
caveat: 50-row index; this describes the publication catalog rather than the caseload data itself.

title: Bankruptcy Chapters by District
idea: Heatmap of district against bankruptcy chapter code shaded by filings, showing where Chapter 7 versus 13 dominates and why.
harm_angle: Districts pushing debtors into Chapter 13 extract years of payments from people who could have discharged.
caveat: county is cast to number on a name column and likely all-null; only 50 rows available.

title: EU Acts Still in Force
idea: Timeline of documents by date of adoption colored by in-force status, showing the accumulation and decay of the EU legal stock.
harm_angle: Rules still in force decades on are the ones actually governing people's daily lives across Europe.
caveat: Only 53 rows -- an API probe, not a corpus pull; country cast to number and likely all-null.

title: Who Authors EU Law
idea: Ranked bars of EU institutions by number of acts authored, split by subject matter, showing which body actually writes the rules.
harm_angle: Rules written by unelected bodies still bind citizens who never voted on them.
caveat: 53-row sample; subject_matter may be a multi-value field.

title: Language Availability Gaps
idea: Heatmap of document type against available language and format, exposing which EU legal texts are not published in every citizen's language.
harm_angle: A citizen who cannot read a binding rule in their own language cannot comply with or contest it.
caveat: 53 rows; language is probably a single value per row from the API request, not the full availability set.

source_names: HUDOC European Court of Human Rights Case-Law

harm_angle: Each violation judgment is a person whose government was formally found to have abused them.
caveat: 2000-row mart is likely a capped page pull, not the full HUDOC corpus; violation may be a multi-value text field.

source_names: HUDOC European Court of Human Rights Case-Law
title: Which Rights Get Violated
idea: Heatmap of Convention article against respondent state shaded by violation count, exposing which specific rights each government breaks.
harm_angle: Article 3 and 5 clusters are torture and unlawful detention findings against named states.

source_names: HUDOC European Court of Human Rights Case-Law
title: Importance Level and Outcome

harm_angle: Low-importance-flagged cases are real people whose claims get less judicial attention.
