source_names: HUDOC European Court of Human Rights Case-Law
title: Judgment Volume Over Time
idea: Timeline of judgments per quarter split by respondent state, showing when the Court's docket surged and against whom.
harm_angle: Surges against one state are usually a systemic abuse producing hundreds of near-identical victims.
caveat: 2000-row cap likely truncates the historical series.

title: Every Killing on One Map
idea: Point map of all recorded police killings colored by armed status, with clustering by agency, showing the national geography of lethal force.
harm_angle: Every point is a named person killed, and the clusters name the departments doing it.
caveat: county is cast to number on a name column and likely all-null; lat/lon completeness unverified.

title: Agencies That Kill Repeatedly
idea: Ranked bars of law enforcement agencies by killing count over the full period, with the share of victims unarmed shown inside each bar.
harm_angle: Departments that kill year after year with the same profile are institutions, not accidents.
caveat: Agency names are free text with variants; ORI identifier population unverified and it is the real join key.

title: Charges Almost Never Filed
idea: Timeline of killings against the count where criminal charges were filed against an officer, with the near-flat charge line as the finding.
harm_angle: A decade of killings with almost no charges is the accountability gap stated numerically.
caveat: criminal_charges is free text needing classification; disposition may lag by years for recent cases.

title: Killings by Tract Demographics
idea: Scatter of killings per tract against that tract's Black population share and median household income, showing where lethal force concentrates.
harm_angle: Poor and Black neighborhoods absorb police killings at rates the national average hides completely.
caveat: Tract demographics are a fixed 2019 ACS snapshot applied to all years; median income field is untyped.

title: Prosecutor Party and Officer Charges
idea: Heatmap of chief prosecutor political party and race against the rate officers were charged, testing whether who holds the prosecutor's office changes accountability.
harm_angle: Whether an officer faces charges may depend on the elected prosecutor rather than on what happened.
caveat: Prosecutor fields are volunteer-coded and likely sparse; small cell counts will be noisy.

title: Body Camera Presence and Outcome
idea: Grouped bars of body-camera presence against official disposition and charging outcome, testing whether footage actually changes accountability.
harm_angle: If footage does not change outcomes, the cameras funded as a reform are doing nothing for victims' families.
caveat: Body camera field is sourced from WaPo and only covers shootings in that database, biasing coverage.

title: Officers With Prior Shootings
idea: Network of named officers to the incidents they were involved in, isolating officers appearing more than once.
harm_angle: An officer allowed to remain armed after a prior killing is a foreseeable risk to the next person.
caveat: Officer names are frequently withheld and the field is likely mostly blank; sensitive to misidentification.

harm_angle: A county where Black residents are jailed at ten times the white rate is running two different justice systems.

source_names: Vera Institute Incarceration Trends by County
title: Rural Jail Growth While Cities Fell
idea: Small multiples of jail population rate by urbanicity over time, showing incarceration rising in rural counties as urban rates declined.
harm_angle: Rural jail growth means people locked up far from family, lawyers and services.
caveat: Urbanicity is a fixed classification applied across all years; jail reporting coverage varies by year.

title: Renting Out Jail Beds
idea: Timeline per county of jail population held for federal agencies -- ICE, Marshals, BOP, BIA -- showing which local jails run as federal detention for revenue.
harm_angle: Counties paid per federal detainee have a cash incentive to keep beds full of immigrants and pretrial defendants.

source_names: Vera Institute Incarceration Trends by County
title: Jails Above Rated Capacity
idea: Scatter of jail population against rated capacity per county-year, with the parity diagonal, marking every point above the line as overcrowding.
harm_angle: Overcrowded jails are where deaths, assaults and denied medical care happen.

source_names: Vera Institute Incarceration Trends by County

harm_angle: Pretrial detention is people who have not been convicted losing jobs and housing because they cannot pay bail.

source_names: Vera Institute Incarceration Trends by County
title: Women's Incarceration Growth
idea: Timeline of female jail and prison population rates by region, showing the fastest-growing incarcerated population in the country.
harm_angle: Incarcerating mothers at rising rates puts children into foster care as a second-order harm.
caveat: Female prison rate coverage varies; prison data is state-attributed to counties by Vera's method.

source_names: Vera Institute Incarceration Trends by County
title: Admissions Churn vs Standing Population
idea: Scatter of jail admissions rate against jail population rate per county, separating counties that hold few people long from those that cycle thousands through briefly.
harm_angle: High-churn counties are arresting huge numbers for short holds, which destroys jobs without any conviction.

harm_angle: Counties with structurally low wages are where working full time still does not cover rent.

harm_angle: A one-industry county has no cushion when that industry leaves.

caveat: Percent-change columns may be sparsely populated; composition shifts can drive both axes.

source_names: Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
title: Public versus private pay gap by county

idea: Timeline small multiples of establishment counts for the hardest-hit counties, showing sustained business die-off rather than one bad quarter.
harm_angle: Sustained business closure strips a community of both jobs and services.

harm_angle: Every point below full funding is a retiree's promised check that may not arrive.

harm_angle: Counting participants, not plans, shows how many people are actually standing on thin ice.

idea: Scatter of retired-participant share against funding percentage, showing the mature plans with the most people already drawing and the least money behind them.
harm_angle: A plan that is mostly retirees and badly funded has no workforce left to fix it.
caveat: Participant count fields cast unverified.

title: Actuary firm concentration
idea: Ranked bars of actuarial firms by number of plans and total participants certified, showing how few firms sign off on the country's pensions.
harm_angle: A handful of firms certifying everyone's pension assumptions is a single point of failure for retirees.

title: Assumption changes before bad years
idea: Plans flagged as changing actuarial assumptions or method, tracked against their funding percentage the following year, testing whether assumption changes dress up weak plans.
harm_angle: Changing the math instead of funding the plan is how a shortfall stays invisible until it is a retiree's problem.
caveat: Requires linking consecutive plan years by EIN and plan number; change indicators may be sparse.

title: Plans whose assets fell while fees rose
idea: Scatter of change in total assets against administrative expenses per participant, one dot per plan. The bottom-right region is workers paying more for a shrinking pot.
harm_angle: Retirement savers pay rising fees on a fund that lost money.

title: Administrative cost per participant ranked
idea: Ranked bars of administrative expenses divided by participant count by plan sponsor, isolating the plans that are expensive for the people in them.
harm_angle: High per-head admin cost is a direct deduction from workers' retirement.
caveat: Participant counts include separated and beneficiary categories inconsistently; partial coverage.

title: Final filings: plans being wound down
idea: Timeline of final-filing flags per year with sponsor state, showing waves of plan terminations and where they land.
harm_angle: Plan terminations are the moment promised retirement benefits get renegotiated downward.

title: Preparer firms behind the filings
idea: Network linking preparer firms to the plans and total assets they touch, showing how concentrated the pension-compliance industry is.
harm_angle: A few firms sign off on the paperwork protecting millions of workers' pensions.

title: Late and delinquent filers
idea: Distribution of days from plan year end to date received, flagged for the delinquent-filer program, showing who reports late and how late.
harm_angle: Late reporting keeps workers in the dark about the health of their own plan.
caveat: Extensions are legitimate and separately flagged; they must be netted out first.

title: Union membership decline curve
idea: Total reported members across union filings by year, the long decline of organized labor in its own filings.
harm_angle: Fewer members means fewer workers with anyone bargaining for their wages and safety.

title: Spending per member by union
idea: Scatter of disbursements per member against membership size, showing unions spending far more per head than their peers.
harm_angle: Dues money spent on overhead instead of representation is money taken from the workers paying it.
caveat: Financial fields cast unverified; short-form filers report less detail, biasing comparisons.

title: Unions in financial distress
idea: Timeline of unions whose liabilities exceed assets or that report a shortage amount, showing locals heading toward collapse.
harm_angle: A local going broke stops enforcing the contract, and the members lose their only leverage.
caveat: shortage_amount semantics such as embezzlement loss versus accounting shortfall are unverified.

title: Missing filings and late reporting
idea: Cohort grid of unions by year showing filed versus missing years, exposing locals that stopped reporting while still operating.
harm_angle: An unaudited local is a place where members' dues disappear with no one watching.

title: Election intervals by local
idea: Distribution of gaps between reported next-election dates by union, showing locals that go many years without an officer election.
harm_angle: Members with no election have no way to remove leadership that is not fighting for them.

title: Union geography and weight
idea: Map of unions by headquarters state sized by members, showing where organized labor still has weight.
harm_angle: Headquarters state understates worker geography, but still shows where labor institutions survive.
caveat: Address is the filing address, not where members actually work.

title: Rail Worker Injuries by Job Code
idea: Ranked bars of employee job descriptions by casualty count and by median days away from work, showing which rail jobs break people.
harm_angle: Specific rail crafts absorb injuries at rates their employers have known about for decades.

title: Railroads Ranked by Casualty Count
idea: Ranked bars of reporting railroads by casualties per year, split by whether the railroad is freight, passenger, commuter, or short line.
harm_angle: Short lines with thin margins may be injuring workers at multiples of the big-carrier rate.
caveat: No exposure denominator such as employee-hours in this table, so raw counts favor big railroads unless normalized from elsewhere.

caveat: Coded fields need lookups; the free-text specific_location may be needed for real detail.

title: Drug and Alcohol Testing After Injury

title: Body part injured by mining occupation

harm_angle: Shows which mine jobs systematically destroy which parts of workers' bodies.

idea: Distribution of total mining experience among injured workers, split by degree of injury. If fatal and permanent-disability curves skew low-experience, the industry is hurting its newest workers hardest.
harm_angle: Newest miners may absorb the most severe injuries with the least training.
caveat: Experience fields may be text or zero-filled; grain is one injury record not one worker.

title: Days lost per accident by controller
idea: Ranked bars of median lost workdays per injury, one bar per controlling company, limited to controllers above a minimum injury count. Surfaces operators whose accidents are most damaging, not just most numerous.
harm_angle: Identifies the corporate parents whose miners lose the most working days to injury.
caveat: Controller names are unstandardized text; days_lost may be zero for fatalities.

title: Equipment makers behind the injuries
idea: Ranked bars of injury counts by equipment manufacturer and model, restricted to accidents where equipment was the injury source. Points at machines that keep hurting people.
harm_angle: Names the machinery repeatedly implicated in miner injuries.
caveat: Manufacturer field likely sparse; no denominator for how many machines are in service.

title: Injury clock across the shift
idea: Small multiples of injury counts by hours-into-shift (accident time minus shift start), one panel per mining method. Shows whether fatigue late in the shift drives the harm.
harm_angle: Fatigue-driven injury peaks are an argument about shift length, which is a policy lever.
caveat: Time fields are likely text HHMM; overnight shifts need wraparound handling.

title: Every US mine on one map
idea: Point map of all mines colored by current status (active, abandoned, idled) and sized by employee count. The abandoned clusters are the interesting part.
harm_angle: Communities living next to idled and abandoned mines carry the residual hazard.
caveat: Lat/lon may be null or zero for many mines; status labels need grouping.

title: Who owns the mines: controller concentration
idea: Ranked bars of mines per controlling company with a cumulative line, showing how few controllers own most of the country's mines.
harm_angle: A handful of controllers set safety culture for most US miners.
caveat: Controller names change over time; the file only carries the current controller.

title: Miner representation gap by state
idea: Heatmap grid of states against the share of mines reporting a miners' representative and a safety committee. States with near-zero representation stand out as bare rows.
harm_angle: Miners without a representative have no safe channel to report hazards.
caveat: Indicator fields may be Y/N/blank with blanks meaning unknown rather than no.

title: Gassy mines and methane liberation
idea: Dot plot of reported methane liberation per mine against its gas category, highlighting mines classified low but liberating high volumes.
harm_angle: A mis-categorised gassy mine is an explosion waiting for the men underground.
caveat: Methane liberation is likely populated only for underground coal; most rows blank.

title: Ownership churn before closure
idea: Timeline of controller-begin dates against mine status-change dates, testing whether mines change hands shortly before going idle or abandoned.
harm_angle: Late ownership flips can strand cleanup and benefit obligations on workers and the public.
caveat: Only the current controller is in the file so real churn history is missing.

title: Penalty proposed versus penalty actually paid
idea: Scatter of proposed penalty against amount paid, one dot per violation, with the 45-degree line drawn. Everything below the line is a discount the operator received.
harm_angle: Every dollar discounted is enforcement pressure that never reached the operator who endangered miners.
caveat: Money fields are wrapped in try_to_double, hinting they arrive as text; open cases inflate the unpaid side.

title: Repeat significant-and-substantial offenders
idea: Ranked bars of significant-and-substantial violation counts per controller, with a second bar for average penalty per violation. Big count plus small penalty is the accountability gap.
harm_angle: Operators who keep endangering miners while paying trivial fines face no real deterrent.
caveat: Controller naming is inconsistent and needs grouping before ranking.

title: Which safety standards get cited most
idea: Ranked bars of the top cited standards, colored by average likelihood of injury and number of persons affected. Shows which specific rules the industry routinely ignores.
harm_angle: The most-cited standards are the everyday hazards miners live with.
caveat: Part-section is a code needing a lookup for human labels.

title: Contest and the shrinking fine
idea: Slope chart from proposed penalty to final amount due, split by whether the violation was contested. If contested violations slope down harder, contesting is a reliable discount.
harm_angle: Legal contesting may function as a routine discount mechanism for well-lawyered operators.
caveat: Contested flag population unknown; pending dockets will look like unpaid.

title: Time to abatement by negligence level
idea: Distribution of days between violation issue and termination, faceted by negligence level. Long tails on high-negligence violations mean dangerous conditions persisted.
harm_angle: Miners keep working in a hazard for every day between citation and fix.
caveat: violation_issue_dt is cast with try_to_double in the model, suggesting the raw value is number-like; parsing may fail.

title: Enforcement pressure over the decades
idea: Timeline of violations issued per year with a second line for dollars assessed, so shifts in enforcement intensity across administrations become visible.
harm_angle: When enforcement drops, miners bear the risk before anyone notices.
caveat: No production or hours denominator so counts confound activity with enforcement.

title: Injury Rate By Industry 2023
idea: Ranked bars of injury cases per 100 full-time workers by industry description, using hours worked as the denominator, showing the most dangerous industries that year.
harm_angle: Workers in the top industries are getting hurt at many times the rate of the average job, and most never see this comparison.
caveat: Hours worked and case counts are stored without numeric casting in this model, so they may be text; establishments self-report.

title: Establishments Reporting Zero Injuries
idea: Map by state of the share of establishments claiming no injuries at all, with high-hazard industries filtered in, exposing implausible clean records.
harm_angle: An employer reporting zero injuries in a hazardous industry is either exceptional or hiding harm from the workers it happened to.
caveat: The zero-injury flag's exact semantics are unverified; small establishments legitimately report zero.

title: Days Away Per Case By Industry
idea: Dot plot of average days away from work per lost-time case by industry, showing which industries produce not just more injuries but worse ones.
harm_angle: Long recovery times mean lost wages and lost jobs, a harm that raw case counts completely hide.
caveat: Both fields are uncast in the model and may be text; industries with few cases will produce noisy averages.

title: Illness Type Fingerprint By Industry
idea: Heatmap grid of industry against the mix of skin disorders, respiratory conditions, poisonings, and hearing loss, giving each industry a distinct harm signature.
harm_angle: Occupational illness is slow, invisible harm that shows up years later as deafness or lung disease, and this names the industries producing it.
caveat: Illness columns are uncast and likely heavily zero; underreporting of illness versus injury is a known bias in this filing.

title: Deaths Concentrated By Employer Size
idea: Scatter of establishment size band against total deaths, testing whether small establishments kill workers at higher rates than large ones.
harm_angle: If small workplaces have far higher fatality rates, the inspection regime is aimed at the wrong employers.
caveat: Deaths are rare per establishment so most rows are zero; size is a coded band whose meaning is not in the model.

title: Injury Rate By Industry 2024
idea: Ranked bars of injury cases per hours worked by industry for 2024, the same lens as the prior year so the two can be read side by side.
harm_angle: Names the industries where getting hurt is a routine part of the job.
caveat: Numeric fields uncast in the model; self-reported data with known underreporting.

title: State Injury Rate Map 2024
idea: Map shading each state by injury cases per hour worked across all reporting establishments, showing enforcement and hazard geography together.
harm_angle: Workers in high-rate states are absorbing risk that workers elsewhere are not, often under weaker state enforcement.
caveat: State is the establishment address; multi-state employers report per establishment, which is good, but industry mix differs by state and will confound.

title: Employers Who Amended Their Numbers
idea: Ranked bars of stated change reasons on amended filings, showing how often and why establishments revise their reported injury counts.
harm_angle: Revisions that lower injury counts after the fact are a quiet way to disappear a worker's injury from the public record.
caveat: change_reason fill rate unknown; the mart holds one row per filing so before-and-after comparison may not be possible within one year file.

title: Hearing Loss Hotspots
idea: Map of establishments reporting hearing loss cases, plotted by zip code and sized by case count, isolating the noise-damage geography.
harm_angle: Hearing loss is permanent, uncompensated, and almost never makes the news, yet it is one of the most common industrial injuries.
caveat: Hearing loss counts are uncast and likely sparse; zip codes may be malformed or five-plus-four mixed.

title: Big Employers With Clean Records
idea: Dot plot of establishments with very large employee counts and very low reported case counts, ranked by how far below their industry norm they sit.
harm_angle: Large employers reporting implausibly clean numbers are the best candidates for a look at whether injuries are being discouraged from being reported.
caveat: Requires an industry-norm baseline computed from the same file; genuinely safe employers will be flagged alongside suspicious ones.

title: Injury Rate By Industry 2025
idea: Ranked bars of injury cases per hours worked by industry for 2025, the most recent year of establishment summaries.
harm_angle: The current-year picture of which industries hurt the most workers.
caveat: 2025 file may be partial if filing season was still open at ingest; numeric fields uncast.

title: Who Stopped Filing
idea: Ranked bars by state and industry of establishments present in earlier-year files but absent in 2025, mapping where mandatory reporting quietly lapsed.
harm_angle: An establishment that stops filing is a workplace whose injuries are now invisible, with no penalty visible in the data.
caveat: Requires reading the three year files together; establishment_id stability across years is unverified and closures look identical to non-filing.

title: Severity Versus Frequency Quadrant
idea: Scatter of case frequency against average days away per case by industry, splitting industries into frequent-and-minor versus rare-and-devastating.
harm_angle: Rare-but-devastating industries get overlooked by counts-based enforcement even though they ruin more lives per incident.
caveat: Uncast numeric fields; small-denominator industries will fly to the corners.

title: Establishment Type And Risk
idea: Small multiples by establishment type of the injury rate distribution, testing whether contract and staffing sites report differently from direct employers.
harm_angle: Temp and contract workers are widely believed to absorb the worst risk while appearing on nobody's injury log.
caveat: establishment_type coding is not documented in the model; may not distinguish staffing arrangements at all.

title: Corporate Families Behind The Injuries
idea: Ranked bars grouping establishments by parent company name and employer id, showing the corporate groups with the largest total injury burden.
harm_angle: Establishment-level reporting hides that one corporation may be responsible for thousands of injuries across hundreds of sites.
caveat: company_name is free text needing normalization and the employer id may be masked or blank; the catalog lists it as a key but that is unverified.

title: What Actually Injures Workers
idea: Ranked bars of the classified event type and source of injury across all 2023 cases, showing the physical mechanisms that hurt people most often.
harm_angle: Naming the specific machines, falls, and substances that hurt people turns an abstract injury count into a fixable list.
caveat: The classification fields are model predictions (the _pred suffix), not human coding, so accuracy is unknown.

title: Injuries By Hour Of Shift
idea: Heatmap grid of time started work against time of incident, showing how injury risk builds through a shift.
harm_angle: If injuries spike in hours nine through twelve, shift-length rules are directly costing workers their bodies.
caveat: Both time fields are text in this model and may be inconsistently formatted; time_unknown suggests a large missing share.

title: Which Jobs Get Hurt
idea: Ranked bars of occupation codes by case count and by average days away, naming the specific job titles that absorb the most harm.
harm_angle: Puts a job title on the injury, which is how a reader recognizes their own work in the data.
caveat: Occupation codes are predicted with a confidence score and flagged whether reviewed; unreviewed low-confidence codes may dominate.

title: Days Between Incident And Death
idea: Distribution of the gap between incident date and date of death for fatal cases, showing how many workers die weeks after the accident.
harm_angle: Delayed deaths are often excluded from fatality headlines, so the true toll of a workplace is understated.
caveat: date_of_death fill rate is unknown and fatal cases are rare; both dates are text-cast and may fail.

title: Seasonal Injury Calendar
idea: Cohort grid of incident date by month and day of week, faceted by industry, showing heat-related and seasonal injury waves.
harm_angle: Summer heat spikes in outdoor industries are a preventable, repeating, named cause of worker harm.
caveat: 500,000-row cap on this mart per the model comment suggests the year is truncated, which would bias any seasonal pattern.

title: Injury Mechanisms 2024
idea: Ranked bars of predicted event and source categories for 2024 cases, the current-year version of what physically hurts workers.
harm_angle: A current list of the specific hazards putting people in hospital.
caveat: Predicted classification fields; 500,000-row cap suggests truncation.

title: Amputation And Crush Geography
idea: Map of cases whose predicted nature is amputation or crush injury, plotted by state and zip, showing the machine-injury belt.
harm_angle: Amputations are life-changing and largely preventable with guarding, so their geography is a map of where guarding rules are not enforced.
caveat: Relies on predicted nature codes; zip-level mapping may be sparse and the row cap could distort geography.

title: Same Employer Same Injury Repeats
idea: Ranked bars of establishments with multiple cases sharing the same predicted event type, exposing employers that keep producing the identical accident.
harm_angle: A workplace that injures three people the same way in one year has a known hazard it chose not to fix.
caveat: Depends on establishment_id being stable and on the predicted event code being accurate enough to group by.

title: Outcome Severity By Occupation
idea: Heatmap grid of occupation group against incident outcome (days away, restricted duty, other, death), showing which jobs produce the worst outcomes.
harm_angle: Restricted duty can be a way to keep a case off the serious-injury log while the worker is still hurt.
caveat: Occupation codes are predicted; outcome vocabulary is not documented in the model.

title: Narrative Language Patterns
idea: Ranked bars of the most common phrases in the free-text incident narratives, grouped by industry, letting workers' own descriptions of what happened surface.
harm_angle: The narrative fields are the closest thing in the data to the injured person's own account of what was done to them.
caveat: Narratives may be heavily redacted or blank; text analysis of hundreds of thousands of rows is a big lift and the row cap truncates.

title: Injury Mechanisms 2025
idea: Ranked bars of predicted event and source categories for 2025 cases, the most recent detailed injury picture.
harm_angle: The freshest available list of what is hurting workers right now.
caveat: 330,447 rows suggests a partial year; predicted classification fields.

title: Classifier Confidence By Industry
idea: Distribution of occupation-code confidence scores split by whether a human reviewed the code, faceted by industry.
harm_angle: If the occupation attached to an injury is a low-confidence machine guess, every downstream claim about which workers get hurt is shaky.
caveat: soc_probability may be text; the reviewed flag's vocabulary is undocumented.

title: Where On The Body
idea: Ranked bars of predicted injured body part crossed with industry, giving a body map of each industry's characteristic damage.
harm_angle: Back, hand, and eye injuries each imply a different failure of protective equipment or job design.
caveat: Predicted body-part codes; accuracy unknown and partial-year data.

title: Longest Recovery Cases
idea: Distribution of days away from work per case with the extreme tail labelled by industry and occupation, showing the injuries that end careers.
harm_angle: A worker with 180 days away is usually a worker who never returns to that job or that income.
caveat: Days-away values may be capped at a maximum by the reporting form, which would truncate the tail artificially.

title: Incident Location Words
idea: Ranked bars of the reported incident-location field, showing whether injuries happen on the employer's premises or out in public and private worksites.
harm_angle: Off-premises injuries fall into enforcement gaps because no single site owner is clearly responsible.
caveat: Location field is free text and likely needs categorization before it charts at all.

title: Claims against the pension backstop over time
idea: Timeline of claim metrics by program type, showing when the insurer of last resort absorbed the biggest waves of failed plans.
harm_angle: Every claim is a group of retirees whose promised pension got capped.
caveat: This is a long, tall metric table: metric_name must be filtered carefully and units differ by row.

title: State map of insured participants
idea: State choropleth of insured pension participants, showing where the private defined-benefit system is still meaningful and where it has vanished.
harm_angle: States with collapsed defined-benefit coverage have retirees dependent on savings and Social Security alone.
caveat: State is populated only for the subset of tables that break down geographically.

title: Single-employer versus multiemployer divergence
idea: Slope chart of key financial-position metrics for the two programs across years, showing the multiemployer program's separate trajectory.
harm_angle: Multiemployer plan members faced benefit cuts single-employer members did not.
caveat: Metric names differ between programs so a like-for-like pairing must be hand-built.

title: Which statistical tables get quietly dropped
idea: Heatmap grid of table name against data year with color as row presence, exposing reporting series that stop being published.
harm_angle: A discontinued statistical series is accountability that quietly disappears.
caveat: Absence may reflect the ingest rather than the agency discontinuing the table.

source_names: PBGC Single-Employer Plans Trusteed by PBGC
title: Pensions Lost, By Year
idea: Timeline of participants in plans taken over by the federal insurer each year since 1974, with recessions visible in the shape.
harm_angle: Every point is thousands of workers whose promised pension was cut to an insurance cap.
caveat: Participant column name is misspelled in source; left-10 date parse may fail on some rows.

source_names: PBGC Single-Employer Plans Trusteed by PBGC
title: The Trusteeship Lag
idea: Distribution of the gap between plan termination and federal takeover, showing how long workers waited in limbo.
harm_angle: A multi-year gap is years of retirees not knowing what their check will be.
caveat: Either date may be null; negative gaps possible if source dates are swapped.

source_names: PBGC Single-Employer Plans Trusteed by PBGC
title: Where Pension Failure Landed
idea: Map of trusteed plans by sponsor state, weighted by participants, showing the deindustrialization footprint.
harm_angle: Whole regional workforces lost retirement security together.
caveat: Sponsor state is the headquarters, not where the workers were.

source_names: PBGC Single-Employer Plans Trusteed by PBGC
title: Serial Sponsors Of Failed Plans
idea: Ranked bars of employers by EIN with more than one trusteed plan -- companies that failed workers repeatedly.
harm_angle: Same employer, multiple broken promises, no visible consequence.
caveat: EIN may be blank or masked on older cases and sponsor names change through bankruptcy.

title: Map of tribal land holdings
idea: Map of tribal land features by state, sized by area, the base geography for every tribal-impact story.
harm_angle: Establishes which communities land sits where before any harm overlay.
caveat: 102 rows -- likely a layer catalog rather than full parcel geometry.

title: Land base by state ranked
idea: Ranked bars of total tribal land area by state, showing the enormous variance in what was left to tribes.
harm_angle: Quantifies how little land remains in states that dispossessed most aggressively.
caveat: area_sqmi may be blank for boundary-only layers; summing across layers double-counts.

title: How stale is the tribal map
idea: Dot plot of each layer by its last-updated date, showing which tribal geography the federal government has quietly stopped maintaining.
harm_angle: Stale official boundaries mean tribes get miscounted in every federal program keyed to geography.
caveat: last_updated may be text or missing; only 102 rows to work with.

title: Fragmentation of the land base
idea: Distribution of feature areas per state, revealing checkerboarded, fragmented holdings versus contiguous reservations.
harm_angle: Fragmented land is unfarmable, unfinanceable and unpoliceable -- the practical legacy of allotment.
caveat: Needs real parcel geometry; a 102-row layer index cannot show fragmentation.

title: Withdrawn cosponsorships
idea: Timeline of cosponsorship withdrawals by congress and party, the rare public act of a member backing away from a bill.
harm_angle: Withdrawals mark the moment lobbying or backlash flipped a member off a bill.
caveat: Withdrawn dates are present only for withdrawals, so n is small and may be very sparse.

title: The bipartisan cosponsorship web
idea: Network of members linked by shared cosponsorships, colored by party, showing whether cross-party ties actually exist or just get claimed.
harm_angle: When cross-party ties collapse, bills that would help people stop moving entirely.
caveat: 367k rows makes the raw network unrenderable; needs aggregation to member-pair counts.

title: Original versus late signers
idea: Distribution of days from bill introduction to cosponsorship, split by original-cosponsor flag, showing who commits early and who waits for safety.
harm_angle: Members who only sign safe bills late are members not spending capital on their constituents.
caveat: Introduction date lives in the billstatus table, not here -- strictly this needs the sibling table.

title: Cosponsorship load by member
idea: Ranked bars of cosponsorships per member per congress, showing signature-machine members versus members who barely sign anything.
harm_angle: High cosponsor counts with no passed bills is a member performing work rather than doing it.
caveat: Does not distinguish serious legislating from bulk signing.

title: The law-making funnel
idea: Flow diagram from bills introduced to bills with action to bills enacted, per congress, showing how tiny the enacted slice is.
harm_angle: Almost everything introduced dies, so the bills that survive reveal whose interests actually clear the funnel.
caveat: law_type and law_number are populated only for enacted bills; nulls must be read as not-enacted, not missing.

title: Sponsors who never pass anything
idea: Ranked bars of members by bills sponsored versus bills enacted, exposing high-volume sponsors with a zero success rate.
harm_angle: Members who introduce constantly and pass nothing are performing representation, not delivering it.
caveat: Cross-congress comparison needs majority or minority status, which is not in this table.

title: Time from introduction to law
idea: Distribution of days from introduction to enactment by congress, showing whether the process is slowing down.
harm_angle: Slower lawmaking means urgent harms wait longer for any legal response.
caveat: latest_action_date is not the enactment date for every bill; approximation only.

title: Cosponsor count versus survival
idea: Scatter of cosponsor count against whether a bill became law, showing whether broad support actually predicts passage or is decoration.
harm_angle: If cosponsorship does not predict passage, public support signals are theatre.
caveat: latest_action_text is number-cast in the model, which will null it -- avoid relying on that column.

title: Dead-on-arrival heatmap
idea: Heatmap grid of congress by bill type shaded by share of bills with only a single action, the graveyard of never-considered legislation.
harm_angle: Bills that never get a second action are issues the leadership decided nobody needed to hear about.
caveat: n_actions semantics unverified; may count procedural noise.

title: Antipsychotics in Nursing Homes
idea: Map the facility-level percentage for MDS items covering antipsychotic use and restraints, by county. Viewer sees regions where chemical restraint is routine.
harm_angle: Sedated residents cannot complain, fall less visibly, and die sooner - this is the quiet abuse pattern in long-term care.
caveat: MDS item descriptions are free text and must be filtered to the right questions; county_name is cast to a number which suggests a mis-typed column.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Minimum Data Set frequencies

idea: Scatter short_stay_percent against long_stay_percent per facility for the same MDS item. Viewer sees facilities that treat their long-stay residents very differently from their rehab patients.
harm_angle: Long-stay residents have no advocate and no discharge date - divergence is where neglect hides.
caveat: Percentages are try_to_double casts over text; small resident counts make percentages unstable.

title: Facilities That Report Everything the Same
idea: Flag facilities whose responses across many MDS items are implausibly uniform or identical quarter to quarter.
chart_shape: heatmap grid of facility against item
harm_angle: Copy-paste assessments mean nobody actually looked at the resident.
caveat: Uniformity can be genuine for stable small facilities; needs a careful null model.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Minimum Data Set frequencies
title: Reporting Over Time by Facility
idea: Timeline of report_date coverage per CCN, showing facilities that stop reporting.
chart_shape: cohort grid of facility against report date
harm_angle: A facility that stops reporting is a facility no one is measuring while residents still live there.
caveat: Gaps may reflect ingest partitioning rather than real non-reporting; 31M rows needs aggregation.

title: Vessels Going Dark
idea: For each mmsi, find gaps in the hourly position stream while the vessel was underway, and map where those blackouts start. Viewer sees the specific waters where transponders switch off.
harm_angle: Transponder blackouts are the cover for illegal fishing, sanctions evasion and dumping - all of which land on coastal communities.
caveat: Gaps also come from receiver coverage holes rather than deliberate darkening; 58M rows means heavy aggregation.

title: Anchorage Loitering Hotspots
idea: Heatmap of positions where speed_category is moored or slow, outside designated anchorages. Viewer sees vessels parked where they should not be.
harm_angle: Loitering tankers offshore of port communities mean idling emissions and unregulated transfers next to where people live.

title: Draft Changes at Sea
idea: Track draft_meters per vessel over a voyage. A change in reported draft away from any port suggests a ship-to-ship transfer.
chart_shape: timeline per vessel plus map of change points
harm_angle: Ship-to-ship transfers at sea are how sanctioned and untaxed cargo enters the supply chain.
caveat: Draft is manually entered by crew and is notoriously stale or wrong.

title: Traffic Density Near Populated Coast
idea: Density heatmap of vessel positions by vessel_type_code across US waters for 2024.
harm_angle: Heavy traffic lanes hugging shorelines are the pollution and collision exposure for coastal towns.
caveat: 2024 only; imo_number is about 56 percent blank or placeholder per the model comment - use mmsi, never imo_number.

title: Political Groups Born Before Elections
idea: Timeline of Form 8871 registrations by month with election months marked, showing the pre-election surge of new groups.
harm_angle: Groups spun up weeks before a vote spend and dissolve before anyone can trace them.
caveat: established_date parse reliability unverified; text dates are a known trap on this platform.

title: Groups That Claimed Exemption
idea: Ranked bars of registrations claiming exemption from 8872 or 990 reporting, trended by cycle.
harm_angle: Claiming exemption is the legal on-ramp to spending without disclosure.
caveat: Indicator encoding unverified; blanks may not mean no.

title: Address Clusters Of 527s
idea: Dot plot of mailing addresses hosting many different 527 organizations -- the shared-office political industry.
harm_angle: One consultant office fronting dozens of grassroots-sounding groups misleads every voter who reads the name.
caveat: Address strings are unnormalized and suite lines will split true clusters.

title: What They Say They Are For
idea: Ranked bars of stated purpose themes by state, contrasted with the group name.
harm_angle: Vague boilerplate purpose statements are how the real backer stays invisible.
caveat: purpose is long free text and grouping requires a keyword scheme that is a judgment call.

title: Political Money By Reporting Period
idea: Timeline of total contributions (Schedule A) and expenditures (Schedule B) across all 527s by period end date.
harm_angle: The raw scale of undisclosed-donor political money moving each cycle.
caveat: Totals are report-level; amendments may double count without dedup on form_id_number.

title: Pre-Election Spending Spikes
idea: Small multiples by state of expenditure totals around pre-election report dates, showing last-minute money dumps.
harm_angle: Money landing after the last disclosure deadline shapes votes with no time for scrutiny.

title: Groups That Raise But Never Spend
idea: Scatter of contributions against expenditures per organization, highlighting the off-diagonal warehousers of cash.
harm_angle: Cash parked in a political shell is money whose purpose no voter ever learns.

title: Final Report Then Silence
idea: Timeline of groups filing a final report, cross-checked against later filings under the same EIN.
harm_angle: Declaring the group dead and then re-emerging is how a donor network resets its record.
caveat: final_report_ind encoding unverified; EIN reuse across successor groups is assumed.

title: People Who Run Many PACs
idea: Ranked bars of individuals serving as director or officer across the largest number of distinct 527 organizations.
harm_angle: A handful of operators steer dozens of nominally separate political groups.

harm_angle: The overlap map shows that independent-looking groups share the same handful of controllers.

title: Officers By Home State
idea: Map of officer counts by their listed state against the organization state, revealing out-of-state control.
harm_angle: Local-sounding groups run from another state are astroturf by definition.
caveat: Officer address may simply repeat the organization address, collapsing the comparison.

title: Titles That Do The Work
idea: Distribution of officer titles, showing how many groups have only a treasurer and no real board.
harm_angle: A one-person board means no internal check on how the money is used.
caveat: Title text is uncontrolled and needs grouping to be readable.

title: Which States 527s Register In
idea: Ranked bars of election-authority IDs by issuing state, showing where federal 527s also play at state level.
harm_angle: State-level registration is where the same money reaches local races with the least scrutiny.
caveat: Only 17,853 rows; coverage may be partial and state_issued fill rate is unverified.

title: Groups Registered In Many States
idea: Dot plot of organizations by count of distinct state election authorities they hold IDs with.
harm_angle: Multi-state operations concentrate influence while looking like separate local efforts.
caveat: Thin table; requires joining the 8871 registry for organization names.

title: The 527 Affiliation Web
idea: Network graph of organizations to their declared related entities, colored by relationship type.
harm_angle: Declared affiliations reveal which separate-looking committees are actually one machine.
