idea: Flow diagram from organization state to related-entity state, showing national networks wearing local names.
harm_angle: Out-of-state parents behind local committees hide who is really funding a race.
caveat: Requires the organization state from the 8871 registry and address fields may be the same office.

title: Complaint Rate by ZIP
idea: Map of ZIP codes shaded by complaints per capita, showing the neighborhoods where consumer finance harm concentrates.
harm_angle: Complaint-dense ZIPs are the neighborhoods where debt collectors and servicers work hardest.
caveat: Row count differs between catalog and mart comment (34M vs 17M), suggesting a duplicated or partially reloaded table; per-capita needs external population.

title: Companies That Never Give Relief
idea: Ranked bars of companies by complaint volume with each bar split by response type, isolating firms that close nearly everything without relief.
harm_angle: A company that closes every complaint without relief has learned the process costs it nothing.
caveat: Company names are free text with subsidiary variation; response categories changed definition over time.

title: Response Time Drift
idea: Distribution of days from date received to date sent to company, small-multipled by year, showing whether the pipeline slowed.
harm_angle: Delay in routing a complaint is extra weeks of a wrongful foreclosure or garnishment continuing.
caveat: Both date fields are left as raw text in the mart and must be parsed; text dates are a known trap here.

title: Issue Mix by Product Over Time
idea: Heatmap of product against issue shaded by complaint volume, small-multipled by year, exposing new harms as they emerge.
harm_angle: A rising issue cell is a new way consumers are being harmed before regulators name it.
caveat: Product and issue taxonomies were revised by CFPB, so cells are not comparable across the whole span.

title: Servicemember and Older-American Tags
idea: Grouped bars of relief rate by the tags field, testing whether flagged vulnerable consumers get better or worse outcomes.
harm_angle: Older Americans and servicemembers flagged as vulnerable and still denied relief are the clearest harm signal in the file.
caveat: tags is populated on only a minority of complaints and is self-identified.

title: Narrative Language Clusters
idea: Network of complaint narratives clustered by shared language, per product, surfacing scripted harms that repeat across thousands of consumers.
harm_angle: Identical language across thousands of complaints means one company practice hitting thousands of people the same way.
caveat: Narratives are opt-in and present on a minority of rows; text clustering at 17M+ rows is heavy compute.

title: Bank Branch and Asset Map
idea: Map of institutions as points sized by total assets and colored by charter class, showing where banking capacity actually sits.
harm_angle: Counties with no institution headquartered nearby are the ones served only by payday lenders.
caveat: Mart is a 10,000-row API slice, explicitly not the full institution universe.

title: Deposits vs Loans by Institution
idea: Scatter of domestic deposits against total assets colored by charter agent, showing which institutions gather local deposits without lending locally.
harm_angle: Deposits taken from a community and lent elsewhere is capital extraction from that community.
caveat: 10,000-row slice; the loan side is not in this table so the extraction claim needs another source.

title: Bank Formation and Death
idea: Timeline of establishment and effective-end dates as a cohort grid, showing the decades-long consolidation of American banking.
harm_angle: Every closed community bank is a town that lost its only local lender.
caveat: Date fields are untyped in the staging alias list; the 10,000-row slice may skew toward currently active institutions.

title: Holding Company Concentration
idea: Network of institutions to their multi-bank holding company flag and specialization group, showing how many nominally separate banks share an owner.
harm_angle: Consolidation behind holding companies means apparent local choice is one balance sheet.
caveat: hctmult is a flag, not a holding company id, so the real network needs an RSSD parent link this table lacks.

title: Past-Due Loans as an Early Warning
idea: Scatter of 90-day-plus past due loans against tier 1 capital per institution, marking banks whose bad loans exceed their cushion.
harm_angle: A bank whose bad loans exceed its capital fails, and depositors and borrowers in that town absorb it.
caveat: Only 302 rows -- a probe extract, not the full call report set; past_due and tier1 columns are left untyped.

title: Loan-to-Deposit Stretch
idea: Distribution of total loans over total deposits by institution, showing which banks are lending far beyond their funding base.
harm_angle: Overstretched banks pull credit first when conditions tighten, and small borrowers are cut first.
caveat: 302-row extract; the doctype_html column suggests the scrape captured page markup, a data-quality red flag.

title: The Scrape Broke Here
idea: Dot plot of rows carrying a real RSSD id and a parsed reporting period against those carrying HTML markup, making the ingest failure the visible finding.
harm_angle: A broken bank-financials ingest means no one can check which banks are failing the communities they fund.
caveat: Diagnostic only; confirms a pipeline problem rather than a public harm.

title: EITC Take-Up by ZIP
idea: Map of ZIP codes shaded by EITC claims as a share of returns, showing where the largest anti-poverty credit reaches and where it does not.
harm_angle: Low-income ZIPs with low EITC take-up are households leaving thousands of dollars of owed refund unclaimed.
caveat: Most numeric columns are left untyped text in the mart; ZIP-level SOI suppresses small cells.

title: Paid Preparer Dependence
idea: Scatter of paid-preparer share against average AGI by ZIP, showing that the poorest filers most often pay someone to claim their own refund.
harm_angle: Low-income filers paying a preparer lose a slice of their refund to get money they are already owed.
caveat: prep is untyped; refund-anticipation columns (ral, rac) may be discontinued in recent years.

title: Refund Anticipation Product Geography
idea: Map of ZIPs shaded by refund anticipation loan and check counts, marking the neighborhoods targeted by high-cost tax-refund products.
harm_angle: Refund anticipation products charge triple-digit effective rates to people waiting on their own tax refund.
caveat: RAL/RAC columns were discontinued in later SOI years, so coverage may be a narrow window; untyped.

title: Income Bracket Composition by State
idea: Small multiples of the AGI-stub distribution per state over tax years, showing where the middle of the income distribution hollowed out.
harm_angle: A state whose middle brackets thin out is one where households moved down, not up.
caveat: agi_stub bracket definitions shift with inflation across years and must be rebased.

title: Free Tax Help Deserts
idea: Map overlaying VITA and TCE volunteer-prepared return counts against low-income return density, exposing ZIPs with need and no free help.
harm_angle: Low-income ZIPs with no free preparation are exactly where paid preparers and refund loans take the biggest cut.
caveat: VITA columns may be sparsely populated and are untyped; not all SOI years carry them.

title: Credit Union Consolidation Since 1994
idea: Timeline of distinct reporting credit unions per quarter, split by charter type, showing thirty years of institutions disappearing.
harm_angle: Every credit union that vanishes is a member-owned lender replaced by a for-profit one.
caveat: Account-code grain means distinct-count needs deduping to institution-quarter first.

title: Small Credit Unions Under Stress
idea: Scatter of asset size against a delinquency or net-worth account code per credit union, marking small institutions in the danger zone.
harm_angle: Members of a failing credit union lose the only lender that would approve them.
caveat: Requires the NCUA account-code dictionary to identify the right acct_code; acct_desc may substitute but is free text.

title: Credit Union Coverage Map
idea: Map of credit unions by ZIP and city, sized by asset code value, showing which communities still have a member-owned lender.
harm_angle: ZIPs with no credit union are served only by banks and payday lenders on worse terms.
caveat: Address is the headquarters, not branches, so coverage is overstated for multi-branch institutions.

title: Account Code Reporting Gaps
idea: Heatmap of account code against quarter shaded by reporting institution count, exposing which financial disclosures credit unions quietly stopped filing.
harm_angle: Discontinued disclosures are the metrics regulators stopped being able to check on members' behalf.
caveat: acct_status semantics unverified; form changes over 30 years will dominate the pattern.

title: Filer Geography by Industry
idea: Map of filer business addresses colored by SIC industry group, showing where each industry's corporate headquarters cluster.
harm_angle: Industries headquartered far from where they operate answer to no local community.
caveat: countryba and countryma are cast to number on name columns and are likely all-null; mart comment says 6,699 rows while the catalog says 55,635.

title: Incorporated There Operating Here
idea: Flow diagram from state of incorporation to state of business address, showing the Delaware funnel in one picture.
harm_angle: Incorporating away from where you operate is how companies choose which state's law protects the people they harm.
caveat: stprinc population unverified; row-count discrepancy between catalog and mart comment suggests a partial load.

title: Filers Without an Address
idea: Dot plot of filers by how many address and identifier fields are populated, exposing entities that file with almost no traceable location.
harm_angle: A filer with no findable address is a company no injured party can serve.
caveat: Diagnostic; address blankness may reflect the extract rather than the filing.

title: Industry Concentration by SIC
idea: Ranked bars of SIC codes by filer count, showing which industries dominate the public-company universe.
harm_angle: Concentrated industries set prices and wages for everyone in them.
caveat: Descriptive floor chart; SIC is a legacy taxonomy that mis-sorts modern firms.

title: Insider Filing Lag By Company
idea: Plot the gap between the transaction period and the filing date for each Form 4, ranked by company. Companies whose insiders chronically file late surface as a persistent bad-actor band.
harm_angle: Retail shareholders trade blind while insiders sit on unreported sales past the legal two-day window.
caveat: period_of_report is untyped text in the mart while filing_date is a date - the subtraction may need parsing; no transaction amount column exists.

title: Rule 10b5-1 Adoption Wave
idea: Track the share of filings flagged as made under a 10b5-1 trading plan over time, split by filing volume as a company-size proxy. Shows who reached for the legal-cover mechanism and when.
harm_angle: 10b5-1 plans can launder opportunistic selling into pre-scheduled trades; the adoption curve shows who reached for the shield.
caveat: aff10b5one may be sparsely populated or a blank-string sentinel; only exists on newer form versions.

title: Amended Filings As Cleanup Signal
idea: Count filings whose document type indicates an amendment per issuer and per year. Heavy amenders are companies whose original disclosures were wrong.
chart_shape: heatmap grid of issuer by year
harm_angle: Every amendment marks a period where the public record was wrong and someone traded against it.
caveat: document_type values unverified; the amendment suffix convention is assumed.

title: Form 3 Silence After Onboarding
idea: For each issuer, chart initial Form 3 statements that never produce a later Form 4 against those that do. Insiders who register and never report a trade are either clean or invisible.
harm_angle: Registered insiders with no follow-up filings are a blind spot in the only public record of executive self-dealing.
caveat: Requires linking filings by insider identity but the mart carries only issuer CIK - the reporting person may not be identifiable.

title: Filing Bursts Around Quiet Dates
idea: Plot filing-date density by day of week and week of year across all issuers, looking for pile-ups on Fridays and pre-holiday windows - the classic bury-it dates.
chart_shape: heatmap grid of weekday by week
harm_angle: Disclosures timed to be missed are disclosures designed not to inform the people they legally protect.
caveat: filing_date is a try_to_date cast - a parse failure would silently null rows and skew the density.

title: Options Exercised at the Right Moment
idea: Scatter of exercise date against expiration date colored by transaction value, isolating exercises timed far ahead of expiry.
harm_angle: Early exercises clustered before price moves are how executives convert information into cash.
caveat: Single quarter; several date fields are try_to_date-cast and may be widely null.

title: Strike Price vs Market Reality
idea: Distribution of conversion and exercise prices by security title, showing how far in the money insider derivatives are granted.
harm_angle: Deep-in-the-money grants are compensation disclosed as an option rather than as pay.
caveat: Needs external market price for a true moneyness read; single quarter.

title: Equity Swaps and Timeliness Flags
idea: Grouped bars of transaction timeliness flags against whether an equity swap was involved, exposing where the most complex trades are also the latest reported.
harm_angle: The most opaque insider instruments being the least timely filed is a disclosure gap investors cannot see.
caveat: Both flag columns may be sparsely populated; the footnote-suffixed twin columns are cast oddly and likely null.

title: Buy vs Sell Balance by Code
idea: Stacked timeline of transaction value by transaction code, separating open-market sales from grants and gifts, showing what insiders actually do with equity.
harm_angle: Open-market selling clustered before bad news is the mechanism retail investors lose money to.
caveat: Single quarter; transaction_value is computed as shares times price and is null when either is missing.

title: Selling Clusters in Time
idea: Heatmap of trading day against issuer shaded by net insider disposition value, exposing days where an issuer's whole insider group sold at once.
harm_angle: Coordinated same-day selling by every insider at a company is the clearest pre-bad-news pattern there is.
caveat: Needs a join to submissions for issuer identity; one-quarter window limits how many clusters appear.

title: Ownership Drawdown Paths
idea: Timeline of shares owned after each transaction per insider, showing individuals steadily liquidating their entire stake.
harm_angle: An executive quietly zeroing out their stake while telling investors to hold is the harm.
caveat: Requires owner identity from the reportingowner table; a quarter is too short for a full drawdown path.

title: Indirect Ownership Vehicles
idea: Ranked bars of the nature-of-ownership free-text values by transaction value, exposing the trusts and LLCs through which insiders hold stock.
harm_angle: Indirect holding structures obscure who actually profits from insider trades.
caveat: nature_of_ownership is free text with enormous variation and is null for direct holdings.

source_names: SEC EDGAR Insider Transactions Reporting Owners
title: Who the Insiders Are
idea: Ranked bars of insider relationship types -- officer, director, ten-percent owner -- by count, split by whether a title is disclosed.
harm_angle: Undisclosed titles let control persons trade without investors knowing their role.
caveat: relationship is a packed flag string in SEC filings and may need parsing; single quarter.

source_names: SEC EDGAR Insider Transactions Reporting Owners
title: Insider Geography
idea: Map of insider home states and ZIPs by filing count, showing the concentration of corporate control in a handful of places.
harm_angle: Corporate control clustered in a few wealthy ZIPs is the geography of who owns American companies.
caveat: Addresses are often the company's, not the person's; ZIP population unverified.

source_names: SEC EDGAR Insider Transactions Reporting Owners
title: Insiders Sitting on Many Boards
idea: Network of owner CIKs to the accession numbers they appear on, isolating individuals reporting at multiple issuers.
harm_angle: Interlocking insiders coordinate across companies in ways no single filing reveals.
caveat: Requires joining to submissions to get issuer identity; owner_cik population and stability unverified.

title: Filing Timeliness by Issuer
idea: Distribution of days from period of report to filing date per issuer, exposing companies whose insiders routinely file late.
harm_angle: Late insider filings mean ordinary investors trade blind while executives have already sold.
caveat: Single-quarter slice (2025Q1) only; date parsing depends on a DD-MON-YYYY format holding.

title: Amended Filings as a Signal
idea: Timeline of original versus amended submissions per issuer, flagging companies that repeatedly restate insider disclosures.
harm_angle: Repeated amendments hide the real trade date from investors reading the original filing.
caveat: One quarter only; document_type value set unverified.

title: Filing Volume by Ticker
idea: Ranked bars of issuers by insider filing count in the quarter, giving the base rate against which unusual activity is measured.
harm_angle: Baseline volume is what makes an insider selling spike legible to a retail investor.
caveat: Descriptive floor chart; one-quarter window.

title: Who Each Country Owes
idea: For a chosen debtor country, break out debt stock by creditor counterpart across years - bilateral, multilateral, private - so the creditor mix and its shift is visible in one frame.
harm_angle: Debt service crowds out health and schooling budgets in the poorest countries; the creditor mix decides who can force austerity.
caveat: The mart wraps country_name and counterpart_area_name in try_to_number, which will null out text country names - a modelling bug that likely kills this until fixed.

title: Debt Service Versus Stock Squeeze
idea: Scatter each country's annual debt service against total external debt stock, one point per country-year, with a trail showing the path. Countries drifting to the high-service corner pay more than they can carry.
harm_angle: When service payments outrun the economy, the cut falls on clinics and teachers, not on creditors.
caveat: Series must be pivoted out of the wide year columns; try_to_number on country_code may destroy ISO3 text codes.

title: The Bilateral Creditor Shift
idea: Small multiples per debtor region showing the share of debt owed to one specific bilateral creditor over four decades. Reveals where lending power migrated between 1990 and today.
harm_angle: Which government holds the debt determines whether restructuring is possible when a crisis hits ordinary people.
caveat: Counterpart names may be nulled by the numeric cast; regional grouping is not in the source and must be added.

title: Projection Cliff Check
idea: Plot the last reported year against the first projected year for every country-series to expose where the data actually stops and the modelling begins.
harm_angle: Analysts and journalists cite projections as fact; showing the cliff protects readers from a manufactured number.
caveat: Requires knowing which columns are actuals versus projections - the description says 2025+ but that is not encoded in the mart.

title: Debt Crisis Cohort Grid
idea: Group countries by the decade they first crossed a debt-service threshold and follow each cohort forward. Shows whether relief programmes broke the cycle or only paused it.
harm_angle: Repeat debt crises in the same countries mean a generation grows up under austerity twice.
caveat: Threshold choice is analyst-defined; text country names may be nulled by the numeric cast.

source_names: FARA Foreign Agents Registration Act Database
title: Foreign Principal Payment Flows
idea: Chart receipts and disbursements per registrant against the foreign principal represented, showing which foreign interests buy the most US influence work.
harm_angle: Foreign money shaping US policy debates is only visible in this filing; the amounts show whose voice is bought.
caveat: Only 30 rows in the mart - a token sample, not the real FARA corpus; foreign_principal_country is wrapped in try_to_number and will be nulled.

source_names: FARA Foreign Agents Registration Act Database
title: Registration To Termination Lifespan
idea: Plot each registration as a horizontal bar from registration to termination date, sorted by length, exposing short-lived engagements clustered around specific events.
harm_angle: Short registrations timed to a vote or a scandal are the sharpest signal of targeted foreign lobbying.
caveat: 30 rows only; termination_date is likely null for active registrations.

title: Foreign Principals By Country
idea: Map the count and activity span of foreign principals by the country they represent, showing which governments maintain the deepest standing US representation.
harm_angle: Standing foreign representation is a permanent lobbying presence that ordinary constituents cannot match.
caveat: Country field is free text needing normalisation; the mart is 48k rows across four record shapes so the grain is mixed.

title: Registrant To Principal Network
idea: Build a bipartite network of registrants and the foreign principals they represent. Firms serving many rival governments simultaneously are the interesting nodes.
harm_angle: A lobbying firm representing rival governments at once is selling access, not advocacy.
caveat: Registrant and principal names need entity resolution; the four record shapes may not all carry both sides of the pair.

title: Short-Form Registrant Churn
idea: Track short-form registrations - the individual staff working a foreign account - and their termination dates, showing which firms cycle people rapidly.
harm_angle: Rapid staff churn on a foreign account keeps individual accountability from ever attaching to anyone.
caveat: Short-form fields may be null on most rows since the mart mixes record types.

title: Registration Waves After World Events
idea: Plot new registration counts per month per represented country and read the timeline against major geopolitical events.
harm_angle: A surge of paid US representation right after an invasion or a sanction shows who is buying reputation management during a crisis.
caveat: Event overlay is external context, not in the data; registration_date depends on a MM/DD/YYYY cast holding.

title: Where The Agents Sit
idea: Map registrant addresses by city and ZIP to show the physical concentration of the foreign-influence industry.
harm_angle: Concentration in a few blocks near the Capitol shows influence is a proximity business closed to everyone else.
caveat: Address fields may be sparse across record shapes; ZIP formatting unverified.

title: Contribution Sample Shape Check
idea: Profile the 500-row API slice by report type, filing form and entity type to document exactly what shape the API returns versus the bulk files.
harm_angle: Knowing the API sample is a sample stops anyone publishing a number that represents 500 rows as national truth.
caveat: This mart is explicitly a 500-row default-page sample and is not analytically usable for findings.

title: Occupation Text Vocabulary
idea: Chart the distinct occupation and employer strings in the sample against their frequency, previewing how messy the free-text donor fields are.
harm_angle: Employer text is the only link from a donor to the company that benefits; its messiness decides whether that link can ever be made.
caveat: 500-row sample - the vocabulary shape will not generalise to the 84M-row bulk file.

title: Corporate Parents Behind PACs
idea: Rank connected organisation names by how many committees they sponsor, exposing the corporate and union parents behind the PAC layer.
harm_angle: The PAC name on a filing is rarely the company writing the cheque; the connected org is who actually wants the vote.
caveat: connected_org_nm fill rate unverified and likely blank for many committee types.

title: Committee Type Mix By State
idea: Heatmap committee type and designation counts by state, showing where super PAC and party infrastructure is dense versus thin.
chart_shape: heatmap grid of state by type
harm_angle: States with thin committee infrastructure have races nobody is watching, where local harm goes unchallenged.
caveat: cmte_st reflects mailing address, not where the money is spent.

title: Filing Frequency As Transparency Dial
idea: Compare committees filing monthly versus quarterly versus terminated, by type and party, showing who reports often enough to be watchable in real time.
harm_angle: Quarterly filers can spend through an entire primary before anyone sees a number.
caveat: Filing frequency codes need decoding; some frequencies are legally mandated rather than chosen.

title: Uncontested District Map
idea: Map every House district by the number of registered candidates per cycle, colouring districts where only one major-party candidate ever registers.
harm_angle: A district with one candidate is a district where voters have already lost before election day.
caveat: District geometry is not in this source; party affiliation codes need grouping into major/minor.

title: Candidate Lives Far From District
idea: Compare each candidate's mailing state against the state of the office sought, flagging the carpetbagger cases.
harm_angle: Candidates who do not live where they would govern are less accountable to the people they represent.
caveat: Mailing address is often a campaign office or PO box, so mismatches include false positives.

title: Incumbency Persistence Grid
idea: Cohort grid of candidates by first cycle seen, tracking how many remain in later cycles and whether their incumbent status ever changes.
harm_angle: When challengers vanish after one cycle and incumbents never do, the system is self-sealing.
caveat: cand_ici codes need decoding; cand_id stability across cycles assumed.

title: Third Party Ballot Squeeze
idea: Chart minor-party candidate counts per state per cycle relative to major-party counts, showing where alternative candidacies have disappeared.
harm_angle: Where third parties cannot register, voters have exactly two options chosen by two organisations.
caveat: Party affiliation codes are numerous and inconsistently used; ballot-access law differences confound the picture.

title: New Committees Ahead Of The Cycle
idea: Compare the 2026 committee roster against the 2024 roster to isolate newly registered committees, ranked by type and connected organisation.
harm_angle: A wave of brand-new committees before an election is money arriving with no track record to check.
caveat: Requires the 2024 file alongside; the 2026 file is described as a snapshot with only ~57% linkage resolution.

title: Committee Name Recycling
idea: Find committee names reused under a different committee id across cycles and chart the reuse patterns.
chart_shape: network of name to id links
harm_angle: Recycled names let a discredited operation restart clean while looking like the same familiar group to donors.
caveat: Name normalisation is fuzzy; legitimate re-registrations produce false positives.

title: Linkage Resolution Coverage Gap
idea: Chart the percentage of linkages that resolve to a known committee and candidate by cycle, making the 2026 coverage hole visible.
harm_angle: An unresolvable link is a dollar that cannot be traced to a candidate - a hole in the accountability chain.
caveat: Resolution requires joining to the committee and candidate masters; the description already states 2026 resolves only ~57%.

title: Multi-Committee Candidates
idea: Rank candidates by count of authorised committees per cycle and chart the distribution, isolating the outliers running many vehicles at once.
harm_angle: Multiple vehicles per candidate fragment the money trail so no single filing shows the true total.
caveat: Committee designation types include joint fundraising and leadership PACs which legitimately multiply the count.

title: Election Year Mismatch Flags
idea: Flag linkages where the candidate election year and the FEC election year disagree, mapped by cycle - a data-quality tell that also catches carryover money.
harm_angle: Mismatched election years hide money raised for one race being spent on another.
caveat: Mismatch may be a routine FEC convention rather than a signal; needs a rule check.

source_names: FEC All Candidates Financial Summary weball
title: Money Raised Versus Vote Share
idea: Scatter total receipts against general-election percentage for every candidate-cycle, coloured by incumbency. The money-buys-outcome curve, and its exceptions.
harm_angle: If money reliably predicts the winner, the vote ratifies a fundraising race most people cannot enter.
caveat: gen_election_precent fill rate unverified and only exists for candidates who reached the general; dollar columns are untyped text in the mart.

source_names: FEC All Candidates Financial Summary weball
title: Self-Funded Candidates
idea: Chart candidate contributions and candidate loans as a share of total receipts, ranked, to isolate campaigns bankrolled by their own candidate.
harm_angle: When personal wealth is the entry ticket, the pool of people who can run shrinks to the already rich.
caveat: Dollar columns are untyped in the mart and must be cast; loan repayment nets are not accounted for.

source_names: FEC All Candidates Financial Summary weball
title: Small Donor Versus PAC Dependence
idea: Plot each candidate on a two-axis map of individual-contribution share versus other-committee-contribution share, showing who is funded by people and who by organisations.
harm_angle: A candidate funded overwhelmingly by committees owes their seat to organisations, not constituents.
caveat: Itemised versus unitemised individual money is not split here, so 'small donor' is an approximation.

source_names: FEC All Candidates Financial Summary weball
title: Debt-Carrying Campaigns
idea: Rank candidates by debts owed at cycle close against cash on hand, showing which campaigns ended in the red.
harm_angle: Campaign debt often means unpaid local vendors and staff who never get made whole.
caveat: The file has no creditor detail, so who is owed is invisible here.

source_names: FEC All Candidates Financial Summary weball
title: Refund Rate As Compliance Signal
idea: Chart individual and committee refunds as a share of receipts per candidate, highlighting campaigns that had to give back an unusual amount.
harm_angle: High refunds usually mean money was taken that should not have been - illegal, over-limit, or from a source the campaign had to disown.
caveat: Refunds also occur for routine over-limit corrections; needs a baseline to be meaningful.

title: Committees Per Candidate
idea: Rank candidates by how many committees are linked to them in a cycle. A long tail of many-committee candidates is a structural signal of money routing.
harm_angle: Money split across many committees is money that is harder for a voter to trace back to the candidate who benefits.
caveat: Positional columns only; c7 carries a uniqueness test suggesting a linkage id, the rest is guesswork.

title: Committee Reassignment Flow
idea: Sankey the committees that switch from one candidate to another across cycles. Reused committee shells carry history and donors with them.
harm_angle: A committee that changes candidates carries its donor list and its cash - a transfer of political power invisible on any ballot.
caveat: Requires column decoding and a stable committee id across cycles; the file may not preserve one.

title: Candidate Registry Column Autopsy
idea: Chart the fill rate and distinct-value count of every positional column c1 through c15 so the unnamed FEC candidate file becomes readable.
harm_angle: An unreadable candidate registry means nobody can audit who actually ran; the map is blind until the columns are named.
caveat: The mart exposes only positional columns c1..c15 with no names - every downstream idea for this source is speculative until the header is recovered.

title: Incumbent Versus Challenger Field Size
idea: Once the positional columns are mapped, plot registered candidates per office and state per cycle split by incumbent status. Districts with a single registered name are uncontested by default.
chart_shape: heatmap grid of state by cycle
harm_angle: Voters in permanently uncontested districts have no real choice on the ballot.
caveat: Depends entirely on decoding c1..c15; column meanings unverified.

title: Perennial Candidates
idea: Count how many distinct cycles each candidate id appears in and rank the persistent repeat-runners against one-and-done entrants.
harm_angle: Perennial candidates absorb ballot attention and campaign money without ever competing; mapping them separates real races from noise.
caveat: Column identities unknown; the unique test on c1+c4 hints c1 is candidate id and c4 an election year, but that is inference only.

title: PAC To Candidate Money Network
idea: Build a network of committees and the candidates they fund, weighted by dollars, and cluster it. The clusters are the real coalitions, not the parties.
harm_angle: The coalition map shows which industries own which blocs of legislators, regardless of party label.
caveat: 866k rows means aggregation is required; transaction_tp mixes contributions and independent expenditures which must be separated.

title: Money Follows The Vote
idea: Plot the timing of PAC contributions to a candidate against legislative calendar milestones, showing pre-vote and post-vote clustering.
harm_angle: Contributions clustering right before a vote are the clearest visible form of purchased access.
caveat: transaction_dt is untyped text in MMDDYYYY and needs parsing; the legislative calendar is external.

title: Hedging Both Sides
idea: Find committees that fund opposing candidates in the same race and chart the size of the hedge per committee.
harm_angle: A donor funding both sides is not buying an outcome, it is buying access whoever wins - which is worse.
caveat: Requires knowing which candidates share a race, which needs the candidate master joined in.

title: Memo Text Blind Spot
idea: Chart the share of transactions carrying a memo code or memo text by committee type, exposing where the machine-readable amount is not the whole story.
harm_angle: Memo-flagged rows are money that automated trackers double-count or miss entirely, corrupting every published total.
caveat: Memo semantics in FEC files are notoriously subtle; misreading them produces wrong totals.

idea: Chart the share of datasets flagged high-value across thematic categories, showing which legally-mandated areas Greece has actually published.
harm_angle: Missing high-value datasets are a legal transparency duty unmet, and the public cannot see the gap without this chart.
caveat: is_hvd fill rate unverified; 5,000-row sample.

title: Creation To Modification Drift
idea: Plot the gap between date created and metadata modified per organisation, isolating datasets published once and never touched again.
harm_angle: A dataset never updated since publication describes a world that no longer exists.
caveat: Both date fields are untyped text in staging; metadata dates are often auto-touched by portal migrations.

title: Format Openness By Category
idea: Chart resource formats per thematic category, separating open machine-readable formats from closed and document formats.
harm_angle: Categories published only as documents are categories where the numbers cannot be analysed by anyone.
caveat: resource_formats is a packed multi-value string; sample of 5,000.

source_names: Wayback CDX Census DOJ Epstein Library
title: When The Page Changed
idea: Plot every capture on a timeline, marking each point where the content digest changed from the prior capture. Each change is a third-party-attested edit to the government page.
harm_angle: Quiet edits and removals from a government document library are the public record being changed without notice.
caveat: 1.54M captures need heavy aggregation; digest changes can also come from unrelated page furniture like ad tokens or timestamps.

source_names: Wayback CDX Census DOJ Epstein Library
title: Error Status Windows
idea: Chart HTTP status codes over time per URL, showing the windows when the DOJ library returned errors or redirects instead of content.
chart_shape: heatmap grid of URL by day
harm_angle: Periods when a public document library returned errors are periods when the public was locked out of records it owns.
caveat: status_code is a string; Wayback capture density varies wildly so an absence of captures is not an absence of the page.

source_names: Wayback CDX Census DOJ Epstein Library
title: Page Size Shrinkage
idea: Plot content length per URL over time, so pages that suddenly got smaller - documents dropped from a listing - stand out as steps down.
harm_angle: A listing page that shrinks is a listing page from which documents were removed.
caveat: Byte length changes with compression and page furniture, so a step down is a lead not a proof.

source_names: Wayback CDX Census DOJ Epstein Library
title: Capture Attention Curve
idea: Plot capture frequency per day across the whole census, showing when public and archival attention spiked - a proxy for when people noticed something.
harm_angle: Attention spikes mark the moments the public was watching, and the quiet troughs mark the safest moments to change something.
caveat: Capture frequency reflects archiving bots and crawl schedules as much as human attention.

source_names: Wayback CDX Census DOJ Epstein Library
title: URL Birth And Death Grid
idea: Build a grid of every distinct URL against time, shaded by whether it was captured successfully, so URLs that appear and later vanish read as terminated rows.
chart_shape: cohort grid of URL by month
harm_angle: A URL that stops resolving is a document the government took away without announcing it.
caveat: Absence of captures does not prove absence of the page; needs status codes to distinguish gone from unarchived.

title: Race and Ethnicity Reporting Holes
idea: Grid of PPP dollars by reported race and ethnicity per state, with the unreported share shown as its own band. Viewer sees that the demographic question is mostly blank - which is itself the finding.
chart_shape: heatmap grid with an explicit unreported band
harm_angle: If who got relief was never recorded, no one can prove the money missed Black and Latino owners.
caveat: Race and ethnicity are famously mostly blank in PPP - the chart must foreground the blank rate not hide it.

title: Lenders and Where They Lent
idea: Heatmap of servicing_lender_name against borrower county, colored by rural_urban_indicator and lmi_indicator. Viewer sees lenders that served only affluent urban borrowers.
harm_angle: Relief routed through lenders means people without a banking relationship never got any.
caveat: Only loans of 150k and above are in this file - the small-borrower tail is entirely absent.

title: Dollars Per Job Reported
idea: Distribution of current_approval_amount divided by jobs_reported, faceted by naics_code. Viewer sees industries where the per-job subsidy was wildly higher than others.
harm_angle: Some sectors got many times more public money per worker protected than others did.
caveat: jobs_reported is self-reported and unverified; division blows up where jobs is zero or null.

title: Undisbursed and Unresolved
idea: Ranked view of loans with large undisbursed_amount or still-unresolved loan_status, by lender and state.
harm_angle: Money still sitting undisbursed years later is relief that never reached a single payroll.
caveat: Status snapshots are as-of the file release date and may be stale.

title: Proceeds Not Spent on Payroll
idea: Stacked shares of payroll, rent, utilities and mortgage interest proceeds by industry and loan size band. Viewer sees where a payroll program funded landlords instead.
harm_angle: A program sold as saving jobs that largely paid rent is a different program than the one Congress described.
caveat: Proceeds fields are borrower-declared allocations, not audited spending.

title: Every police shooting on one map
idea: Point map of fatal police shootings colored by whether a body camera was present, with density visible in urban cores.
harm_angle: Shows exactly where police kill people and whether anyone was recording.
caveat: Coordinates are often block-level; covers shootings only and excludes other in-custody deaths.

title: Age distribution of the killed by race
idea: Overlaid distributions of victim age split by race, showing whether some groups are killed markedly younger.
harm_angle: Being killed younger means more years of life lost, concentrated in specific communities.
caveat: Race is partly imputed - the race_source field records how it was determined and should be shown alongside.

title: Unarmed and fleeing: the hardest cases
idea: Heatmap grid of armed-with against flee status with cell color as count, isolating the unarmed-and-fleeing corner that drives most controversy.
harm_angle: Unarmed people shot while running away are the clearest case of avoidable death.
caveat: Armed-with and threat-type are as-reported by the department and may be self-serving.

title: Body-camera presence trend since 2015
idea: Timeline of the share of fatal shootings with a body camera recorded, nationally and per state. A stall well below full coverage means the accountability promise never landed.
harm_angle: Without footage, the only account of a killing is the officer's.
caveat: The field records camera presence not whether footage was released or even retained.

title: Mental-health crisis calls that end in death
idea: Small multiples by state of the share of fatal shootings flagged mental-illness-related over time, showing where crisis response has been left to armed police.
harm_angle: People in psychiatric crisis are dying because the responder sent was armed.
caveat: The flag depends on after-the-fact reporting and is likely undercounted.

title: What Gets Amended and When
idea: Timeline of amendment records by form type and change category — adding lobbyists, deleting employers, other — showing when filers quietly rewrite the record.
harm_angle: Amendments after the fact are how a lobbying relationship gets written out of the version the public already read.
caveat: Checkbox fields are likely X-or-blank strings; the separate effective-date fields may be the real timing, not exec_date.

title: Filings Amended Over and Over
idea: Ranked bars of filings by their highest amendment number, exposing filings revised ten or more times.
harm_angle: A filing amended repeatedly means the public never saw a stable, true version of who was lobbying whom.
caveat: amend_id may be text; heavy amendment could be routine for certain form types and needs that control.

title: Lobbyists Added Versus Deleted
idea: Slope chart of added versus deleted lobbyist names per reporting period, revealing churn in who is registered to lobby.
harm_angle: High churn masks who was actually in the room at the moment a bill moved.
caveat: Name fields split across last, first, title and suffix and may be blank for most rows.

title: What Attribute Gets Changed Most
idea: Ranked bars of the changed-attribute field by frequency, split by filer type. Shows which parts of a lobbying registration are most often quietly rewritten.
harm_angle: Silent edits to who a lobbyist represents change the accountability record after the fact.
caveat: Attribute names may be terse internal codes needing a lookup that is not in the model.

title: Registration Churn Timeline
idea: Timeline of change-log entries per legislative session with correction-flagged entries called out. Spikes near session deadlines are the tell.
harm_angle: Deadline-clustered corrections suggest filings written to beat a clock, not to inform the public.
caveat: log_dt may be text; session_id boundaries need a legislative calendar to interpret.

title: Where California Lobbying Lives
idea: Map of filer city and ZIP by count of registered filers, showing the concentration of lobbying operations around the capitol.
harm_angle: Physical proximity to power is itself a form of access ordinary constituents do not have.
caveat: City strings unnormalized; ZIP may be nine-digit or blank.

title: Responsible Officers Across Entities
idea: Network graph of responsible-officer names linked to the entities they sign for, exposing individuals who front many separate lobbying registrations.
harm_angle: One person signing for a dozen entities is a single point of influence dressed up as a dozen.
caveat: Officer names are free text; the same person will appear with punctuation and spelling variants.

title: Who Lobbyists Give To
idea: Ranked bars of recipients by total contributions received from registered lobbyists over the whole period.
harm_angle: A lobbyist writing checks to the official they are lobbying is the plainest conflict there is.
caveat: Only 6505 rows; this may be a lightly-used disclosure form rather than the full money picture.

title: Contributions Clustered Near Deadlines
idea: Timeline of contribution dates against the filing period boundaries, testing whether giving spikes at particular moments in the legislative calendar.
harm_angle: Timing tells you whether the money is routine support or the purchase of a specific moment.
caveat: Small row count means apparent seasonality could be noise; date fields may be text.

title: Giver to Recipient Money Flow
idea: Sankey from filer to recipient weighted by amount, showing the concentrated channels between lobbyists and officeholders.
harm_angle: Concentrated flows name the specific relationships worth a reporter's time.
caveat: 6.5k rows keeps this readable but also means it is a thin slice of California influence money.

title: Lobbying Filings Over Two Decades
idea: Timeline of cover-page filings by form type, showing the volume and mix of the four-form disclosure family across years.
harm_angle: Filing volume is the visible surface of an influence industry most Californians never see.
caveat: 525k rows across four form types with different meanings; mixing them without labels misleads.

title: The Biggest Lobbying Firms by Volume
idea: Ranked bars of firms by count of filings and by distinct filers represented over the full period.
harm_angle: The handful of firms that file most are the firms that shape most of what passes.
caveat: Firm names are free text and firm_id may be blank on older filings.

title: What They Say They Lobbied On
idea: Cluster the lobbying-activity free text into subject themes and plot theme by year as a heatmap grid, showing which issues drew the industry when.
harm_angle: Following the issue heat shows which laws had industry standing over them while ordinary people did not.
caveat: lobbying_activity is unstructured text of wildly varying length and may be blank on most rows; theming is subjective.

title: Where Lobbying Firms Are Based
idea: Map of firm city and state by filing count, testing how much California lobbying is done by out-of-state operations.
harm_angle: Out-of-state money shaping California law is influence with no local accountability.
caveat: City and state fields on cover pages are often blank on older forms.

title: Filing Lateness Distribution
idea: Distribution of days from the period end date to the report date per form type, revealing systematically late disclosure by form and by filer.
harm_angle: Late disclosure means the public learns who lobbied after the vote is already over.
caveat: Date columns may be text; statutory deadlines differ by form type and are not in the data.

title: Named Individuals Behind Each Filing
idea: Ranked bars of individuals by how many distinct filings name them, showing the people who appear on the most lobbying paperwork.
harm_angle: The same few names appearing on hundreds of filings is a concentration of access.
caveat: Name split across four fields plus a title; the same person will appear multiple ways.

title: Titles of the People Filed
idea: Ranked bars of entity titles such as officer, partner, or employee by frequency, showing the seniority profile of who signs California lobbying disclosures.
harm_angle: Whether a chief executive or a junior clerk signs tells you how seriously the disclosure is treated.
caveat: Title is free text with enormous variety and needs grouping.

title: Line Item Depth Per Filing
idea: Distribution of line items per filing by form type, showing which filings list dozens of associated parties versus a bare one.
harm_angle: A filing listing fifty parties describes an operation far bigger than one listing one.
caveat: line_item semantics are undocumented; it may be a sequence number rather than a count.

title: Who Lobbies for Whom
idea: Network graph of individual lobbyists linked to their employers, with lobbyists serving multiple employers highlighted.
harm_angle: A lobbyist working for three competing employers at once carries information and access between them.
caveat: Only 1500 rows; may cover a narrow window of sessions rather than the full history.

title: Lobbyist Roster Size by Employer
idea: Ranked bars of employers by number of individual lobbyists on their roster per session.
harm_angle: Roster size is the plainest measure of who can put the most bodies in a hallway.
caveat: Small table; rosters may be undercounted if in-house lobbyists register through a different form.

title: Lobbyists Who Switch Employers
idea: Slope chart across sessions of individual lobbyists changing employer, showing revolving-door movement inside the lobbying industry.
harm_angle: Movement between employers carries relationships built at public expense into private hands.
caveat: Requires lobbyist_id to be stable across sessions, which is unverified and a classic id trap.

title: Who Spends the Most on Lobbying
idea: Ranked bars of employers by session total spend, showing California's biggest buyers of influence.
harm_angle: The organizations spending most on access are shaping laws that touch people who cannot buy a lobbyist.
caveat: Only 1730 employer rows; amounts may be stored as text needing a numeric cast.

title: Spending by Interest Category
idea: Timeline of quarterly amounts aggregated by interest category, showing which industries ramp spending in which quarters.
harm_angle: Quarterly ramps line up with specific bills and reveal what an industry was fighting.
caveat: Eight quarter columns are wide-format and must be unpivoted; the column-to-calendar mapping is not documented in the model.

title: Spending Spikes Against Baseline
idea: Small multiples per employer of the eight quarterly amounts, so a viewer can spot the employer whose spend jumps five-fold in one quarter.
harm_angle: A sudden spike is a fight over a specific bill, and the bill is where the harm lives.
caveat: Wide-format quarters with unclear calendar alignment; nulls may be zeros or may be missing data.

title: Employers Who Hire Many Firms
idea: Ranked bars of employers by number of distinct lobbying firms retained in a session, showing who blankets the capitol.
harm_angle: Hiring six firms at once buys access through six separate relationships that all point one way.
caveat: Only 524 rows; may be a thin slice of actual retainer relationships.

title: Relationships That Terminated
idea: Timeline of termination dates for employer-firm retainers, testing whether terminations cluster right after particular legislative moments.
harm_angle: A retainer ending right after a bill passes tells you the relationship was about that bill.
caveat: termination_dt is likely blank for most active relationships, leaving a small n.

title: The Employer Firm Bipartite Web
idea: Bipartite network of employers on one side and firms on the other, with firms serving competing employers highlighted.
harm_angle: A firm representing both sides of an issue is a conflict the public never sees disclosed.
caveat: 524 edges is readable, but labeling interests as competing requires outside judgment not present in the data.

title: Every Firm Ranked by Take
idea: Ranked bars of all lobbying firms by session total, a complete leaderboard of a very small industry.
harm_angle: With only 256 firms, a tiny industry mediates access to a state of thirty-nine million people.
caveat: 256 rows suggests one session snapshot rather than full history; amounts may be text.

title: Firm Revenue Across Quarters
idea: Small multiples of the eight quarterly amounts per firm, showing which firms grow steadily and which live off single windfall quarters.
harm_angle: Windfall quarters mark the moments a firm was paid to kill or pass something specific.
caveat: Wide-format quarter columns with undocumented calendar mapping.

title: Market Concentration of Influence
idea: Cumulative distribution of firms against share of total lobbying dollars, showing what fraction of firms capture most of the money.
harm_angle: If ten of 256 firms take most of the money, influence in California has ten gatekeepers.
caveat: Depends on session_total_amt being populated and comparable across all firms.

title: Billing Per Reporting Period
idea: Timeline of per-period and cumulative billings by firm across reporting periods, showing the money curve of each firm-client relationship.
harm_angle: The billing curve of a specific firm-client pair is the price tag on a specific legislative outcome.
caveat: Only 170 rows — extremely thin. This may be a sampled or partially-loaded table; verify completeness before drawing any conclusion.

title: What the Activity Description Says
idea: Dot plot pairing the lobbying activity text with the billing amount, so the most expensive engagements sit next to what the firm claimed it was doing.
harm_angle: Vague activity text on a six-figure engagement is disclosure that discloses nothing.
caveat: 170 rows and free-text activity fields; too thin to generalize, treat as illustrative only.

title: Firm Headcount Over Sessions
idea: Ranked bars of firms by number of individual lobbyists attached per session, tracking which firms staff up before big sessions.
harm_angle: Staffing up ahead of a session is a firm telling you where the fight will be.
caveat: 577 rows; sessions may not be covered evenly.

title: Lobbyists at More Than One Firm
idea: Network graph of lobbyists to firms, highlighting individuals attached to multiple firms simultaneously or in sequence.
harm_angle: An individual bridging two firms is an undisclosed channel between two sets of clients.
caveat: lobbyist_id stability across sessions unverified; names may be the only reliable link.

title: Candidates With the Most Committees
idea: Ranked bars of candidates by number of distinct linked committees, showing which politicians run the widest web of money vehicles.
harm_angle: A candidate with many committees can move money in ways a single-committee candidate cannot, and voters see none of it.
caveat: Only ids here, no candidate names; the chart is unreadable without joining a candidate name source.

title: Committee Type Mix by Election Year
idea: Timeline of linkage counts by committee type and designation across election years, showing which money vehicle types proliferated when.
harm_angle: Shifts in vehicle type track how money routes around each new rule.
caveat: Election year fields may be text; two year columns exist and their difference is undocumented.

title: The Candidate Committee Web
idea: Network graph of candidates linked to committees, where committees shared between two candidates are the interesting edges.
harm_angle: Shared committees are informal alliances that never appear on a ballot.
caveat: Whether one committee genuinely links to multiple candidates is unverified; the graph may be a clean forest with no shared nodes.

title: Who Declares A Promoter
idea: Ranked bars by region of advertisers that declared a promoter name and address versus those that left it blank.
harm_angle: Voters shown a political ad by an entity with no declared promoter cannot know who is talking to them.
caveat: Only 469 rows; declaration requirements differ by region so blanks may be lawful.

title: Declared Scope Versus Region
idea: Heatmap grid of declared scope against region showing where advertisers claim narrow local scope while running elsewhere.
harm_angle: Scope mismatches are how ad spend crosses jurisdictions that never approved it.
caveat: Tiny table; scope values may be a short controlled list.

title: Regulatory Id Coverage
idea: Distribution of records with and without a declared regulatory identifier by region.
harm_angle: A missing regulatory id is a political advertiser that cannot be traced to a registered entity.
caveat: 469 rows total; may be too thin to generalize.

title: Where Each Advertiser Bought Votes
idea: Choropleth of political ad spend by country subdivision for a selected advertiser with a small-multiple grid across the top advertisers.
harm_angle: Concentrated ad spend on a handful of subdivisions shows exactly whose opinion was being bought.
caveat: Table sits at exactly 500,000 rows suggesting a load cap; multi-currency spend needs normalizing.

title: Outside Money By Subdivision
idea: Ranked bars of subdivisions by total spend divided by number of distinct advertisers finding places saturated by few voices.
harm_angle: A district blanketed by one advertiser hears one argument and calls it the debate.
caveat: Likely row cap at 500k; subdivision naming is inconsistent across countries.

title: Spend Concentration Curve
idea: Distribution curve of cumulative spend share against advertiser rank per country showing how few advertisers dominate.
harm_angle: Political speech dominated by a handful of buyers is not a marketplace of ideas.
caveat: Requires converting many currency columns to one; truncation cap applies.

title: Advertisers That Changed Identity
idea: Chain or network view following old advertiser ids to new ones revealing entities that renamed or re-registered.
harm_angle: An advertiser that changes id sheds its spending history and the public loses the paper trail.
caveat: Ids only with no names; the chart is meaningless without joining to the advertiser stats table.

title: Id Churn Volume
idea: Ranked count of how many remapping events exist and whether any old id maps to multiple new ids.
harm_angle: The scale of identity churn tells you how leaky the political ad archive really is.
caveat: Two-column lookup table with no dates; genuinely thin on its own.

title: The Biggest Political Buyers
idea: Ranked bars of advertisers by total dollar spend annotated with total creatives and number of regions covered.
harm_angle: Names the entities buying the most political persuasion worldwide.
caveat: Multi-currency spend means a dollar-only ranking undercounts non-US buyers.

title: Spend Per Creative
idea: Scatter of total spend against total creatives where the outliers are advertisers either mass-producing cheap variants or buying a few very expensive placements.
harm_angle: Thousands of near-identical creatives is the signature of micro-targeted persuasion.
caveat: Creative counts may include withdrawn ads.

title: Advertisers Spanning Many Elections
idea: Ranked bars of advertisers by number of distinct elections touched showing cross-election operators.
harm_angle: An entity working many elections at once is running an operation, not a campaign.
caveat: The elections field is a packed list in one column and needs parsing.

title: Public Ids Behind The Names
idea: Distribution of advertisers by whether they carry any public identifier split by region.
harm_angle: An advertiser with no public id is a name with nothing behind it.
caveat: The public ids column is a packed list and may be mostly empty.

title: The Final Week Spending Surge
idea: Timeline of weekly spend aggregated across advertisers per election cycle showing the blowout in the last weeks before a vote.
harm_angle: Late money arrives when there is no time left to fact-check it.
caveat: Election cycle labels may not map cleanly to actual voting dates.

title: Advertiser Spending Fingerprints
idea: Small multiples of weekly spend curves for the top advertisers revealing steady spenders versus burst spenders.
harm_angle: Burst spending patterns identify operations timed to swamp a news cycle.
caveat: Weekly grain may have gaps that must be zero-filled to read correctly.

title: New Advertisers Appearing Late
idea: Scatter of each advertiser's first observed week against their total cycle spend flagging big spenders that appeared only weeks before the vote.
harm_angle: Pop-up advertisers with large budgets and no history are the classic dark-money shape.
caveat: First-observed week is an artifact of the archive, not necessarily entity formation.

title: Cross Currency Spending Footprint
idea: Heatmap grid of advertiser against currency showing advertisers buying in currencies far from their apparent home.
harm_angle: Buying political ads in a foreign currency is a signal worth chasing on foreign influence.
caveat: Currency of purchase does not prove nationality of the buyer.

title: Creative Identity Churn
idea: Chain view of old to new creative ids showing how much of the ad archive has been re-keyed.
harm_angle: Re-keyed creatives break links from journalism and research back to the original ad.
caveat: Two-column lookup at the 500k row cap with no dates; thin on its own, needs the creative stats table.

title: Remap Fan Out Check
idea: Distribution of how many new ids each old id maps to and vice versa exposing merges and splits in the archive.
harm_angle: Merges and splits in the archive change what the public record says was ever published.
caveat: Genuinely thin: two id columns only and likely mostly one-to-one.

title: Micro Targeting By Age And Gender
idea: Heatmap grid of age targeting against gender targeting weighted by impressions showing which demographics are singled out.
harm_angle: Ads aimed at one narrow demographic mean that group hears claims nobody else can rebut.
caveat: Targeting fields are packed strings; the 500k row count suggests a load cap.

title: Geo Exclusion Is The Tell
idea: Ranked bars of the most frequently excluded geographies in ad targeting next to the most included showing who advertisers deliberately hide from.
harm_angle: Deliberately excluding a region from an ad is a decision about who is allowed to hear the message.
caveat: Geo fields are packed lists needing parsing; possible row cap.

title: Cost Per Thousand Impressions Spread
idea: Scatter of impressions against spend by ad type and region exposing ads that cost far more per view than their peers.
harm_angle: Wildly high cost per view can indicate premium placement aimed at a tiny decisive audience.
caveat: Impressions are often bucketed ranges rather than exact counts.

title: The Life Of An Ad
idea: Timeline of ads by first served and last served timestamps sorted by advertiser showing burst campaigns versus long runners.
harm_angle: Ads that ran for a day and vanished are the ones nobody had time to challenge.
caveat: Timestamp fields may be text; possible 500k row cap.

title: Platform Ad Grants In Political Space
idea: Small multiples by region of ads flagged as funded by platform ad grants with spend and impressions.
harm_angle: Free platform credit flowing into political messaging is the platform putting a thumb on the scale.
caveat: Flag may be almost entirely false; an unnamed trailing column in the model suggests a parsing issue.

title: Global Political Ad Spend Map
idea: World and subdivision map of total political ad spend drilling from country to secondary subdivision.
harm_angle: Shows which democracies are being advertised at hardest.
caveat: Only 1,289 rows so subdivision coverage is coarse; multi-currency columns need normalizing.

title: Spend Per Capita By Country
idea: Ranked bars of spend per capita by country using an external population figure revealing saturation rather than raw size.
harm_angle: Small countries saturated with political ads are the most vulnerable to influence operations.
caveat: Requires an external population source not present in this table.

title: Lobbying spend by issue area
idea: Ranked bars of reported income and expenses grouped by lobbying issue, showing which policy areas attract the most paid persuasion.
harm_angle: The issues with the most money aimed at them are the issues where the public interest is most outgunned.
caveat: LOBBYING_ISSUES is likely a delimited multi-value field needing explosion; income and expenses are mutually exclusive by filer type.

title: Which agencies get lobbied
idea: Ranked bars of government entities named in filings, showing which agencies and committees are the most-worked doors.
harm_angle: An agency saturated with lobbying contact is one whose rulemaking the affected public cannot match.
caveat: GOVERNMENT_ENTITIES is a delimited list; naming inconsistency across years is likely.

title: Revolving door of lobbyist names
idea: Network of lobbyists to the registrant firms they worked for over time, surfacing individuals who move between firms while keeping the same clients.
harm_angle: The same handful of people carry influence across firms and administrations regardless of who won the election.
caveat: LOBBYIST_NAMES is a delimited free-text list with no person id; name disambiguation is the whole difficulty.

title: Foreign-backed lobbying over time
idea: Timeline of filings flagged as having a foreign entity listed, split by issue area, showing where overseas interests concentrate their spend.
harm_angle: Foreign money shaping domestic rules is influence the affected public has no vote over.
caveat: FOREIGN_ENTITY_LISTED semantics unverified; may be Y/N or a free-text name.

title: Clients who stop and restart
idea: Slope chart of client lobbying spend before and after a termination date, catching clients who formally terminate and quietly re-register.
harm_angle: Termination-and-restart is how sustained influence gets to look like occasional engagement in the public record.
caveat: TERMINATION_DATE is try_to_date over untyped text and may fail widely; needs client_id stable across cycles.

title: Small donors versus maximum givers
idea: Distribution of contribution amounts across all 12.6M lines, with the spike at the legal annual maximum called out against the long low-value tail.
harm_angle: The pile-up at the legal cap shows who can afford to give the maximum every single year and who gives once and stops.
caveat: Amounts parsed with try_to_number over text; installment lines legitimately repeat and would inflate per-donor totals if summed naively.

title: Donor money by postal code
idea: Map of contribution totals by contributor postal code, showing the specific neighbourhoods that fund federal politics.
harm_angle: A country's political money coming from a few wealthy postal codes means everyone else's priorities arrive unfunded.
caveat: Postal code formatting and blanking rules for small donors unverified; privacy thresholds may remove low-value givers entirely.

title: Election-cycle giving pulse
idea: Timeline of daily contribution totals across the full record with electoral events overlaid, showing how giving detonates around campaigns and flatlines between.
harm_angle: Between-election silence is when policy actually gets made, and it is the period nobody is funding scrutiny of.
caveat: Date parsing over untyped text may drop older rows; electoral_event population unverified.

title: Donors who give to every side
idea: Network of contributor names linked to the parties they funded, isolating the givers who bankroll multiple parties at once.
harm_angle: Donors hedging across every party are buying access regardless of who wins, which no voter got to weigh in on.
caveat: No contributor id exists; matching on name alone will merge distinct people with common names and split the same person across spellings.

title: Non-monetary gifts nobody counts
idea: Ranked bars of recipients by non-monetary contribution value against cash value, exposing entities funded largely in goods and services rather than money.
harm_angle: In-kind support is real influence that never shows up in the headline fundraising numbers voters see.
caveat: NON_MONETARY_AMOUNT may be mostly zero or null; valuation methods for in-kind gifts vary by filer.

title: Who funded the 2001 city races
idea: Ranked bars of candidates by total contributions received, split by office, the plain money picture of that cycle.
harm_angle: Establishes who was bankrolled before any argument about what they later did in office.
caveat: Dates parsed permissively from text; 248 near-duplicate key collisions were resolved by hash tiebreaker and may be genuine double entries.

title: Bundlers behind the checks
idea: Network of intermediaries to the candidates they delivered money to, sized by bundled total, exposing the fixers rather than the named donors.
harm_angle: Bundlers convert many small legal donations into one large relationship that no contribution limit constrains.

title: Statement Of Reasons Depth

harm_angle: A designation with no stated reason cannot be challenged by the person it destroys.

title: Corporate Structures Under Sanction

title: Designated Ships By Flag And Type

title: Alias Strength As Match Confidence

title: UN Listing And Review Lag

harm_angle: A designation never reviewed in twenty years is a person or entity with no realistic route off the list.

title: Committee Composition Of The List
idea: Break designations down by UN list type and record type over time, showing which Security Council committees actually generate listings.
harm_angle: Committees that list nobody for years show which conflicts the Security Council chose not to touch.

title: Interpol Notice Linkage Coverage

harm_angle: A UN designation with no Interpol notice is a name on a list that no police force will ever act on.

title: Designation Roles Named
idea: Rank the recorded designation and title text - minister, commander, financier - to show which roles the UN actually sanctions.
harm_angle: If the list names commanders but never the financiers, the money that funds the violence is untouched.

title: Taxonomy Commentary Over Time
idea: Timeline of species-registry comment volume by year and commentator showing when the taxonomic record was actively curated.
harm_angle: Reference infrastructure quality determines whether species-level environmental harms can be tracked at all.

title: Who Curates The Species Record
idea: Ranked bars of commentators by number of comments showing how few people maintain the national taxonomy.
harm_angle: A national reference maintained by a handful of unpaid experts is fragile public infrastructure.

title: Curation Staleness Check
idea: Distribution of time since last update per comment revealing how much of the record has gone untouched for decades.
harm_angle: Stale reference data quietly corrupts every downstream environmental and health analysis that uses it.

title: The Shrinking Expert Bench
idea: Timeline of expert record update dates showing whether the roster of taxonomic experts is being maintained or abandoned.
harm_angle: When the expert bench empties the country loses the ability to identify the species it regulates.

idea: Ranked listing of experts by prefix category and comment content as a reference inventory.

harm_angle: When funders merge or vanish from the registry, the money trail behind published research becomes harder to follow.

harm_angle: Duplicate funder identities let the same money appear as two independent sources of support.

title: Preregistration state snapshot
idea: Ranked bars of the registration-state flags across the sample, showing how many registrations are public, embargoed, withdrawn or pending approval.
harm_angle: Embargoed and withdrawn preregistrations are the studies whose plans the public cannot check against the published result.

title: Embargo end dates ahead
idea: Timeline of embargo end dates against registration dates, showing how long study plans stay hidden after being filed.
harm_angle: A long embargo means the pre-stated hypothesis stays secret through exactly the period when the results get published.
caveat: SAMPLE ONLY: 10 rows, so this is a template rather than a chart. Genuinely thin until the full registry is landed.

title: Why papers get retracted
idea: Ranked bars of retraction reasons across 71k records, separating honest error from fabrication, plagiarism and paper-mill activity.
harm_angle: Retractions for fabrication mean patients and policymakers acted on findings that were never real.
caveat: REASON is a delimited multi-value field needing explosion; reason vocabulary has changed over the database's life.

title: Time from publication to retraction
idea: Distribution of the gap between original publication date and retraction date, split by reason, showing how many years bad science stays in the literature.
harm_angle: Every year between publication and retraction is a year of clinicians and policymakers citing something false.
caveat: Both dates were parsed out of M/D/YYYY H:MM text; failures become null and would bias the distribution toward well-formatted recent records.

title: Journals and publishers ranked
idea: Ranked bars of journals and their publishers by retraction count, with volume-adjusted framing shown alongside the raw count.
harm_angle: Publishers with high retraction loads are the gatekeepers whose quality control failed the readers who trusted them.
caveat: Raw counts favour large journals; without a denominator of total papers published this chart can defame a big honest journal.

title: Retraction geography by institution
idea: Map of retraction counts by country with the top institutions named, showing where research-integrity failures cluster.
harm_angle: Systemic pressure to publish falls hardest on early-career researchers in the countries at the top of this map.
caveat: COUNTRY and INSTITUTION are delimited multi-value fields; multi-country papers need fractional or duplicated attribution.

title: Repeat-retraction authors
idea: Ranked bars of authors appearing in the most retraction records, the small group whose work has been pulled again and again.
harm_angle: A researcher with dozens of retractions has usually built a career, and trained students, on work that was never sound.
caveat: AUTHOR is a delimited free-text list with no author id; common names will merge distinct people, which is a defamation risk demanding manual verification.

title: Global research organisation map
idea: Point map of all 135k research organisations by geocoded location, coloured by organisation type, showing where research capacity physically sits.
harm_angle: Whole regions with almost no registered research organisations are regions whose problems nobody is funded to study.
caveat: Lat/long come from GeoNames and may be city centroids rather than campus points.

title: Research capacity per country
idea: Ranked bars of organisations per country by type, with the empty tail of countries left visible rather than truncated.
harm_angle: The countries at the bottom of this list depend entirely on outsiders to define what gets researched about them.
caveat: Registry coverage itself is uneven; low counts may reflect registration behaviour rather than actual capacity.

title: Founding waves of institutions
idea: Timeline of organisations by year established, coloured by continent, showing the historical waves of institution-building.
harm_angle: Which regions built research institutions in which century is the long shadow behind today's knowledge inequality.
caveat: ESTABLISHED is parsed from text and is likely null for a large share of entries, biasing toward well-documented Western institutions.

title: Identifier coverage across the registry
idea: Heatmap grid of country against the share of organisations carrying each external identifier, showing where the crosswalk fabric is thin.
harm_angle: Organisations missing crosswalk identifiers are invisible to every automated accountability system built on those identifiers.
caveat: Identifier columns may hold blank strings rather than nulls; distinct-count and value sampling required before reading fill rates.

idea: Map NIH award dollars per capita by state and congressional district over FY2000-FY2026. Viewer sees a permanent funding archipelago - a handful of states absorb most biomedical research money while whole regions stay dark decade after decade.

caveat: Per-capita needs an external population denominator; cong_dist formatting may be inconsistent across years.

title: The Same Hundred Institutions

title: Institutions With Repeat Retractions
idea: Ranked dot plot of institutions by raw retraction count, shaded by country.
harm_angle: Institutions that keep producing retracted work are failing the patients and students downstream.

harm_angle: Kingdoms with thin trees (fungi, microbes) are the ones missing from environmental impact reviews.
caveat: Requires parsing the hierarchy string to identify the top-level branch; string format unverified.

title: Orphans And Dead Ends
idea: Network view of a sample of the tree highlighting taxa whose parent is missing or whose branch terminates immediately, mapping the broken joints of the official catalogue.
harm_angle: A broken reference spine means downstream regulatory lists silently drop organisms.
