title: Native Versus Introduced By Jurisdiction
idea: Stacked ranked bars of each jurisdiction (Continental US, Alaska, Hawaii, Canada, territories) split by whether recorded taxa are native or introduced.
harm_angle: Places dominated by introduced species are places where an ecosystem people depend on has already been replaced.
caveat: Jurisdiction list is coarse and territory coverage may be very thin; origin values may include unclassified codes.

title: Island Invasion Ratio
idea: Dot plot ranking jurisdictions by the share of their recorded taxa marked introduced, with island jurisdictions expected to sit far out on the tail.
harm_angle: Island communities lose food, fisheries, and cultural species first when invasives take over.
caveat: Ratio is sensitive to how completely natives were catalogued in each jurisdiction; unequal effort could fake the signal.

title: Introduced Species Arrival Timeline
idea: Timeline of introduced-origin records by their update year and jurisdiction, approximating when each place started logging new arrivals.
harm_angle: Shows whether the official record keeps pace with invasions that wreck local agriculture and water.
caveat: update_date is a record-maintenance date, not an arrival date; the mapping is an approximation and may be worthless if bulk-stamped.

title: Jurisdictions Nobody Surveyed
idea: Ranked bars of taxa-per-jurisdiction against a rough land or water area reference, exposing US territories with near-zero catalogued biodiversity.
harm_angle: US territories with no species records get no environmental review protection, and the people there bear the cost.
caveat: Area reference is not in this source and would have to come from elsewhere; without it this is only a raw count.

title: Seven Kingdoms Reference Card
idea: A simple labelled bar or table-chart of the seven kingdoms, used as the legend and color key for every other taxonomy chart.
harm_angle: Not a harm chart on its own; it is the scaffolding that makes the biodiversity gap charts readable.
caveat: Only 7 rows; genuinely thin, this is a legend not a finding.

title: Kingdom Update Recency
idea: Slope or dot chart of the last update date for each of the seven kingdom definitions, showing how long the top-level scheme has sat frozen.
harm_angle: A frozen classification scheme means newer science about microbes and fungi never reaches regulators using this reference.
caveat: Seven rows and a maintenance date; almost certainly a curiosity rather than a story.

title: Name Length Distribution
idea: Distribution of assembled scientific-name length and word count across a million taxa, showing the long tail of deeply-qualified subspecies names.
harm_angle: Very long qualified names mark contested or repeatedly-revised organisms, which are the ones that fall through legal listing cracks.
caveat: Two-column lookup only; this is a shape-of-the-data chart, weak on its own without joining the core taxa table.

title: Genus Crowding
idea: Ranked bars of the most crowded genera by count of complete names sharing the same first word, showing where naming has exploded.
harm_angle: Crowded genera are where misidentification happens, which matters when a protected species is mistaken for an unprotected sibling.
caveat: Requires splitting the first token of the name string; hybrid and uncertain names may pollute the split.

title: Legacy Ocean Codes Crosswalk Health
idea: Distribution of how many legacy NOAA ocean codes point at each modern taxon id, exposing many-to-one collapses in the crosswalk.
harm_angle: A messy crosswalk means historical fisheries and ocean-survey data cannot be reliably compared to today's, hiding long-run decline.
caveat: Grain is one row per code-taxon pair; cannot confirm from metadata whether reverse one-to-many also occurs.

title: Orphaned Legacy Codes
idea: Ranked bars of legacy ocean code blocks by how many of their codes have no modern taxon match, mapping where old ocean data becomes untranslatable.
harm_angle: Untranslatable historical ocean data is lost evidence about fisheries collapse that coastal communities lived through.
caveat: Unmatched codes may simply not be loaded into this table at all, which would make the gap invisible rather than measurable.

title: Who The Catalogue Trusts
idea: Ranked bars of non-publication evidence sources by type and name, showing which databases and websites the national taxonomy leans on.
harm_angle: If the public record of species depends on a handful of private or defunct websites, the evidence base can vanish overnight.
caveat: Only 1,071 rows; source_type value vocabulary unverified.

title: Evidence Rot Timeline
idea: Timeline of acquisition dates for cited non-publication sources, showing the age profile of the evidence the catalogue still relies on.
harm_angle: Decades-old website citations mean the underlying proof for a species record may no longer exist to check.
caveat: acquisition_date may be sparsely populated or text; small table.

title: Version Drift Of Cited Databases
idea: Dot plot of cited databases by their recorded version against acquisition date, exposing sources frozen at an ancient version.
harm_angle: Frozen source versions mean corrections made upstream never propagate into the official US record.
caveat: version is a free-text field and may be unparseable; tiny table.

title: Two Centuries Of Taxonomic Evidence
idea: Timeline of cited publications by actual publication date, showing how much of the modern species catalogue rests on nineteenth-century papers.
harm_angle: Species protection decisions resting on 1880s descriptions are decisions made on evidence nobody alive has verified.
caveat: Date fields are stored as listed and actual publication dates and may be text or partially missing.

title: The Publishers Behind The Species List
idea: Ranked bars of publishers and publication venues by number of cited works, showing concentration in a few journals and societies.
harm_angle: Concentration means a narrow set of institutions effectively decides what counts as a species in US law.
caveat: publisher strings are free text and will need heavy normalization; duplicates will inflate the tail.

title: Listed Versus Actual Publication Date Gap
idea: Distribution of the gap between the date a paper claims and the date it actually appeared, a known trap in naming priority disputes.
harm_angle: Backdated publications decide which name wins, and the losing name can be the one a protection statute cites.
caveat: Both date fields may be text with mixed formats; gap may be zero for most rows.

title: Missing Identifiers In The Bibliography
idea: Ranked bars by decade of the share of cited publications with no ISBN or ISSN, showing how much of the evidence base is untraceable.
harm_angle: Untraceable citations mean the public cannot audit why a species is or is not on a list.
caveat: Identifier blanks may be empty strings rather than nulls, so a naive fill check will mislead.

title: How Well Evidenced Is Each Species
idea: Distribution of taxa by how many supporting documents they carry, exposing the huge population of species backed by a single citation.
harm_angle: Single-citation species are the weakest links in every downstream environmental protection list.
caveat: Nearly two million rows; grain is per taxon-document, so heavy aggregation needed and evidence count may be inflated by duplicate document ids.

title: Load Bearing Documents
idea: Ranked bars of the individual documents supporting the most taxa, identifying the handful of papers holding up thousands of species records.
harm_angle: If one 100-year-old monograph underwrites thousands of species, one revision can upend a whole regulatory category.
caveat: Document ids are namespaced by prefix; joining the wrong prefix would merge unrelated documents.

title: Evidence Type Mix Over Time
idea: Timeline of link creation by document type prefix (publication, expert, other source), showing the shift from published papers to database citations.
harm_angle: A drift toward citing databases instead of papers means the evidence chain gets shorter and less checkable.
caveat: update_date is a maintenance timestamp not a creation date; may be bulk-stamped.

title: Original Description Coverage Gap
idea: Heatmap grid of taxonomic group against whether any of its links is flagged as the original description, mapping species whose founding document is not recorded.
harm_angle: Species with no recorded founding description are the ones easiest to quietly delist.
caveat: Requires joining to the taxa table for grouping; indicator fields may be sparsely used.

title: Author Name Normalization Collisions
idea: Ranked bars of short author forms that collapse multiple distinct full author records into one string, showing where the normalization loses people.
harm_angle: Collapsing distinct scientists into one name erases attribution and makes conflict-of-interest checks impossible.
caveat: Two-column table; the interesting comparison really requires the full-author lookup alongside it.

title: Short Author String Shape
idea: Distribution of stripped author string lengths and token counts, a quick data-quality read on a 214,000-row lookup.
harm_angle: Weak on its own; it flags whether the author key is clean enough to trust for any attribution analysis.
caveat: Genuinely thin source, two columns and no dates; descriptive only.

title: Names That Got Overturned
idea: Distribution of accepted taxa by how many rejected synonyms point at them, exposing organisms that have been renamed a dozen times.
harm_angle: Heavily-renamed species slip between statutes written under old names, so protections lapse by accident.
caveat: 315k pairs; whether chains of synonyms are flattened to the final accepted name is unverified.

title: Synonym Churn Timeline
idea: Timeline of synonym links by update year, showing waves of mass renaming and which years the catalogue was heavily rewritten.
harm_angle: Mass renaming waves are exactly when a legal species list silently goes out of date.
caveat: update_date may be bulk-stamped at ingest, which would collapse the timeline to one spike.

title: Synonym Chains Network
idea: Network view of the most tangled clusters where many rejected names funnel into a small set of accepted names, drawn as a hub-and-spoke map.
harm_angle: Tangled name clusters are where trade, fisheries, and import bans lose track of what is actually being moved.
caveat: Only shows chains if intermediate synonyms are themselves present as accepted targets, which is unverified.

title: Who Named The World
idea: Ranked bars of the individual naming authorities credited on the most scientific names, showing the small group of people whose judgments define the catalogue.
harm_angle: A handful of historical naming authorities shape what counts as a distinct species and therefore what gets protected.
caveat: Author strings are free text with year suffixes and parentheses; needs normalization and one person may appear many ways.

title: Naming Authority By Kingdom
idea: Heatmap grid of top naming authorities against kingdom, showing which specialists dominate which branch of life.
harm_angle: Concentration by kingdom shows which branches of life depend on a single expert's living memory.
caveat: kingdom_id fill on the author lookup is unverified; may be largely null.

title: Naming Years Extracted From Citations
idea: Timeline built by pulling the year out of each author citation string, showing the two-century arc of scientific naming activity.
harm_angle: Long naming droughts mark the eras when whole groups of organisms went undescribed and therefore unprotected.
caveat: Depends entirely on the year being embedded in a free-text string; extraction may fail on a large share of rows.

title: Rank Ladders Side By Side
idea: Small multiples, one per kingdom, showing its ladder of ranks and the required-parent rule at each step, revealing that different kingdoms use different ladders.
harm_angle: Incompatible rank ladders mean cross-kingdom biodiversity comparisons used in policy are quietly apples-to-oranges.
caveat: Only 182 rows; a structural explainer more than an investigation.

title: Rank Rule Violations Map
idea: Heatmap grid comparing each kingdom's declared required-parent rule against the ranks actually used, flagging where the catalogue breaks its own rules.
harm_angle: A reference system that violates its own structure produces records downstream systems cannot validate.
caveat: Needs the core taxa table to see actual usage; this table alone only holds the rules.

title: Credibility Ratings Across Life
idea: Ranked bars of taxa by credibility rating within each kingdom, showing how much of the official species list is flagged as unverified.
harm_angle: Species carrying a low credibility flag can be challenged out of protection, and nobody outside the field knows which those are.
caveat: Rating vocabulary and fill rate unverified; may be dominated by one default value.

title: Completeness Versus Currency Grid
idea: Scatter or heatmap of completeness rating against currency rating, sized by taxa count, showing the corner of the catalogue that is both incomplete and out of date.
harm_angle: The incomplete-and-stale corner is where an entire group of organisms can disappear without the record noticing.
caveat: Both rating fields may be sparsely filled; the interesting corner could be empty for a boring reason.

title: Why Names Get Rejected
idea: Ranked bars of the reasons recorded for a name being unaccepted, broken out by kingdom, showing the mechanics of taxonomic demotion.
harm_angle: Understanding why names die tells you how a protected organism can be legislated out of existence on paper.
caveat: unaccept_reason is only populated for non-accepted names; the denominator needs care.

title: Description Rate Since 1996
idea: Timeline of taxa by their initial catalogue timestamp and update date, showing whether the pace of describing new organisms is rising or collapsing.
harm_angle: A collapsing description rate means we are losing organisms faster than we can name them, and unnamed things get no protection.
caveat: initial_time_stamp is when the record entered ITIS, not when the species was described; the two are often decades apart.

title: The Unnamed And The Uncertain
idea: Cohort grid of taxa flagged as unnamed or with uncertain parentage, arranged by kingdom and rank, mapping the fuzzy edges of the official tree.
harm_angle: Organisms sitting in the uncertain zone are invisible to any statute that requires a named species.
caveat: Indicator fields may be single-character codes with an unclear vocabulary.

title: Which Species Curators Argue About
idea: Ranked bars of taxa by number of attached curator comments, surfacing the organisms that generated the most internal debate.
harm_angle: Heavily-commented taxa are contested calls, and contested calls are where a protection decision is most fragile.
caveat: Bridge table only; the comment text lives in a separate table not in this slice, so the chart is counts without content.

title: Comment Reuse Across Taxa
idea: Distribution of comments by how many taxa they are attached to, showing boilerplate notes stamped across thousands of records.
harm_angle: Boilerplate curator notes masquerading as per-species reasoning inflate the apparent rigor of the record.
caveat: Cannot see comment text from this table, so boilerplate versus genuine reuse cannot be distinguished here.

title: Are Common Names Evidenced
idea: Ranked bars comparing how many vernacular names carry a supporting document against those that do not, by language.
harm_angle: Unevidenced common names are how a fish gets sold under a protected species' name with nobody able to check.
caveat: This table only holds the links that exist; the unevidenced denominator must come from the vernaculars table.

title: Common Name Evidence Sources
idea: Ranked bars of the documents most often cited to justify common names, showing which few references define what the public calls things.
harm_angle: A handful of field guides effectively set the labels used on menus, permits, and import forms.
caveat: Document prefixes namespace the ids; mixing prefixes would merge unrelated sources.

title: Whose Languages Are In The Record
idea: Ranked bars of vernacular names by language, showing how heavily the national species catalogue leans on English over Indigenous and other languages.
harm_angle: Species that only have Indigenous names are invisible to an English-only record, and so are the communities who depend on them.
caveat: Language values are free text and may be inconsistently spelled; Indigenous language coverage may be near zero, which is itself the finding.

title: Unapproved Common Names
idea: Ranked bars by language of the share of vernacular names not flagged approved, showing which languages' names the catalogue declines to bless.
harm_angle: Systematically withholding approval from non-English names is a quiet form of erasure in the official record.
caveat: approved_ind vocabulary unverified; may be near-uniformly one value.

title: One Name Many Animals
idea: Ranked bars of common names shared by the most distinct taxa, mapping the names that cannot identify anything on their own.
harm_angle: Ambiguous common names are the loophole in seafood, timber, and wildlife-trade labelling rules.
caveat: Case and punctuation variants will need normalization or the collision count will be understated.

title: Species With No Common Name
idea: Distribution of catalogued taxa by whether they have any vernacular name at all, broken out by kingdom.
harm_angle: An organism with no common name never appears in a public comment period, so no one ever objects to its loss.
caveat: Needs the core taxa table for the full denominator; this table only holds taxa that do have names.

title: NSF Award Sizes by Program
idea: Distribution of award_amount split by program_name, with each award as a point. Viewer sees whether some programs fund a few giants and others many smalls.
harm_angle: Small-award programs are where new and minority-serving institutions get in; shrinking them closes the door.
caveat: Only 125 rows in the mart - this is a sample, not the real NSF corpus; conclusions cannot generalize.

title: Award Length Versus Money
idea: Scatter award_amount against the span from start_date to end_date, colored by state. Viewer sees whether long projects actually get proportionally more money.
harm_angle: Underfunded long projects burn out early-career researchers and get abandoned mid-question.
caveat: 125 rows only; date fields go through a text-to-date cast that may fail silently.

title: Program Officer Portfolios
idea: Ranked bars of total dollars and award count per program_officer. Viewer sees how much discretion sits with individual named officials.
harm_angle: A handful of named officials steering public research money with no visible check on them.
caveat: Tiny sample; program_officer may be blank on most rows.

source_names: NASA Open APIs And Data Portal
title: NASA API Surface Inventory
idea: Chart each NASA API by response media type and record count, documenting exactly which endpoints were captured and what they return.
harm_angle: Knowing this is a 54-row API inventory rather than a science dataset prevents anyone building a finding on top of a probe.
caveat: 54 rows only - an endpoint census, not data; the payload sits in an unparsed raw_json column.

source_names: NASA Open APIs And Data Portal
title: Unparsed Payload Depth
idea: Profile the raw JSON blob per API by size and key structure, showing how much usable content is sitting unparsed behind a single column.
chart_shape: heatmap grid of API by key presence
harm_angle: An unparsed blob is data the platform holds but cannot read - a self-inflicted blind spot worth measuring.
caveat: raw_json structure varies per API; 54 rows; this is a data-engineering diagnostic more than a public-interest chart.

title: Vendors that keep showing up on the exploited list
idea: Ranked bars of catalog entries per vendor, colored by how many carry the ransomware-campaign flag. Repeat vendors ship the software that keeps getting broken into.
harm_angle: Hospitals and utilities run this software; repeat vendors put patients and customers at risk.
caveat: No install-base denominator so big vendors naturally top the list.

title: The patch clock: added to due date
idea: Distribution of days between the date a vulnerability was added and its federal remediation due date, over time. Shortening windows signal escalating urgency.
harm_angle: Every day of the window is a day federal systems holding citizen data stay open.
caveat: Due date is a deadline not a compliance record; the catalog cannot show who actually patched.

title: Ransomware-linked flaws over time
idea: Timeline of catalog additions per month split into ransomware-flagged and not, showing whether the exploited landscape is increasingly criminal-monetized.
harm_angle: Ransomware-linked flaws are the ones that shut down clinics and school districts.
caveat: Additions reflect agency attention as much as real-world exploitation.

title: Weakness families behind exploited bugs
idea: Ranked bars of weakness classes across the catalog, so the same handful of decades-old coding mistakes shows up as the dominant cause.
harm_angle: The same avoidable mistakes keep exposing the public's systems.
caveat: The weakness field is likely a delimited list needing unnesting and is partly blank on older entries.

title: Twenty-six reports and their publishing rhythm
idea: Timeline dot plot of publication dates by report type, showing the cadence of Europol's threat assessments and any long gaps.
harm_angle: Long gaps between assessments mean the public flies blind on organized crime for years at a stretch.
caveat: Only 26 rows and no substantive content columns - this is a document register, not data.

title: Which languages the warnings reach
idea: Ranked bars of report count by language and geographic scope, showing which European publics can read their own threat assessment.
harm_angle: People who cannot read the assessment in their language are excluded from the debate about their own safety.
caveat: 26 rows; language coverage may reflect what was scraped rather than what was published. Genuinely thin source - two ideas is the honest ceiling.

source_names: CNS North Korea Missile Test Database
title: Launch sites and their firing histories
idea: Map of launch facilities sized by number of tests, with color showing the dominant missile class fired from each. Reveals site specialization.
harm_angle: Neighboring populations under flight paths bear the risk of failed launches.
caveat: Only 303 rows; several coordinate fields may be blank for older tests.

source_names: CNS North Korea Missile Test Database
title: Test failure rate as the program matured
idea: Timeline of tests per year with the share coded as failures overlaid, showing the learning curve of the program across four decades.
harm_angle: A maturing program changes the threat calculus for civilians across the region.
caveat: Outcome is free text with unknowns; the date column is not date-cast in the model.

source_names: CNS North Korea Missile Test Database
title: Apogee and range by missile class
idea: Scatter of apogee against distance travelled, colored by missile class, separating lofted tests from full-range demonstrations.
harm_angle: Range envelopes define which civilian populations sit inside the threat radius.
caveat: Apogee and distance are free text including 'Unknown' and must be parsed.

source_names: CNS North Korea Missile Test Database
title: Unconfirmed tests as a share of the record
idea: Distribution of confirmation status over time, showing how much of the chronology rests on unverified reporting.
harm_angle: Policy built on unverified test claims can escalate against a phantom.
caveat: Confirmation coding may be sparse and inconsistently applied across eras.

source_names: nagix North Korea missile flight tests
title: Firing bearings from the peninsula
idea: Radial distribution of launch bearings, showing the dominant firing corridors and which neighbours sit at the end of them.
harm_angle: Bearings point at the populations that live under the trajectory.
caveat: Facility and missile are slug codes needing a lookup file that may not be landed here.

source_names: nagix North Korea missile flight tests
title: Landing points over time
idea: Map of computed landing locations colored by year, showing the outward creep of impact zones as the program advanced.
harm_angle: Fishing fleets and coastal communities sit inside those impact zones.
caveat: The landing column may be a nested or text structure rather than clean coordinates, and this is a derived mirror not a primary source.

source_names: nagix North Korea missile flight tests
title: Glide vehicles enter the record
idea: Timeline flagging tests marked as glide vehicles, isolating the newest and hardest-to-intercept category.
harm_angle: Hypersonic glide tests change what any defensive system can protect civilians from.
caveat: Glide flag may be sparsely populated and only present in recent years.

title: The arsenal curve since 1945
idea: Stacked timeline of warhead stockpiles by state, showing the Cold War peak and the plateau that never returned to zero.
harm_angle: Every warhead on the curve is a standing threat to civilian populations.
caveat: Estimates not counts; threshold states are absent by construction.

title: Who joined the club and when
idea: Timeline dot plot of each state's first non-zero stockpile year, making the proliferation sequence legible in one strip.
harm_angle: Each new entrant widens the set of populations living under nuclear risk.
caveat: First non-zero year in an estimate series is not the same as a first test date.

title: Which gangs hit which sectors
idea: Heatmap grid of ransomware group against victim sector, color as victim count. Shows explicit sector specialization by criminal crew.
harm_angle: Sector specialization means specific hospitals, schools and utilities are being deliberately targeted.
caveat: Sector is loose free text and victim names are attacker-claimed. The country column is cast to a number in the model, which suggests it is not a usable country label.

title: Gang lifecycles and rebrands
idea: Timeline of first-seen to last-seen victim posts per group, one bar each, so takedowns and immediate rebrands appear as adjacent bars.
harm_angle: When a takedown is followed instantly by a rebrand, the disruption did not protect anyone.
caveat: Rebrand linkage is inference not data; crowdsourced collection has gaps when the project was offline.

title: Delay between attack and public leak
idea: Distribution of days from discovered to published, split by sector. Short delays suggest immediate extortion pressure; long ones suggest failed negotiations.
harm_angle: Victim organizations are given very little time before their data goes public.
caveat: Discovered is when the tracker saw the post not when the attack happened; both fields are uncast text.

title: Critical-infrastructure victims over time
idea: Timeline of victim counts restricted to healthcare, water, energy and education sectors, showing whether attacks on life-critical services are rising.
harm_angle: Patients and residents lose service when these organizations are locked out.
caveat: Sector labels are inconsistent and must be hand-mapped before filtering.

title: Sabotage Target Types Over Time
idea: Timeline of incidents by targettype and eventcategory. Viewer sees the shift from information operations to physical sabotage of infrastructure.
harm_angle: Sabotage of rail, water and power hits ordinary civilians, not the states being pressured.
caveat: Only 153 curated incidents - a research dataset with selection bias baked in.

title: Where Incidents Land in Europe
idea: Map incidents by c_where, sized by count and colored by apparent goal.
harm_angle: Shows which countries and communities absorb the physical risk of a conflict they are not party to.
caveat: c_where is free text and will need geocoding; 153 rows.

title: Disposable Agents Pattern
idea: Compare incidents flagged disposableagentsinvolved against those that are not, across target types and years. Viewer sees the shift toward recruiting local proxies.
harm_angle: Locally recruited proxies are the people who go to prison while the sponsors never appear.
caveat: The flag is a coder judgement in a 153-row curated set - not a census.

title: Default Rates by Neighborhood
idea: Map loss_rate and is_defaulted by borrower_zip and project_county, weighted by gross_approval_amount. Viewer sees geographies where SBA lending systematically fails.
harm_angle: High-default neighborhoods lose the businesses, the jobs, and the owners personal guarantees together.
caveat: Loss rate is only defined where chargeoff amount is populated; the default definition excludes still-open loans.

title: Lenders With Outlier Losses
idea: Scatter each lender loan volume against its chargeoff rate. Viewer sees lenders originating heavily into loans that predictably fail.
harm_angle: Lenders who profit on origination while borrowers eat the default are a repeatable predatory pattern.
caveat: Lender names need normalization across 35 years of mergers; chargeoff dates may be missing for recent loans.

title: Jobs Promised Per Dollar
idea: Plot jobs_supported against gross_approval_amount by naics_description and state. Viewer sees which industries and places convert public loan guarantees into actual jobs.
harm_angle: Loan guarantees are justified as job creation - this shows where that justification is empty.
caveat: jobs_supported is self-reported at application and never verified after the fact.

title: Loan Volume Through Recessions
idea: Timeline of approvals and dollars by fiscal year, split by program and business_age. Viewer sees credit vanishing for new businesses exactly when downturns hit.
harm_angle: Credit that disappears in a downturn kills the youngest businesses and their workers first.
caveat: business_age coding likely changed over the decades of FOIA releases.

title: Policy diffusion across states
idea: Heatmap grid of state by year shaded by medical and recreational approval status, showing the wave of legalization spreading.
harm_angle: Residents in late-adopting states kept getting arrested for what was legal next door.
caveat: 1500 rows across states and years; approval versus implementation columns must not be conflated.

title: Approved but not implemented
idea: Slope chart per state of approval year versus implementation year, ranking the longest delays between a law passing and taking effect.
harm_angle: A law approved but unimplemented means patients still cannot legally get medicine.
caveat: App and imp column pairs are boolean-ish by year; deriving the first-true year per state is required.

title: Ballot measures versus legislatures
idea: Ranked bars of states by whether legalization came by ballot or by legislature, with court action marked.
harm_angle: Where legislatures refused and voters had to force it, the gap reveals unrepresentative lawmakers.
caveat: legislative_action is number-cast over what looks like a text field, likely nulling it.

title: Restrictive versus permissive regimes
idea: Scatter of the permissiveness scale against the pharmaceutical-model scale per state-year, mapping the two competing regulatory philosophies.
harm_angle: Restrictive regimes leave patients paying cash for unregulated product.
caveat: Scale and z-score columns are unexplained without the source codebook.

title: AI Incidents Are Accelerating
idea: Single timeline of reported AI incidents and controversies per year.
harm_angle: Each count is a real person misidentified, denied, or injured by an automated decision.
caveat: Only 14 rows and it is a derived aggregate - a headline line, with no drilldown behind it.

title: Incidents Against Model Releases
idea: Overlay the annual incident count with an annotated timeline of major model launches to show whether harm reports track deployment.
harm_angle: Shows whether the industry ships faster than harm gets recorded.
caveat: Model-release annotations are not in the data - they would be hand-added context; 14 rows total.

title: Who holds the spectrum
idea: Ranked bars of active licenses by entity name and radio service, showing spectrum concentration in a handful of holders.
harm_angle: Concentrated spectrum ownership sets who gets coverage and at what price.
caveat: entity_name needs heavy normalization; a single company appears under many spellings and FRNs.

title: Expired but never cancelled
idea: Scatter of expiration date against cancellation date, with licenses expired years ago and never cancelled forming a visible band.
harm_angle: Spectrum warehoused on dead licenses is spectrum unavailable to communities with no service.
caveat: Depends on how license_status is maintained; nulls in cancellation_date may just mean still-active.

title: Spectrum deserts by county
idea: County map of active license density per capita, with the emptiest counties named -- the places where wireless service is thin by license, not just by marketing.
harm_angle: Residents of low-license counties have no reliable emergency or broadband coverage.
caveat: fcc_county_code is an FCC-internal code, not FIPS, so a crosswalk is required.

title: License churn timeline
idea: Timeline of grants, expirations and cancellations per year by radio service, showing which services are growing and which are being abandoned.
harm_angle: Abandoned service classes strand the users who still depend on them.
caveat: Date fields are try_to_date over text; malformed dates silently become null.

title: Shared addresses, different names
idea: Network of licensees linked by identical address or EIN, revealing shell-like clusters holding spectrum under many names.
harm_angle: Entities splitting holdings across names can evade concentration limits meant to protect consumers.
caveat: EIN in FCC ULS is a known masked or blank-string trap on this platform -- verify distinct values before trusting it.

title: Aircraft Registered to Trusts
idea: Ranked bars of registrant types and registrant names by aircraft count, isolating trust registrations that mask the real owner.
harm_angle: Trust registration lets a beneficial owner fly a US-flagged aircraft with their name nowhere in the public record.
caveat: type_registrant is a numeric code needing a lookup; identifying trusts may require name-string matching.

title: Addresses Hosting Many Aircraft
idea: Ranked bars of registrant street addresses by number of registered aircraft, surfacing the handful of mailboxes that hold hundreds of planes.
harm_angle: A single mailbox on four hundred aircraft is the aviation version of a shell-company address.
caveat: Address strings need normalizing; large legitimate leasing companies will top the list and must be labeled.

title: Aging Fleet by Aircraft Type
idea: Distribution of year of manufacture by aircraft type and airworthiness date, showing which categories are flying decades past their build year.
harm_angle: Old airframes in charter or commercial use put passengers on equipment built before they were born.
caveat: year_mfr may be blank on older records; status_code needs a lookup to exclude non-flying registrations.

title: Registrations About to Expire
idea: Timeline of expiration dates against last action dates, showing the backlog of registrations lapsing and whether the registry keeps up.
harm_angle: Aircraft flying on lapsed registration are outside the tracking system entirely.
caveat: Date fields may be text in compact form; expired records may simply be retained history rather than active violations.

title: Co-Owner Chains Behind One Tail Number
idea: Network graph linking aircraft to their registrant plus up to five additional named parties, revealing co-ownership webs behind single tail numbers.
harm_angle: Layered co-ownership is how aircraft used for questionable purposes stay untraceable to a person.
caveat: Five fixed name slots cap the chain; those fields are likely blank on the vast majority of rows.

title: The Deadliest Crossings in America
idea: Map of individual grade crossings by cumulative killed and injured, sized and colored, so the specific intersections that keep killing people are named.
harm_angle: A crossing that has killed five people over twenty years is a fixable intersection nobody fixed.
caveat: No lat/lon in this table's select list — geography is city, county, state plus a crossing id, so a true point map needs a crossing inventory join.

title: Warning Devices Versus Deaths
idea: Heatmap grid of crossing warning type against fatality and injury rate per incident, showing which protection levels actually protect people.
harm_angle: Unprotected passive crossings kill at a different rate, and communities that never got gates know which ones they are.
caveat: Twelve expanded warning code slots make encoding messy; this is incidents only, with no denominator of crossings by warning type.

title: Sight Obstruction and Driver Blame
idea: Cross-tab of view obstruction against highway user action as a heatmap, testing how often driver error coincides with a crossing the driver could not see down.
harm_angle: Blaming the driver at a blind crossing moves liability off the railroad and onto the dead.
caveat: Both fields are railroad-reported after the fact, which is itself a bias that must be stated on the chart.

title: Who Dies at Crossings by Age and Sex
idea: Cohort grid of user age against user sex shaded by fatality rate, showing whether older or younger drivers die disproportionately.
harm_angle: If one age group dies far more, crossing design is failing a knowable population.
caveat: Age and sex fields are likely sparse and are recorded by the responding railroad, not the victim.

title: Whistle Ban Zones and Collisions
idea: Small multiples over years of incident and fatality counts in whistle-ban versus non-ban crossings, testing the tradeoff communities were sold.
harm_angle: Quiet zones trade noise for risk, and the people who bear the risk did not always get the vote.
caveat: Whistle ban flag fill rate unverified; no denominator of quiet-zone crossings exists in this table.

title: Derailments With Hazmat Released
idea: Map of accidents where hazmat cars released, sized by persons evacuated, across the full history. East Palestine-shaped events, all of them.
harm_angle: Every dot is a town told to leave its homes because a train came apart.
caveat: Lat/lon populated-ness unverified across the full history; older records likely lack coordinates entirely.

title: Primary Cause Mix by Railroad
idea: Heatmap grid of reporting railroad against primary accident cause, showing which carriers derail from track defects versus human factors versus equipment.
harm_angle: A railroad whose accidents are mostly track defects is under-maintaining infrastructure that runs through towns.
caveat: Cause codes are self-reported by the railroad, a well-known bias toward human-factor attribution.

title: Crew Hours on Duty Before an Accident
idea: Distribution of engineer and conductor hours on duty at the time of the accident, split by railroad. The long right tail is fatigue.
harm_angle: Crews worked past exhaustion are a scheduling decision made by management and paid for by everyone on the train.
caveat: Hours-on-duty fields may be sparse; there is no baseline of non-accident shifts, so this shows the accident distribution only, not relative risk.

title: Train Length and Speed Against Damage
idea: Scatter of car counts and gross tonnage against total damage cost, colored by whether anyone was hurt. Tests the long-train hypothesis.
harm_angle: If longer heavier trains produce worse outcomes, the industry's efficiency push has a human cost.
caveat: No exposure denominator; longer trains may simply be more common now. Damage cost is self-reported and not inflation-adjusted.

title: Damage Cost Just Under the Threshold
idea: Distribution of total damage cost with fine bins near the federal reporting threshold, looking for a suspicious pile-up of accidents reported just below it.
harm_angle: Bunching just under the reporting threshold would mean railroads are managing the number instead of the risk.
caveat: The threshold changes over time and is not in the data; without the threshold schedule the shape cannot be interpreted.

title: Who Gets Hurt In Plane Crashes
idea: Ranked bars of injury counts by person category (crew, passenger, ground) crossed with injury level, showing who bears the physical cost of aviation accidents.
harm_angle: Ground casualties and cabin crew are the people who never chose the risk, and this shows how often they pay for it.
caveat: Grain is event x aircraft x category x level, so totals must be summed carefully; person-category vocabulary unverified.

title: Fatality Severity Mix Over Time
idea: Timeline of the fatal share of injuries by year, showing whether aviation accidents have become more survivable.
harm_angle: A flat survivability curve would mean decades of safety spending never reached the people in the seats.
caveat: The only date in this table is a record-change date, not the accident date; the real event date lives in the separate NTSB events table.

title: Crew Versus Passenger Survival Gap
idea: Slope chart comparing fatal versus non-fatal rates for crew against passengers within the same events, testing whether the front of the plane fares differently.
harm_angle: If passengers die at higher rates than crew in the same crashes, cabin design and evacuation rules are failing the people who bought a ticket.
caveat: Comparing within event requires that both categories are populated for the same ev_id; not verifiable from metadata.

title: Mass Casualty Events Distribution
idea: Distribution of events by total injured persons, with the long tail of mass-casualty accidents labelled.
harm_angle: The tail is the small number of events that account for most human loss, and they are the ones worth auditing.
caveat: Requires summing across the aircraft/category grain; double counting is a real risk if the grain is misread.

title: Multi Aircraft Collisions
idea: Ranked bars of events with more than one aircraft key, comparing injury outcomes in midair and ground collisions against single-aircraft accidents.
harm_angle: Collisions involve people in an aircraft they never boarded, the clearest case of harm imposed on a bystander.
caveat: Multi-aircraft events are identified only by counting distinct aircraft_key per ev_id; aircraft_key may just be a within-event sequence number.

title: Who Edits The Injury Record
idea: Timeline of record changes by the user id that made them, showing which accounts revise injury counts and when.
harm_angle: Late revisions to fatality counts are worth knowing about, because the first published number is the one the public remembers.
caveat: Only the latest change is stored per row, so this cannot show a full revision history; userid may be masked.

title: Operators With Repeat Crashes
idea: Ranked bars of operator names by number of accident aircraft, separating commercial certificate holders from private operators.
harm_angle: Repeat-crash operators keep flying paying passengers between incidents.
caveat: oper_name is free text with heavy spelling variation and no operator id to dedup on.

title: Time Since Last Inspection
idea: Distribution of days between the last inspection and the accident, split by inspection type and FAR part.
harm_angle: Maintenance gaps that end in wreckage are a regulatory failure, not bad luck.
caveat: Needs the event date from the events table; inspection date may be sparse.

title: Homebuilt Versus Certified
idea: Small multiples comparing damage and fire outcomes for homebuilt versus factory-built aircraft, by category.
harm_angle: Shows whether the lightly-regulated homebuilt lane carries more lethal outcomes.
caveat: Fields are text flags; encoding of Y/N and blanks unverified.

title: Emergency Beacon Failure Rate
idea: Ranked bars of emergency locator beacon manufacturers and models by share where the beacon did not aid locating the wreck.
harm_angle: A beacon that fails is the difference between rescue and death by exposure.
caveat: ELT fields likely sparse and only populated for fully investigated accidents.

title: Where Planes Come Down
idea: Map of accident points sized by total fatalities, revealing corridors and airports with repeat clusters.
harm_angle: Communities under repeat crash corridors bear a risk they never chose.
caveat: dec_latitude and dec_longitude fill rate unknown; the text lat/long columns are uncast.

title: Ground Casualties Of Aviation
idea: Timeline of injuries and deaths on the ground rather than on the aircraft -- the bystanders of aviation accidents.
harm_angle: People on the ground never boarded the plane and still paid for it.
caveat: Ground injury counts are rare, so the series may be too sparse to trend.

title: Weather Versus Fatality Rate
idea: Heatmap grid of basic weather condition against light condition, shaded by share of events with a fatality.
harm_angle: Night and instrument-condition flying kills at rates regulation could address.
caveat: Visibility and ceiling remain text strings and need casting.

title: Notification Lag To NTSB
idea: Distribution of days between the event and NTSB notification, by state and investigating agency.
harm_angle: Late notification means evidence and survivor accounts degrade before anyone looks.
caveat: Notification date may be sparse or auto-filled equal to the event date.

title: Seasonality Of Fatal Flights
idea: Cohort grid of month by year shaded by fatal events, testing whether the summer flying season is a recurring killing season.
harm_angle: Predictable seasonal spikes are preventable if staffing and oversight followed them.
caveat: ev_year and ev_month are text; only a rolling window is loaded so long trends are truncated.

title: Portal Catalog Coverage
idea: Grid of BTS datasets by mode and subject, showing which transport modes have public data and which do not.
harm_angle: Modes with no public data are modes where nobody can prove harm.
caveat: Only 21 rows - this is a catalog listing, not transport data. Genuinely thin.

title: Freshness of Transport Datasets

idea: Distribution of days between fail_date and date_received, by manufacturer and component. Viewer sees how long harm sits unreported.
harm_angle: Long lags mean the regulator is always looking at last year danger.

title: Complaint Deserts

harm_angle: Under-reported regions get less regulatory attention for the same defects.

title: Component Harm Heatmap
idea: Heatmap of component against model_year colored by fatal-complaint rate. Viewer sees defect classes concentrated in specific model-year cohorts.
harm_angle: Buyers of a specific model year are unknowingly driving a known lethal cohort.
caveat: Component text is free-form and needs grouping; model_year is a text column.

title: Investigations That Go Nowhere
idea: For each manufacturer, plot the share of investigations where resulted_in_recall is false, against investigation volume.
harm_angle: An investigation closed with no recall leaves the defect on the road and the driver unwarned.
caveat: Grain is investigation-recall link, not investigation - must group by nhtsa_action_number first per the model header.

title: How Long Probes Stay Open
idea: Distribution of days from open_date to close_date, by manufacturer and component, with still-open probes as an open tail.
harm_angle: Every extra month a probe stays open is a month the defective vehicles keep driving.
caveat: Open-ended probes need explicit censoring treatment or they bias the median down.

title: Probe Volume Versus Fleet Size
idea: Ranked bars of investigations per manufacturer over time, showing whether regulator attention tracks market share.
harm_angle: Regulators that focus on the same familiar names miss the defects at everyone else.
caveat: No fleet-size denominator exists inside this source.

title: Who Triggered the Recall
idea: Timeline of recalls split by recall_trigger - investigation, manufacturer, or OVSC - weighted by potentially_affected_units. Viewer sees whether regulators or makers drive safety action.
harm_angle: When makers never self-report, the regulator is the only thing between a defect and a driver.
caveat: influenced_by coding may be inconsistent across decades; unit counts are manufacturer estimates.

title: The Long Manufacturing Tail
idea: For each recall, plot the span from begin_manufacture_date to notification_date. Viewer sees defects sold for years before anybody was told.

title: Scale of Exposure by Maker
idea: Ranked bars of cumulative potentially_affected_units per manufacturer, split by component class.
harm_angle: Raw scale of how many people are driving something known to be defective.

title: Remedy Language Patterns

title: Civilian deaths versus combatant deaths

harm_angle: Conflicts that kill mostly civilians are the ones where the war is aimed at ordinary people.

harm_angle: Large declines are proof that lethal violence is a policy outcome, not fate.

source_names: FEMA IA registrations|FEMA NFIP communities|Mapping Inequality
title: Three-layer flood injustice
idea: Three-source chain: historic HOLC grade, current NFIP participation and map age, and actual flood-aid outcomes for the same places.
harm_angle: One neighborhood can be graded hazardous, left off the flood map, and denied the payout - all by government action.
caveat: Three different geographies joined by name and county; each hop loses precision and the FEMA load is partial.

title: Revoked But Still Listed As Deductible
idea: Join revoked employer ids to the eligible-donee list to find organizations that lost exempt status but still appear as eligible for deductible gifts.
harm_angle: Donors giving to an organization the IRS revoked will lose the deduction and may be funding a shell.
caveat: Both tables sit at exactly 500,000 rows and are likely truncated, so absence from the donee list may be a load artifact rather than fact.

title: Daily cash against monthly books
idea: Overlay the daily deposit series on the monthly receipts series for matching categories, showing where the daily operating picture diverges from the official monthly statement.
harm_angle: Divergence between the daily cash reality and the monthly published books is where fiscal-crisis narratives get built or debunked.
caveat: Category vocabularies differ between the two statements and have no shared code; the deposits table's 10,000-row cap may not overlap the receipts window.

title: Declared parents versus claimed exceptions
idea: Compare entities that declare a parent relationship against those filing an exception, charting the ratio by managing registrar and jurisdiction.
harm_angle: Registrars where almost every entity files an exception are the weak links letting global ownership stay hidden.
caveat: registration_managinglou was cast with try_to_double and will likely be null; node id types must be confirmed to be LEIs.

source_names: IRS SOI income data|OWID Gini index|FEC contributions
title: Inequality and political money together
idea: State timeline of income concentration against the share of political contributions coming from the top ZIPs.
harm_angle: As income concentrates, so does the money that picks who governs.
caveat: OWID Gini is national, not state-level, so state comparison may need a different inequality measure.

source_names: World Bank international debt statistics|IPC food insecurity
title: Debt service against hunger
idea: Country scatter of external debt service as a share of revenue against the population in acute food insecurity.
harm_angle: Repaying creditors is measurably competing with feeding people.
caveat: Country code standards differ between sources; the IDS mart's column names are unverified.

title: Program mix behind bad outcomes
idea: Institutions in the high-debt low-earnings quadrant broken out by the program families they offer, naming the fields of study that drive the debt.
harm_angle: Knowing which programs produce unpayable debt tells a prospective student exactly what to avoid.
caveat: The institution file is institution-level and carries no CIP column, so this needs the field-of-study file, which may not be in this slice.

title: Debt in, mortgage out
idea: Institution median student debt and 10-year earnings against mortgage approval rates in the states where those graduates are likely to live.
harm_angle: Student debt may be the thing that blocks the first house.
caveat: Graduates do not stay near the school; the geographic link is weak by construction.

title: Barred but still enrolling
idea: Institutions or their parents appearing on the federal exclusion list, with their enrollment, Pell share and default rate at the time.
harm_angle: Students can still be borrowing to attend a place the government has already judged unfit.
caveat: Name matching across SAM and Scorecard; exclusions often name individuals, not schools.

source_names: EDFacts|CDC injury and violence by county
title: Schools in high-injury counties
idea: County injury and violence rates against school proficiency and subgroup participation for districts in that county.
chart_shape: scatter with small multiples by subgroup
harm_angle: Children learning in places where violence is a daily background condition.
caveat: EDFacts mart is 33 rows - probably a stub; CDC county coding of intent needs the codebook.

title: College access in jail-heavy counties
idea: County jail rate against local college net price, Pell share and completion rate, with HBCU and tribal colleges highlighted.
harm_angle: Two public investments in the same young people - one builds, one cages.
caveat: College zip-to-county derivation needed; ecological across very different populations.

title: Federal money per outcome
idea: Federal assistance dollars flowing to each institution against its completion rate, default rate and earnings, sized by enrollment.
harm_angle: Institutions that take public money and leave students with debt and no degree.
caveat: Recipient-name matching is the whole risk; UEI-to-institution crosswalk not present in metadata.

source_names: EAC Election Administration and Voting Survey|MEDSL House returns
title: Rejected ballots and margins
idea: County-jurisdiction ballot rejection and provisional rates plotted against the winning margin in the same district-year - where rejections exceed the margin.
chart_shape: scatter with a diagonal threshold line
harm_angle: Ballots thrown out for paperwork can exceed the margin that decides who governs.
caveat: EAVS columns are opaque question codes (A1A, B13C) needing the codebook; district-to-county mapping is many-to-many.

title: Provisional ballots and turnout
idea: State map of provisional and rejected ballot rates against turnout change, showing where administration itself suppresses the count.
harm_angle: Voters who showed up and still were not counted.
caveat: EAVS column names unverified; survey response completeness varies by state.

source_names: FEC all-candidate financial summary|MEDSL Senate returns
title: Money raised vs votes won 1980-2024
idea: Long timeline of the correlation between campaign receipts and vote share by cycle, showing whether money's predictive power has grown.
harm_angle: If money predicts outcomes ever better, the ballot matters less each cycle.
caveat: Joining on state and cycle rather than candidate id will be coarse; FEC candidate name matching would be needed for precision.

title: Dark spending against margin of victory
idea: District scatter of outside independent-expenditure dollars per vote against the eventual winning margin, flagging blowouts that still drew heavy outside money.
harm_angle: Money poured into races that were never close signals influence-buying, not persuasion.
caveat: MEDSL district identifiers and FEC candidate districts need reconciliation; the IE mart's column names are unverified.

source_names: MEDSL House returns|FEC candidate summary|Committee membership
title: Safe seats, big money, big gavels
idea: Three-way view: districts by margin of victory, the winner's receipts, and whether they hold a committee chair.
harm_angle: The least competitive seats accumulate the most money and the most power.
caveat: Requires the FEC-to-bioguide crosswalk; MEDSL and FEC district codes need reconciliation.

source_names: MEDSL President returns|Election Administration and Voting Survey
title: Ballot rejection against state partisan lean
idea: Dot plot of state provisional and mail rejection rates against the presidential two-party margin, asking whether rejection concentrates in particular political geographies.
harm_angle: If rejections cluster politically, some voters' ballots are worth less than others'.
caveat: The survey's coded columns need the codebook; survey years and election years must be aligned carefully.

title: Voting after the disaster
idea: Jurisdictions hit by a declared disaster in an election year, and what happened to their polling places, mail ballots, and rejection rates that cycle.
harm_angle: Displaced people lose the address that lets them vote.
caveat: EAVS is biennial and coarse; disaster timing vs survey period alignment is tricky.

title: Voting access where tenants live
idea: Counties with large subsidized-tenant populations against polling place counts, mail-ballot rates, and provisional ballot rates.
harm_angle: Disabled and low-income tenants face the longest distance to the ballot.
caveat: EAVS question codes must be decoded; county-level averaging hides precinct siting.

title: Voting machinery in jail-heavy counties
idea: County scatter of polling-place counts and registration volume per capita against the county incarceration rate.
harm_angle: Counties that cage the most people may also run the thinnest voting infrastructure.
caveat: EAVS jurisdiction ids are not always county FIPS (New England towns); ecological.

title: Elected margin vs how they vote
idea: Winning margin in each Senate race against the senator's later ideology score, showing whether close races produce moderates.
harm_angle: Tests whether competitive districts actually restrain extremism, or do not.
caveat: Candidate-name to bioguide matching is fuzzy; a member crosswalk mart exists but its coverage is unverified.

title: Polling places on tribal land
idea: Counties overlapping tribal lands compared with peer counties on polling places per registered voter and mail-ballot availability.
harm_angle: Long drives to the only polling place are a quiet way to cut a community out of an election.
caveat: BIA layer is boundary metadata; overlap must be computed spatially and county-level averaging hides reservation interiors.

title: Who owns the dirtiest fleets
idea: Utilities ranked by the number of their plants carrying unlined ash impoundments or single-pipeline dependency, naming the owners behind the risk.
harm_angle: Naming the parent utility is what turns a scattered set of hazardous sites into one accountable owner.
caveat: utility_id is documented as the utility key but a plant's reported utility may be the operator rather than the ultimate owner.

source_names: EIA utility directory|EIA reliability metrics|FEC contributions
title: Outage minutes vs utility political money
idea: Scatter each utility's average customer outage duration against political contributions from its employees, by state.
harm_angle: Customers sit in the dark while the utility funds the regulators' campaigns.
caveat: EIA marts are passthroughs with unverified column names; utility name matching to donor employers is lossy.

title: Retiring capacity next to ash ponds
idea: Map of plants with unlined ash impoundments sized by the capacity scheduled to retire, showing communities about to inherit an orphaned waste site.
harm_angle: When the plant closes the jobs go and the unlined ash pond stays, leaching into the same neighborhood.
caveat: plant_code is documented as the grain key in both models but the overlap rate is unverified; planned retirement is an intention.

source_names: EIA plant directory|EPA eGRID plant emissions|Senate lobbying
title: Dirtiest plants, loudest owners
idea: Map plants ranked by emissions rate, colored by whether the parent utility lobbies federally and how much.
harm_angle: The communities breathing the worst air live next to the plants with the best lobbyists.
caveat: The plant-to-owner-to-lobby-client chain is name-based; eGRID and EIA plant ids may not align in the marts.

title: Solar Adoption Against Retail Price
idea: Scatter of residential rooftop installations per customer against residential price per MWh by utility, showing whether high prices drove adoption or whether some high-price utilities suppressed it.
harm_angle: High-price territories with near-zero rooftop uptake are where the utility, not the economics, blocked the escape route.
caveat: Both need the same data_year filter; the sales table's service_type segmentation can double the denominator.

title: Smart Meters Did Not Fix Outages
idea: Scatter of AMI penetration against SAIDI by utility, testing whether the expensive metering rollout customers funded actually shortened outages.
harm_angle: If the meters ratepayers financed bought no reliability, that spend was a transfer with no benefit back.
caveat: Both tables are utility-year grain but reporting populations may differ; unmatched utilities must not be dropped silently.

title: Paying More For Worse Power
idea: Scatter of residential price per MWh against SAIDI outage minutes per utility, isolating the quadrant where customers pay the most and get the least reliable service.
harm_angle: The high-price high-outage quadrant names the utilities charging premium rates for third-rate service.
caveat: Requires utility_number to be a clean join key across both marts and matching data years; the sales table is segmented by service_type and must be filtered first.

source_names: EIA-861 Reliability|EIA-861 Sales to Ultimate Customers
title: Who sits in the dark the longest
idea: Rank utilities by average outage minutes per customer against average residential price, showing customers paying the most for the least reliable service.
harm_angle: Some households pay top rates and still lose power for hours every year.
caveat: Both marts are passthroughs; reliability metric column names unverified.

title: Outage Minutes At County Grain
idea: Map at county grain of outage minutes attributed by joining utility reliability to the counties each utility serves, turning utility-level metrics into a geography people recognize.
harm_angle: County-level outage burden is the form in which a reader can see their own home on the map.
caveat: Counties served by several utilities need customer-weighted blending, and county names lack FIPS codes in the territory table.

title: Who owns the dirtiest plants
idea: Roll emissions per megawatt-hour up to the utility and parent owner, ranked, with each utility's plant fleet shown as stacked segments.
harm_angle: A handful of owners control the plants doing the most damage per unit of power.
caveat: EIA-860 mart column names unverified; plant code alignment across the two files assumed.

title: Who Owns The Dirtiest Plants
idea: Network graph linking owners to plants weighted by owned share and colored by the plant's CO2 rate, showing which firms hold the dirtiest slice of the fleet.
harm_angle: Attributing emissions to the firms that own the fractions moves blame from the plant to the boardroom.
caveat: The owner table covers only jointly-owned generators, so wholly-owned dirty plants will be missing entirely; owner names are unnormalized free text.

title: Fracking intensity and water violations
idea: County-level scatter of fracking jobs per year against health-based drinking water violations, animated across years.
harm_angle: Communities that host drilling may also lose their drinking water quality.
caveat: Geography join at county grain; FracFocus columns unverified; correlation does not establish a contamination path.

title: Frack Chemicals Matched To Substance Registry
idea: Join fracking ingredient chemical identifiers to the FDA substance registry to identify which pumped chemicals are also regulated pharmaceutical or food substances with known toxicity profiles.
harm_angle: Chemicals with documented toxicity being pumped under homes is the exposure the disclosure regime was supposed to prevent.
caveat: CAS formatting differs between sources and needs normalizing; match rate unverified.

title: Storms explain outages until they do not
idea: Plot each utility's outage minutes against storm-event frequency in its territory. Utilities well above the storm-explained line are failing for other reasons.
harm_angle: Utilities blame the weather for outages the weather does not explain.
caveat: Territory-to-county mapping is approximate; reliability metric names unverified.

title: Pipeline incidents near subsidized homes
idea: Map significant pipeline incidents within a radius of assisted housing, sized by households and colored by whether there were injuries.
harm_angle: Families with no choice about where they live sit next to the line that ruptured.
caveat: Pipeline mart columns unverified; only 2039 incidents so counts will be small.

title: Pipeline incidents and pipeline lobbying
idea: Timeline of significant pipeline incidents and injuries alongside pipeline-sector lobbying spend by year.
harm_angle: Safety rules stall while the same operators keep rupturing lines near homes.
caveat: Only 2039 incident rows; PHMSA mart column names unverified.

title: Two incident systems one pipeline
idea: Compare pipeline-related spill reports in the response-center feed against the formal pipeline incident record, showing events that only appear in one.
harm_angle: Events that never reach the official pipeline record are invisible to the people living over the line.
caveat: Both marts are passthroughs; matching by date and location is approximate.

source_names: USGS Orphaned Oil and Gas Wells|SDWA Public Water Systems
title: Abandoned wells over drinking water
idea: Map orphaned well density against water systems that draw from groundwater, weighted by population served.
harm_angle: Unplugged wells leak into the aquifers that supply people's tap water.
caveat: Well file column names unverified; groundwater source flag reliability unknown; geography-only join.

title: Excluded operators still running facilities
idea: Entities on the federal exclusion list whose names match detention facility operators or their parents.
harm_angle: A government barring a company in one hand while paying it to hold people in the other.
caveat: Facility list gives no operator name, only facility type - the operator link may not exist in metadata.

source_names: NAAG multistate AG settlements|MEDSL presidential returns
title: Which AGs join which fights
idea: Settlement participation by state and party of the AG's state, over time, showing which states systematically sit out consumer cases.
harm_angle: If your state's AG never joins, you never get the restitution cheque.
caveat: Participating-AG fields are delimited text lists needing parsing; party fields are the source's own coding.

source_names: EPA air emissions reports|EPA facility registry|EPA ECHO
title: Emissions volume vs enforcement attention
idea: Facility scatter of reported pollutant mass against inspection count and penalties, flagging high-emission facilities never inspected.
harm_angle: The biggest emitters near the most vulnerable people can go years untouched.
caveat: FRS_ID coverage across the three marts is unverified; emissions reporting thresholds vary by program.

source_names: EPA ECHO Exporter|Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
title: Polluter concentration versus local wages
idea: Scatter of county-level noncompliant-facility density against county average weekly wage, testing whether the worst-polluted counties are also the lowest-paid.
harm_angle: Low-wage counties may be absorbing pollution as the price of the only jobs available.
caveat: ECHO is a facility snapshot with no year while QCEW is quarterly; the time alignment is approximate at best.

source_names: EPA ECHO|CDC Injury and Violence County
title: Non-compliant plants in already-hurt counties
idea: County map combining the count of facilities in significant non-compliance with county-level health harm rates, highlighting counties carrying both burdens.
harm_angle: The same counties absorb both unchecked pollution and the worst health outcomes.
caveat: The CDC file measures injury and violence, not pollution-caused illness; correlation is not the mechanism.

source_names: EPA ECHO|CDC county injury and violence|FEC contributions
title: Pollution burden, health burden, political voice
idea: County grid of facility penalty gaps, health outcome rates, and contribution volume per capita, sorted to find high-burden low-voice counties.
harm_angle: The counties least able to fund politics are the ones carrying the most harm.
caveat: Three-way county join needs consistent FIPS; the CDC county mart's measure definitions are unverified.

title: Emissions climb after the last inspection
idea: For facilities with long inspection gaps, chart reported emissions over the years since last inspection. Rising lines during unwatched years is the pattern.
harm_angle: Nobody checks, emissions rise, and the people downwind breathe it.
caveat: Emissions file column names unverified; self-reported emissions may not respond to inspections at all.

title: Air violators and what they actually paid
idea: Distribution of penalty amounts per formal air enforcement action against the facility's high-priority-violator flag. Shows how cheap a serious violation is.
harm_angle: A high-priority violator can settle for less than the cost of fixing the problem.
caveat: Air facility registry identifier to ECHO facility identifier alignment is assumed, not verified.

title: Biggest polluters smallest penalties
idea: Scatter total on-site toxic releases against total EPA penalties per facility on a log scale. The high-release zero-penalty cluster is the enforcement hole.
harm_angle: The neighborhoods eating the most pollution are next to facilities that never pay.
caveat: TRI is a single year while ECHO penalties are cumulative; the ratio needs care.

title: Pollution rolled up to the parent company
idea: Use the corporate crosswalk to roll facility releases and penalties up to the ultimate parent, then rank parents by pounds released per dollar of penalty.
harm_angle: One corporate parent can be the largest polluter in the country while every individual plant looks small.
caveat: Crosswalk carries a confidence score and a review flag; low-confidence matches will distort parent totals.

title: Penalty size vs donor employer
idea: Compare average penalty per violation for facilities whose parent appears as a donor employer versus those that never do.
harm_angle: Tests whether politically connected polluters pay less per violation.
caveat: Confounded by facility size and program; name match only.

title: Subsidized housing next to violators
idea: Map subsidized housing projects within a short radius of facilities in significant non-compliance, sized by number of assisted households.
harm_angle: Families placed in federally subsidized housing are placed next to the plants nobody is enforcing against.
caveat: Geography-only join; radius choice drives the answer and must be disclosed.

source_names: EPA ECHO Exporter|NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database
title: Polluting facilities in flood-struck counties
idea: County map overlaying flood-event frequency with the count of hazardous-waste facilities, highlighting counties where floods repeatedly hit facilities holding toxics.
harm_angle: Floodwater running through a hazardous-waste site carries contamination into people's homes.
caveat: Storm events use a zone FIPS that is sometimes a forecast zone not a county; the ECHO fips format must be reconciled first.

title: Who owns the polluters
idea: Chain facilities to parent companies to public filers via the crosswalk, then to institutional holders. Network of the biggest asset managers behind the worst penalty gaps.
harm_angle: The pollution people live next to is owned, in the end, by a handful of institutions.
caveat: Needs a filer-to-security bridge that may not exist in the catalog; crosswalk parent filer id fill rate unverified.

title: Polluters lobbying while in violation
idea: Timeline per company of quarters in noncompliance against lobbying spend on environment issues, matched by company name.
harm_angle: Companies lobby to loosen the rules they are currently breaking.
caveat: Name matching between facility operators and lobbying clients is weak; parents lobby, facilities pollute.

title: Polluters on the federal payroll
idea: Rank facilities in significant noncompliance whose operators also hold federal contracts, sized by contract dollars.
harm_angle: Federal purchasing power rewards the same firms EPA lists as chronic violators.
caveat: Facility-to-contractor name matching is the weak link; there is no shared entity id.

title: Polluters on the federal payroll
idea: Chain facilities to parent companies to federal contract recipients via the crosswalk's unique entity identifier, then plot contract dollars against penalty gap per company.
harm_angle: Taxpayers pay companies that are simultaneously escaping penalties for poisoning neighborhoods.
caveat: Crosswalk identifier fill rate unverified; a company can have many identifiers.

title: Control Equipment Versus Actual Emissions
idea: Scatter of a plant's reported emission rate against whether its boilers report existing sulfur and nitrogen controls, testing whether installed controls actually show up in the emissions.
harm_angle: Controls that exist on paper but do not lower the measured rate mean a community got a promise instead of clean air.
caveat: Join relies on the eGRID ORIS code matching EIA plant_code, which is likely but unverified; the two sources are also different report years.

title: Violators On The Full Facility Map
idea: Map of all regulated facilities with current high-priority-violator sites highlighted, showing violation density against the full industrial backdrop.
harm_angle: Seeing violators against the total facility field shows whether a neighborhood is unlucky or systematically targeted.
caveat: registry_id population in the ICIS air table is unverified and FRS lat/lon coverage is unknown.

title: Climate Emitters In The Regulated Universe
idea: Map joining greenhouse gas reporters to the full FRS facility register, showing what share of the biggest emitters also carry other environmental program obligations.
harm_angle: A major climate emitter with thin other oversight is a site nobody is checking on any other axis.
caveat: GHGRP frs_id may be blank or masked on many rows -- classic false-populated-key risk, so count distinct values first.

title: Inspections That Lead Nowhere
idea: Flow diagram from compliance evaluations through to formal actions with penalties, showing how much of the inspection funnel evaporates before any consequence.
harm_angle: The width of the drop-off between inspection and penalty is the exact measure of how safe it is to pollute.
caveat: Both tables carry activity_id, but whether the same id actually links an evaluation to its resulting action is unverified.

title: Air violations found without inspection
idea: Timeline of air violations against federal inspections in the same state-year, showing whether violations are found by looking or only self-reported.
harm_angle: Violations only ever self-reported means the true violation count is unknown.
caveat: Overlap of the program system id between the air and cross-program inspection tables is unverified.

title: Cases opened versus cases concluded
idea: Flow diagram from case facilities named to case facilities in concluded enforcement, showing attrition between accusation and resolution.
harm_angle: Facilities that appear in a case but never in a conclusion are the ones that walked.
caveat: Neither table has a date, so this is a static snapshot; the conclusion table may simply be incomplete rather than showing real attrition.

title: Inspections that lead nowhere
idea: Scatter of inspections per permit against penalty dollars collected per permit, isolating heavily inspected permits that never pay.
harm_angle: Permits inspected constantly and never fined show enforcement that stops before it bites.
caveat: NPDES_ID is a permit not a company; penalty nulls versus zeros must be resolved.

title: Chronic noncompliance mapped
idea: Point map of discharge facilities colored by how many quarters they spent in significant noncompliance.
harm_angle: Puts chronic water violators on a map next to the neighborhoods downstream.
caveat: Coordinate population unverified; the noncompliance code meaning needs confirmation.

source_names: NPDES Quarterly Noncompliance History|NPDES Formal Enforcement
title: Quarters in noncompliance before anyone acts
idea: For each facility, count consecutive noncompliant quarters before the first formal enforcement action. The distribution of that lag is the tolerance the agency shows.
harm_angle: Communities live with years of illegal discharge before anything formal happens.
caveat: Quarterly file column names unverified; facilities that never get an action create censored data.

title: Which industries never comply
idea: Ranked bars of industry sectors by the share of permit-quarters spent in significant noncompliance.
harm_angle: Identifies whole sectors that operate outside their permits as normal practice.
caveat: Permits carry multiple industry codes; the primary indicator flag must be used or sectors double-count.

title: Inspection coverage of large generators
idea: Map of large-quantity waste generators colored by years since last evaluation, showing the biggest unwatched sites.
harm_angle: The largest generators going uninspected is the highest-consequence oversight gap in hazardous waste.
caveat: Handler ids may need the activity-location suffix to join correctly; coordinates may be sparse.

title: Violations that never draw a penalty
idea: Dot plot of handlers by violation count against total penalty dollars, isolating high-violation zero-penalty handlers.
harm_angle: Handlers with dozens of violations and no fine reveal a regulator that never escalates.
caveat: Join needs handler id plus activity location; penalty amounts are text casts.

title: Lead exposure mapped to places
idea: Map of counties and zips shaded by the worst lead sample from any system serving them.
harm_angle: Turns an abstract system id into the actual streets where the lead is.
caveat: Sample measure is uncast; a system serves many zips so attribution is approximate.

source_names: SDWA Lead and Copper Samples|SDWA Geographic Areas
title: Lead sample results mapped to zip
idea: Map the highest lead sample results per water system to the zips it serves, with an action-level threshold line.
harm_angle: Households in specific zips are drinking lead at levels above the action threshold.
caveat: Sample grain is per-sample not per-system percentile; units may be mixed and need normalizing.

title: Lead in water and 1930s redlining grades
