idea: Overlay lead sample results on historic redlining polygons and compare distributions by grade. Tests whether the worst-graded neighborhoods still get the worst water.
harm_angle: The neighborhoods redlined ninety years ago are still the ones drinking the worst water.
caveat: Water systems are large and rarely align to neighborhood polygons; the geographic assignment is coarse.

title: Do site visits prevent violations
idea: Slope chart of violation rate before and after a sanitary survey per system, testing whether inspections actually work.
harm_angle: If inspections do not reduce violations, the whole oversight ritual needs rebuilding.
caveat: Confounded by the fact that troubled systems get inspected more; needs careful framing.

title: Violations weighted by people served
idea: Ranked bars of water systems by health-based violations multiplied by population served, ranking harm by headcount.
harm_angle: Ranks by how many actual humans drank the bad water, not by how many systems misbehaved.
caveat: Population counts may be stale; snapshot duplication must be resolved first.

source_names: SDWA Violations and Enforcement|SDWA Public Water Systems
title: People drinking water in violation
idea: Aggregate health-based drinking water violations weighted by the population each system serves, ranked by state. The unit is people, not systems.
harm_angle: Millions of people drink from systems in ongoing health-based violation.
caveat: Overlapping violation periods can double count; population served reliability unverified.

title: Schools and daycares on bad water
idea: Filter to systems flagged as serving a school or daycare and chart their health-based violation rate against all other systems.
harm_angle: Children drink from water systems that fail health standards at their own school.
caveat: The school and daycare flag fill rate is unverified and may be mostly blank.

title: Active Facilities on Superfund Ground
idea: Match Superfund sites to registry facilities by site identifier or address and map where currently-regulated operations sit on or beside a contaminated site.
harm_angle: Running a permitted operation on top of a contaminated site compounds exposure for the same neighborhood twice.
caveat: No shared id is confirmed between the two tables — the join may have to be fuzzy on address, which is unreliable at this scale.

source_names: Superfund site boundaries|HUD subsidized housing|EPA ECHO
title: Subsidized housing inside Superfund footprints
idea: Map subsidized housing developments falling within or adjacent to Superfund site boundaries, with resident counts.
harm_angle: Families placed by a federal program onto federally recognized contaminated land.
caveat: Only 2114 boundary features; spatial containment join with no shared id and unverified geometry columns.

title: Corporate release footprint map
idea: Map of all facilities owned by one parent company sized by 2023 releases, drawing a single corporation's national pollution footprint.
harm_angle: Shows one company's total harm across every community it operates in, at once.
caveat: Join is the toxic-release facility id on both sides; parent name standardization coverage unverified.

source_names: FracFocus chemical disclosures|USGS water data|FEC contributions
title: Fracking chemicals near monitored water
idea: Map fracking disclosure sites against nearby water monitoring stations showing contaminant readings, with operator political giving as a side panel.
harm_angle: Households on well water living downgradient of undisclosed chemical injection.
caveat: Spatial proximity join, not an id join; FracFocus and USGS marts have unverified geometry columns.

source_names: National Inventory of Dams|NOAA Storm Events
title: Poor-condition dams in flood-frequent counties
idea: County map of flood event frequency with poor-condition high-hazard dams overlaid as points.
harm_angle: The dams most likely to fail are in the counties that flood most.
caveat: Dam mart column names unverified; condition assessment is often blank or withheld.

title: Lobbying spend vs the penalty gap
idea: For heavily lobbying parent companies, plot total EPA penalties against inspection counts and the ECHO penalty-gap flag at their facilities.
harm_angle: Communities near the least-penalized facilities are disproportionately nonwhite.
caveat: ECHO facility names are site names, not corporate parents; the name join needs an ownership layer that may not exist.

source_names: USCG National Response Center Incidents|EPA ECHO
title: Spill reports at facilities with clean records
idea: Map reported spill and release incidents against facilities that show no enforcement history, flagging facilities that keep spilling and never get cited.
harm_angle: Repeated spills into a community can leave no trace in the enforcement record.
caveat: The incident mart shows almost no aliased columns; field names unverified. Company name matching required.

title: Spill callers matched to corporate parents
idea: Fuzzy-match NRC responsible-company names to the crosswalk's facility and legal names, then rank release counts by ultimate parent instead of by local subsidiary.
harm_angle: Counting spills per parent instead of per subsidiary is what turns a scatter of small incidents into one company's pattern.
caveat: Name-only fuzzy matching with no shared id; false matches would attribute spills to the wrong company, so this needs manual verification before publication.

title: Orphaned wells near unwatched water
idea: Spatially pair orphaned wells with the nearest water-quality station and map the well clusters that sit far from any monitoring point.
harm_angle: Households drinking groundwater near unplugged wells with no nearby monitoring have no way to find out what is in their water.
caveat: Requires spatial proximity computation, not an id join; both lat/long sets are parsed from text and may be sparse.

title: Watersheds with no eyes on them
idea: Join monitoring stations to the HUC-8 watershed index and map every subbasin with zero stations, sized by watershed area and states touched.
harm_angle: A large multi-state watershed with no monitoring station is a place where contamination cannot be proven no matter who gets sick.
caveat: Station extract may be partial (5,818 rows) so zero-station watersheds could be an artefact of the pull, not reality.

source_names: Global Witness land defenders|Federal assistance|Ecuador procurement
title: Killings near extractive projects
idea: Map killings of land and environmental defenders against the locations of internationally funded extractive and infrastructure projects.
harm_angle: People die defending land while the projects behind the pressure draw public financing.
caveat: Only 232 defender records; project geolocation is not present in the funding marts.

title: Prop 65 chemicals released by facility
idea: Filter toxic-release reports to chemicals on the California cancer and reproductive-harm list, then map facilities by pounds released of listed chemicals.
harm_angle: Communities live next to plants releasing chemicals a state has formally declared cause cancer.
caveat: Prop 65 file column names unverified; CAS formatting differs across sources.

title: Known-carcinogen fracking additives
idea: Rank operators by number of wells disclosing an additive whose chemical identifier is on the cancer list, mapped to well locations.
harm_angle: People drinking well water near these sites are exposed to chemicals formally listed as carcinogens.
caveat: FracFocus mart is a passthrough; column names and trade-secret withholding rate unverified.

title: Listed companies behind the facilities
idea: Join the crosswalk's parent CIK to the ticker map and chart facility counts per publicly traded company, naming tickers investors can actually look up.
harm_angle: Ties a named tradeable company to a specific count of polluting facilities, which is the form the harm has to take to reach shareholders.
caveat: parent_cik is untyped text in the crosswalk versus a number in the ticker model; formatting and leading zeros will break the join.

title: Pollution rolled up the ownership chain
idea: Take EPA facility-to-parent matches and walk them up the GLEIF ownership graph, charting facility counts under each ultimate global parent.
harm_angle: The true owner of a cluster of polluting facilities is often several layers above the entity named on the permit.
caveat: Two match layers stacked means errors compound; low-confidence crosswalk rows must be excluded first.

title: Emissions versus grid mix
idea: Join by ISO code and year and scatter fossil share against annual emissions, revealing countries with clean grids but high total emissions from other sectors.
harm_angle: Identifies countries whose emissions come from sectors no energy policy is touching.
caveat: Both tables mix aggregates with countries; must filter on valid ISO3 in both before joining.

source_names: EPA drinking water violations|HUD public housing authorities
title: Bad water at public housing
idea: Water systems with health-based violations serving counties with large public housing stock, ranked by affected units.
join_key: county FIPS via SDWA service areas
harm_angle: Children in public housing may be drinking water the government already flagged as unsafe.
caveat: Water system id to county requires the SDWA geographic-areas bridge; service areas do not map cleanly to housing sites.

title: Subsidized housing on contaminated ground
idea: Assisted housing projects within Superfund site counties, ranked by units and by NPL status of the nearby site.
harm_angle: Children in subsidized housing may be growing up on the country's worst ground.
caveat: County-grain co-location is not proximity; project coordinate quality is unverified.

source_names: USGS orphaned oil and gas wells|Vera Incarceration Trends
title: Abandoned wells in abandoned counties
idea: County counts of orphaned wells against incarceration and urbanicity measures, mapping the places industry left behind.
harm_angle: The counties left holding the cleanup bill are the same ones filling the jails.
caveat: Correlational with no mechanism; well-to-county assignment may need geocoding.

title: Prime Keeps What Share
idea: Join prime contract obligations to reported subawards and plot the share passed down per prime.
chart_shape: scatter of prime value against pass-through share
harm_angle: Every dollar a prime keeps for coordination is a dollar not spent on the delivered service.
caveat: The subaward mart is a 5,000-row sample and its prime key may only exist inside a raw JSON blob.

title: Grants In Contracts Out
idea: For each county, compare inbound assistance dollars against outbound contract dollars earned by local firms. Viewer sees counties that receive help versus counties that get paid.
harm_angle: Places that only ever receive assistance and never win contracts are held in permanent dependence.
caveat: Both are 20M-row tables; FIPS text columns may have lost leading zeros.

title: Bad Audits Still Getting Money
idea: Join audited entities with material weakness findings to their subsequent federal assistance awards. Viewer sees organizations that kept receiving grants after failing their audits.
chart_shape: cohort grid of finding year against subsequent award dollars
harm_angle: Grantees that failed their audit and kept the money are why services in poor communities stay broken.
caveat: UEI population in the audit file is unverified; EIN is a known masking trap on this platform.

source_names: FATCA FFI List|ICIJ Offshore Leaks Entities
title: Reporting Banks in Leaked Jurisdictions
idea: Overlay registered financial-institution counts per country with offshore entity counts per jurisdiction, showing which places host both the formal reporting institutions and the hidden vehicles.
harm_angle: A jurisdiction hosting both the reporting bank and the shell it reports for is where the compliance regime eats its own tail.
caveat: Country name to jurisdiction code mapping is not present in either table and must be built by hand.

title: Housing Bank Members Versus Branch Presence
idea: Join housing-bank membership to bank branch data by FDIC cert to see whether banks drawing federal housing liquidity actually maintain branches in the communities they claim to serve.
harm_angle: Banks taking cheap federal housing money while closing branches in the same counties are taking subsidy without service.
caveat: The membership cert column may be blank for non-bank members; district-to-county mapping needed.

title: Which Credit Unions Got Absorbed
idea: Dot plot of merged-away credit unions positioned by their pre-merger assets and member count from the insured list, showing the profile of what gets swallowed.
harm_angle: If the credit unions being absorbed are disproportionately low-income-designated, consolidation is stripping poverty-serving lenders specifically.
caveat: Only 27 merger rows and the insured list is a snapshot, so merged institutions may already be absent from it.

title: Banks And Thrifts Side By Side
idea: Map comparing the state footprint of national banks against thrifts, showing states where one form of chartered lender has effectively vanished.
harm_angle: A state with no thrifts and few national banks is a state whose residents borrow from out-of-state institutions with no local branch to answer to.
caveat: Both are small undated snapshots and charter numbers are namespaced separately, so they must be kept distinct rather than merged.

title: Auditor Concentration By Industry
idea: Heatmap grid of audit firm against filer industry code, built by joining audit filings to financial-statement filers on the company id.
harm_angle: If one audit firm checks nearly every company in an industry, an industry-wide accounting practice never gets challenged.
caveat: CIK formatting differs between sources (zero padding) and the DERA slice is only one quarter, so coverage will be partial.

source_names: PCAOB Form AP audit partner filings|SEC financials
title: Audit partners with a pattern
idea: Network of audit partners to the issuers they signed, sized by later restatements or going-concern flags.
harm_angle: A single partner's leniency can leave thousands of investors and pensioners exposed.
caveat: PCAOB mart columns unverified; the restatement signal (prevrpt) meaning needs confirming.

title: Filer Names Attached To Company Ids
idea: Ranked bars linking filing manager names to their regulator company ids, producing the roster that makes every other institutional-ownership chart nameable.
harm_angle: Without a name-to-id bridge, institutional ownership is unreadable to the public it affects.
caveat: Assumes the filing id is populated and identically formatted in both tables; unverified.

title: Portfolio Turnover Per Manager
idea: Join positions to submission metadata by accession number and plot each manager's quarter-over-quarter position changes as a slope chart, separating churners from long holders.
harm_angle: Managers churning through companies every quarter make decisions that close plants and cut jobs on a three-month horizon.
caveat: The singular submission mart appears to duplicate the positions columns; the plural submissions model holds the filer and period fields — confirm which is live before joining. 202M position rows makes this expensive to run.

title: Manager Portfolios Over Time
idea: Timeline of each manager's total disclosed position value and issuer count per quarter, built by joining submissions to holdings on the filing id.
harm_angle: Tracking who is accumulating stakes in hospital chains, landlords, and utilities shows who is about to control services people cannot opt out of.
caveat: Holdings is a 101-million-row view so this is compute-heavy; value scale conventions changed over time and must be normalized.

title: Filers who stopped filing
idea: Stack the six quarterly submission tables into one panel and chart CIKs that appear in early quarters and vanish from later ones, by industry.
harm_angle: A company that quietly stops filing has usually gone private, been acquired or collapsed, and its workers and creditors find out last.
caveat: Only about six quarters of coverage, so a gap may be a normal non-filing period rather than an exit; form type must be controlled for.

title: Filers who are not listed anywhere
idea: Join quarterly filers to the ticker map and chart the filers with no ticker at all, by industry, isolating the reporting companies with no public market.
harm_angle: Companies that report but do not trade are often debt issuers whose bondholders include pension funds ordinary people depend on.
caveat: CIK is a number in the ticker staging model but untyped in the DERA marts; type mismatch will silently drop joins.

source_names: SEC ticker map|SEC financial statement data
title: Ticker to CIK to EIN bridge coverage
idea: Show how many public filers can actually be linked to a tax id, by year, as a data-availability map underpinning every other cross-source idea.
harm_angle: Nothing gets held accountable across datasets if the id bridge is empty.
caveat: This is a coverage diagnostic; EIN population in the DERA sub files is exactly the thing being tested.

title: Cash funds inside the fund complexes
idea: Join the money-market fund list to the full series/class registry on CIK and series id, and chart what share of each complex's classes are cash funds.
harm_angle: Complexes heavily weighted to money-market cash carry the run risk that hits savers first in a liquidity squeeze.
caveat: cik_number is trimmed text while registrant_cik is untyped; formats may not match without normalisation.

title: Trading venues that hide their owner
idea: Join market identifier codes to the LEI reporting-exception file and chart the venues whose operating entity claims an exception rather than naming a parent.
harm_angle: A trading venue whose ultimate owner is legally undisclosed is market infrastructure with no visible accountable person.
caveat: LEI fill rate in the MIC registry is unverified and may be low enough to make the joined set tiny.

title: Dealer Density Against Neighborhood Wealth
idea: Overlay FFL premise locations onto census tracts characterized by minority_population and tract income from HMDA. Viewer sees gun dealer concentration relative to neighborhood demographics.
harm_angle: Dealer density in poor and minority tracts is the front end of the local gun-violence pipeline.
caveat: Joining a point layer to HMDA tracts requires a geographic crosswalk that is not in either source; HMDA is 2015-2017 only.

title: Aid dollars against hunger severity
idea: Country timeline of food-insecure population against US food aid obligations, showing whether money follows need or politics.
harm_angle: People starve in countries that get little aid while better-connected countries get more.
caveat: Country naming differences; aid sector coding must be filtered to food and may be inconsistent.

title: Foreign interest in specific bills
idea: Timeline of active foreign-principal registrations by country against the introduction dates of bills naming that country.
harm_angle: Legislation about a country may be shaped by paid representatives of it.
caveat: Requires text search of bill titles; FARA country column presence unverified.

title: Same firm, two disclosure regimes
idea: Identify shops registered under both FARA and the Lobbying Disclosure Act and compare their declared foreign-principal work against their domestic lobbying income.
harm_angle: Firms can route a foreign client's ask through the weaker disclosure channel.
caveat: Both sides name-only; the FARA mart's client and principal columns are unverified.

title: Aid, repression, and paid representation
idea: Country grid of US assistance received, democracy score trajectory, and the number of registered US foreign agents working for that government.
harm_angle: Governments hiring US representation while their own citizens lose rights, on the US dime.
caveat: The FARA mart's country and principal fields are unverified; country naming differs across sources.

source_names: County geography|EPA drinking water violations|Vera Incarceration Trends
title: Bad water, heavy jails
idea: County-level drinking-water health violations against incarceration rate and race composition.
harm_angle: The same communities absorb unsafe water and disproportionate policing.
caveat: SDWA violations key on public water system id, not county - the bridge is the SDWA geographic-areas table and may be lossy.

source_names: County geography dimension|HRSA shortage areas|FEMA IA registrations
title: Doctor desert plus disaster
idea: Counties that are both medical shortage areas and repeat disaster-aid counties, ranked by combined exposure.
harm_angle: When the storm hits a county with no doctors, the injury count becomes a death count.
caveat: HPSA designations are sub-county; FEMA load is partial so repeat-county counts will be understated.

source_names: County geography dimension|Vera Incarceration Trends|CDC WONDER mortality
title: One county, three burdens
idea: A county grid combining incarceration rate, mortality rate and a third stressor, with counties ranked by how many burdens they sit in the worst decile of.
harm_angle: Finds the places where every measurable form of state failure lands on the same people.
caveat: CDC WONDER mart looks state/national grain, not county - the third axis may not exist at county level.

title: Correctional infrastructure map
idea: Correctional and law-enforcement facilities from the infrastructure layer, mapped against county jail capacity and rated-capacity utilisation.
chart_shape: point map with county choropleth beneath
harm_angle: Shows overcrowding as a physical fact you can point at.
caveat: HIFLD mart is a 500-row sample; layer coverage for corrections is unverified.

source_names: County geography dimension|QCEW employment and wages|Vera Incarceration Trends
title: Where the jail is the biggest employer
idea: County employment by industry against jail population, flagging counties where corrections employment is a top share of local jobs.
harm_angle: Communities that economically depend on caging people have a reason to keep the beds full.
caveat: QCEW mart exposes mostly code columns in the model; employment and wage measures may not be modeled.

source_names: State dimension|VA veteran suicide by state|Vera Incarceration Trends
title: Veteran suicide and state punishment
idea: State veteran suicide rates against state incarceration rates and the general-population suicide rate, over time.
harm_angle: Two forms of state abandonment of the same men, side by side.
caveat: Association only; state-level aggregation hides the veterans actually incarcerated.

title: Corruption and freedom together
idea: Join by country and year and plot the corruption index against the freedom total score, marking countries that diverge -- clean-scoring autocracies and corrupt democracies.
harm_angle: Divergent countries are where one accountability mechanism has failed while the other still looks intact.
caveat: The Freedom House country column is nulled by a number cast; edition-to-year alignment also needs checking.

source_names: Federal Register documents|DOJ Civil Rights cases
title: Rulemaking and enforcement out of step
idea: Volume of civil-rights-related rulemaking over time against actual case filings, by administration.
harm_angle: Announcing a rule is cheap; enforcing it is what changes whether anyone is protected.
caveat: Federal Register mart exposes little beyond docket in the model; topic classification is inferred from text.

title: Rule changes and payout changes
idea: Timeline of FEMA rule and notice publications against changes in award rates and average award sizes in the following months.
harm_angle: A quiet rule change can cut thousands of families off without any announcement.
caveat: Federal Register mart exposes little in the model; attributing award changes to a rule needs careful controls.

title: Former members now on the payroll
idea: Count departed members of Congress whose names appear as lobbyists, by year left and party, showing the pipeline volume.
harm_angle: Public service converting into private access at a measurable rate.
caveat: Name matching on packed lobbyist name strings; nicknames and middle initials will cause misses.

title: Ideology versus district reality
idea: Join the member spine to DW-NOMINATE by ICPSR and plot each member's ideology against their state and district over time, surfacing members far from their own constituency.
harm_angle: Members who vote far from their district leave those constituents unrepresented on every bill.
caveat: ICPSR fill rate in the legislators file is unverified and may be blank for many historical members.

title: Broadcast owners' political giving
idea: Map broadcast and spectrum licenses by owner against those owners' political contribution totals, by state.
harm_angle: The companies controlling local information also fund the officials regulating them.
caveat: FCC ULS EIN was previously found masked on this platform; owner names need heavy normalization.

title: Rule, contract, lobbyist: one docket
idea: For a chosen docket, a single timeline of the rulemaking steps, the lobbying filings naming the agency, and the contracts awarded under the resulting program.
harm_angle: Lets a reader follow one decision from the pressure to the money to the outcome.
caveat: Docket numbers do not appear in the lobbying or contract marts, so two of the three hops are agency-name based.

title: Chairs who bury their own issues
idea: Join bills to sponsors' committee seats by bioguide and show whether members who chair a committee actually pass bills in that committee's subject area.
harm_angle: Chairs sitting on issues in their own jurisdiction are the single biggest chokepoint on relief legislation.
caveat: Committee membership is a current snapshot with no congress column, so historical bills cannot be matched to the right-era committee.

title: From agency chair to lobby registrant
idea: Match tracked officials to lobbyist names appearing in lobbying filings after their government service, with the time gap between the two.
harm_angle: The cooling-off period exists on paper; this measures how short it actually is.
caveat: lobbyist_names is a packed text field needing parsing; only 406 people on the tracker side.

title: Appointees and their former employers' contracts
idea: For each tracked appointee, timeline of their former employer's federal contract dollars before, during, and after their tenure.
harm_angle: Agencies staffed by the industry they buy from, with the invoices to show it.
caveat: Only 406 tracked people; prior-employer field presence unverified in the mart.

title: Lobbying before the rule drops
idea: For each agency, plot lobbying filings naming that agency by quarter against the count of rules it published and their average comment window length.
harm_angle: Short comment windows on heavily lobbied rules mean the public never gets a real say.
caveat: Agency naming differs between the two sources; comment_window_days is derived and may be null for most documents.

title: Agencies that spend vs agencies that rule
idea: Compare each agency's obligation volume against its rulemaking output, flagging big spenders with almost no public rule activity.
harm_angle: Money moving through agencies that the public has no rulemaking window into.
caveat: Agency naming conventions differ; the Federal Register agency field may hold sub-agencies.

title: The most-lobbied votes in Congress
idea: Rank roll-call votes by the volume of lobbying filings naming the underlying bill, showing where outside pressure concentrated.
harm_angle: Identifies the exact decisions industry paid hardest to shape.
caveat: specific_issues is free text; matching it to a roll-call requires bill-number extraction that may fail often.

title: Absence on the votes that mattered
idea: Join the member-by-vote matrix to roll-call metadata and show missed-vote rates specifically on the closest-margin votes.
harm_angle: Skipping a one-vote-margin roll call is the most consequential absence a member can take.
caveat: Composite join key across three columns; metadata covers only 3364 roll calls versus 945k vote rows, so coverage may be partial.

title: Aid, arms, and conflict deaths
idea: Per recipient country, timeline of US security assistance and the country's own military spending against conflict fatalities.
harm_angle: Money labeled as help arriving alongside the violence it was meant to prevent.
caveat: Country naming differs across all three; assistance category filtering is needed to isolate security aid.

title: Court versus Congress divergence
idea: Overlay the JCS institutional medians with the DW-NOMINATE congressional medians on one timeline to show the years the court sat furthest from the elected branches.
harm_angle: The widest divergence years are when rights were decided against what voters had just chosen.
caveat: Two different scalings of the same nominal common space; comparability is an assumption, not a fact.

source_names: DOJ Epstein Library manifest|Wayback captures of the DOJ listing
title: What quietly disappeared
idea: Timeline of files appearing and vanishing from the public DOJ index, comparing each monthly manifest with archived captures.
chart_shape: timeline with appearance and disappearance markers
harm_angle: Records removed without notice are how accountability gets undone in the dark.
caveat: Requires exact URL normalization; a missing file may reflect site restructuring rather than removal.

title: Dealers near subsidized housing
idea: Gun-dealer premises and subsidized housing projects mapped in the same cities, with counts within short distances.
harm_angle: Concentrating both the guns and the poorest tenants in the same blocks is a policy outcome.
caveat: ZIP-level proximity is crude; many licensees are home-based collectors, not storefronts.

source_names: CDC Anxiety and Depression Indicators|HRSA Shortage Areas
title: Mental distress against mental health shortage
idea: State timeline of reported anxiety and depression against the count of mental-health shortage designations, testing whether designations respond to need.
harm_angle: Need rises and the designation that unlocks help does not follow.
caveat: The survey indicator is self-reported and pandemic-era heavy; designations are slow-moving by design.

source_names: NCHS Drug Poisoning by County|Vera Incarceration Trends
title: Overdose deaths and jail admissions
idea: County scatter of overdose death rate against jail admission rate for drug offenses, over time. Tests whether punishment substitutes for treatment.
harm_angle: Counties answer an overdose crisis with jail cells instead of care, and people keep dying.
caveat: Incarceration column names unverified; banded death rates limit the analysis.

source_names: CDC health insurance coverage|CDC anxiety and depression
title: Coverage loss and distress together
idea: Join the two Household Pulse indicator tables by state, subgroup and time period and plot uninsured rate against distress rate.
harm_angle: Groups losing coverage and reporting rising distress at the same time are the ones with nowhere to go for help.
caveat: Same survey so the join should be clean, but suppression and wide CIs on small subgroups can manufacture apparent correlation.

source_names: CDC Health Insurance Indicators|CFPB Consumer Complaints
title: Uninsurance and medical debt complaints
idea: State scatter of uninsured rate against medical-debt complaint rate per capita, over time.
harm_angle: Losing coverage shows up months later as collections.
caveat: Complaint volume reflects who knows to complain, which biases toward better-off states.

source_names: CDC Injury and Violence County|WaPo Fatal Force
title: Police killings against county injury burden
idea: County map of police-killing rate against overall violent injury rate, highlighting counties where one is high and the other is not.
harm_angle: In some counties police violence is a large share of all violent death, and nobody counts it that way.
caveat: Fatal Force has county name and state not FIPS; mapping is a text join.

source_names: CDC NNDSS Weekly|CMS Nursing Home Infection Control Deficiencies
title: Infection control citations and disease weeks
idea: State timeline of infection-control deficiency citations against reportable disease counts, testing whether citation waves follow outbreak waves or precede them.
harm_angle: Homes get cited only after residents are already sick.
caveat: Survey scheduling drives citation timing more than outbreaks do; confounded.

title: Waterborne disease weeks after water violations
idea: State-week timeline of reportable waterborne illness counts against drinking-water violation onsets, with a lag window shaded.
harm_angle: People get sick in the weeks after a water system fails, and the two records are never read together.
caveat: Disease file column names unverified; state-week grain is too coarse to attribute any single outbreak.

source_names: CDC Provisional Overdose Deaths|MEDSL Presidential Returns
title: Overdose deaths and vote swing
idea: State-level scatter of change in overdose death rate against change in presidential vote share between cycles.
harm_angle: Communities losing people to overdose are also the ones whose politics shifted hardest.
caveat: State grain hides everything that matters; this is descriptive, not causal.

source_names: CFPB Consumer Complaints|CMS Hospital General Information
title: Medical debt complaints near which hospitals
idea: Map medical-debt-tagged consumer complaints by zip against hospital ownership type in that zip. For-profit clusters would be the story.
harm_angle: Patients in some hospital markets end up in collections far more often.
caveat: Consumer complaint zip is truncated in the public file; tagging complaints as medical debt is a judgment call.

title: Trial investigators on the sponsor's payroll
idea: For each sponsor, the share of its trial investigators who also received payments from it, and the size of those payments.
harm_angle: The evidence base doctors rely on produced by people the maker pays.
caveat: The ClinicalTrials mart is 500 rows here and NPI on investigators is likely sparse.

title: Retracted science behind approved products
idea: Match trial publications to retraction records and time the retraction against the product's approval and marketing dates.
harm_angle: Treatments stay on the market after the evidence behind them is withdrawn.
caveat: Title-based matching is unreliable; both marts have unverified columns.

source_names: CMS Dialysis Facility Listing|Medicare Dialysis Facilities
title: Dialysis chains and patient outcomes
idea: Rank dialysis chains by facility-level outcome measures per patient treated, showing the spread between the best and worst corporate operators.
harm_angle: Kidney patients cannot choose their clinic, and the chain they land in changes their odds.
caveat: Second file's column names unverified; its 12.4M row count suggests a claims-level grain, not facility.

title: Two companies, most of the dialysis chairs
idea: Map dialysis facilities by chain ownership with quality measures, alongside the institutional holders of the two dominant public operators.
harm_angle: A duopoly decides where kidney patients can get treatment and how good it is.
caveat: Chain-ownership field presence in the dialysis mart is unverified; the ticker link is name-based.

title: Excluded clinicians still affiliated
idea: Ranked bars of facilities by how many of their affiliated providers appear on the federal exclusion list.
harm_angle: An excluded clinician still on a facility's roster is treating patients who believe the federal ban list protects them.
caveat: LEIE NPI is sparsely populated so this undercounts badly; affiliation data may be stale.

source_names: Nursing home MDS measures|Nursing home penalties|Federal assistance
title: Resident condition vs fines vs funding
idea: Facility grid pairing resident clinical measures with fine history and federal dollars, sorted to surface well-funded but repeatedly fined homes.
harm_angle: Residents' measured decline sitting next to money and penalties that changed nothing.
caveat: The 31M-row MDS mart's grain is unverified; the assistance join is name-based on the last hop.

title: Charity care versus star rating
idea: Scatter of a hospital's charity care spend against its overall star rating coloured by ownership to see whether hospitals that give least also rate worst.
harm_angle: A hospital that neither gives charity care nor delivers quality is extracting from its community in both directions.
caveat: HCRIS fiscal years will not align with the Care Compare snapshot date.

source_names: Hospital cost reports|SEC 13F holdings|CMS hospital directory
title: For-profit hospital margins vs quality
idea: Scatter hospital operating margin against quality star rating, colored by ownership type and institutional investor presence.
harm_angle: Patients in the highest-margin hospitals may be getting the lowest-rated care.
caveat: HCRIS is hospital-only and 6103 rows; linking hospital systems to tickers is name-based.

source_names: CMS Home Health Agencies|CMS Home Health Enrollments
title: New agencies clustering where oversight is thin
idea: Map new home-health agency enrollments per year by county against the quality ratings of existing agencies there.
harm_angle: Fly-by-night agencies open where nobody is checking, and homebound patients get whoever shows up.
caveat: Enrollment date field unverified; quality rating column names unverified.

source_names: CMS hospice directory|CMS home health directory|SAM.gov exclusions
title: Excluded operators in home-based care
idea: Map hospice and home health agencies whose owners appear on the federal exclusion list, ranked by patient volume.
join_key: NPI (the exclusions mart carries an NPI column)
harm_angle: The most vulnerable patients, at home and dying, cared for by barred operators.
caveat: NPI population in the SAM exclusions mart is unverified and likely sparse.

source_names: CMS Hospice General Information|CMS Hospice Enrollments
title: Hospice churn and ownership change
idea: Timeline of hospice enrollments, terminations and ownership changes by state, with quality measures overlaid.
harm_angle: Dying patients are handed between owners chasing the reimbursement.
caveat: Termination and ownership-change fields unverified in the enrollment file.

source_names: CMS Hospital General|Medicare Inpatient Hospitals by Provider
title: Charges payments and quality
idea: Scatter each hospital's average charge markup over Medicare payment against its mortality and safety measure counts.
harm_angle: The hospitals charging the biggest markup are not the ones delivering the best outcomes.
caveat: Inpatient file column names unverified; charge markup is meaningless for insured patients but real for the uninsured.

source_names: CMS Hospital General|CMS Provider of Services
title: Service lines quietly closed
idea: For hospitals, track which service and unit flags disappear between snapshots such as obstetrics, psychiatric units and emergency, mapped by county.
harm_angle: Whole counties lose the ability to deliver a baby or handle a crisis.
caveat: The services file may be a single snapshot, which would make disappearance impossible to compute.

title: Nonprofit hospitals with audit findings
idea: Match hospitals to their auditee tax id and compare hospitals with adverse audit findings against their patient safety and mortality measure counts.
harm_angle: Hospitals that cannot manage their federal money may not be managing their patients either.
caveat: No shared id; hospital name to auditee name matching is fuzzy and audit field names unverified.

source_names: CMS Long-Term Care Hospitals|Inpatient Rehab Facilities|Hospital General
title: Where patients get moved to
idea: Map the co-location of long-term care hospitals and rehab facilities inside or beside acute hospitals, which is the pattern behind hospital-within-hospital billing.
harm_angle: Patients get transferred across a hallway into a separately billed facility.
caveat: Address matching at zip grain will overcount; needs street-level comparison.

title: Dialysis chains in the enrollment spine
idea: Dialysis chain facilities matched to their Medicare enrollment records, showing the corporate control ids behind clinic brands.
harm_angle: Tying clinic brands to control ids is how a chain's full footprint becomes visible to the patients inside it.
caveat: NPI population in the dialysis table unverified; the control id is a numeric cast that may null out.

source_names: Medicare dialysis facility claims|CMS Open Payments|CFPB complaints
title: Dialysis billing, industry money, patient debt
idea: Facility grid of Medicare billing volume, industry payments to affiliated clinicians, and medical-debt complaints in the same ZIPs.
harm_angle: Patients on dialysis carrying debt from care that generated payments everywhere but to them.
caveat: CFPB has no provider id, so the last hop is geographic; the 12M-row dialysis mart's grain is unverified.

source_names: Medicare DME by Referrer|CMS Open Payments
title: Referral volume against industry payments
idea: Scatter each referring provider's equipment referral dollars against payments received from equipment manufacturers.
harm_angle: Patients get equipment they may not need because the referrer is on a payroll.
caveat: Equipment file column names unverified; payment records must be filtered to device makers.

title: Markup against margin
idea: Per hospital, plot charge-to-payment ratio against reported net margin. The high-markup high-margin quadrant is where uninsured patients get billed hardest.
harm_angle: Uninsured patients pay list price at the hospitals that need it least.
caveat: Cost report fiscal years do not align with the claims year; ratios need careful period matching.

title: Ownership versus charge markup
idea: Hospital charge-to-payment ratio grouped by proprietary or nonprofit status and hospital subgroup, testing whether for-profit hospitals mark up harder.
harm_angle: If investor-owned hospitals systematically inflate list prices, the uninsured patient pays for the ownership model.
caveat: CCN join across the two tables unverified; ownership coding unverified.

source_names: CMS Medicare Physicians by Provider|HRSA Shortage Areas
title: Where the doctors actually bill
idea: County choropleth of billing providers per capita against shortage designation, showing designated counties that nonetheless have providers, and undesignated counties that have none.
harm_angle: People in undesignated deserts get no federal shortage help because the designation missed them.
caveat: Billing address is not where care is delivered; provider FIPS field names unverified.

title: What it costs versus what Medicare pays
idea: Slope or scatter comparing the pharmacy acquisition cost of drugs against Part D drug cost per claim to size the markup taxpayers and patients absorb.
harm_angle: The gap between what a pill costs and what the program pays is money that could have been care.
caveat: Part D prescriber table is at prescriber grain with no NDC so this needs the drug-level Part D file to actually join; as written it is only a national-average comparison.

title: Provider churn out of shortage areas
idea: Compare provider enumeration and deactivation counts by zip against shortage designation, as a slope chart of net providers over time in shortage vs non-shortage zips.
harm_angle: Shortage areas get thinner every year while the designation stays static.
caveat: NPPES deactivation field population unverified; NPPES is a snapshot, not history.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Deficiencies|CMS Facility-Level MDS Frequency
title: Antipsychotic use vs abuse citations
idea: Cross each home's MDS clinical measure percentages against its count of abuse and neglect deficiency tags. Small multiples by state show whether chemical-restraint-style measures cluster with abuse findings.
harm_angle: Residents may be sedated instead of staffed, and the citation record would show it.
caveat: MDS item descriptions are free text; identifying the right clinical item is unverified.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Deficiencies|CMS Nursing Home Fire Deficiencies
title: Life-safety failures and health failures together
idea: For each facility plot fire and life-safety citation counts against health citation counts. Facilities failing both axes are the ones where an emergency would be worst.
harm_angle: Residents who cannot self-evacuate live in buildings failing both care and fire standards.
caveat: Survey cycles differ between the two files; counts may not cover the same window.

title: Harm found versus dollars charged
idea: Facility-level scatter of harm-level citation count against total fines, naming the quadrant of homes that harm often and pay nothing.
harm_angle: Homes that repeatedly harm residents and are never meaningfully fined are the clearest picture of enforcement failure in elder care.
caveat: CCN join assumed clean across both tables; fine amounts may be text.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Deficiencies|CMS Nursing Home Penalties
title: Cited but never fined
idea: For every facility, count harm-level deficiencies and total fines, then map facilities with many harm citations and zero dollars of penalty. The empty quadrant is the enforcement gap.
harm_angle: Residents in homes that get cited repeatedly and never pay anything have no lever that forces change.
caveat: Penalty file may be a rolling window while deficiencies go back further; a zero could just mean out-of-window.

title: Citations rolled up to the chain
idea: Deficiency counts aggregated to the affiliation entity behind each facility, ranked, naming the owners with the worst combined records.
harm_angle: Families can look up a home but not its owner; rolling citations up to the owner is what makes a chain accountable.
caveat: affiliation_entity_id population unverified and may be largely blank; CCN formats may differ between the two tables.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Deficiencies|HRSA Health Professional Shortage Areas
title: Bad homes in care deserts
idea: County map shading harm-citation rate for nursing homes, overlaid with shortage-area scores. Counties that are both a shortage area and full of cited homes have no alternative to go to.
harm_angle: Families in shortage counties cannot move a relative out of a bad home because there is nowhere else.
caveat: Deficiency file carries zip not FIPS; zip-to-county crosswalk is an extra hop and imperfect.

title: Harm-level citations by chain owner
idea: Roll deficiency scope and severity codes (the letters that mean actual harm or jeopardy, not paperwork) up to chain owner and rank chains by share of harm-level citations per bed. Reveals which corporate chains systematically produce harm citations.
harm_angle: Residents of specific chains face a measurably higher rate of harm-level violations.
caveat: chain_name is free text and may not resolve cleanly to one owner; scope and severity letter meanings must be mapped correctly.

source_names: Nursing home penalties|Nursing home deficiencies|Federal assistance
title: Fined homes still drawing public money
idea: Per facility, deficiency count and fine total against federal assistance dollars received, ranked by dollars per deficiency.
harm_angle: Homes that repeatedly endanger residents are funded by the same government that fines them.
caveat: Assistance data has no CCN, so the last hop is name-based; ownership chains obscure the real recipient.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Penalties|CMS SNF Enrollments
title: Fines follow the owner not the building
idea: Link penalties to the enrollment record's owning organization and NPI, then draw a network of owners to facilities sized by fines. Shows owners whose whole portfolio is penalized versus one bad building.
harm_angle: Chain owners can absorb single-facility fines while every one of their homes underperforms.
caveat: Enrollment file owner fields are unconfirmed; the NPI-to-owner mapping may be facility-level only.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Penalties|FEC Independent Expenditures
title: Nursing home money into elections
idea: Match nursing home chain owners to political spenders by name and chart penalty totals against political spend by cycle.
harm_angle: Chains fined for harming residents fund the politics that sets the rules.
caveat: Pure name matching; chain owner names rarely match committee names directly.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Penalties|NursingHome411 State-Level Nursing Home Data
title: Fines vs staffing at nursing homes
idea: Plot each nursing home's total fine dollars against its reported total nurse staffing hours per resident per day, colored by chain. Shows whether the thinnest-staffed homes are the ones being fined, or whether fines land somewhere else entirely.
harm_angle: Residents in chronically understaffed homes absorb the harm while the penalty system may be aimed elsewhere.
caveat: Penalty file grain is one row per fine, needs aggregation to CCN; staffing snapshot date may not align with penalty dates.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Penalties|USASpending Federal Contracts
title: Fined homes still winning federal money
idea: Match nursing-home operators to federal contract and assistance recipients by name and location, then chart fine dollars against federal dollars received in the same year.
harm_angle: Homes penalized for harming residents can keep drawing taxpayer money with no visible consequence.
caveat: No shared id: this is a name and address match and will produce false pairs; flag as fuzzy.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Penalties|UK Companies House PSC
title: Foreign beneficial owners of US care homes
idea: For chains traceable to UK entities, map penalties in the US against the persons with significant control disclosed in the UK register.
harm_angle: Residents' care is set by owners who never appear in any US filing.
caveat: Requires a name bridge across two national registers; most chains will not resolve.

source_names: CMS Nursing Home Care Compare|HHS OIG LEIE
title: Excluded operators still running homes
idea: Ranked bars or map of nursing homes whose chain or legal business name matches an excluded entity on the federal ban list.
harm_angle: A banned operator still running a home means the federal exclusion did not reach the residents it was meant to protect.
caveat: Name-only match with no shared identifier so false positives are certain without careful matching.

title: Tracing nursing homes to ultimate owners
idea: Build the ownership tree from facility to chain to global parent using relationship records, drawn as a network sized by beds and colored by rating.
join_key: name to LEI then LEI hierarchy
harm_angle: The people who actually control a resident's care may be several holding companies away.
caveat: Nursing homes rarely have a legal entity identifier; the first hop is a name match and will mostly fail.

title: Three-year payment persistence
idea: Slope chart of the same physicians' total industry payments across the three program years to identify a stable paid class versus one-off recipients.
harm_angle: Doctors on industry payroll year after year are not receiving incidental hospitality — they are retained.
caveat: NPI is blank for a substantial share of Open Payments records so persistence tracking loses the unmatched tail.

title: Industry roster versus drug billing
idea: Providers on the industry-payment roster compared with everyone else on the share of Medicare revenue coming from drugs, within specialty.
harm_angle: If being on industry's roster tracks with billing more drugs, the patients getting those infusions are the endpoint of the payment.
caveat: Roster presence is not payment amount; npi in the profile table is text and must be checked for blanks.

title: Trial investigators on the payroll
idea: Match trial investigators to payment records by provider id and chart payment totals against trial outcomes reported for the sponsor's own product.
harm_angle: The doctors judging whether a drug works are paid by the company that makes it.
caveat: The trials mart is 500 rows in the catalog, likely a stub; provider id presence there is unverified.

source_names: CMS Open Payments PY2024|Medicare Physician by Provider
title: Paid doctors and their billing
idea: Scatter of industry payments received against Medicare payments billed per NPI coloured by specialty to see whether industry money tracks billing volume.
harm_angle: High-volume billers are the highest-value marketing targets so the most-influenced doctors see the most patients.
caveat: Different program years; both are annual aggregates.

source_names: CMS Open Payments|NADAC Drug Acquisition Cost
title: Marketing spend vs generic price gap
idea: For drugs that appear in payment records, plot total industry payments against the brand-to-generic price ratio from acquisition-cost data. Big marketing on big-ratio drugs is the money mechanism.
harm_angle: Patients and Medicaid pay the brand premium that the marketing spend defends.
caveat: Open Payments NDC fields may be largely blank; NDC formatting differs between sources.

source_names: CMS Open Payments|Nursing home penalties|NPI-to-CCN facility affiliation
title: Industry money inside penalized facilities
idea: Chain manufacturer payments to clinicians, clinicians to the facilities they work in, and facilities to their fine totals.
harm_angle: Residents in the worst-fined homes cared for by the most heavily paid prescribers.
caveat: Facility affiliation grain is many-to-many; attribution of payments to a facility is inherently approximate.

source_names: CMS Open Payments PY2024|Medicare Part D Prescribers
title: Payments versus brand prescribing
idea: Scatter of a prescriber's total industry payments against their brand share of Part D claims to test whether paid doctors prescribe more brand-name drugs.
harm_angle: Every extra brand prescription driven by a payment is a higher copay and a higher tax bill for the same molecule.
caveat: Program years may not align between the two sources; NPI population in Open Payments is partial.

source_names: CMS Open Payments|Medicare Part D Prescribers
title: Pharma money and opioid prescribing
idea: Scatter each prescriber's total industry payments against their opioid claim rate, with a fitted band. The tail of high-money high-opioid prescribers is the story.
harm_angle: Patients receive more opioids from doctors being paid by the companies that make them.
caveat: Payment year and prescribing year must be aligned; suppression flags blank out small-volume prescribers.

source_names: CMS Open Payments|CMS Part D Prescriber by Drug
title: Paid for this drug prescribed this drug
idea: For each named drug in the payment record, compare the prescriber's claims for that exact drug before and after the payment. Slope chart of drug-specific prescribing across the payment date.
harm_angle: Patients get the branded drug the prescriber was paid to hear about, not necessarily the best one.
caveat: Drug names must be matched as text; the Part D drug file is a single year so a before-and-after may be impossible.

source_names: CMS Open Payments|Medicare Part D prescriber by drug
title: Payment per prescriber vs prescribing volume
idea: For a given drug, scatter each prescriber's industry payments from that drug's maker against their Part D claim count for it.
harm_angle: A meal or speaking fee that shifts what a patient is handed at the pharmacy.
caveat: Manufacturer-to-drug-brand mapping is not in the data; Part D covers only Medicare patients.

title: Health committee members' pharma network
idea: Three-source view: manufacturers paying clinicians, those manufacturers' PAC and employee giving, and the health-committee members who receive it.
join_key: manufacturer name -> employer -> FEC id -> BIOGUIDE
harm_angle: One industry's money touching both the prescriber and the legislator who regulates them.
caveat: Three name-based hops; each one loses matches and adds false positives.

source_names: CMS Open Payments|HHS OIG Exclusion List
title: Industry paid them before exclusion
idea: For providers later excluded, chart industry payments in the years leading up to the exclusion date against a matched comparison group. Tests whether payment intensity precedes exclusion.
harm_angle: If money is an early warning of misconduct, patients were harmed while the signal sat in public data.
caveat: LEIE NPI sparsity; exclusion reasons vary and many are unrelated to prescribing.

source_names: CMS Open Payments|HHS OIG exclusion list
title: Excluded providers who still took industry money
idea: Timeline per provider of industry payments with the exclusion period shaded, counting dollars received while excluded.
harm_angle: Providers banned from federal health programs remain valuable to manufacturers.
caveat: LEIE NPI is known to be sparsely populated; many exclusions are name-only records.

source_names: CMS Opioid Treatment Programs|NCHS Drug Poisoning Mortality by County
title: Overdose deaths where treatment is not
idea: County map of overdose death rate with treatment-program locations dotted on top. The dark counties with no dots are the treatment deserts.
harm_angle: People die of overdose in counties with no licensed treatment program within reach.
caveat: Treatment program file carries zip only; the death rate is banded into ranges, not a continuous number.

title: Opted out but still ordering
idea: Providers who filed an opt-out affidavit yet remain on the ordering and referring roster, counted by specialty and privilege type.
harm_angle: Providers outside the program still authorizing its spending is a gap where equipment and hospice fraud lives.
caveat: NPI text formats may differ between tables and the overlap may be small.

title: Excluded providers still authorized to refer
idea: Count provider ids present on the active order-and-referring list that also appear on the exclusion list, plotted over exclusion year.
harm_angle: An excluded clinician who can still legally order tests is a live billing channel.
caveat: The order-and-referring file is a snapshot with no date; exclusion list provider id sparsity applies.

title: Three-source outlier prescriber map
idea: Build a per-provider profile of billing volume, opioid rate, and exclusion status, then plot the joint distribution and highlight the never-excluded extreme outliers.
harm_angle: The most extreme prescribers who were never touched by enforcement are the ones still seeing patients.
caveat: Three-way join multiplies the risk that any one id column is masked; suppression flags remove small counts.

title: Prescribing by provider taxonomy
idea: Heatmap of opioid and antipsychotic prescribing rates by provider taxonomy code, revealing which specialties carry the load and which are unexpectedly high.
harm_angle: Patients seeing certain specialties are far more likely to leave with a controlled prescription.
caveat: NPPES mart is a passthrough; taxonomy column name unverified. NPPES EIN is known-masked though taxonomy should be fine.

source_names: Part D prescribers|DEA ARCOS shipments|CMS Open Payments
title: The three ledgers of one opioid market
idea: For a chosen county, three aligned timelines: pills shipped in, opioid prescriptions written, and industry payments to local prescribers.
harm_angle: One county's epidemic told through supply, prescription, and payment at once.
caveat: ARCOS is DEA-number grain and prescriber data is NPI grain; there is no direct DEA-to-NPI bridge in these marts.

source_names: Medicare Part D prescribers|NCHS drug poisoning by county
title: Prescribing versus overdose deaths
idea: Aggregate opioid prescribing to geography via prescriber state FIPS and overlay it on the county overdose death-rate bands.
harm_angle: Counties with heavy prescribing and top-band death rates are where the pipeline from clinic to grave is shortest.
caveat: Part D carries prescriber STATE fips only in the mart column list, so county-level alignment may be impossible without a city or zip crosswalk; years also differ.

title: Brand prescribing where a cheap generic exists
idea: For drug pairs with both a brand and a generic acquisition price, rank prescribers and states by share of brand prescribing weighted by the price gap.
harm_angle: Patients and taxpayers pay the brand premium because of who wrote the script.
caveat: Name-to-code matching is fuzzy; the price file covers pharmacy acquisition, not what the patient paid.

source_names: CMS Provider of Services|CDC Injury and Violence County
title: Trauma capacity vs injury rate
idea: County map of trauma and emergency service availability against injury rates, highlighting high-injury counties with no capacity.
harm_angle: People are injured most in the counties with the least ability to treat them.
caveat: Service codes need correct decoding; snapshot date unknown.

source_names: CMS Quality Payment Program|Medicare Part D Prescribers
title: Quality scores vs patient risk mix
idea: Scatter each provider's quality score against their beneficiary average risk score. A negative slope means the scoring system punishes doctors who take the sickest patients.
harm_angle: Doctors serving the sickest and poorest patients get scored down, pushing them out of those neighborhoods.
caveat: Quality score field names unverified; risk score comes from the Part D file so specialty mix confounds it.

source_names: DEA ARCOS opioid shipments|CDC drug poisoning mortality
title: Pills shipped vs people who died
idea: County map of opioid dosage units shipped per capita against the overdose death rate, with a lag control.
harm_angle: The shipment ledger is the clearest paper trail to a county's dead.
caveat: ARCOS is 178M rows at ZIP grain; needs a ZIP-to-county crosswalk. Reporting year coverage unverified.

title: Pill flood versus treatment supply
idea: County map of historical opioid shipment volume overlaid with the location of opioid treatment programs, showing the counties that got the pills and never got the treatment.
harm_angle: The counties flooded with pills and left with no methadone clinic are where dependence became death.
caveat: Joining ARCOS county text to treatment-program ZIPs requires a geographic crosswalk not in either table.

title: Distributor money and the shipment surge
idea: Timeline of the largest distributors' shipment volume alongside their lobbying spend and PAC contributions across the surge years.
harm_angle: The money that kept the pills moving is on the record next to the bodies.
caveat: ARCOS reporter names must be name-matched to lobbying clients and PAC sponsors; three-hop error compounds.

source_names: DEA ARCOS Retail Drug Summary|NCHS Drug Poisoning Mortality by County
title: Pills shipped in bodies out
idea: County-level scatter of opioid morphine-equivalent grams shipped per capita against overdose death rate, animated by year. The lag between the shipment peak and the death peak is the mechanism.
harm_angle: Communities flooded with pills buried people years later.
caveat: ARCOS county is a text name needing FIPS mapping; death rates are banded ranges.

title: Pills shipped then people died
idea: Scatter or lagged timeline of county-level MME shipped against later overdose deaths at state level to show the supply-to-death lag.
harm_angle: The lag between shipment peak and death peak is the window in which intervention was possible and did not happen.
caveat: ARCOS county grain versus CDC state grain forces aggregation up; ARCOS date coverage may end before the CDC series begins.

title: Pharmacies that outrun their prescribers
idea: For each county, compare pills received by pharmacies against opioid claims written by prescribers in that county. Pharmacies receiving far more than local prescribing explains is the anomaly.
harm_angle: Diversion happens where supply exceeds any legitimate local demand, and neighborhoods pay for it.
caveat: Part D is Medicare-only so it understates total prescribing; geography join is a last resort.

title: Where health workers train vs where they land
idea: Flow diagram from states with health-program-heavy institutions to states where providers actually enroll, showing net importers and exporters of clinicians.
harm_angle: States that train clinicians and lose them all stay short of care.
caveat: There is no person-level link between graduating and enrolling; this is an aggregate inference only.

title: Dialysis clinics in unreliable grids
idea: Map dialysis facilities inside utility service territories with the worst outage metrics. Missed dialysis from a blackout is a life-threatening event.
harm_angle: Dialysis patients in weak-grid areas miss treatment when the power fails.
caveat: Service territory to facility mapping requires the territory file and is geographic, not id-based.

source_names: EPA ECHO|CMS Nursing Home Care Compare
title: Nursing homes downwind of violators
idea: Map nursing homes within a radius of chronically non-compliant air facilities, weighted by resident count. Residents cannot leave the building.
harm_angle: Nursing home residents with lung disease live next to plants in ongoing air violation and cannot move.
caveat: Geography-only join; nursing home coordinate population unverified.

source_names: Superfund Site Boundaries|NCHS Leading Causes of Death
title: Cancer mortality near Superfund density
idea: State-level scatter of Superfund sites per capita against cancer death rate, with a clear note that this is ecological correlation only.
harm_angle: If contamination tracks mortality even at state grain, the fenceline question gets sharper.
caveat: Ecological fallacy risk is severe at state grain; this can only motivate a finer-grain look, never conclude.

source_names: openFDA CAERS Cosmetic Adverse Events|Device Enforcement
title: Cosmetics harm with no recall lever
idea: Timeline of cosmetic adverse-event reports by product category next to the count of formal enforcement actions in the same period, showing an enforcement floor near zero.
harm_angle: Cosmetics injure people in a regulatory regime with almost no recall power.
caveat: No join key at all; this is a side-by-side comparison, not a real join. CAERS columns unverified.

title: Clearance Pathway Versus Recall Risk
idea: Scatter of product codes by number of equivalence clearances against number of subsequent recalls, testing whether the shortcut pathway produces more failures.
harm_angle: If the fast pathway recalls more, the shortcut is being paid for in patient injuries.
caveat: Both sides need product_code populated; the recall table's k_number list may be a better but messier link.

title: Injury rate by device risk class
idea: Heatmap of adverse-event volume by device class and medical specialty panel, testing whether the risk classification predicts actual harm.
harm_angle: If low-risk-classed devices produce high harm, the classification itself is failing patients.
caveat: No denominator for how many of each device are in use; raw counts favor common devices.

title: Repeat-recall manufacturers chain
idea: Three-source chain: recall records carry establishment and clearance number lists, establishments give the plant, adverse events give the injury count. Rank plants by recalls and injuries jointly.
harm_angle: Repeat-offender plants keep shipping and patients keep getting hurt.
caveat: The list columns are packed multi-value strings that must be exploded; unverified whether they parse cleanly.

title: Injuries Before the Recall Landed
idea: For each recalled product code, plot the monthly adverse-event curve with the recall initiation date marked. The area under the curve before the marker is the preventable harm.
harm_angle: Every death report before the recall date is a person the system already had evidence about.
caveat: MAUDE is 2020Q1-forward only, so recalls before 2020 will show an empty pre-period that falsely looks like zero harm.

title: Full-approval devices that still injure
idea: Rank fully approved devices by adverse events per year on market, compared against the shortcut-cleared population.
harm_angle: The strictest approval pathway is not preventing injury, which undercuts the whole framework.
caveat: Product code presence in the approval file unverified; denominators such as units sold do not exist anywhere here.

title: Recalled drugs and what they cost
idea: Match recall product code lists to acquisition prices and chart total recalled-product value by recall class over time, separating cheap generics from expensive brands.
harm_angle: Recalls that hit cheap generics disappear quietly while the patients relying on them lose supply.
caveat: product_ndc_list is a packed multi-value field; code format alignment unverified.

source_names: FDA drug recalls|NADAC drug acquisition cost|Part D prescriber by drug
title: Recalled drugs still being dispensed
idea: Timeline per drug code of the recall date against continued Part D claim volume and acquisition cost, showing dispensing after the alert.
key_fields: RECALL_NUMBER|product description|recall date|NDC|price|effective date|drug name|total claims
harm_angle: Patients kept receiving a product the maker already pulled.
caveat: FDA recall records carry drug codes inside free-text product descriptions rather than a clean NDC column.

source_names: openFDA drug recalls|Medicare Part D prescribers
title: Recalled drugs still being prescribed
idea: Match recalled products to prescribed generics by name and show prescribing volume for drugs that were under recall.
harm_angle: Patients still filling a recalled prescription are being exposed to a product the maker already admitted was unsafe.
caveat: Name-based join across a list-valued column and a single name column; Part D is a single 2022 snapshot so timing alignment is crude.

source_names: openFDA Drug Enforcement|Part D Prescriber by Drug
title: Recalled drug still being dispensed
idea: For recalled products, plot Medicare Part D claim volume in the quarters after the recall date. Any volume after the line is exposure.
harm_angle: Patients keep filling prescriptions for products already pulled for safety.
caveat: The Part D file appears to be one snapshot year, which may make the after-recall window impossible.

title: Recalls Traced to Their Plant
idea: Join recalls to registered establishments by facility identifier and map which physical plants generate the most recalls, including foreign ones.
harm_angle: Naming the plant rather than the brand is how you find the facility that keeps shipping defective devices.
caveat: The recall side stores facility ids as a comma-joined list string that must be split; fill rate on both sides unverified.

source_names: FDA device establishment registry|FDA MAUDE adverse events|SEC 13F holdings
title: Device makers, injuries, and their owners
idea: Chain a manufacturing establishment to its adverse-event reports to the institutional investors holding the parent company.
harm_angle: Injury counts attached to the shareholders who benefit from the production pace.
caveat: Two name hops with no shared id; most device makers are private or foreign subsidiaries.

title: Who dies from drug harm
idea: Heatmap grid of age band against gender shaded by the share of cases ending in death.
harm_angle: Shows precisely which patients bear the fatal end of drug harm.
caveat: Age needs normalization across age unit codes; the two id eras must be reconciled before joining.

title: Deaths reported vs money spent by drug
idea: Chain case demographics to outcome codes to count death outcomes per drug, then plot against total industry payments naming that drug.
harm_angle: The drugs with the biggest promotional spend may also carry the biggest body count in the safety database.
caveat: Requires the FAERS drug table whose row count is unknown and may be empty; drug-name text matching across sources is fuzzy.

title: Supplier behind the harmed patients
idea: Network linking ingredient file holders to the drugs named in adverse event reports, tracing harm back to the ingredient maker.
harm_angle: Connects a patient's injury to the offshore factory that made the ingredient.
caveat: There is no shared id: linking requires fuzzy matching file subject text to free-text drug names, which may not work at all.

title: Drugs with the highest death share
idea: Ranked bars of primary-suspect drugs by the share of their cases carrying a death outcome, not raw counts.
harm_angle: Ranks by lethality rather than popularity, which is the number patients actually need.
caveat: Free-text drug names need normalization; denominators are report counts, not prescriptions, so this is not a true rate.

title: Drug-reaction signal grid
idea: Heatmap grid of drugs against reaction terms shaded by disproportionate reporting, a classic safety-signal screen.
harm_angle: Surfaces drug-harm pairs that are over-represented before regulators publicly act.
caveat: Both tables are large; disproportionality is easy to misread as causation and needs careful framing.

title: Recalled Devices Still Listed as Distributed
idea: Cross the recall list against device distribution status by product code, flagging device identifiers still marked in distribution after a life-threatening recall.
harm_angle: A recalled device still listed as in distribution is a device that may still reach a patient.
caveat: Product code is a category, not a specific device, so an overlap may be coincidental rather than the same product.

title: Implants ranked by injury reports
idea: Use the device identification database to name and categorize devices, then rank implantable categories by adverse-event reports per marketed device.
harm_angle: Patients carrying implants have no public ranking of which ones fail.
caveat: GUDID mart is a passthrough with unverified columns; the unique device identifier in MAUDE may be mostly blank.

title: Cleared by predicate injuring by the thousand
idea: Rank clearance pathways by adverse-event reports per cleared device, showing which shortcut clearances produce the most harm reports.
harm_angle: Devices waved through on similarity to an older product go into bodies and fail.
caveat: MAUDE baseline_510k_number is likely sparse; matching may cover only a fraction of reports.

title: How long a bad device stays on market
idea: For each device product code, plot the first cluster of injury and death reports against the eventual recall date. The horizontal gap is months of exposure.
harm_angle: Patients are implanted with devices that regulators already had injury reports on.
caveat: MAUDE dates are text-derived; product code populated-ness in enforcement records unverified.

title: Which plants produce the injuries
idea: Attach adverse-event reports to registered manufacturing establishments by facility identifier and map plants sized by injury reports.
harm_angle: A single plant can be the source of injuries showing up nationwide.
caveat: MAUDE has manufacturer name not FEI; the join likely needs the enforcement file as a bridge or name matching.

title: Biosimilar entry and what happened to price
idea: For each reference biologic, plot acquisition price over time with biosimilar approval dates marked. Flat lines after entry are a competition failure.
harm_angle: Patients never see the savings that biosimilar approval was supposed to deliver.
caveat: Purple Book columns unverified; product-name-to-code matching is fuzzy for biologics.

title: Listed carcinogens inside approved products
idea: Use the substance registry to resolve chemical identities, then count approved drug and food substances whose identity matches a listed carcinogen.
harm_angle: Substances a state calls carcinogenic are inside products people take daily.
caveat: Substance registry column names unverified; a listing does not mean the exposure level is harmful.

source_names: FEC itemized individual contributions|CMS Open Payments
title: Doctors who take pharma cash and give it
idea: Cross physicians receiving industry payments with political donors whose occupation is physician, comparing giving rates for high-payment vs low-payment doctors.
harm_angle: Industry money may travel from a manufacturer through a clinician into politics.
caveat: Name-matching individuals is unreliable and risks false positives on common names; occupation field is free text.

source_names: HHS OIG Exclusion List|CMS Facility Affiliation
title: Which facilities employ excluded clinicians
idea: Use the provider-to-facility crosswalk to attach excluded NPIs to facilities, then rank facilities by count of affiliated excluded clinicians.
harm_angle: Patients walking into a hospital have no way to know it staffs excluded clinicians.
caveat: Affiliation file is a snapshot with no dates; cannot tell if the affiliation was current at exclusion time.

title: Excluded but still enrolled
idea: Count providers with an active exclusion who appear in current Medicare enrollment records, mapped by state.
harm_angle: Patients treated by providers the government already judged unfit.
caveat: LEIE NPI sparsity is the main risk; the enrollment snapshot date may postdate reinstatement.

source_names: HHS OIG Exclusion List|Medicare Part D Prescribers
title: Excluded providers still prescribing
idea: Timeline per provider: exclusion date marked, Medicare Part D claim counts plotted by year. Any bars to the right of the exclusion marker are prescribing that should not exist.
harm_angle: Patients get prescriptions from providers the government already judged unfit.
caveat: LEIE NPI column is known to be sparsely populated; many excluded individuals have no NPI at all.

title: Two exclusion lists that disagree
idea: Overlap comparison of entities on the health exclusion list versus the federal debarment list, showing how many appear on only one.
harm_angle: A company barred from Medicare can still win federal contracts because the lists do not talk.
caveat: No shared id between the two; matching is by name, so both false positives and misses are likely.

title: Shortage Areas With No Safety Net Clinic
idea: Overlay shortage-designated counties with safety-net clinic locations to find high-shortage counties that have no clinic at all.
harm_angle: A county with a severe doctor shortage and zero safety-net clinics is a place where poor people simply do not get care.
caveat: Both tables also carry an organization id which may offer a tighter join; FIPS formatting must match.

title: Adverse actions that never became exclusions
idea: State-year lines comparing adverse licensure actions against federal exclusions originating in that state. A widening gap means state boards act and the federal list does not follow.
harm_angle: A clinician stripped of a license in one state can keep billing federal programs elsewhere.
caveat: NPDB has no provider ids; state-level only, so this is an aggregate comparison not a matched one.

title: Shortage designation versus actual providers
idea: Map overlaying HPSA designation score with the count of active NPIs per county to find places designated as fine that have almost no providers and vice versa.
harm_angle: If the designation map is wrong the funding that follows it goes to the wrong places and real shortages stay unfunded.
