caveat: NPPES address is a registration address not proof of practice; ZIP to county crosswalk needed.

title: Care deserts by district vote
idea: District-level dot plot of shortage severity against margin of victory, testing whether the worst-served places are also the least contested.
harm_angle: People in safe districts with no doctors have no political lever either.
caveat: County-to-district mapping is many-to-many; districts change with redistricting.

source_names: HUD Assisted Housing|HRSA UDS Health Centers
title: Subsidized Housing Without Nearby Care
idea: Map HUD projects and HRSA health centers together by ZIP, shading ZIPs that hold assisted housing but no funded health center.
harm_angle: Concentrating low-income families where there is no safety-net clinic is two federal programs failing the same people from opposite directions.
caveat: ZIP co-location is a crude proxy for access — a clinic one ZIP over would read as absent — and the HRSA address is the grantee headquarters, not every clinic site.

source_names: ICE Detention Facility List|CMS Hospital General
title: Detention facilities and nearest hospital quality
idea: Map each detention facility to its nearest hospital and color by that hospital's mortality measure counts, showing where a medical emergency in detention goes.
harm_angle: People held in detention depend on whatever hospital happens to be nearby, and some are the worst in the state.
caveat: The facility list has only 163 rows and may lack coordinates; nearest-neighbor is a geographic guess.

source_names: ICE Detention Stints|ICE Detention Facility List
title: Length of stay by facility operator
idea: Distribution of detention length by facility and operator type, showing which private operators hold people longest.
harm_angle: People are held far longer at some operators than others for the same reasons.
caveat: Facility code alignment between the stint file and the facility list is unverified.

source_names: IRS 990 e-file Index|CMS HCRIS Cost Reports
title: Executive pay against charity care
idea: For hospital filers present in both, scatter reported top-officer compensation against uncompensated care share, by year.
harm_angle: Hospitals paying executives most may be giving away the least care.
caveat: The 990 file is only an index; actual compensation lives in the filing XML not in the mart, so this may be blocked.

source_names: IRS Exempt Org Business Master File|CMS Hospital General
title: Tax-exempt hospitals and their quality scores
idea: Rank tax-exempt hospitals by asset size against their overall rating and mortality measure counts, showing whether the exemption buys anything.
harm_angle: Communities give hospitals a tax break and may get worse care than the for-profit next door.
caveat: No shared id between the exempt org file and the hospital file; name and state matching only.

title: Researchers funded publicly and privately
idea: For institutions and named investigators, plot federal award dollars against industry payments received, revealing who is double-funded.
harm_angle: The same people setting treatment evidence are paid by both the public and the sellers.
caveat: Name matching only; the grant file has entity ids but the payment file has none.

title: Researchers paid by both sides
idea: For institutions receiving large NIH grants, plot federal research dollars against industry payments received by their affiliated clinicians.
harm_angle: Trial results patients rely on may come from labs funded by the product's maker.
caveat: NIH RePORTER mart columns unverified (passthrough); linking clinicians to institutions requires a facility affiliation table.

source_names: DailyMed SPL Setid Map|openFDA Drug Enforcement
title: Label changes around recalls
idea: Timeline of label version updates for products that were later recalled, showing whether the label quietly changed before the recall.
harm_angle: Manufacturers can amend the warning label instead of pulling the product.
caveat: Label mart columns unverified; label version history may not be captured in the mart.

source_names: NOAA Storm Events|CMS Nursing Home Care Compare
title: Nursing homes in repeat disaster counties
idea: County map of heat, flood and hurricane event frequency with nursing home bed counts overlaid, highlighting counties with many beds and many events.
harm_angle: Residents who cannot evacuate themselves live in the counties hit most often.
caveat: Nursing home FIPS presence unverified; storm event counts need normalization by county area or population.

title: Margin up staffing down
idea: Two-line small multiples per chain: reported net margin ratio from cost reports against nurse hours per resident day. Chains where the lines diverge are converting care hours into profit.
harm_angle: Residents lose bedside hours in exactly the facilities posting the best financials.
caveat: HCRIS is documented as hospital-heavy; SNF coverage in it is unverified and may be thin.

title: Two sources one nursing home
idea: Dot plot comparing the same facility's staffing and rating values as reported by CMS and as compiled by LTCCC to find where the two records disagree.
harm_angle: Where the public records disagree a family reading one of them is being misled.
caveat: LTCCC compiles from CMS so most values will agree; the interest is entirely in the exceptions.

source_names: OSHA ITA Case Detail|CMS Hospital General Information
title: Hospital worker injuries vs patient safety
idea: Match hospitals by name and zip, then scatter staff injury rate against the hospital's patient safety measure counts. Places unsafe for staff may be unsafe for patients.
harm_angle: A hospital that hurts its nurses is probably hurting its patients too.
caveat: Name and zip matching; hospital establishment names in injury filings are often corporate, not facility.

title: Public grants behind retracted work
idea: Match retracted papers to grant numbers and rank institutions by federal dollars attached to retracted output.
join_key: grant number in the paper record
harm_angle: Public money funded science that turned out to be wrong, and patients may have been treated on it.
caveat: Grant numbers in retraction records are inconsistently captured; matching will be partial.

source_names: SAM.gov exclusions|OIG exclusion list|NPPES provider registry
title: The two ban lists that disagree
idea: Count providers excluded by one federal list and not the other, and how many are still actively enumerated in the national provider registry.
harm_angle: Two federal ban systems that do not talk to each other, and the patients in the gap.
caveat: NPI population in both exclusion marts is unverified; the NPPES deactivation status column is unverified.

source_names: SEC 13F holdings|Nursing home deficiencies|Skilled nursing facility enrollments
title: Ownership chain to the bedside
idea: Chain institutional holdings to the enrolled operator entity to the deficiency record at each facility.
harm_angle: Puts a fund's name at the end of a chain that ends in a resident's injury.
caveat: The issuer-to-operator hop is name-only; most skilled nursing operators are privately held.

source_names: SEC 13F positions|13F filer identity|CMS nursing home penalties
title: Who owns the worst nursing homes
idea: Trace institutional holders of nursing-home operator stocks and plot their holdings against those operators' fine totals per bed.
harm_angle: Residents' care quality traced back to the funds that profit from cutting it.
caveat: CUSIP-to-operator-name mapping is not in the data; nursing home chains are usually privately held so coverage may be tiny.

source_names: SEC insider transactions|FDA device recalls|FDA MAUDE adverse events
title: Adverse events, insider sales, then recall
idea: Three-track timeline per device maker: reported patient injuries, insider selling, and the eventual recall date.
key_fields: transaction date|shares|issuer name|recall date|firm name|event date|device brand|event type
harm_angle: The people harmed by a device are the last to know what insiders already priced in.
caveat: MAUDE manufacturer names are free text; the insider data window is one quarter.

source_names: SEC insider transactions|Insider filing metadata|FDA drug recalls
title: Insider selling before a recall
idea: Event-time chart of insider sale volume in the weeks before a company's drug recall announcement versus a matched baseline.
key_fields: ACCESSION_NUMBER|transaction date|shares|price|issuer name|RECALL_NUMBER|recall initiation date|firm name
harm_angle: Executives may exit before the public learns the product is dangerous.
caveat: The insider mart covers only 2025Q1 per the catalog name, so the overlap window with recalls is very narrow.

title: Pharma lobbying and doctor payments together
idea: Manufacturer-level view pairing federal lobbying spend with total industry payments made to physicians in the same year.
harm_angle: Patients get prescriptions shaped by two spending channels neither of them can see.
caveat: Manufacturer legal names in Open Payments rarely match LDA client names exactly.

source_names: USASpending federal assistance|CDC drug poisoning mortality by county
title: Overdose money vs overdose deaths
idea: County map of federal substance-abuse assistance dollars per capita against the overdose death rate, highlighting high-death low-funding counties.
harm_angle: The counties dying fastest may be the ones the money never reaches.
caveat: Program filtering to substance-abuse assistance requires CFDA or program text parsing; assistance place-of-performance FIPS may be sparse.

title: Veteran mortality vs local hospital quality
idea: State-level comparison of veteran all-cause mortality against the share of hospitals rated worse than average on mortality measures.
harm_angle: Veterans in states with weaker hospitals die at higher rates.
caveat: VA file columns unverified; veterans often use VA facilities not in the hospital file at all.

source_names: VA State Suicide Data|HRSA Shortage Areas
title: Veteran suicide against mental health shortage
idea: State scatter of veteran suicide rate against mental-health shortage designation coverage, with a trend line.
harm_angle: Veterans die by suicide in states where mental health care is formally declared insufficient.
caveat: VA file column names unverified; state grain is coarse and designation is a policy artifact.

source_names: Health Canada Drug Product Database|openFDA Drug Enforcement
title: Recalled here still sold there
idea: For active ingredients recalled in the US, check whether the same ingredient remains marketed in Canada, as a two-column comparison over time.
harm_angle: A safety decision in one country does not travel, and patients across the border keep taking it.
caveat: Ingredient name matching across two naming conventions; the Canadian mart columns are unverified.

source_names: NCHS drug poisoning by county|FJC criminal records
title: Overdose deaths vs drug prosecutions
idea: County overdose intensity band against federal drug-case filings in the covering district, over time.
harm_angle: Prosecuting more people has not been followed by fewer deaths - the chart makes that testable.
caveat: County-to-district mapping is many-to-one; CDC bands are coarse text with suppression.

source_names: CDC provisional overdose deaths|Vera Incarceration Trends
title: Overdose deaths after release
idea: State provisional overdose death series against jail discharge volumes, aligned monthly, to probe the post-release death spike.
harm_angle: People die in the first two weeks after release, and the data can show the shape of it.
caveat: State-level aggregation cannot establish the individual-level post-release spike; Vera discharge counts are annual.

source_names: HRSA shortage areas|Vera Incarceration Trends|NCHS drug poisoning
title: Triple-deficit counties
idea: Three-source county grid: no doctors, high jail rate, high overdose band - ranked by how many of the three a county fails.
chart_shape: heatmap grid with a composite rank
harm_angle: Names the counties where the state has withdrawn care and substituted punishment.
caveat: Three different suppression and binning regimes; composite ranks are sensitive to how each axis is scaled.

source_names: CDC injury and violence by county|Mapping Police Violence
title: Violent death, by whose hand
idea: County violent-death rates decomposed to show what share involves police, ranked among the highest-rate counties.
harm_angle: In some counties a meaningful share of violent deaths are caused by the people paid to prevent them.
caveat: MPV needs geocoding to county; CDC intent categories may already include legal intervention, risking double counting.

source_names: NCHS leading causes by state|MEDSL presidential returns
title: Mortality and the political map
idea: State age-adjusted death rates by cause over time set against the state's partisan lean, showing divergence after policy splits.
harm_angle: Where you live, and who runs it, may be deciding how long you live.
caveat: Correlational and politically charged; confounded by age, income and rurality.

title: Camp record versus camp memory
idea: Dot plot per camp of the official NARA record count against the Densho archived object count to show which camps have government records but no surviving testimony.
harm_angle: Camps documented only by the government that ran them have no counter-narrative left.
caveat: Both marts hold only tens of rows so this comparison is currently impossible; camp name strings differ between sources.

title: Records and the testimony beside them
idea: County-level counts of incarcerated Japanese Americans with Densho oral histories and photographs attached as the human receipts.
harm_angle: Numbers plus the voices of the people counted.
caveat: Densho mart is 25 rows in the catalog - likely a metadata stub, not the full repository.

title: One person two legs of a trade
idea: Flow diagram chaining transatlantic arrival ports into intra-American departure ports to trace how people were landed and then trafficked onward.
harm_angle: Following the second leg shows the trade did not end at the American shore for the people who survived it.
caveat: VOYAGEID does not link the same people across databases; the join is conceptual via port and year not identity.

title: The second sale
idea: Voyages arriving from Africa versus onward intra-American voyages from the same ports, by decade, showing the internal redistribution.
harm_angle: Makes the industrial scale and the repeat sale of human beings legible as a system.
caveat: Port name vocabularies differ between the two files; VOYAGEID may not be shared across databases.

source_names: WPA slave narratives|Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database|DocSouth
title: From the ship to the interview
idea: Three-source chain linking embarkation regions and arrival ports to the states where WPA interviewees were recorded, with DocSouth texts as the narrative layer.
harm_angle: Connects the accounting of the trade to the individual people who lived its aftermath.
caveat: Only a state-level geographic link exists; DocSouth mart is 144 rows and may be a catalogue stub.

source_names: NARA WWII Japanese American incarceration records|ICE detention facilities
title: Two camp maps, eighty years apart
idea: Map WRA camp locations and populations next to today's ICE detention facilities and capacity, on the same base map and scale.
harm_angle: The state's habit of mass administrative detention is visible as one continuous line, not a closed chapter.
caveat: Direct comparison is rhetorical, not statistical; WRA record grain is person-level while the ICE facility list is a directory.

title: Narrative counties, modern jails
idea: States with dense WPA interview coverage set against present-day Black jail incarceration rates.
harm_angle: A long-arc argument about where the machinery of control persisted.
caveat: WPA interview location reflects where interviewers worked in 1936, not where people were enslaved - a serious confound.

title: Complaint rate against denial rate by lender
idea: Scatter each lender's consumer complaint rate against its denial rate for minority applicants, sized by loan volume.
harm_angle: The lenders generating the most complaints are the ones turning down the most people of color.
caveat: The complaint file has company name not a legal entity identifier; a name bridge is needed and the mortgage mart is only 28k rows.

source_names: HMDA Historic|CDC Injury and Violence County
title: Disinvestment and health harm
idea: County scatter of long-run mortgage denial rate against injury and violence rates, animated across decades.
harm_angle: Places starved of credit for forty years show it in the injury numbers.
caveat: Tract to county rollup is mechanical but the causal chain is long and contestable.

title: Denials Then Complaints
idea: Map ZIPs by mortgage denial rate alongside mortgage-servicing complaint rate, finding places where people are both refused credit and mistreated once they get it.
harm_angle: Neighborhoods that are both hard to borrow in and hard to be serviced in absorb both ends of the harm.
caveat: HMDA is tract-level and DC-only; complaints are ZIP-level, so the join is approximate.

title: Lenders that deny and get complained about
idea: Scatter lender denial rate against consumer complaint rate per loan, sized by volume, flagging the upper-right quadrant.
join_key: lender name (name-match; LEI on one side only)
harm_angle: Borrowers pushed out of homeownership and then ignored when they complain.
caveat: CFPB has no LEI, so the join is company-name based; the HMDA sample size may be too small.

title: Denials by 1930s redline grade
idea: Overlay modern loan denial rates on historic redlining polygons by census tract, as a distribution comparison across grades.
harm_angle: The maps drawn in the thirties still predict who gets a mortgage.
caveat: Tract-to-polygon overlay is approximate; redlining coverage is city-limited; the mortgage mart row count is small.

title: Public housing served by violating systems
idea: Match assisted-housing projects to their serving water system by zip and count assisted households on systems with health-based violations.
join_key: ZIP to water system service area
harm_angle: Federally housed families are served water the government already knows is out of compliance.
caveat: Zip to water system mapping is many-to-many and imprecise.

source_names: EPA Superfund Site Boundaries|HUD Assisted Housing
title: Subsidized housing on Superfund edges
idea: Map assisted-housing projects whose points fall inside or adjacent to Superfund site boundaries, sized by households.
harm_angle: Low-income families are housed at the fenceline of the country's worst contaminated sites.
caveat: Superfund mart is a passthrough with unverified geometry columns; only 2114 sites so coverage is limited.

title: Uninsured Because The Program Was Absent
idea: Match disaster aid registrations to their community's flood-program participation and map age to test whether denial reasons citing insurance cluster in communities that never joined the program or had stale maps.
harm_angle: Households denied aid for lacking flood insurance their community never made available were set up to fail.
caveat: Join is by county and community name only which is fuzzy; the aid table is a 12 percent truncated load.

source_names: FEMA Individual Assistance Registrations|HUD Assisted Housing
title: Disaster aid where subsidized housing is
idea: Map disaster assistance registration density by zip against assisted-housing units, showing whether aid reached the subsidized stock.
harm_angle: The tenants least able to rebuild may be the ones the aid missed.
caveat: FEMA mart is a passthrough with no aliased columns; field names entirely unverified.

title: Disaster aid approval by historic redline grade
idea: Overlay registration and approval outcomes on 1930s redlining polygons and compare approval rates across grades in the same city.
harm_angle: The same neighborhoods graded worst in 1937 may get the least disaster money today.
caveat: Zip to polygon overlay is coarse; redlining coverage is limited to specific cities.

source_names: FEMA NFIP Community Status|NOAA Storm Events
title: Flooded communities not in the flood program
idea: County map of repeated flood events overlaid with communities suspended from or not participating in the flood insurance program.
harm_angle: Households in non-participating communities flood repeatedly with no insurance to rebuild.
caveat: Community status column names unverified; community-to-FIPS mapping needed.

title: Capital strength vs who gets denied
idea: Scatter bank capital ratios against mortgage denial rates for minority applicants, testing whether weak banks ration credit hardest.
harm_angle: Credit rationing lands on the same neighborhoods every downturn.
caveat: The call reports mart is only 302 rows and likely a sample; no direct RSSD-to-LEI key exists in either mart.

title: Cheap federal funding vs who gets lent to
idea: Compare mortgage approval rates in low-income tracts for Federal Home Loan Bank members against non-members of similar size.
harm_angle: Subsidized funding meant to expand housing access may not be reaching the tracts that need it.
caveat: FHLB membership mart columns unverified; the HMDA sample here is small.

source_names: HUD subsidized housing projects|EPA ECHO facilities
title: Subsidized housing next to polluters
idea: Map subsidized housing developments within a short distance of facilities in significant noncompliance, ranked by resident count.
harm_angle: The government houses low-income families next to the facilities it fails to police.
caveat: Proximity join with no shared id; HUD unit counts and ECHO coordinates both need validation.

source_names: HUD subsidized housing|FEC contributions|MEDSL House returns
title: Subsidized housing and political voice
idea: District map of subsidized housing units per capita against political contributions per capita and turnout, showing the voice gap.
harm_angle: The neighborhoods most dependent on federal housing have the least political money behind them.
caveat: ZIP-to-district mapping is not in any of the three sources and would need a crosswalk.

source_names: HUD Section 8 contracts|FHFA House Price Index
title: Expiring contracts in hot markets
idea: Section 8 contract expiration dates mapped against local house price growth, flagging where owners have the most incentive to exit.
harm_angle: Every expiring contract in a hot market is a household one step from eviction.
caveat: Contract table lacks explicit geography columns in the staging list; FHFA join key is a name field.

title: Two Halves Of The Assisted Stock
idea: Combine project-based rent subsidy contracts with public housing authority unit counts by geography to show the full picture of federally assisted units and where both are thinning at once.
harm_angle: Counties losing both public housing and project-based subsidy at the same time leave tenants nowhere to go.
caveat: The contracts table has no geography columns in the model so the join requires the property id via another source.

title: Wall Street ownership of subsidized housing
idea: Trace Section 8 property owners to publicly traded landlords and the institutional funds holding them, sized by subsidized units.
harm_angle: Public rent subsidies flowing to shareholders while tenants face the worst conditions.
caveat: Owner names in HUD data are often shell LLCs that never surface a public parent.

source_names: IRS exempt org master file|HUD Section 8 multifamily contracts
title: Nonprofit landlords of subsidized housing
idea: Map Section 8 contract properties whose owners are registered nonprofits, comparing contract rents to for-profit owners nearby.
harm_angle: Tenants pay the same either way while the tax treatment differs sharply.
caveat: HUD contract mart columns unverified; owner names are entity strings needing normalization.

title: Redlining Grade to Modern Denial
idea: Overlay the 1930s HOLC grade polygons on present-day mortgage denial rates by census tract, testing whether D-graded neighborhoods still get refused ninety years later.
harm_angle: Families in historically redlined tracts are still denied credit today, which is how a 1930s policy still costs people houses.
caveat: HMDA mart is a DC-2023 sample only; HOLC polygons must be spatially joined to tracts, which is not a key join.

title: Ninety Years of Price Divergence
idea: Slope chart of house price index growth for tracts inside A-graded versus D-graded HOLC areas, measuring the wealth gap the grades created.
harm_angle: The dollar gap between an A-tract and a D-tract home is inherited wealth that redlining took from specific families.
caveat: FHFA place_id is not raw FIPS at every level and tract series are annual and sparse; spatial join required.

source_names: National Inventory of Dams|HUD Assisted Housing
title: Subsidized housing in dam failure zones
idea: Map high-hazard dams in poor condition and the assisted housing downstream, sized by households at risk.
harm_angle: Public housing sits below dams the government itself rates as high hazard and poor condition.
caveat: Downstream inundation zones are not in the data; a simple radius is a crude proxy.

source_names: SBA 7(a) and 504 loans|Mapping Inequality redlining grades
title: Small business lending on redlined ground
idea: Overlay historic redlining grades with modern SBA loan density and average loan size in the same neighborhoods.
harm_angle: The lines drawn in the 1930s still predict who can borrow to start a business.
caveat: Spatial join, not an id join; SBA addresses need geocoding which may not be in the mart.

title: Subsidised housing beside orphaned wells
idea: Spatially pair rural subsidised housing projects with nearby orphaned oil and gas wells and map the projects with the most wells within a short radius.
harm_angle: Low-income rural tenants who cannot move are the people most likely to be living on top of somebody's abandoned well.
caveat: Requires spatial proximity, not an id join; both coordinate sets are parsed from text and orphan-well coverage is state-dependent.

source_names: GLEIF LEI register|GLEIF parent-child relationships|HMDA mortgage data
title: Denial rates rolled up to the parent
idea: Roll HMDA lender denial rates up the corporate ownership tree via LEI relationships, comparing subsidiaries of the same parent.
harm_angle: A parent company's lending discrimination is invisible when each subsidiary is looked at alone.
caveat: HMDA mart is only 28k rows here, likely a sample; the GLEIF relationship mart's columns are unverified.

title: The redline is still there
idea: HOLC grade against modern mortgage denial rate and rate spread for the tracts inside each graded neighborhood.
harm_angle: A 1937 map drawn by the government still predicts who gets a loan today.
caveat: HOLC polygons to census tracts is a spatial join, not an id; tract boundaries changed over decades.

title: Graded D, sited toxic
idea: Share of Superfund and other regulated sites falling inside each HOLC grade across the mapped cities.
chart_shape: map plus stacked bars by grade
harm_angle: Neighborhoods marked hazardous for lending became the ones marked acceptable for poison.
caveat: Spatial overlay required; Superfund boundary file is 2,114 features and may not cover all site types.

title: Eighty years of price gap
idea: House price index trajectories for tracts by their original HOLC grade, indexed to a common start.
chart_shape: indexed line chart, one line per grade
harm_angle: The wealth families could build was decided by a colour on a map before they were born.
caveat: FHFA join key is a name field; tract-level HPI availability and matching to HOLC areas is unverified.

source_names: HUD public housing authorities|HMDA loan records
title: Two housing systems in one county
idea: County public-housing capacity and waitlist proxies against private mortgage approvals by race in the same county.
harm_angle: Where the private market shuts people out and the public system has no room, people end up on the street.
caveat: HMDA county code needs zero-padding to match; months-waiting is a weak waitlist proxy.

title: Subsidized units in disaster counties
idea: Counties with the most subsidized units that also register the most disaster damage, with award rates for those counties.
harm_angle: When subsidized housing floods, tenants have nowhere in the market to go.
caveat: HUD summaries are at varying summary levels so county aggregation must be filtered carefully.

source_names: HUD FHA single-family portfolio|FEMA IA registrations
title: FHA borrowers in disaster counties
idea: FHA-insured loan concentrations in counties with repeated disaster registrations, showing where federal credit risk and household risk overlap.
harm_angle: The government insures the loan and then decides whether to pay the family - two arms, one household.
caveat: FHA snapshot columns unverified in metadata; snapshot grain may be current-only.

title: Redline, denial, jail
idea: Three-source chain at tract-to-county level: historic HOLC grade, present-day mortgage denial rate, present-day incarceration rate.
harm_angle: Follows one policy decision from 1937 to a cell in 2024.
caveat: Aggregating tract data to counties destroys most of the signal - the ecological fallacy is the main threat here.

title: Policing where the subsidy is
idea: Subsidized-housing project locations against police-killing locations in the same cities, with project tenant demographics attached.
harm_angle: Public housing residents may be the most heavily policed tenants in the country.
caveat: Proximity is not causation; MPV coordinates need geocoding and both sets have address quality issues.

title: Two DHS counts of the same month
idea: CBP's published monthly encounter totals against OHSS's encounter tables for identical months, with the differences highlighted.
harm_angle: When one department publishes two different numbers, at least one of them is shaping a narrative.
caveat: CBP mart is 9 rows of wide month columns; definitions likely differ, so gaps may be innocent.

title: Two Agencies One Number
idea: Timeline overlaying DHS OHSS monthly enforcement counts against ICE's own quarterly statistics for the same actions, showing where the two official records disagree.
harm_angle: When two federal sources disagree on how many people were detained, nobody outside can hold either accountable.
caveat: Different period grains (monthly vs quarterly) and different metric definitions may make disagreement an artifact, not a finding.

title: Certified but Never Approved
idea: Slope chart per fiscal year comparing OFLC labor certifications granted against the corresponding USCIS petition approvals, exposing the attrition between the two gates.
harm_angle: Workers certified by Labor and then denied by USCIS lose jobs and status inside a process the government approved half of.
caveat: No shared id -- the join is by visa class and year only, which is a weak bridge; USCIS counts are untyped text.

title: From Detainer to Detention to Removal
idea: Sankey following people from detainer issuance through detention stints to departure or release, showing where the funnel narrows and who falls out.
harm_angle: Following the same people end to end shows how many were detained and removed despite a lifted detainer or no conviction.
caveat: Requires the anonymized person key to mean the same person in both tables; both carry a person_hash column but cross-table stability is entirely unverified and is the whole idea's failure point.

title: From detainer to detention
idea: Person-hash chain from a jail detainer to a detention stint to a removal, with time between each step by state.
harm_angle: Shows the machine end to end, and where people get stuck in it.
caveat: Person hashes may not be consistent between the two files, which would break the chain entirely.

source_names: ICE detention stints|ICE detention facility codes
title: Bond amounts by facility
idea: Median initial bond set and median days detained for each detention facility, ranked, with facility type and operator grouping shown.
chart_shape: ranked dot plot with two dots per facility
harm_angle: Where you are locked up decides what your freedom costs - same law, different price.
caveat: Bond fields have duplicate-likely flags; 'lowest seen' variants suggest deduplication issues in the source.

title: Published totals vs the record rows
idea: ICE's own quarterly published counts against counts derived from the person-level detention records, by area of responsibility.
harm_angle: Where an agency's public numbers do not match its own records, the public number is doing work.
caveat: Definitional differences (stays vs stints vs people) can explain gaps innocently; duplicate flags in the stint file matter.

source_names: USCIS processing data|EOIR immigration court cases
title: Backlog upstream, backlog downstream
idea: Processing time and pending counts by USCIS form type over time, next to immigration-court pending caseload - the queue that pushes people into the court queue.
harm_angle: Every month in the queue is a month of legal limbo for a real household.
caveat: EOIR mart may not expose date fields; USCIS quarters may be text.

source_names: EOIR immigration court cases|ICE detention stints
title: Detained means you lose
idea: Case outcomes for detained vs non-detained respondents by court, shown as paired bars, with the median time in detention alongside.
harm_angle: Being locked up while your case runs may be the single biggest predictor of deportation.
caveat: The EOIR mart currently exposes only case_type - the rest of the case fields may not be modeled yet, which would kill this outright.

title: Charge severity vs detainer
idea: Distribution of the most-serious conviction charge behind detainers against the federal charging mix in the same district, testing the 'worst first' claim.
harm_angle: Tests whether people deported as criminals were actually convicted of anything serious.
caveat: Charge coding schemes differ between ICE and FJC; district-to-state mapping is approximate.

title: Border sectors and their representatives
idea: Encounter volume by border sector against the vote margins in the districts those sectors sit in, over cycles.
harm_angle: The people living on the border are governed by policy set by people who do not.
caveat: Sector-to-district mapping does not exist in the data and must be hand-built.

source_names: EOIR immigration court cases|MEDSL presidential returns
title: Court backlog by political geography
idea: State-level immigration court caseload and outcome mix plotted against the state's presidential vote margin over the same years.
harm_angle: Shows whether the machinery of deportation runs hardest where the politics demand it.
caveat: EOIR mart may lack a state/court column; correlation is ecological and politically loaded.

title: Detention capacity by district politics
idea: Detained-days per congressional district against the district's partisan margin, testing whether detention sites cluster where the political cost is lowest.
harm_angle: Detention gets sited where the people held there have no vote and the locals have no objection.
caveat: Facility-to-district mapping does not exist in the data and must be geocoded; ecological reasoning.

source_names: ICE detention stints|NCHS leading causes of death
title: Deaths in and around detention
idea: Facility-level detained population and release reasons, with medical-release patterns compared against state mortality baselines.
harm_angle: Whether people are dying, or being released to die, out of ICE custody.
caveat: Release-reason coding may not identify deaths; state mortality is not a valid comparison population.

source_names: ICE detention stints|HRSA health professional shortage areas
title: Detention in medical deserts
idea: Detention facilities mapped onto primary-care shortage areas, with detained-days volume, asking who provides care to people held in counties with no doctors.
harm_angle: People with no ability to leave are held where medical care barely exists.
caveat: Detainee care is contracted, not local - the shortage measure describes the county, not the facility clinic.

title: Which jails hand people to ICE
idea: County detainer counts against jail admissions and the county's ICE-held population, showing the local sheriffs that function as the front door of deportation.
harm_angle: A local jail policy decides whether a traffic stop becomes deportation.
caveat: Detainer facility names must be matched to counties by hand; Vera's ICE-hold field may be sparse.

source_names: DHS OHSS enforcement data|OWID refugee population by origin
title: Fleeing there, blocked here
idea: Encounters and removals by citizenship plotted against the global refugee outflow from the same country and year.
harm_angle: Countries producing the most refugees may be exactly where the US turns people back.
caveat: Country name normalization between DHS tables and OWID is the whole risk; OHSS is aggregate tables with awkward wide columns.

title: Certified wage vs local wage
idea: Certified prevailing wages on visa applications against the actual average wage for that industry and county from QCEW.
harm_angle: If certified wages sit below the local average, the program is a wage-suppression tool.
caveat: Prevailing-wage column presence is unverified in the mart; worksite city needs geocoding to county FIPS.

title: Same industries, both ends
idea: Industries with the heaviest legal guest-worker certification next to the industries and states with the heaviest detainer activity - the two doors of the same labor market.
harm_angle: Employers can import workers legally and have the undocumented ones removed, both at public expense.
caveat: ICE data has no employer or industry field - the industry side is inferred from geography only.

source_names: ICE facility codes|QCEW employment and wages
title: Detention as the local economy
idea: Counties hosting detention facilities, with corrections-sector employment and wage share relative to total county employment.
harm_angle: Towns whose payroll depends on detention will fight to keep people locked up.
caveat: QCEW mart may not expose employment/wage measures; facility county field must be normalized to FIPS.

title: Certified but never approved
idea: Volume of labor certifications granted against the corresponding USCIS petition approvals and denials by form type and quarter.
harm_angle: Workers can clear one agency and be stopped at the next, losing everything in the gap.
caveat: Visa-class to form-number mapping is manual; USCIS data is aggregate.

source_names: OFLC foreign labor certification|OSHA injury summaries
title: Guest workers in the dangerous shops
idea: Employers with heavy H-2/PERM certification matched to their OSHA injury rates, ranked by injuries per 100 workers.
harm_angle: Visa-bound workers cannot quit a dangerous job without losing their status.
caveat: Employer name matching across two agencies is fuzzy; OSHA ITA covers only establishments required to report.

title: The detention economy, three ways
idea: Three-source chain for facility counties: detained days, corrections employment share, and federal contract dollars, on one county ranking.
chart_shape: ranked bars with three stacked measures
harm_angle: Shows the full local incentive to keep beds occupied.
caveat: Every hop needs name or geocode matching; QCEW measure columns unverified.

title: Detention beds and the contracts that fill them
idea: Facility-level detained days per year plotted against ICE contract obligations to the operator at that location. Who gets paid per person-day.
harm_angle: Ties the length of people's detention to the money a private operator earns from it.
caveat: Facility-to-contractor link needs name matching; contract place-of-performance is often the HQ, not the jail.

title: Federal versus local cages
idea: State-level federal inmate counts against state prison and county jail populations from Vera, showing which layer of government holds people where.
harm_angle: Makes visible which government is responsible when incarceration rises.
caveat: BOP mart is 50 aggregate rows; grain and date coverage unclear.

title: School outcomes and county jail rate
idea: County jail rate against school proficiency and program participation for the districts in that county, split by subgroup.
harm_angle: The school-to-prison story told at the level where both budgets are set.
caveat: EDFacts mart is only 33 rows in the catalog - probably a metadata stub, which would kill this.

source_names: Vera Incarceration Trends|NCHS drug poisoning by county
title: Cage or care
idea: County map coloured by whether the response to overdose intensity looks like jail or like treatment capacity, using the double-burden logic already built.
harm_angle: Counties that answer an overdose crisis with jail rather than treatment are choosing to punish sick people.
caveat: CDC county rate is a binned text band with heavy suppression; a mart already implements this comparison so novelty is in the framing.

source_names: Vera Incarceration Trends|CMS opioid treatment providers
title: Jail beds per treatment slot
idea: For each county, the ratio of jail population to registered opioid treatment providers, mapped and ranked.
harm_angle: In treatment deserts the jail becomes the detox ward, and people die in custody.
caveat: CMS provider mart columns unverified from metadata; provider counts need population normalization.

title: Jail rate against county income
idea: County jail rate plotted against income distribution measures, with the racial jail gap as the dot colour.
harm_angle: The clearest single picture of who America cages: poor, and disproportionately Black.
caveat: IRS SOI is ZIP-grain and must be rolled up to counties, which introduces error; ecological fallacy.

source_names: Racial jail disparity mart|MEDSL presidential returns
title: Disparity ratio and county politics
idea: Black-to-white jail population ratio by county against the state's presidential vote pattern over recent cycles.
harm_angle: Racial disparity in jails is not confined to one political geography - the chart tests where it is worst.
caveat: MEDSL presidential returns are state-level, not county-level, so the political axis may not exist at county grain.

title: Federal prison spending per inmate
idea: BOP facility-type populations against contract obligations for prison services, food and healthcare, over time.
harm_angle: Cost per person held is the number nobody publishes plainly.
caveat: BOP mart is 50 aggregate rows; identifying prison-services contracts requires product-code filtering.

source_names: National Inventory of Dams|NTSB aviation events
title: Two Inspection Regimes Compared
idea: Side-by-side comparison of inspection-to-incident intervals in dam and aviation oversight, as a study of how differently federal safety regimes watch their assets.
harm_angle: Shows which hazards the state watches closely and which it watches only after people die.
caveat: Not a real join -- a rhetorical pairing; grains and denominators are not comparable.

source_names: National Inventory of Dams|FEMA IA registrations
title: High-hazard dams above damaged homes
idea: High-hazard-potential dams in poor condition, mapped against counties with heavy flood-damage registrations downstream.
harm_angle: People living below a failing dam are one storm from losing everything, and the record already names the dam.
caveat: Downstream is not the same county as the dam; NID condition fields have heavy nulls and the catalog notes a twin table.

source_names: Freedom in the World|ICE enforcement statistics
title: Sending people back to unfree places
idea: Removals by destination country plotted against that country's freedom score in the same year.
harm_angle: The US may be deporting people into exactly the conditions asylum law exists to prevent.
caveat: Country name normalization; ICE statistics are quarterly aggregates so per-country volumes may be coarse.

source_names: UCDP organized violence events|DHS OHSS encounters
title: Violence there, arrivals here
idea: Country-year conflict deaths against border encounters by citizenship, lagged, to see how fast violence turns into migration.
harm_angle: Treats migration as a consequence of violence rather than a choice, which changes who is at fault.
caveat: Lag selection is analyst choice; OHSS citizenship categories collapse many countries into 'other'.

source_names: Freedom in the World|Vera Incarceration Trends
title: Incarceration rate vs freedom score
idea: US state incarceration rates plotted against national freedom scores worldwide, showing where individual states would rank as countries.
chart_shape: ranked dot plot with country reference lines
harm_angle: Some US states cage people at rates no democracy on the list matches.
caveat: No real join key - this is a rhetorical placement of two scales on one chart.

title: Demographics of who gets confirmed fast
idea: Join judge demographics to the normalized appointment records by nid and show confirmation delay by race, gender and appointing party.
harm_angle: If nominees of color wait systematically longer, the Senate is rationing the bench by identity.
caveat: nid must be confirmed as a clean shared key; the wide judges table also duplicates service fields, so double counting is easy.

source_names: JCS Courts of Appeals ideology|FJC judges
title: Ideology by who appointed them
idea: Match appellate judges by name to the FJC directory and plot lifetime ideology score against appointing president and party.
harm_angle: Shows whether one party's appointees are systematically further from center on the courts that decide most federal appeals.
caveat: Name-only join with no shared id -- fuzzy matching will produce false pairs, especially for common surnames.

title: Private prison contracts vs federal population
idea: Timeline of federal detention contract dollars against the federal inmate population held in private facilities.
harm_angle: Money keeps flowing to private operators even as the population they hold changes.
caveat: The BOP mart has only 50 rows; contract filtering to detention requires product-service or NAICS selection.

title: Judges' holdings vs the cases they hear
idea: Match disclosed financial interests to the corporate parties appearing before the same judges, counting cases heard despite a disclosed interest.
harm_angle: Litigants may face a judge with money riding on the outcome.
caveat: Disclosure content is largely unextracted PDFs (has_been_extracted flag); SCDB party names need matching.

source_names: Judge financial disclosures|Judicial Common Space appellate ideology
title: Wealth and ideology on the appeals bench
idea: Scatter each appellate judge's disclosed asset count against their ideology score, colored by appointing party.
harm_angle: Shows whether the bench deciding people's rights is drawn from one economic stratum.
caveat: Asset count proxied by disclosure page count unless extraction exists; name-match across sources is fragile.

source_names: DOJ False Claims Act settlements|USASpending contracts
title: Fraud settlement, then more contracts
idea: For each False Claims Act defendant, plot the settlement date against subsequent federal contract dollars.
harm_angle: Companies that defrauded the government keep the government as a customer.
caveat: The FCA settlements mart holds only 12 rows, so this is anecdote-scale unless the source is re-ingested.

title: Sentences In vs Population Held
idea: Timeline comparing aggregate federal sentence-months imposed against BOP reported population, showing whether prison growth tracks sentencing or policy.
harm_angle: Prison population growing faster than sentences means people are being held longer for the same conduct.
caveat: BOP mart is 50 summary rows with possibly one snapshot date, so the time axis may not exist on that side.

title: District Court Caseload Balance
idea: Compare criminal and civil case volume and time-to-termination in the same district and year to see whether criminal docket pressure is starving civil plaintiffs of court time.
harm_angle: Civil plaintiffs waiting years because the criminal docket eats the courtroom are denied a remedy by scheduling.
caveat: Both tables use the same district codes but comparability of the two date fields is unverified.

source_names: FJC judicial service records|Supreme Court Database|Judge financial disclosures
title: Tenure, wealth, and rulings
idea: Judge-level grid of years on the bench, disclosed financial complexity, and the direction of their rulings in business cases.
harm_angle: Whether who a judge is predicts who wins in front of them.
caveat: SCDB is Supreme Court only, so overlap with the full FJC roster is small; disclosures are largely unextracted.

title: State AGs Fill the Federal Gap
idea: Timeline of FTC action volume against multistate AG settlement volume by issue area, showing state AGs stepping up exactly when federal enforcement retreats.
harm_angle: When federal enforcement drops and state AGs do not fill it, consumers in those years have no protector at all.
caveat: Issue taxonomies differ entirely between the two sources and must be hand-mapped; FTC mart may be a partial scrape.

source_names: Supreme Court Database|SCOTUS ideology scores|Senate lobbying
title: Business wins at the Court
idea: Timeline of the business-party win rate at the Supreme Court against the Court's ideology median and corporate lobbying volume.
harm_angle: A shift on the bench that quietly changes who wins against a corporation.
caveat: SCDB party-type coding needs interpretation; lobbying data does not cover judicial outcomes directly.

title: Settlement size against ability to pay
idea: Plot each corporate settlement amount as a share of the company's reported assets, ranking the penalties that were rounding errors.
harm_angle: Penalties too small to deter mean the harm is simply a cost of doing business.
caveat: The NAAG mart is a passthrough with unverified columns; defendant-to-filer name matching is needed.

title: Detention contracts and county jail growth
idea: Timeline per county of federal detention-related contract dollars against jail population, marking counties where both rise together.
harm_angle: Federal money can turn a local jail into a revenue center that fills itself.
caveat: Requires filtering contracts to detention by product-service or NAICS code; Vera coverage lags recent years.

source_names: Vera Incarceration Trends|ICE Detention Facility List
title: Counties Renting Beds to ICE
idea: Map counties whose jails report ICE-held population next to the ICE facility list, showing which local jails are formally contracted and which hold quietly.
harm_angle: Counties holding immigrants for federal cash have a financial reason to keep detention full.
caveat: ICE list has city/state only and no county code, so the join is name-based and lossy.

title: Jail Disparity and Lethal Force
idea: Scatter of county Black-to-white jail rate ratio against police killings per capita, testing whether the same counties over-jail and over-kill.
harm_angle: Counties that both jail and kill Black residents disproportionately are running one system with two outputs.
caveat: MPV county column is cast to number on a name field and likely null, so counties must come from lat/lon or ZIP.

source_names: BLS QCEW|NCHS Drug Poisoning by County
title: Job losses before the overdose wave
idea: County timeline of manufacturing employment against overdose death rate, aligned on the employment peak, testing the lag.
harm_angle: Where the work went away, people died, and the lag is measurable.
caveat: QCEW column names unverified; banded death rates; correlation at county grain is not causation.

source_names: BLS QCEW employment and wages|OSHA injury summary
title: Injury rate against the industry wage
idea: Industry scatter of average weekly wage against injuries per 100 workers, showing the lowest-paid work is often the most dangerous.
harm_angle: The people paid least carry the highest physical risk, and the two datasets prove it together.
caveat: NAICS aggregation levels differ; OSHA 300A covers only establishments required to report electronically.

title: Injury reporting coverage by industry
idea: Compare employment counted in wage records against employment covered by injury filings, by industry and state. The gap is who is invisible to the safety system.
harm_angle: Whole industries of workers have no injury record at all because their employers never file.
caveat: The injury program covers only establishments above a size and industry threshold, so part of the gap is by design and must be explained.

title: Underfunding curve into takeover
idea: Plot actuarial funding percentage over time for plans that were later taken over, aligned on takeover year at zero.
harm_angle: The slide toward retirees losing money is visible years ahead in the actuary's own numbers.
caveat: Schedule SB column names unverified; plan number is noted in prior work as a zero-filled trap in some sources.

title: Benefit cuts and injury rates at same firms
idea: Join on tax id to plot change in plan participants against change in injury rate per employer, testing whether cost-cutting and unsafe conditions travel together.
harm_angle: The same squeeze that cuts benefits also takes the guardrails off the floor.
caveat: Both tax id columns need distinct-count verification; the Form 5500 slice may be small.

title: Plan assets against the backstop's exposure
idea: State-level map comparing Form 5500 plan asset totals to insured-participant counts, showing states where the pension backstop carries the most concentrated risk.
harm_angle: Concentrated backstop exposure means whole regional workforces sharing one point of failure.
caveat: Form 5500 is only a ~33k-row partial slice; PBGC state rows exist only for some tables, so the overlap may be small.

source_names: Form 5500 pension filings|PBGC pension insurance data
title: Plans that went to the PBGC
idea: Timeline of plan terminations landing at the PBGC, with participant counts, showing which industries dumped the most workers' pensions.
harm_angle: Workers' promised retirement cut to a federal maximum they never agreed to.
caveat: The PBGC mart shows only STATE as a standard key; EIN presence there is unverified.

title: Warning signs before a pension collapses
idea: For plans the pension insurer eventually took over, chart funding-related filing values in the years before takeover against plans that survived.
harm_angle: Retirees lose benefits after years of warning signs sitting in public filings.
caveat: Form 5500 mart is only 33k rows, likely a slice; plan number field needed for a clean join and is unverified.

source_names: DOL OFLC Foreign Labor Certification|BLS QCEW
title: Certified wages against local prevailing wage
idea: By industry and county, scatter certified guest-worker wage offers against actual average weekly wages. Offers below the local average are the wage-suppression signal.
harm_angle: Guest workers are certified at wages that pull the local floor down for everyone.
caveat: Certification column names unverified; wage units must be normalized.

source_names: OFLC labor certifications|OSHA injury case detail
title: Visa-dependent workers and injuries
idea: By employer and industry, plot certified guest-worker volume against the injury case rate at the same establishments.
harm_angle: Workers who cannot quit without losing status may be the ones getting hurt.
caveat: Employer names differ between the two systems; the case detail mart's column names are unverified.

title: Federal contractors relying on guest labor
idea: Rank federal contractors by certified guest-worker positions per contract dollar, matched by employer name.
harm_angle: Public contracts are performed by workers who cannot quit without losing status.
caveat: Name matching only; employer names differ between the two systems.

source_names: DOL OLMS union filings|OSHA injury summary
title: Union presence and injury rates
idea: By industry and state, compare reported injury rates at establishments in heavily unionized sectors against weakly unionized ones.
harm_angle: Whether a worker's chance of getting hurt depends on having a union.
caveat: OLMS filings identify unions, not employers, so the link to establishments is industry-level only.

title: Injury rates where unions exist
idea: Match employers to union presence via union filings by employer name, then compare injury rate distributions between covered and uncovered establishments in the same industry.
harm_angle: Whether a worker has a union may be the difference in whether they get hurt.
caveat: Union employer coverage is partial and name-based; industry controls are essential or the result is meaningless.

source_names: FEC contributions|DOL OLMS union filings|BLS QCEW
title: Union density vs donor concentration
idea: State scatter of union membership share against the share of political money coming from the top 1 percent of donors.
harm_angle: Where collective bargaining is weakest, political money is most concentrated.
caveat: OLMS membership rollups by state are unverified; donor concentration requires careful de-duplication.

title: Injury rate per worker-hour by operator
idea: Chain the three files to compute injuries per employee-hour by operator, then rank operators and show their unpaid penalty balance alongside.
harm_angle: The operators hurting the most miners per hour worked are identifiable by name.
caveat: Employment fields are periodic snapshots; hours must be reconstructed and may be wrong.

source_names: MSHA Mine Accidents & Injuries|MSHA Mine Safety Violations
title: Did the citation come before the injury
idea: Timeline per mine plotting violations and injuries on the same axis, showing mines cited for a hazard that then injured someone in the same category.
harm_angle: An injury after a warning about the same hazard is a preventable one.
caveat: Matching a violation standard to an injury source requires a hand-built mapping; both date fields carry parsing risk.

source_names: MSHA Mines|Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
title: Mining counties and what happened after
idea: County map of mine closures overlaid with subsequent employment and wage trajectories, showing which mining counties recovered and which never did.
harm_angle: Counties where the mine closed and employment never came back are places abandoned by both industry and policy.
caveat: The MSHA county FIPS is cast with try_to_number in the model, which strips leading zeros and will break the join to the QCEW text FIPS.

title: Fatality rate by controller and commodity
idea: Ranked bars of fatalities per thousand employees by controlling company, split coal versus metal, naming the operators with the deadliest records.
harm_angle: Names the corporate parents whose miners die most often.
caveat: Employment is a snapshot not exposure hours; controller attribution is current-only so historic deaths get assigned to today's owner.

title: Violations per employee by mine
idea: Map of mines sized by violations per employee rather than raw violation count, which surfaces small dangerous operations that raw counts bury.
harm_angle: Small mines with high per-worker violation rates are the most dangerous places to work and the least watched.
caveat: Employee counts are a current snapshot while violations span decades; the ratio mixes time frames.

title: Mining counties' mortality premium
idea: Compare age-adjusted mortality in counties with active mines against comparable non-mining counties with similar wages.
harm_angle: The health cost of extraction paid by everyone in the county, not just the workers.
caveat: The CDC WONDER mart is state by ICD chapter (880 rows), so county-level comparison may not be possible.

title: Violations before the fatality
idea: For every fatal mine accident, chart the violation history of that mine in the preceding 24 months, aligned to the accident date at zero.
harm_angle: Miners die at mines that were already cited repeatedly for the same hazards.
caveat: Whether the violation and accident types can be matched to the same hazard is unverified.

title: Operators who pay fines vs operators who pay politics
idea: Per mine controller, unpaid penalty balance and injury count against political contributions from employees naming the operator.
harm_angle: Miners keep getting hurt at operators whose money goes to campaigns instead of penalties.
caveat: Controller and violator naming is inconsistent; employer name match to donor records is lossy.

title: Penalties assessed versus paid
idea: Per operator, plot proposed penalty against amount actually paid over time. The growing wedge between the two lines is uncollected accountability.
harm_angle: Mines rack up fines they never pay and keep operating with the same hazards.
caveat: Amount fields may include partial payments and appeals; the wedge could be timing, not evasion.

title: Three Year Injury Rate Trajectories
idea: Slope chart per establishment of injury rate across 2023, 2024 and 2025, isolating workplaces that got sharply more dangerous and ones whose numbers suddenly went clean.
harm_angle: A workplace whose injury rate doubled without any enforcement response is a group of workers being left in a known hazard.
caveat: Establishment id stability across annual files is unverified; a renumbered establishment would look like a new site.

title: Injury rates that fall too fast
idea: For establishments present in all three years, chart injury rate per 100 workers as a slope. Steep drops without a change in hours are the reporting-suppression signal.
harm_angle: Injury numbers that improve on paper without changing on the floor hide real harm.
caveat: Establishment ids may be reassigned year to year; the 2025 file may be partial.

title: Industry injury rate vs wage
idea: Scatter industry injury rate against average weekly wage by industry code, sized by employment. The bottom-right quadrant is dangerous and badly paid.
harm_angle: The most dangerous jobs are also the worst paid, and the same workers take both.
caveat: QCEW column names unverified; industry code digit level must be aligned between the sources.

source_names: OSHA ITA 300A|Federal Audit Clearinghouse Single Audits
title: Grant recipients with unsafe workplaces
idea: Join on tax id to link organizations receiving federal grants to their own injury filings, ranked by injuries per employee.
harm_angle: Federally funded organizations injure their own staff and keep the money.
caveat: OSHA tax id fill rate unverified; audit file column names unverified.

title: Summary Totals Versus Case Counts
idea: Scatter of each establishment's reported summary totals against the number of individual cases it actually filed, with the off-diagonal points being reporting mismatches.
harm_angle: An employer reporting fewer detailed cases than its own summary claims has injuries that exist on one form and not the other.
caveat: The case-detail file is row-capped, which will manufacture false mismatches unless the cap is accounted for.

source_names: OSHA ITA 300A Summary|OSHA ITA Case Detail
title: Establishments reporting zero injuries
idea: Compare each establishment's summary claim of no injuries against the presence of individual case records with the same establishment id. Contradictions are under-reporting.
harm_angle: Workers get hurt at places that officially report a clean record.
caveat: establishment_id stability across the two files is unverified; the summary flag may be legitimately true.

title: Federal contractors with worst safety records
idea: Match employers via tax id or entity id, then rank federal contractors by injury and fatality rate against contract dollars received.
harm_angle: The government keeps buying from employers whose own filings show workers dying.
caveat: USASpending carries entity ids not tax ids; the bridge likely needs a name match or the audit file.

title: Repeat Hazard Employers Across Years
idea: Ranked bars of employers producing the same predicted injury event type in all three years, the clearest signal of a hazard nobody fixed.
harm_angle: Three straight years of the same accident at the same site means the harm is a management choice, not bad luck.
caveat: All three case-detail marts appear row-capped (500k, 500k, 330k), so an employer may be missing purely due to truncation.

source_names: OSHA ITA Case Detail|DOL OFLC Foreign Labor Certification
title: Injuries at guest-worker employers
idea: Match employers by name and zip across injury cases and foreign-labor certifications, then compare injury severity distributions between certified and non-certified employers in the same industry.
harm_angle: Visa workers who cannot change employers may be absorbing the worst injuries.
caveat: Name and zip matching only; both files list employers differently, so false pairs are likely.

title: Pension dumps and shareholder returns
idea: Event-time chart of a company's institutional holdings and reported financials around the date its pension plan went to the PBGC.
harm_angle: Retirees' losses converting into shareholder gains, visible on one timeline.
caveat: The PBGC mart exposes only STATE as a standard key; the CUSIP hop has no id bridge in the warehouse.

title: Pandemic loans and workplace injuries
idea: Match employers by name and address, then compare injury rates at loan recipients that kept headcount against those that did not.
harm_angle: Employers paid to keep people employed may have kept them in unsafe conditions.
caveat: Name and address matching across two very different files; self-reported job counts are unreliable.

title: Pension funding vs company scale
idea: For public filers, plot plan net assets and participant counts against the company's size, ranking the most underfunded relative to peers.
harm_angle: Retirees' security quietly eroding inside companies that look healthy.
caveat: Form 5500 sponsor EIN vs SEC EIN may differ (the plan sponsor is often a subsidiary); the 33k-row mart may be a partial year.

source_names: SEC financial statement data|OSHA injury summary
title: Public companies' injury rate vs profit
idea: Scatter each filer's reported financial scale against the injury rate at its establishments, joined on EIN.
harm_angle: Shareholders see the earnings; workers absorb the cost that never appears on the statement.
caveat: EIN in the SEC DERA sub file is often blank or formatted differently from OSHA's; both need normalization.

source_names: Senate lobbying disclosures|MSHA mine safety violations
title: Mining lobby spend vs unpaid penalties
idea: Timeline of mining-sector lobbying spend overlaid on the share of MSHA proposed penalties that were never paid, by year.
harm_angle: Miners keep getting hurt while the fines meant to deter it go uncollected.
caveat: Name-matching mine operators to lobbying clients is lossy; controller vs violator naming differs.

title: Lobbying dollars vs worker injury rate
idea: By industry, plot lobbying spend on labor and workplace-safety issues against the industry's reported injury and death totals per hours worked.
harm_angle: The industries hurting the most workers may be the ones paying most to keep the rules soft.
caveat: LDA filings have no NAICS; industry must be inferred from client name. Injury data is self-reported and one filing year at a time.

title: Contractors importing cheaper labor
idea: Compare federal contract dollars per employer against their volume of guest-worker certification requests and the offered wage relative to prevailing wage.
harm_angle: Public contracts subsidize employers who suppress the wage floor for everyone in the trade.
caveat: Name-matching only; wage columns in the OFLC mart unverified.

title: Federal contractors that hurt workers
idea: Rank the largest federal contractors by injury rate per 100 workers, sized by federal dollars received, so the worst safety records with the biggest checks stand out.
harm_angle: The government pays companies that injure their own workers and never links the two records.
caveat: USASpending has no EIN, so the join is name- or NAICS-based; OSHA 300A EIN may be sparse or masked.

title: Nonprofit Sponsors Who Failed Pensions
idea: Join on EIN to see whether nonprofit sponsors whose pensions failed kept filing and operating afterwards.
harm_angle: An employer that survives while its workers pensions do not is the accountability gap itself.
caveat: PBGC EIN fill rate and format unverified, and most sponsors are for-profit and absent from 990s.

title: Deaths at work, charges never filed
idea: Mines with fatal accidents and repeat serious violations, checked against whether any federal criminal case appears in that district and period.
harm_angle: Killing a worker through repeated violations rarely produces a criminal defendant.
caveat: No direct key links a mine to a criminal case; absence of a match is not proof of no prosecution.

title: Which deaths get covered
idea: Media coverage volume around each police-killing date and location against the victim's race, age and armed status.
harm_angle: Whose death becomes news, and whose disappears, is itself a form of harm.
caveat: GDELT mart is a 1,015-row file manifest, not events - this probably cannot be built from what is modeled.

source_names: California lobbying cover pages|California lobbyist contributions|California lobbyist employers
title: California employers behind the lobbyists
idea: Network of lobbyist employers to the firms they hire to the campaign contributions those lobbyists made, showing which industries dominate Sacramento.
harm_angle: State policy in the largest state economy shaped by a small, mostly invisible client list.
caveat: Passthrough marts; column names unverified. Employer and firm link tables are tiny (170-1730 rows) so coverage may be partial.

title: The committee web behind one candidate
idea: Network for a chosen candidate showing every linked committee, its type and designation, and its connected organization.
harm_angle: Shows how many legal vehicles surround one name on a ballot.
caveat: The FED_FEC_COMMITTEES and FED_FEC_CANDIDATES marts have unnamed c1-c15 columns; the fed_fec_bulk_* versions must be used instead.

title: Cosponsorship follows the check
idea: Event-time chart centered on a PAC contribution date, showing the rate at which the recipient cosponsors that industry's bills in the weeks before and after.
harm_angle: Turns a vague influence claim into a measurable before-and-after timing pattern.
caveat: Cosponsor date column presence unverified; PAC industry classification is not in the data.

source_names: FEC committee-to-candidate|Voteview roll-call votes|Congress legislators directory
title: Industry PAC money vs the vote
idea: For a given roll-call, plot each member's PAC receipts from the affected industry against how they voted, sorted so the money gradient across yes and no is visible.
harm_angle: Puts a price tag next to a vote that changed what people pay or breathe.
caveat: Requires the FEC-id-to-bioguide-to-ICPSR crosswalk to be well populated; industry tagging of PACs is not in the data and must be added.

source_names: FEC itemized individual contributions|BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
title: Donor dollars per worker by county
idea: County map of itemized political giving divided by total employment, showing which counties punch far above their economic weight in political money.
harm_angle: Political voice concentrates in a few wealthy counties while working counties are silent.
caveat: ZIP-to-county mapping is not in either source; would need a crosswalk. QCEW grain (industry x quarter) unverified.

source_names: FEC itemized individual contributions|Congress legislators directory
title: Who funds a member from outside the district
idea: For each member, the share of itemized individual dollars coming from outside their own state, ranked, with district poverty as a shading.
harm_angle: Constituents are outbid by out-of-state money in their own representation.
caveat: 84M-row table; needs the committee-to-candidate linkage to attribute donations to members. Donor state may be blank on many rows.

source_names: FEC leadership PAC sponsors|Congress committee membership
title: Leadership PACs and gavel power
idea: Rank members by leadership-PAC receipts and mark who holds a chair or ranking-member title, showing whether the gavel is where the slush money goes.
harm_angle: Committee power converts directly into a personal political war chest.
caveat: Needs the FEC-to-bioguide crosswalk; leadership PAC mart column names unverified.

title: Charities that lobby heavily
idea: Rank tax-exempt filers by lobbying spend appearing in lobbying filings against their filing size band, exposing charities functioning as trade groups.
harm_angle: Tax-subsidized entities buying policy that costs the public more than the subsidy.
caveat: The 990 index is an index only (no financial fields); lobbying client names must be name-matched to EINs.

source_names: IRS Statistics of Income (ZIP level)|FEC contributions
title: Political giving per dollar of income
idea: ZIP-level map of itemized political contributions divided by aggregate adjusted gross income, showing where money is most politically active.
harm_angle: Political voice tracks wealth geography almost perfectly, and the map proves it.
caveat: SOI ZIP data is aggregated and suppressed for small ZIPs; FEC ZIP fields include ZIP+4 variants.

source_names: Senate lobbying disclosures|Congress committee membership|FEC committee-to-candidate transfers
title: Committee seat, lobby target, PAC check
idea: Three-step chain: lobbying filings naming a committee as the government entity contacted, the members who sit on that committee, and the PAC dollars those members received in the same cycle.
harm_angle: Shows whether the members with jurisdiction over an industry are the ones its PACs pay.
caveat: government_entities is a free-text list; needs parsing. Member-to-FEC-candidate id bridge lives in a separate crosswalk model and may be partial.

source_names: Senate lobbying disclosures|FEC itemized individual contributions
title: Lobby firms that also bundle donations
idea: For each lobbying registrant, plot total reported lobbying income against the total campaign dollars given by donors listing that firm as employer, revealing firms that buy access twice.
harm_angle: The same handful of shops move both the policy ask and the campaign cash that softens the target.
caveat: Employer field is free text and dirty; name-matching lobby registrants to donor employers will need heavy normalization.

title: Lobbying spend against bill fate
idea: Plot quarterly federal lobbying dollars reported against a bill's subject area next to whether the bill ever moved past introduction, so the viewer sees which subjects get money and which get action.
harm_angle: Bills that would protect people die quietly in the subjects where industry spends the most.
caveat: No shared id: lobbying issue codes must be text-matched to bill subjects; income vs expenses split by registrant type is unverified.

source_names: Senate STOCK Act trades|Congress committee membership
title: Senators trading their own jurisdiction
idea: For each senator, the share of disclosed trades in sectors their committees oversee, ranked, with trade timing relative to committee hearings.
harm_angle: Lawmakers may profit from information the public paid them to act on.
caveat: Name-only source with no bioguide id; coverage ends Dec 2020 and legal terms restrict use to journalism.

source_names: Senate STOCK Act trades|SEC ticker map|USASpending contracts
title: Senator trades in federal contractors
idea: Chain a senator's disclosed trade to the company's ticker to its federal contract flow, showing trades placed ahead of award surges.
harm_angle: Public officials may position ahead of the spending they help authorize.
caveat: Ticker-to-contractor-name link is name-based and lossy; trade amounts are ranges, not values.

title: Does money follow the extremes
idea: Scatter each member's ideology score against total receipts, by cycle, testing whether polarization pays.
harm_angle: If extremism raises more money, the incentive structure explains the dysfunction people live with.
caveat: Crosswalk completeness unverified; receipts must be aligned to the right cycle.

title: Political Groups Wearing Charity Hats
idea: Join on EIN to find 527 political organizations that also hold a 501(c) exempt registration.
harm_angle: Dark-money groups holding both statuses can take undisclosed donations and route them politically.
caveat: EIN formats differ between files (dashes, padding) and may not join without cleaning.

source_names: IRS 527 registrations|527 directors and officers|IRS exempt org master file
title: Officers running many 527s at once
idea: Network of directors and officers to the multiple political organizations they control, sized by each organization's reported spending.
key_fields: EIN|org name|officer name|ADDRESS|organization name|ruling date|NTEE code
harm_angle: A handful of operators can spin up unlimited political vehicles with no accountability.
caveat: Officer names are free text with no id; EIN overlap between 527s and the business master file may be limited.

title: The 527 money that never hits FEC
idea: Compare 527 organizations' reported contributions and expenditures against the subset that also file with the FEC, sizing the disclosure gap.
harm_angle: A whole channel of election money sits outside the system people think covers it.
caveat: The 8872 mart is a passthrough with unverified columns; there is no shared id with FEC committee ids.

title: Officers Behind The Biggest Money
idea: Join on EIN and form id to rank individuals by total contributions flowing through every 527 they officer.
harm_angle: Puts a name on the aggregate dark money one person controls across separate groups.
caveat: Requires a clean EIN join plus name normalization, and amendments may double count.

title: City donors who also give federally
idea: Compare the donor base of NYC municipal races across cycles and the overlap with federal giving from the same names and addresses.
harm_angle: A small overlapping donor class shaping both city services and federal law.
caveat: Name plus ZIP matching produces false positives; the NYC marts' column names are unverified.

source_names: Texas lobby report cover sheets|Texas lobby food and beverage|Texas lobby gifts
title: What Texas lobbyists actually buy
idea: Break total reported Texas lobby spending into its schedules (food, gifts, entertainment, transportation) and rank the registrants by the hospitality share of their spend.
harm_angle: State-level access bought in small dinners never shows up in federal disclosure.
caveat: Mart is a passthrough to staging; exact column names unverified. Schedules may not share a joinable report key across all tables.

title: Banking Deserts Across Both Systems
idea: Map ZIPs with neither an FDIC-insured institution nor a credit union, marking the places with no mainstream depository at all.
harm_angle: A ZIP with no bank and no credit union is a ZIP served entirely by check cashers and payday lenders.
