caveat: FDIC mart is a 10,000-row slice, so absence there is not evidence of absence; both list headquarters, not branches.

source_names: FJC Bankruptcy Cases|IRS Statistics of Income
title: Bankruptcy Where Income Fell
idea: Map ZIPs by bankruptcy filings per return alongside average AGI change, showing the neighborhoods where income loss turns into legal insolvency.
harm_angle: Bankruptcy clusters in falling-income ZIPs are households that ran out of runway, not people gaming the system.
caveat: Bankruptcy debtor ZIPs may be truncated for privacy; SOI ZIP cells are suppressed below thresholds.

source_names: IRS Statistics of Income|CFPB Consumer Complaints
title: Debt Complaints Where Income Is Lowest
idea: Scatter of ZIP-level average AGI against debt-collection complaint rate, showing that collection pressure concentrates where people have least.
harm_angle: Debt collectors work hardest in the ZIPs least able to pay, which is how small debts become garnishments.
caveat: CFPB ZIPs are often masked to three digits; SOI suppresses small ZIP cells; both need per-capita normalization.

source_names: SEC Insider Submissions|SEC Financial Statement Data Sets
title: Insider Selling by Industry
idea: Heatmap of SIC industry against insider net selling value, joining insider filings to filer industry, showing which sectors' executives are heading for the exit.
harm_angle: Sector-wide insider selling ahead of a downturn is information workers and small investors never get.
caveat: CIK formatting differs between sources (zero-padding) and must be normalized; both marts may be partial loads.

title: The Full Insider Trade Picture
idea: Join the three insider tables into one view and plot each named executive's trades against their company on a timeline, which is the only way any of these tables becomes readable.
harm_angle: Naming the executive, the company and the dollar amount together is what turns a filing into accountability.
caveat: All three are a single 2025Q1 slice; accession_number join is documented in the models but its population was not verified here.

title: Foreign Agents Who Also Donate
idea: Match FARA registrant names against itemised donor names and employer strings to find people paid by foreign governments who also give to US campaigns.
harm_angle: A person paid by a foreign government donating to the legislators who vote on that government's interests is influence with two receipts.
caveat: Name-only matching across 84M donor rows will produce heavy false positives; employer text is uncontrolled.

title: Corporate Parent To Legislator Flow
idea: Sankey money from connected organisations through their sponsored committees to individual candidates, collapsing the PAC layer to show who actually funds whom.
harm_angle: Collapsing the PAC layer shows a voter which corporation is funding their representative, which no single filing reveals.
caveat: connected_org_nm fill rate is unverified and blank for many committees; name normalisation needed to group parents.

source_names: FEC Individual Contributions|FEC Candidate Financial Summary
title: Reported Total Versus Itemised Sum
idea: For each candidate, compare the reported total individual contributions against the sum of itemised individual contributions to their committees, showing the unitemised gap.
harm_angle: The unitemised gap is money whose donors are legally invisible - the larger it grows, the less disclosure means.
caveat: Requires the linkage file to connect committees to candidates, and 2026 linkage resolution is described as only ~57%.

source_names: SEC Insider Trading Reports|Senate Stock Watcher
title: Senators Trading Where Insiders Sold
idea: Match senator trades to insider filings by ticker and date window to find cases where a senator traded the same stock in the same week as company insiders.
harm_angle: A senator trading alongside company insiders is either coincidence or shared non-public information, and only the data can start to tell them apart.
caveat: Senate coverage stops Dec 2020 and carries only amount bands; the insider mart has no transaction amount, so both sides are half-blind.

title: Revoked But Still Listed
idea: Join on EIN to find organizations still carrying an active BMF status after appearing on the revocation list.
harm_angle: Donors giving to a revoked charity lose their deduction and the cause loses the money.
caveat: BMF is a snapshot, so lag between the two files may explain most mismatches.

title: Enabler Volume Ranked Properly
idea: Join edges to intermediary nodes to rank law firms by the actual number of offshore entities they created.
harm_angle: Ranks the professional enablers by the real size of the machine they built.
caveat: Edge duplication across leaks inflates counts without dedup.

title: People Behind The Most Shells
idea: Join edges to officer nodes to find individuals controlling the largest number of offshore entities.
harm_angle: Names the humans, not the shells, at the centre of the offshore web.
caveat: Officer identity is name-based, so the same person may hold many node ids.

source_names: FBI NICS Firearm Background Checks|Washington Post Fatal Force
title: Gun prevalence against armed-encounter deaths
idea: State-level scatter of background checks per capita against the share of police killings where the person was armed with a gun.
harm_angle: Higher gun circulation may change how every police encounter begins.
caveat: Checks are not sales and neither table carries population; state key formats differ between the two sources.

source_names: Mapping Police Violence|FBI Crime Data Explorer
title: Killings vs reported crime
idea: State-by-state rate of police killings against reported violent-crime and clearance rates, showing that the two do not track.
harm_angle: Deadly force is not explained by how much crime there is, which points at policy instead.
caveat: FBI CDE is estimates with uneven agency reporting; ORI availability in MPV is flagged 'if available'.

title: What one database sees and the other misses
idea: Overlay the two death counts by state and year and show the gap: cases in one and not the other, by race and by agency.
join_key: victim name + date, or WaPo id
harm_angle: The count of people police kill depends on who is counting - undercounting hides whole categories of death.
caveat: Name-and-date matching is fuzzy; MPV includes non-shooting deaths WaPo excludes by design.

source_names: Washington Post Fatal Force|FBI Crime Data Explorer
title: Police killings against violent crime rate
idea: Scatter of state police-killing count against state violent-crime rate, one dot per state, testing whether states that kill more are the states with more violent crime.
harm_angle: States that kill at high rates without high crime rates are killing for other reasons.
caveat: Fatal Force needs a population denominator this pair does not carry; state name versus abbreviation formats differ.

source_names: WaPo Fatal Force|ATF federal firearms licensees
title: Gun density and armed encounters
idea: County gun-dealer density plotted against police-killing rates and the share of victims recorded as armed.
harm_angle: Tests the officer-safety argument against where guns actually are.
caveat: ATF county field is a licensing code, not FIPS; dealer counts are a weak proxy for gun prevalence.

title: The same counties do both
idea: County dots: Black jail incarceration rate against the per-capita rate of police killings of Black residents, with the diagonal marking counties extreme on both.
harm_angle: Identifies the places where Black residents face both the highest cage rate and the highest chance of being killed.
caveat: MPV has no county FIPS - it must be derived from city/zip; classic ecological fallacy risk.

title: Spending and Giving From the Same Filer
idea: Scatter of an employer's lobbying spend against contributions its lobbyists made in the same period, showing who pairs money with access.
harm_angle: Paying for access and writing the officeholder a check in the same quarter is the mechanism, stated plainly.
caveat: Contributions has only 6505 rows and joins on filer_id, whose relationship to employer_id is unverified — the two id spaces may not be the same.

title: Firm Revenue Versus Disclosed Clients
idea: Compare each firm's session total against the sum of its disclosed per-client billings, showing revenue that has no client attached to it.
harm_angle: Money a firm reports earning but never attributes to a client is influence bought by someone the public cannot name.
caveat: The firm-employer table has only 170 rows against 256 firms, so most firms will show a huge unexplained gap that is a data-completeness artifact, not a finding.

title: Spending History Lost To Renaming
idea: Follow the advertiser id remapping chain into the advertiser stats table to reconstruct spending histories that appear broken across identity changes.
harm_angle: An advertiser whose spending record resets on rename escapes the scrutiny its total spend would attract.
caveat: The remap table has no dates, so the direction and timing of identity changes must be inferred.

title: Twenty-four years of NYC money
idea: Stack all five cycles into one panel and chart the shift in donor geography, small-dollar share and bundling across a quarter century of city elections.
harm_angle: Watching the same city's money move over 24 years shows whether the matching-funds programme actually broadened who funds politics or not.
caveat: Column layouts differ between cycles (2001 has candidate_id and candidate_last_name where later cycles have recipient_id and recipient_name); the 2009 and 2013 layouts were not read and may differ again.

source_names: TEC lobby cover sheets|TEC subject matter
title: Dollars Attached To Issues
idea: Join on report id to attribute cover-sheet expenditure totals to the subject matters each report covers.
harm_angle: Shows which policy areas absorb the most lobby money and therefore whose interests get outspent.
caveat: Reports list many subjects, so dollars must be split or duplicated and either choice distorts.

title: Cover Totals Versus Schedule Detail
idea: Compare each report declared category totals against the sum of its itemized schedule rows to find under-itemized filings.
harm_angle: Filings whose detail does not add up to the total are where disclosure quietly fails.
caveat: Range-reported amounts have no exact value, so gaps may be legal rather than evasive.

title: Cosponsorship and electoral safety
idea: Members' cosponsorship of civil-rights and criminal-justice bills against their district's winning margin.
harm_angle: Whether representatives only defend rights when their seat is safe.
caveat: Bill-topic classification is not in the mart; candidate-to-bioguide matching needed for the returns side.

title: Oversight committee, home-state facility
idea: Members of the committees that oversee DHS, matched to detention facilities in their own states, with detained-days volume.
harm_angle: The people who fund detention rarely have to look at it.
caveat: Committee membership is current-only; district-level facility assignment needs geocoding.

title: Debarred companies still getting paid
idea: Timeline of contract obligations to recipients whose entity id appears on the debarment list, with the exclusion window shaded.
harm_angle: Public money keeps flowing to companies the government already banned.
caveat: Entity id fill rate in the exclusion file unverified; subsidiaries can hold separate ids, which is the loophole itself.

title: SBIR mills that never graduate
idea: Rank firms by number of SBIR awards against subsequent non-SBIR federal contract dollars, exposing serial grant winners that never commercialize.
harm_angle: Innovation money captured by professional applicants instead of reaching working products.
caveat: SBIR mart columns unverified; company name join across sources is lossy.

title: Fund exposure to federal contracting
idea: Rank institutional managers by the share of their portfolio in companies whose revenue depends on federal contracts.
harm_angle: Shows whose retirement savings quietly ride on the defense and detention budget.
caveat: No CUSIP-to-CIK key exists in the warehouse; requires name matching at two hops.

title: Return on a lobbying dollar
idea: Per company, lobbying spend on one axis and federal contract obligations two years later on the other, sized by how often the award was non-competed.
harm_angle: Public money flowing to whoever can afford the lobbying that shapes the solicitation.
caveat: Name-only join; parent vs subsidiary naming will split totals. Contract mart row count is blank in the catalog.

source_names: USASpending contracts|Federal Audit Clearinghouse single audits
title: Failed audits, renewed contracts
idea: For entities with a disclosed material weakness or going-concern finding, plot federal dollars received in the following two years against those without findings.
harm_angle: Audit failures carry no consequence, so the money keeps flowing regardless of performance.
caveat: Single audits mostly cover grantees and nonprofits, so overlap with prime contractors may be thin.

title: Contractor employees' political giving
idea: For the top federal contractors, plot contract dollars against donations from employees naming that company, split by party.
harm_angle: Shows whether the biggest recipients of public money also fund the people who appropriate it.
caveat: Employer text is messy; company name variants will fragment totals.

title: Debarred and still getting paid
idea: Timeline per entity of contract obligations with the debarment window shaded, counting dollars awarded during an active exclusion.
harm_angle: Taxpayers keep funding contractors the government formally banned.
caveat: UEI population in older USASpending rows (pre-2022 DUNS era) is likely sparse; exclusions cover the entity, not always its subsidiaries.

title: Where the prime money actually lands
idea: Sankey from awarding agency to prime contractor to sub-recipient, showing how much of each program's money is passed through versus retained.
harm_angle: Pass-through layers hide who really delivers the service people depend on.
caveat: Sub-awards mart holds only 5000 rows, so coverage is a fraction of prime awards.

title: Sub-recipients nobody audits
idea: Count sub-award dollars going to entities that never appear in the single-audit system despite crossing the audit threshold.
harm_angle: Money passed one layer down escapes the only audit regime that would catch misuse.
caveat: The sub-awards mart holds only 5000 rows; EIN formatting differs between the two sources.

title: Screened entities receiving federal money
idea: Cross the federal consolidated screening list against contract and assistance recipients, plotting matched dollars by agency.
harm_angle: The government's own watchlist may not be wired into its own checkbook.
caveat: Name-match only; the screening list includes many non-blocking lists so matches need list-type filtering.

source_names: OFAC SDN list|NOAA nationwide AIS vessel tracks
title: Sanctioned vessels in US waters
idea: Map AIS tracks for IMO numbers appearing on the SDN list, showing port calls after the designation date.
harm_angle: Sanctioned shipping moving cargo through US waters unchallenged.
caveat: AIS imo_number was previously found roughly 56 percent sentinel-masked on this platform; SDN vessel IMO coverage is small.

source_names: OFAC SDN list|UK Companies House register
title: Sanctioned names on the UK register
idea: Screen the UK company register against OFAC-designated names and map the postcodes where matched companies cluster.
harm_angle: Sanctioned actors keep operating through ordinary-looking companies with real bank accounts.
caveat: Name-only join; huge false-positive risk on common names. The SDN mart exposes few named columns in the model.

source_names: EU sanctions list|UK sanctions list|OFAC SDN
title: Where the three regimes disagree
idea: Comparison of who is sanctioned by the US, UK, and EU, ranked to highlight names appearing on only one list.
harm_angle: Gaps between regimes are the escape hatch a designated actor uses.
caveat: Transliteration differences make cross-list name matching genuinely hard; listing-date columns unverified.

source_names: OpenSanctions default collection|UK Companies House PSC (beneficial owners)
title: Sanctioned people behind UK companies
idea: Match persons with significant control against the consolidated sanctions list and show the ownership network fanning out from each hit.
key_fields: sanctioned name|country|birth date|PSC name|nationality|company number|ownership percent
harm_angle: Beneficial-ownership rules exist precisely to catch this and are apparently not catching it.
caveat: PSC mart is a passthrough with unverified columns; 7M rows on a name join is expensive and noisy.

title: Transatlantic Designation Lag
idea: For targets appearing on both lists, plot the gap between the US start date and the EU publication date, showing who acts first and by how long.
harm_angle: Every week of lag between allied jurisdictions is a week the target has to move assets out of reach.
caveat: Name-only join across transliterations; the EU mart's denormalised grain means the earliest publication date per entity must be picked carefully.

title: Where US And UK Sanctions Diverge
idea: Match vessels by IMO number across the two lists to show ships sanctioned by one country and not the other - the gaps a fleet can sail through.
chart_shape: paired ranked bars with vessel detail
harm_angle: A ship sanctioned in Washington but not London can still load, insure and deliver - the gap is the loophole.
caveat: The OFAC IMO is described as derived and the UK IMO fill rate is unverified - both need a distinct-value check before trusting the join.

title: Debarred At Home Screened Abroad
idea: Match debarred federal contractors against export-screening entries by name to find entities banned on both fronts, plotted by agency and date.
harm_angle: An entity banned twice over that still holds contracts or export licences is an enforcement failure with a paper trail.
caveat: Name matching only - no shared id exists; false positives from common company names are likely.

title: What The US List Misses
idea: Compare the consolidated OpenSanctions universe against the US screening list by name to quantify how much of the global watchlist has no US counterpart.
harm_angle: Targets on every other country's list but not the US one can move money through the largest financial system in the world.
caveat: Name-only join across transliterations; OpenSanctions already ingests the US list so overlap accounting must avoid circularity.

title: Research institutions with audit problems
idea: Rank research institutions by NIH and other federal dollars received against their single-audit findings history.
harm_angle: Public research money concentrated in institutions repeatedly flagged for control failures.
caveat: UEI population in the NIH mart is unverified (the catalog lists DUNS and UEI as standard keys).

title: Retractions per registered institution
idea: Match retraction institution names to the ROR registry and map retraction counts per institution against the institution's country and type.
harm_angle: Naming institutions properly, with their type and country attached, separates systemic integrity failures from individual bad actors.
caveat: Institution names in Retraction Watch are free text in a delimited list; matching to ROR needs alias-aware fuzzy matching and will be imperfect.

title: Organisations that are also funders
idea: Join ROR's FundRef identifier to the Crossref funder registry and chart which research organisations also appear as funders, by country and type.
harm_angle: Institutions that both fund and perform research sit on both sides of their own review process.
caveat: fundref_id fill rate in ROR is unverified; the URI formats may need normalising before they match.

title: Grant Money to Published Science
idea: Link NIH awards to preprints citing the funder and award, and plot dollars against output and time to publication by institution.
join_key: award number in preprint funding metadata
harm_angle: Public money that produces nothing readable is research the public paid for and never got.
caveat: The preprint mart is a 432-row sample and funder award strings are messy free text - the join will be very lossy.

title: Credibility Of Invasive Records
idea: Heatmap grid of jurisdiction against credibility rating for introduced-origin taxa, showing where invasion records rest on weak evidence.
harm_angle: Weakly-evidenced invasion records drive real eradication spending and real restrictions on farmers and fishers.
caveat: Credibility rating fill rate is unverified and may be near-empty.

title: Named In English Only
idea: Cohort grid of taxa by kingdom and rank showing which have an English common name, which have a non-English one, and which have none.
harm_angle: Organisms with no common name in any language never enter a public conversation about whether to protect them.
caveat: Language values are free text and may not normalize cleanly; a million-row join.

title: Same Lenders Before and After
idea: Compare lender behavior in the pre-pandemic SBA book against their PPP book, by borrower geography and demographics.
chart_shape: slope chart of lender geography mix
harm_angle: Lenders who shut out the same neighborhoods in both programs are a durable pattern, not a pandemic accident.
caveat: Lender names differ in format between the two files and neither carries a lender ID.

source_names: Single audits|IRS exempt org master file
title: Nonprofits spending the most federal money
idea: Rank tax-exempt organizations by total federal awards expended, marked by whether their audit disclosed a material weakness.
harm_angle: The largest recipients of public money in the nonprofit sector, with their audit record attached.
caveat: EIN formatting differs (dashes vs none) between the two sources.

title: Bankruptcies after relief ran out
idea: County timeline of consumer and business bankruptcy filings against PPP dollars per business, testing where relief delayed rather than prevented failure.
harm_angle: Relief that only postponed the collapse, and the households caught in it.
caveat: IDB bankruptcy mart columns unverified; county fields need FIPS normalization on both sides.

title: Opportunities posted vs money actually awarded
idea: Timeline per agency of grant opportunities posted against assistance dollars ultimately obligated, showing announced-but-unfunded programs.
harm_angle: Communities plan around money that was advertised and never arrived.
caveat: The Grants.gov mart holds only 100 rows, so this is a shape demo unless the source is re-ingested.

title: Grants to organizations that lost tax exemption
idea: Timeline per organization of assistance dollars received with the revocation date marked, counting post-revocation awards.
harm_angle: Public grant money going to entities the IRS already stripped of standing.
caveat: USASpending assistance has no EIN, so the join is name-based despite EIN being present on the IRS side.

title: PPP jobs claimed vs jobs that existed
idea: County scatter of total PPP jobs reported against actual county employment, flagging counties where claimed jobs exceed plausible payrolls.
harm_angle: Overstated job claims mean relief money bought nothing for the workers it named.
caveat: PPP county names need FIPS mapping; QCEW grain and industry breakdown unverified.

title: Pandemic loans to barred entities
idea: Count and total PPP loans approved to borrowers matching an active federal exclusion at the time of approval, by state.
harm_angle: Emergency money went out with no check against the government's own ban list.
caveat: Pure name-match with high false-positive risk; PPP borrower names are inconsistently formatted.

title: Disaster dollars per poor household
idea: Three-source chain: county income profile, household disaster registrations, and total federal disaster assistance, expressed as dollars per affected low-income household.
harm_angle: Measures whether recovery money reaches the households least able to self-finance repair.
caveat: Three different geographies must be reconciled; FEMA load is partial.

title: Debarred and still paid
idea: Contractors with an active exclusion period that nonetheless show contract actions during that window, ranked by dollars.
harm_angle: Money keeps flowing to firms the government said it would stop paying.
caveat: UEI population in exclusions is unverified; subsidiary structures can make apparent violations legitimate.

source_names: USASpending contracts|ICE facility codes|ICE detention stints
title: Cost per detained day by operator
idea: Three-source chain: contract dollars to operator, operator to facility, facility to detained days - producing a cost-per-person-day ranking.
harm_angle: Puts a public price on each day a person spends locked up.
caveat: Operator-to-facility link needs manual matching; contracts often cover multiple sites at once.

title: Grants for policing vs grants for people
idea: County-level federal assistance split into law-enforcement programs and social programs, against the county incarceration rate.
chart_shape: stacked bars ordered by jail rate
harm_angle: Shows what the federal government actually buys for a struggling county.
caveat: CFDA-to-category classification is a judgment call; place-of-performance FIPS population is unverified.

title: Accidents Matched to the People Hurt
idea: Join accidents to casualties on the shared incident and report keys and plot accident cause against injury severity, connecting a derailment's cause to the specific bodies it broke.
harm_angle: Linking cause to casualty turns a derailment happened into this maintenance decision cost a person their hand.
caveat: Both tables carry incident_key and report_key but their join semantics and fill rates are unverified; a partial join could silently drop the worst cases.

title: Where Two Federal Forms Disagree
idea: Compare the two form totals carried in the crossing table against the casualty records, showing where the federal forms disagree about how many died in the same event.
harm_angle: When two federal forms report different death counts for the same event, the official toll is unreliable.
caveat: The form-total columns may be self-consistent by construction, making any disagreement a definitional artifact rather than a real undercount.

title: Fatal complaints never investigated
idea: Rank make-model-components by count of complaints flagged fatal or crash-involving where no investigation was ever opened.
harm_angle: People died in defect patterns nobody at the agency ever looked at.
caveat: Complaint fatality flags are self-reported and unverified; absence of an investigation record is not proof of no review.

title: The funnel from complaint to recall
idea: Sankey from complaint volume by component into opened investigations into closed investigations into recalls. The width of each drop-off is the enforcement filter.
harm_angle: Most complaints, including fatal ones, never turn into anything that fixes the car.
caveat: Three-way text join on make and model; the investigation file has fewer aliased fields than needed.

title: How long a defect complains before recall
idea: For each make, model, year and component, plot the first complaint date against the recall notification date. The distribution of that gap is how long people drive the defect.
harm_angle: Drivers keep the defective car for months or years after the complaints start.
caveat: Complaint date field is not in the mart alias list; make and model text normalization across files is a real problem.

title: Recall response cars vs aircraft
idea: Side-by-side comparison of recall cadence and affected-unit counts in ground vehicles against airworthiness activity in the aircraft registry, as parallel timelines.
harm_angle: Two federal safety regimes treat the same kind of defect very differently.
caveat: No join key; the two regulatory regimes are not comparable without heavy caveating.

title: Complaints that keep coming after recall
idea: For each recall, count complaints on the same component after the notification date. Persistent volume means the fix did not work or nobody got it.
harm_angle: A recall on paper does not mean the car in the driveway got fixed.
caveat: Recall completion data is not in these files; persistence could reflect unrepaired vehicles rather than a bad fix.

title: Recall lag and automaker influence
idea: Per manufacturer, the average gap between the earliest complaint and the recall date, against the maker's lobbying spend and federal contract flow.
harm_angle: Every month of recall delay is measured in crashes people did not have to be in.
caveat: Complaint-date field presence in the recalls mart is unverified; manufacturer names need normalization.

title: Tribal land turnout chain
idea: Three-source chain: tribal land geography, county election administration measures, and turnout, showing the access-to-turnout link.
harm_angle: Where the polling places are scarce, the turnout gap follows.
caveat: County-level turnout is not available from state-level MEDSL presidential returns; tribal overlap is spatial.

title: Poisoned ground on tribal land
idea: Superfund sites falling inside or adjacent to tribal boundaries, ranked by state, with NPL status and site type.
harm_angle: Contamination sited on tribal land is the most literal form of who counts as expendable.
caveat: Geometry columns may not be usable as-is; adjacency needs real spatial work, not a FIPS join.

title: Care per square mile of tribal land
idea: Tribal land area against the number, type and bed count of Indian Health Service facilities serving it.
chart_shape: map with proportional symbols plus ranked bars
harm_angle: Treaty-obligated healthcare measured against the actual buildings that deliver it.
caveat: BIA mart is 102 boundary rows; service-area assignment is not in the data.

title: Shortage areas the IHS is supposed to cover
idea: Counties designated as primary-care shortage areas that contain IHS facilities, scored by shortage severity against facility capacity.
harm_angle: Where the federal promise of care and the federal measure of scarcity contradict each other.
caveat: IHS county must be derived from zip; HPSA designations are facility- and population-typed, not simply geographic.

title: Native jail rates and IHS coverage
idea: County Native jail incarceration rates against distance to and capacity of the nearest IHS facility.
harm_angle: Native people are jailed at extreme rates in counties with the least federal health presence.
caveat: Vera's Native jail counts are heavily suppressed in small counties; distance must be computed.

title: Federal dollars to tribal counties
idea: Per-capita federal assistance flowing to counties overlapping tribal land versus comparable rural counties, by program.
harm_angle: Whether the trust obligation shows up in dollars or only in rhetoric.
caveat: Counties overlapping tribal land are not the same as tribal governments as recipients; needs recipient-name work too.

source_names: NHTSA Complaints and Investigations and Recalls
title: From Complaint to Recall Clock
idea: Chain complaints to the investigation they triggered to the recall campaign that resulted, and plot the total elapsed time and the deaths accumulated at each stage per manufacturer.
join_key: recall_number to campno plus make model year and component
harm_angle: The gap between the first complaint and the recall letter is measured in people killed by a known defect.
caveat: Complaints have no direct key to investigations - the link is fuzzy on make, model, year and component text.

title: Probes That Never Became Recalls
idea: Investigations with no matching recall_number, ranked by manufacturer and component, against those that did.
harm_angle: A probe closed without a recall means the regulator looked and then let it go.
caveat: The model header warns the investigations grain is investigation-recall links - naive counting will overstate.

source_names: VA veteran suicide by state|FBI NICS checks
title: Veteran suicide and gun access
idea: State veteran suicide rate against handgun background-check volume per capita, over time.
harm_angle: Means-of-death policy is a veterans' policy whether anyone admits it or not.
caveat: NICS is not sales; state-level aggregation obscures individual access.

title: Which CMS data carries an identifier
idea: Grid of CMS datasets by whether they expose an NPI FIPS or ZIP field to show how much of CMS's published data can actually be linked to anything.
harm_angle: Unlinkable published data lets agencies claim transparency while making accountability impossible.
caveat: These key columns may be metadata annotations rather than populated identifiers.

title: Record group coverage gaps
idea: Grid of federal record groups showing which have any AAD-searchable dataset at all to map the agencies whose electronic records are effectively closed.
harm_angle: Whole agencies with no searchable archival records can never be examined by an outside researcher.
caveat: 18 rows makes the gap map mostly empty which is arguably the point but is a weak chart.

title: Library funnel: scouted to modeled
idea: Flow from scouted through queued, landed, sampled, empty, failed, to modeled, counting sources at each stage. Shows where sources die on the way in.
harm_angle: Every source stuck short of modeled is a public record nobody can search yet.
caveat: LIFECYCLE is a derived CASE expression; the sampled test keys off round row counts and can misfire.

title: Modeled vs sampled vs failed by domain
idea: Stacked bars, one per primary domain, split by lifecycle state. Reveals which subject areas are only half-ingested.
harm_angle: Domains that are mostly sampled are domains where we would report on a 10k-row slice and call it the record.
caveat: 249 of 558 modeled rows have a blank primary domain, so the biggest bar may be 'unknown'.

title: The 10,000-row wall
idea: Distribution of landed row counts with a marked spike at exactly 10,000 — the portal probe cap. Shows how much of the library is a capped sample masquerading as a source.
harm_angle: A capped sample looks like full coverage to a reader; the missing rows are the people left out of the story.
caveat: Cap values are inferred from the run message and a round-number rule, not measured against upstream totals.

title: Failure reasons, ranked
idea: Rank last-run failure messages by count after grouping into families: dead link, auth wall, parse error, timeout, page cap. What actually stops ingestion.
harm_angle: Each failure family is a category of public record the platform cannot see at all.
caveat: Messages are free text; grouping is judgement and may be inconsistent across loaders.

title: Landed but never modeled
idea: Sources with landed rows and no mart, sized by row count. The pile of data we hold but cannot query cleanly.
harm_angle: Data sitting unmodelled is evidence collected and shelved.
caveat: TRUST_LAYER derives mart existence from a name-parsing rule that skips multi-source marts.

title: Mart shrinkage vs landing
idea: Scatter of landed rows against mart rows on a log scale with a parity diagonal. Points far below the line are models silently dropping rows.
harm_angle: Silent row loss in a model quietly deletes the people in those rows from every finding.
caveat: Some marts legitimately aggregate; a low ratio is not automatically a bug.

title: Stub marts that pretend to be real
idea: Sources whose mart holds 1-3 rows over a large landing, flagged by the real-mart test. The fake-completion list.
harm_angle: A one-row mart reported as modeled is a claim of coverage that does not exist.
caveat: The 1-3 row heuristic is arbitrary; small legitimate reference tables may be caught.

title: Orphans: data with no registry entry
idea: Landing tables that exist with no registry row, listed by row count. Data we hold and cannot describe.
harm_angle: An undocumented table cannot be provenance-checked, so nothing built on it can be defended.
caveat: IS_ORPHAN is role-relative: a restricted role sees fewer tables and inflates the count.

title: Empty loads that reported success
idea: Sources whose density probe says nearly every column is blank while the run logged success. Success-shaped failure.
harm_angle: A green ingest over an empty table is how a blind spot gets recorded as coverage.
caveat: The probe samples columns rather than reading all of them; the ratio is approximate.

title: Sampled pile: what full size would be
idea: For sampled sources, plot current rows against the estimated full row count from the registry volume note. Shows the size of what we are missing.
harm_angle: The gap bar is the portion of the public record we have not actually read.
caveat: VOLUME is a free-text registry field and may be missing or vague for most rows.

title: Two-decade backlog board
idea: Every scouted and queued source as a waiting card, aged by how long it has sat unbuilt. The to-do list as a chart.
harm_angle: A source that waits years in the queue is a harm nobody is watching for that long.
caveat: Registry load timestamps may all reflect one bulk import rather than true add dates.

title: Row-count distribution of the library
idea: Log-scale histogram of mart row counts across all modeled sources. Shows the spread from single-row stubs to hundred-million-row corpora.
harm_angle: Tiny sources get treated the same as huge ones in a source list, hiding how thin some evidence is.
caveat: Row count says nothing about the coverage or quality of the underlying population.

title: Where the mass actually is
idea: Ranked bars of the top 25 sources by rows against everything else combined. A handful of corpora are most of the library.
harm_angle: If the platform's bulk is a few federal spending files, its blind spots are everything else.

title: Rows per domain vs sources per domain
idea: Scatter with source count on one axis and total rows on the other, per domain. Finds domains that look well covered by count but are thin by volume.
harm_angle: Counting sources flatters coverage; counting rows shows who we can actually see.
caveat: Blank domain on roughly 45% of modeled rows will skew this until classification finishes.

title: The long tail of tiny sources
idea: Sources under a thousand rows, ranked. Which are legitimately small reference lists and which are broken loads.
harm_angle: A broken load hiding among legitimate small tables is an undetected hole.
caveat: Metadata alone cannot separate legitimately small tables from broken ones.

title: Library growth over time
idea: Cumulative modeled sources and cumulative rows by month of last ingest. The build curve of the whole platform.
harm_angle: A slowing curve means whole areas of the public record stay unlit.
caveat: LAST_INGESTED_AT is last load, not first, so re-ingests distort history; 139 modeled rows have it blank.

title: Build sprint rhythm
idea: Ingest runs per day over the project's life, coloured by success and failure. Where the effort actually went.
harm_angle: Sprint-shaped ingestion means coverage follows attention, not need.

title: Retries before a source lands
idea: For each source, the number of runs before its first success. The cost-to-acquire map.
harm_angle: High-retry sources are the ones publishers make hardest to obtain, sometimes deliberately.
caveat: Retry counts conflate our own loader bugs with publisher obstruction.

title: Hardest publishers to ingest
idea: Publishers ranked by the share of their sources that failed or stalled. Who makes their public record hard to take.
harm_angle: A publisher whose data nobody can download is functionally unaccountable.
caveat: PUBLISHER is free text and likely needs normalising before ranking.

title: Bytes per person covered
idea: Rows held per source divided by the population that source is meant to describe. Which populations are recorded thinly.
harm_angle: Thinly recorded populations are the ones whose harms never reach statistical significance.
caveat: Population denominators are external; the mapping from source to population is judgement.

title: Which IDs bridge the most sources
idea: Rank every standard join key by how many sources carry it. NAME, ZIP, EIN and NPI at the top; the exotic keys at the bottom.
harm_angle: The keys at the top decide which connections the platform can even make.
caveat: JOIN_KEYS_STD is a registry claim; a listed key may be blank or masked in the actual table.

title: Hard IDs versus soft matching
idea: Split sources by whether their best key is a hard identifier or only a name and address. Shows how much of the library can only be joined by guesswork.
harm_angle: Name-only joins produce false matches, and a false match can name the wrong person.
caveat: Tier is partly provisional and not all value-verified.

title: Provisional key tiers still unverified
idea: Sources whose key tier is flagged provisional, ranked by row count. Big tables resting on an unchecked assumption.
harm_angle: An unverified key is how the platform confidently connects two unrelated entities.

title: Sources with no join key at all
idea: The islands: sources carrying no standard key. They can be read but never connected.
harm_angle: An unconnectable source can never show that the same actor appears elsewhere.
caveat: Blank key arrays may reflect unfinished tagging rather than a truly keyless source.

title: Key co-occurrence grid
idea: Matrix of standard keys against each other, each cell shaded by how many sources carry both. Shows which key pairs make crosswalks possible.
harm_angle: Every dark cell is a translation between two worlds the platform cannot yet make.
caveat: Registry co-occurrence is not proof the two columns actually share values.

title: Rare keys that unlock one thing each
idea: Keys carried by only one or two sources — CUSIP, DEA number, voyage id, census tract. The single points of failure in the graph.
harm_angle: When only one source carries a key, one dead loader severs a whole line of inquiry.

title: Name-only sources, ranked by size
idea: The biggest sources whose only key is a name string. The largest fuzzy-match liability on the platform.
harm_angle: Large name-only corpora are where a wrong match reaches the most people.
caveat: NAME appears as a key on 158 modeled sources, so this bar will be crowded.

title: National vs single-state coverage
idea: Sources split by geographic scope: national, state, county, city, international. Where the platform is really a Texas-and-California platform.
harm_angle: If coverage clusters in two states, every finding silently excludes the other forty-eight.
caveat: GEOGRAPHIC_SCOPE is free text of unknown consistency.

title: State coverage map of the library
idea: US map shaded by how many state-level sources the platform holds for each state. The literal blind-spot map.
harm_angle: People in unlit states get no accountability journalism from this platform at all.
caveat: Only a handful of ids carry a state prefix (ca, tx, st); most coverage is federal and needs scope parsing.

title: Federal, state, local, international mix
idea: Share of sources by level of government from the id prefix and jurisdiction field. Shows the platform is overwhelmingly federal.
harm_angle: Most harm is administered locally, and local records are where the platform is thinnest.
caveat: Prefix parsing is a naming convention, not a guaranteed field; 404 of 558 modeled ids start with 'fed'.

title: Sources with coordinates versus without
idea: Which sources carry latitude, longitude or geometry keys, by domain. What can ever be put on a map.
harm_angle: Without geography you cannot show that harm concentrates in particular neighbourhoods.
caveat: LATLON and GEOM tags are registry claims and may be sparse in practice.

title: Geography grain ladder
idea: Sources bucketed by finest available grain: point, address, zip, tract, county, state, national only. The resolution ceiling of the library.
harm_angle: Coarse grain hides local concentration, which is where disparate impact usually lives.
caveat: Grain inferred from key tags rather than measured columns.

title: International coverage, such as it is
idea: Non-US sources by country and domain. How far outside the US the platform can actually see.
harm_angle: Cross-border actors escape a US-only lens entirely.
caveat: Roughly 50 international sources; country attribution needs a clean jurisdiction field.

title: Zip-coded but tract-blind
idea: Sources carrying a zip but no census tract. The gap that blocks demographic overlay.
harm_angle: Zip codes are too coarse to prove which communities bear the cost.
caveat: 81 modeled sources claim ZIP against one claiming CENSUS_TRACT, but both are registry claims.

title: Coverage per capita by state
idea: State source count divided by state population. Corrects for big states and finds the genuinely neglected ones.
harm_angle: Small-state residents may be invisible simply because nobody ingested their records.
caveat: Needs an external population table and a reliable state attribution we may not have.

title: Domain coverage versus population harmed
idea: Sources per domain plotted against an external estimate of how many people that domain touches. Finds under-covered high-harm areas.
harm_angle: Under-covered high-harm domains are exactly where nobody is watching.
caveat: The harm-scale axis is external judgement, not warehouse data, and must be labelled as such.

title: The unclassified pile
idea: Count of sources with unclassified or blank domain, tracked over time as classification progresses. Honest picture of what we do not even know we have.
harm_angle: Unclassified data is data no investigator will ever think to search.
caveat: 67 modeled rows are explicitly UNCLASSIFIED and 249 have a blank domain entirely.

title: Low-confidence domain labels
idea: Sources whose domain was machine-assigned with low confidence, plotted against row count. Big tables filed under a guess.
harm_angle: A misfiled source is invisible to the person who needed it.

title: Human-labelled versus machine-labelled
idea: Share of the catalog classified by a person versus by a model, per domain. How much of the map is machine opinion.
harm_angle: If the map of the library is machine-guessed, so is every claim about coverage.

title: Whole domains we simply do not hold
idea: Named list of subject areas with zero or near-zero sources — insurance, agriculture, social security, local policing. The deliberate blind-spot chart.
harm_angle: Naming what we cannot see is the only honest way to publish what we can.
caveat: Requires an external list of expected domains to diff against, which is a judgement call.

title: Entity types the library can see
idea: Count of sources by entity type: organisation, place, person, facility, filing, payment, vessel, aircraft. What kinds of things the platform knows about.
harm_angle: Whatever entity type is missing is a class of actor that can never be tracked.
caveat: ENTITY_TYPES has a long thin tail of one-off values (physician, gpo) that need folding in.

title: People versus institutions
idea: Share of sources whose entity type includes person against those holding only organisations, per domain. Where the record is about individuals.
harm_angle: If a domain holds no person-level records, individual harm in it is structurally invisible.
caveat: Only about 40 modeled sources claim a person entity type.

title: Event data versus snapshot data
idea: Sources split by whether they carry events over time or only a current-state snapshot. What can ever support a trend claim.
harm_angle: Snapshot-only domains can never show that things are getting worse.
caveat: HAS_EVENTS is a registry boolean claim, not measured from columns.

title: Priority tier versus what actually landed
idea: Sources by declared priority tier, split by lifecycle. Did the high-priority list get built, or did the easy stuff get built.
harm_angle: When only the easy sources land, coverage tracks convenience rather than harm.

title: Accountability relevance versus row mass
idea: The registry's accountability-relevance rating plotted against rows held. Are the most relevant sources the ones we have depth in.
harm_angle: Thin coverage on the highest-relevance sources is where accountability quietly fails.
caveat: ACCOUNTABILITY_RELEVANCE is free text of unknown consistency.

title: Themes the library over-serves
idea: Registry theme tags ranked by source count, against the themes with almost nothing. Where editorial attention has already pooled.
harm_angle: Over-served themes crowd out the harms that never had an advocate.
caveat: THEMES is a sparsely populated array on many rows.

title: Walls between us and the record
idea: Sources by access barrier: open bulk download, API key required, rate limited, login, paid, scrape-only, blocked. The friction map of public data.
harm_angle: Every wall is a public record the public functionally cannot read.
caveat: AUTH_REQUIRED and COST are registry text fields and may be sparsely filled.

title: Key-gated sources still blocked
idea: Sources stalled waiting on an API signup or credential, with how long they have waited. The paperwork blind spot.
harm_angle: A dataset behind a signup form is a dataset most citizens will never see.
caveat: Waiting time must be inferred from run history or notes rather than a stored field.

title: Licence terms that limit what we can publish
idea: Sources by licence family, flagging journalism-use-only and redistribution-restricted. What we hold but cannot show.
harm_angle: Restrictive licensing on public records keeps the public from checking the work.
caveat: LICENSE_TERMS is free text; families need manual grouping.

title: Formats we had to fight
idea: Sources by delivery format: CSV, JSON, API, fixed-width, XLSX, PDF, GIS. How much of the record arrives in a shape designed not to be read.
harm_angle: PDF-only publication is a choice that makes oversight expensive.

title: Cost of the public record
idea: Sources that carry a fee, with the fee noted. What it costs to see the public's own data.
harm_angle: Charging for public records prices out everyone but industry.
caveat: The COST field may be almost entirely blank.

title: Duplicate ingests of the same thing
idea: Clusters of sources that appear to hold the same upstream dataset under different ids, sized by duplicated rows. The twins problem.
harm_angle: Double-counting the same filings inflates any pattern built on them.
caveat: Duplicate detection from name and URL similarity is fuzzy and will produce false pairs.

title: Same publisher, many source ids
idea: Publishers ranked by how many separate source ids they occupy. Shows where one agency was ingested piecemeal.
harm_angle: Piecemeal ingestion of one agency makes its total footprint hard to see.

title: Mart drift: models older than their data
idea: Sources whose mart was last built before the source's last successful ingest. Charts served from stale derived tables.
harm_angle: A stale mart serves yesterday's numbers under today's date.
caveat: LAST_ALTERED bumps on metadata-only changes, so this is a noisy drift signal, not proof.

title: URL rot in the registry
idea: Share of registered source URLs that are dead, by publisher and by year registered. The public record decaying in place.
harm_angle: When the original link dies our copy becomes the only public copy, and nobody audits us.
caveat: Requires live link-checking, which is outside metadata; treat as a proposed measurement.

title: Notes as a bug ledger
idea: Registry note text mined into recurring trap families — sentinel values, quote-wrapped ids, epoch date bugs, page caps. The platform's scar tissue.
harm_angle: Recurring traps are recurring chances to publish a wrong number about a real person.
caveat: NOTE is unstructured, so grouping is interpretive.

title: Case-inconsistent source ids
idea: Source ids differing only by case or prefix convention, which is how the same source ends up counted twice. A hygiene chart with real consequences.
harm_angle: A double-counted source inflates every coverage claim built on the catalog.
caveat: 36 modeled ids use an uppercase FED prefix against 404 lowercase; may be cosmetic only.

title: What we claim versus what we verified
idea: For each coverage claim — key present, domain assigned, full not sampled — the share value-verified versus merely asserted. The trust dashboard.
harm_angle: Publishing on unverified claims is how a platform loses the right to be believed.
caveat: Verification status is scattered across several fields and needs a manual mapping.

title: The confidence ladder of the whole library
idea: Every source placed on a rung: raw only, staged, modeled, key-verified, spine-wired, lens-published. How far anything actually got.
harm_angle: Only the top rungs can carry a published accusation, and the chart shows how few there are.
caveat: The upper rungs are not a single stored field and would have to be derived.

title: Time coverage bars per source
idea: One horizontal bar per source spanning its earliest to latest data date, sorted by start. Where the library's history begins and ends.
harm_angle: Comparisons across sources with different windows produce fake trends.
caveat: TEMPORAL_COVERAGE is free text and start dates are not measured anywhere.

title: The window where cross-source work is honest
idea: Shaded band showing the years in which the most sources hold data simultaneously. The only period a cross-source finding can honestly cover.
harm_angle: Claiming a cross-source pattern outside the shared window claims something the data cannot support.
caveat: Depends entirely on start dates that are currently free text.

title: Blind-spot inventory, front and centre
idea: A deliberately plain board of the biggest known holes: portal crawl uncompleted, whole domains absent, states unrepresented, keys unverified. Published beside every finding.
harm_angle: Telling readers what we cannot see is how they judge what we say we can.
caveat: Curating this honestly is a judgement call, not a query.

title: How much of the library is portal crawl
idea: Share of all catalog rows that are auto-probed portal datasets versus curated sources. Stops anyone quoting the big source count as if it were curated.
harm_angle: Inflated source counts make readers trust a platform more than its curated core deserves.
caveat: Portal rows are identified by an id prefix convention rather than a stored flag.

title: Curated core versus total headcount
idea: Two bars: total catalog rows against the subset that is curated, modeled, key-verified and fresh. The honest size of Ripple.
harm_angle: An honest scale claim is the precondition for an honest finding.

title: Coverage of the people, not the records
idea: Rough estimate of what fraction of US adults appear in at least one person-grain source, by domain. Whose lives the platform can and cannot see.
harm_angle: People absent from every dataset are people no data journalism can ever defend.
caveat: Row counts are not distinct people; heavy double-counting makes this indicative at best.

title: Cost per source in warehouse dollars
idea: Each source plotted by rows held against a rough compute cost to keep it queryable. What accountability costs per megabyte.
harm_angle: If the expensive sources are the accountability-relevant ones, the budget becomes the censor.
caveat: No cost field exists in metadata; would need warehouse billing data this pass is not touching.

title: A shelf-map of the library
idea: The catalog drawn as physical library shelving, shelf length by rows, visible gaps where domains are missing. Coverage as a room you can walk.
harm_angle: Seeing the empty shelves persuades more than any coverage percentage.
caveat: Pure presentation device; adds no new measurement.

title: Constellation of the join keys
idea: Keys as stars, sources as the light between them, brightness by how many sources share the key. The platform's night sky.
harm_angle: The dark patches are where nothing can be connected to anything.
caveat: Aesthetic reframing of the key co-occurrence chart.

title: Half-life of a public dataset
idea: Fit a decay curve to how long sources stay fresh before going stale, split by publisher type. How fast the public record rots.
harm_angle: A short half-life means oversight expires faster than the harm does.
caveat: One freshness snapshot cannot fit a decay curve; needs repeated measurement over months.

title: Sources ranked by how hard someone made this
idea: Composite obstruction score from retries, auth walls, formats, licence limits and failures, ranked by publisher. An obstruction index.
harm_angle: A publisher at the top of an obstruction index is choosing who gets to look.
caveat: The composite weighting is invented and measures our friction as much as their intent.

title: The graph if the top hub disappeared
idea: Connection network redrawn with the single most-connected source removed, showing how much goes dark. A fragility stress test.
harm_angle: One agency pulling one dataset could sever most of the platform's cross-checks.
caveat: Simulated removal, not observed; assumes the edge store is complete.

title: What the library would look like fully built
idea: Current coverage overlaid with the full registry backlog if everything queued and scouted landed. The size of the unfinished job.
harm_angle: The gap between held and knowable is the honest measure of what is still hidden.
caveat: Full-size estimates for unlanded sources barely exist in metadata.

title: Sources nobody has ever queried
idea: Modeled sources with no recorded downstream lens, model or review decision referencing them. Data collected and never once looked at.
harm_angle: An unread dataset is a harm nobody checked for.
caveat: Usage and lineage may not be recorded anywhere; likely needs new instrumentation.

title: Time from public release to Ripple ingest
idea: For each source, the lag between the publisher's release and our load. How far behind the public record the platform runs.
harm_angle: A long lag means every finding is archaeology rather than warning.
caveat: Publisher release dates are not stored; only data-through and load date exist.

title: Blind-spot map against the year's harm headlines
idea: Overlay the library's domain coverage on a list of the year's biggest public-harm stories, marking which we could and could not have caught.
harm_angle: It names, in advance, the next story this platform would miss.
caveat: The headline list is external editorial judgement, not warehouse metadata.

title: The catalog as a self-portrait over time
idea: Animate the whole catalog grid month by month as cells change lifecycle colour. Watch the library light up and watch which corners never do.
harm_angle: The corners that never light up are the constituencies nobody built for.
caveat: Lifecycle history is not versioned; only the current state is stored.

title: Key columns that are actually empty
idea: Detected key columns plotted by how populated they really are. The masked-ID trap made visible across every table at once.
harm_angle: A key that looks full and is blank produces confident findings built on nothing.
caveat: Requires the column catalog to cover every mart; it may only cover pack tables.

title: Populated percentage of every column
idea: All catalogued columns as a fill-rate distribution, faceted by chart role. How much of the library is actually blank space.
harm_angle: Blank fields are missing people and missing outcomes, not just missing cells.
caveat: Fill rate is sampled at profile time, not a full scan.

title: Columns nobody can explain
idea: Share of catalogued columns with a machine-guessed gloss versus a curated one, per source. Where the data dictionary is guessing.
harm_angle: A misunderstood column is how a chart says something the data never said.

title: Every column that is entirely empty
idea: Columns whose chart role is empty, grouped by source. Dead weight and hidden truncation.
harm_angle: An empty column can mean the publisher redacted the exact field that mattered.
caveat: Empty at sample time may not mean empty overall for very sparse columns.

title: Redaction surface: fields the publisher blanked
idea: Columns present in the schema but almost entirely null, ranked by how central the field name sounds. Where the record was hollowed out before we got it.
harm_angle: Deliberate blanks are the shape of what an agency decided the public may not know.
caveat: Cannot distinguish deliberate redaction from a genuinely optional field.

title: Chart-role mix per source
idea: Each source as a small bar of its columns split into numeric, date, category, text and empty. Shows which sources can support analysis at all.
harm_angle: An all-text source cannot be measured, so the harm inside it stays anecdotal.

title: The connection graph
idea: Every landing table as a node, every measured overlap as an edge, thickness by matched key count. The platform's whole wiring in one picture.
harm_angle: The shape of the graph is the shape of what can be held accountable across silos.
caveat: Edge confidence is explicitly uncalibrated; some edges are coincidental overlap.

title: Islands in the graph
idea: The same network with unconnected components highlighted. Which clusters of sources talk only to themselves.
harm_angle: An isolated cluster means harm in that domain can never be traced to actors elsewhere.

title: Edges by key type
idea: The graph coloured by the join key that creates each edge. Shows whether the platform is held together by real IDs or by names.
harm_angle: A graph held together by name matching will eventually accuse the wrong person.

title: Match rate distribution of edges
idea: How well each pair of sources actually overlaps, as a distribution by tier. Separates real bridges from thin coincidences.
harm_angle: Thin overlaps presented as connections manufacture relationships that do not exist.
caveat: MATCH_RATE depends on the normalisation choices made per key.

title: Most-connected sources
idea: Rank sources by edge degree. The hubs the whole platform leans on.
harm_angle: If a hub source rots, every connected finding rots with it.

title: Bridges nobody uses
idea: Verified high-overlap edges that no published model or lens currently exploits. Wired but unwalked.
harm_angle: Every unused bridge is a question about who repeats across systems that nobody has asked.
caveat: Needs edge data cross-referenced with mart lineage, which may not be captured on disk.

title: Graph growth over rebuilds
idea: Edge count and entity count by rebuild timestamp. Whether the platform is getting more connected or just bigger.
harm_angle: More rows without more edges means a bigger pile, not a better map.
caveat: Full rebuilds replace rows by run id, so older run history may be gone.

title: Entity spine coverage by source
idea: Share of each source's distinct key values that resolve to a spine entity. Who is in the spine and who falls through.
harm_angle: Rows that never resolve are people and firms the platform can never follow across datasets.
caveat: Spine scope is a hand-written spec list; absence may mean unwired rather than unmatchable.

title: Rejected key wirings
idea: Candidate key columns rejected during spine wiring, grouped by reason: normalises to nothing, single value, sentinel, quote-wrapped. The false-positive museum.
harm_angle: Each rejected key was a connection the platform nearly made wrongly.
caveat: Reject evidence lives in a generated CSV that may be out of date.

title: Edge confidence versus tier
idea: Scatter of heuristic confidence against measured match rate, coloured by declared tier. Checks whether the tier labels mean anything.
harm_angle: If tier labels do not track real overlap, every cross-source claim inherits the error.
caveat: Confidence is documented as uncalibrated, so this is a diagnostic, not a truth.

title: Degrees of separation between domains
idea: For each pair of domains, the shortest path through the connection graph. How many hops from a campaign donation to a nursing-home death.
harm_angle: Long paths mean the money and the harm can never be shown in the same sentence.
caveat: Requires mapping tables back to domains, and paths through weak edges may be illusory.

title: Freshness states across the whole library
idea: Every source as a cell in a grid coloured fresh, due, overdue, stale, dead, unknown. One picture of how current the library really is.
harm_angle: Reporting off stale data accuses people using facts that have since changed.
caveat: Freshness is only as good as the recency-column pick; 'unknown' may dominate.

title: Load date vs data date
idea: Scatter of when a source was last ingested against how current its data actually is. Points far off the diagonal are recently loaded but years old.
harm_angle: A fresh-looking load over two-year-old data makes a reader think they are seeing today.
caveat: This is exactly the load-stamp trap the ledger was built for; needs both fields populated.

title: Data age by domain
idea: Median days behind, per domain, as a dot plot. Which subject areas the platform is chronically late on.
harm_angle: Chronically late domains are the ones where ongoing harm goes unseen longest.
caveat: DATA_AGE_DAYS is negative for intentionally future-dated annual sources.

title: Promised cadence vs delivered cadence
idea: Slope chart pairing each source's stated update cadence with its actual measured lag bucket. Where the publisher's promise and reality diverge.
harm_angle: Agencies that miss their own publishing cadence are agencies hiding in the delay.
caveat: UPDATE_CADENCE is a registry free-text claim; CADENCE_BUCKET is our own inference.

title: Sources with no time axis at all
idea: Count and list sources where no recency column exists. The part of the library that cannot answer 'when'.
harm_angle: Without a date you cannot show a pattern getting worse, only that it exists.
caveat: A null recency column may mean the builder failed to find one, not that none exists.

title: Date columns that are text traps
idea: Sources whose recency column parses as YYYYMMDD text or year text rather than a real date. The silent epoch-bug surface.
harm_angle: A misparsed date puts an event in 1970 and erases it from every timeline.
caveat: Needs the freshness ledger and column catalog both populated for the same sources.

title: Dead sources: rows went to zero
idea: Sources whose measured row count fell to zero. Data we used to have and no longer do.
harm_angle: When a public dataset disappears, the accountability it enabled disappears with it.
caveat: Single-snapshot ledger; a zero may be a failed measurement rather than a real disappearance.

title: Freshness decay curve
idea: Cumulative share of sources against how many days behind they are. How much of the library is within a month, a quarter, a year.
harm_angle: The tail of the curve is the share of findings that would be out of date on publication.
caveat: Static and annual sources distort the tail unless bucketed separately.

title: Cadence mix of the library
idea: Share of sources by cadence bucket, from real-time to static. Tells you what kind of platform this actually is.
harm_angle: A library that is mostly annual snapshots can only find slow harms, never live ones.

title: Never re-ingested since first load
idea: Sources whose only ingest run is their first. One-shot loads pretending to be a maintained feed.
harm_angle: A one-shot load ages into a false claim about the present.
caveat: Run history may have been truncated or re-keyed across rebuilds.

title: Recency column choices, audited
idea: Which column each source uses as its clock, grouped by name pattern. Exposes sources clocked off a load stamp rather than an event date.
harm_angle: Clocking a source off its load stamp makes stale data look permanently fresh.
caveat: The ledger explicitly bans load stamps, so violations may be rare or already fixed.
